questions.q: Which Qur’anic reference is especially associated with cooperation in righteousness, not wrongdoing?
questions.e: Qur’an 5:2 directly addresses cooperation in righteousness, not wrongdoing.

questions.q: Which Qur’anic reference is especially associated with completion and perfection of the religion?
questions.e: Qur’an 5:3 directly addresses completion and perfection of the religion.

questions.q: What is the central theme of Nawawi Hadith 22?
o: Allah being pure and accepting only what is pure
the instruction not to surrender to anger
performing obligations and avoiding prohibitions as a path to Paradise
the principle that harm should neither be inflicted nor reciprocated
questions.e: Hadith 22 of Imam al-Nawawi’s collection is commonly studied for performing obligations and avoiding prohibitions as a path to Paradise.

questions.q: Which place or region is most closely associated with Delhi Sultanate?
questions.e: Delhi Sultanate is associated with northern India, centred on Delhi under principal place/region.

questions.q: Care after his mother’s death is associated with which person or group?
questions.e: Care after his mother’s death is associated with ‘Abd al-Muttalib and then Abu Talib under associated person/group.

questions.q: Which textual or historical basis is most closely associated with Hijrah to Madinah?
questions.e: Hijrah to Madinah is associated with Qur’an 9:40 and authentic Seerah under textual or historical anchor.

questions.q: Which textual or historical basis is most closely associated with Accession of ‘Umar (RA)?
o: accepted history of early Islamic Iraq
Hadith reports on the virtues of ‘Uthman
questions.e: Accession of ‘Umar (RA) is associated with Metropolitan Museum ruler chronology under textual or historical anchor.

questions.q: Which place or region is most closely associated with Safavid dynasty?
questions.e: Safavid dynasty is associated with Iran, especially Isfahan under principal place/region.

questions.q: uraysh boycott is associated with which person or group?
o: the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم and the Muslim community
questions.e: Quraysh boycott is associated with Banu Hashim and Banu al-Muttalib under associated person/group.

questions.q: Select the place most directly connected with Accession of ‘Umar (RA).
questions.e: Accession of ‘Umar (RA) is associated with Madinah under principal place.

questions.q: Which textual or historical basis is most closely associated with Isra and Mi‘raj?
questions.e: Isra and Mi‘raj is associated with Qur’an 17:1 and authentic Hadith under textual or historical anchor.

questions.q: Select the person or group connected with ‘Ali’s mission to Yemen.
questions.e: ‘Ali’s mission to Yemen is associated with ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA) under associated person/group.

questions.q: Identify the main significance associated with Mus‘ab ibn ‘Umayr’s mission to Yathrib.
o: teaching the Qur’an and preparing the growing Madinan community
birth into the Banu Hashim clan of Quraysh
steadfast faith followed by emancipation from enslavement
the Prophet Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم belonged to the respected Hashimite clan
questions.e: Mus‘ab ibn ‘Umayr’s mission to Yathrib is associated with teaching the Qur’an and preparing the growing Madinan community under key significance.

questions.q: Select the textual or historical basis associated with Bay‘ah of Abu Bakr (RA).
questions.e: Bay‘ah of Abu Bakr (RA) is associated with accepted early Islamic chronology under textual or historical anchor.

questions.q: Leading prayers during the Prophet’s final illness is important primarily because of which point?
o: appointment to lead congregational prayer during the final illness
distinctive family relationship behind the title Dhu al-Nurayn
close Companion and first Rashidun caliph
leadership of the first four rightly guided caliphs
questions.e: Leading prayers during the Prophet’s final illness is associated with appointment to lead congregational prayer during the final illness under key significance.

questions.q: Select the statement that best captures the significance of Zayd ibn Harithah’s early faith.
o: public proclamation of the prophetic message
the Prophet’s recognised children in mainstream Seerah
a framework of mutual obligations, security, and communal order
membership among the earliest believers and close Companions
questions.e: Zayd ibn Harithah’s early faith is associated with membership among the earliest believers and close Companions under key significance.

questions.q: Select the textual or historical basis associated with Khadijah’s acceptance of Islam.
o: Sahih al-Bukhari reports on the Yemen mission
questions.e: Khadijah’s acceptance of Islam is associated with Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Revelation under textual or historical anchor.

questions.q: Arbitration over the Black Stone is associated with which person or group?
o: the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم and the Muslim community
questions.e: Arbitration over the Black Stone is associated with the clans of Quraysh under associated person/group.

questions.q: Accession of ‘Ali (RA) is associated with which period or date?
questions.e: Accession of ‘Ali (RA) is associated with 35 AH / 656 CE under period/date.

questions.q: Identify the main significance associated with Acceptance of Islam by ‘Umar (RA).
o: beginning of Qur’anic revelation with the command to read
strengthening of the early Muslim community
guardianship by his grandfather and paternal uncle
teaching religion and administering community affairs
questions.e: Acceptance of Islam by ‘Umar (RA) is associated with strengthening of the early Muslim community under key significance.

مریض کو بروقت دوا دی گئی تھی۔
علامات برقرار رہیں تو مزید معائنہ ضروری ہوگا۔
questions.e: درست ترجمہ: علامات برقرار رہیں تو مزید معائنہ ضروری ہوگا۔

ڈاکٹر مریض کی حالت کی نگرانی کر رہی ہے۔
مریض کو بروقت دوا دی گئی تھی۔
علامات برقرار رہیں تو مزید معائنہ ضروری ہوگا۔

The passengers are confirming the departure time.
If the weather improves, the flight will depart in the evening.
questions.e: درست ترجمہ: If the weather improves, the flight will depart in the evening.

questions.q: “ظرفی” کی درست تعریف منتخب کریں۔
o: کسی اسم کی تخصیص (محدود دائرہ) بیان کرے
ایک لفظ دوسرے کا مادہ ہو (جس سے وہ بنا ہو)
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 214: ظرفی — وقت یا جگہ ظاہر کرے

questions.q: ان اصطلاحات—پیش، کهڑی زبر، کهڑی زیر، جزم / سکون—میں درست اصطلاح اور تعریف کا جوڑا منتخب کریں۔
o: کهڑی زیر — وہ عالمت جو ساکن حرف پر لگائی جاتی ہے، آواز رک جاتی ہے۔
جزم / سکون — سیدھی لکیر جو مخصوص الفاظ میں زبر کی صورت میں آتی ہے۔
پیش — واؤ نما نشان، جس سے آواز گول ہوتی ہے۔
کهڑی زبر — مخصوص الفاظ میں زیر کی خاص صورت۔
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 213: پیش — واؤ نما نشان، جس سے آواز گول ہوتی ہے۔

questions.q: محاورہ «آسمان سر پر اٹھانا» کا مطلب کیا ہے؟
questions.e: آسمان سر پر اٹھانا غیر معمولی شور مچانے کو کہتے ہیں۔

questions.q: «اجمال» کے مقابل مفہوم کا لفظ کون سا ہے؟
questions.e: اجمال اختصار ہے، تفصیل اس کے مقابل ہے۔

questions.q: «مستند» کے قریب ترین معنی کون سے ہیں؟
questions.e: مستند ایسی بات یا دستاویز ہے جس پر اعتماد کیا جا سکے۔

questions.q: محاورہ «بات کا بتنگڑ بنانا» کا مفہوم کیا ہے؟
o: کسی کی بات غور سے سننا
معمولی بات کو بڑھا چڑھا کر پیش کرنا
questions.e: بتنگڑ بنانا کسی چھوٹی بات کو غیر ضروری طور پر بڑا بنانا ہے۔

questions.q: اس لفظ کو کیا کہتے ہیں جو کسی دوسرے لفظ سے نکلا ہو؟
"کھاٹ سے کھٹولا" اسم نکرہ کی کون سی قسم کو ظاہر کرتا ہے؟
ان اصطلاحات—روزمرہ، ضرب المثل، تشبیہ، استعارہ—میں درست اصطلاح اور تعریف کا جوڑا منتخب کریں۔
o: استعارہ — ایک جملہ یا قول جو زندگی کے تجربات یا سچائیوں کو سادہ اور اثر دار انداز میں بیان کرتا ہے۔
تشبیہ — تشبیہ سے مبالغہ کرتے ہوئے مشبہ کا ذکر چھوڑ دینا اور صرف مشبہ بہ کو بطور حقیقت بیان کرنا۔
ضرب المثل — کسی چیز کو کسی دوسری چیز کے مشابہ قرار دینا جس میں دونوں کے درمیان کوئی مشترک خوبی ہو۔
روزمرہ — وہ جملے یا الفاظ جو روزانہ کی بات چیت میں معمولی طور پر استعمال ہوتے ہیں، جن کا مطلب صاف اور واضح ہوتا ہے۔
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 215: روزمرہ — وہ جملے یا الفاظ جو روزانہ کی بات چیت میں معمولی طور پر استعمال ہوتے ہیں، جن کا مطلب صاف اور واضح ہوتا ہے۔

questions.q: یہ تعریف کس اصطلاح کی ہے؟ “جو کسی اور لفظ سے نہ بنا ہو”
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 208: اسمِ جامد — جو کسی اور لفظ سے نہ بنا ہو

questions.q: یہ تعریف کس اصطلاح کی ہے؟ “ایسا اسم جو کسی کام کے کرنے یا ہونے کے معنی دے”
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 208: مصدر — ایسا اسم جو کسی کام کے کرنے یا ہونے کے معنی دے

questions.q: ان اصطلاحات—حرفِ جواب، حرفِ انبساط، حرفِ تعجب، حرفِ تنبیہ—میں درست اصطلاح اور تعریف کا جوڑا منتخب کریں۔
o: حرفِ جواب — جو سوال یا بات کے جواب میں استعمال ہو۔
حرفِ انبساط — جو حیرت یا تعجب ظاہر کرے۔
حرفِ تعجب — جو خبردار کرنے یا متوجہ کرنے کے لیے ہو۔
حرفِ تنبیہ — جو خوشی یا وسع تِ دل کے اظہار کے لیے ہو۔
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 212: حرفِ جواب — جو سوال یا بات کے جواب میں استعمال ہو۔

questions.q: تعریف “وہ اسم جو کسی چیز کی کثرت یا مقدار ظاہر کرے۔” اور مثال “لوگ، درخت، کتابیں، پرندے” کس اصطلاح کو ظاہر کرتی ہیں؟
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 209: جمع — وہ اسم جو کسی چیز کی کثرت یا مقدار ظاہر کرے۔

questions.q: “تملیکی” کی درست تعریف منتخب کریں۔
o: کسی اسم کی تخصیص (محدود دائرہ) بیان کرے
ملکیت ظاہر کرے (کسی چیز کا مالک کون ہے)
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 214: تملیکی — ملکیت ظاہر کرے (کسی چیز کا مالک کون ہے)

questions.q: یہ تعریف کس اصطلاح کی ہے؟ “جو خواہش یا آرزو ظاہر کرے۔”
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 212: حرفِ تمنا — جو خواہش یا آرزو ظاہر کرے۔

questions.q: یہ تعریف کس اصطلاح کی ہے؟ “وہ اسم جو کسی جملے یا فقرے کے ساتھ منسلک ہوتا ہو اور مکمل معنی تب تک نہیں دیتا جب تک کہ دوسرا جملہ اس کے ساتھ نہ ہو۔”
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 209: اسمِ موصول — وہ اسم جو کسی جملے یا فقرے کے ساتھ منسلک ہوتا ہو اور مکمل معنی تب تک نہیں دیتا جب تک کہ دوسرا جملہ اس کے ساتھ نہ ہو۔

questions.q: “ماضی احتمالی” کی درست تعریف منتخب کریں۔
o: وہ حرف جو دو الفاظ یا جملوں کو مالئے
غیر (ایسا ماضی جو شاید یا ممکن ہے کہ ہوا ہو )یقینی یا قیاسی
ایسا ماضی جو خواہش یا شرط کے اظہار کے لیے ہو، حقیقت میں واقع نہ ہوا ہو
وہ حرف جو کسی سبب یا علت کو ظاہر کرے
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 211: ماضی احتمالی — غیر (ایسا ماضی جو شاید یا ممکن ہے کہ ہوا ہو )یقینی یا قیاسی

questions.q:
Read the passage: “A district office moved its forms online. Applications arrived faster, but residents without reliable internet often needed help at a crowded service desk. The director kept the digital system and added a staffed counter in each rural centre.”

Which view best captures the director’s decision?
o: Digital processing and in-person assistance can coexist
questions.e: The director retained online processing while providing an in-person route.

questions.q:
Read the passage: “A district office moved its forms online. Applications arrived faster, but residents without reliable internet often needed help at a crowded service desk. The director kept the digital system and added a staffed counter in each rural centre.”

Why were the rural counters added?
o: To reduce the number of centres
To assist residents who faced a digital access barrier
questions.e: Faster processing did not remove the access problem for residents without reliable internet.

questions.q: Choose the sentence with the proper Adjective.
o: French wines are not available here
He has lost all his wealth
questions.e: “French” is a proper adjective derived from the proper noun France.

questions.q: Choose the sentence with the Adverb of time.
o: I have spoken to him already
questions.e: “Already” refers to a point in time; “seldom” in another option expresses frequency.

questions.q: Choose the option that is correct according to the standard use of English.
o: The doctor told him to give away smoking
The doctor told him to give up smoke
The doctor told him giving up smoking
The doctor told him to give up smoking
questions.e: “Told him to give up smoking” has the required infinitive after told and the gerund after give up.

questions.q: Which sentence uses the correct adjective form?
o: The movie was scary than I expected
The movie was scare than I expected
The movie was scarier than I expected
The movie was more scarier than I expected
questions.e: The comparative of “scary” is “scarier”; adding “more” would form a double comparative.

questions.q: Which of the following sentences is grammatically correct?
o: My friends and I went to the movie.
I and my friends went to the movie.
My friends and me went to the movie.
Me and my friends went to the movie.
questions.e: In a compound subject, “my friends and I” uses the subject pronoun “I” and conventional ordering.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The education in Pakistan needs a urgent reform because the quality is poor.”?
o: Education in Pakistan needs urgent reform because the quality are poor.
Education in Pakistan needs urgent reform because the quality is not poor.
The education in Pakistan needs a urgent reform because the quality is poor.
Education in Pakistan needs urgent reform because the quality is poor.
questions.e: Two abstract general nouns drop the article; reform here is uncountable, so a is wrong.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Hoping for promotion, the report was submitted early by the officer.”?
o: Hoping for promotion, the report was submitted early by the officer.
Hoping for promotion, the officer submitted the report early.
Hoping for promotion, officer submitted the report early.
Hoping for promotion, the officer submitted the report early not.
questions.e: Hoping for promotion, the officer submitted the report early. (The officer hoped.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “In the event that the bill is passed, it will come into effect immediately.”?
o: If the bill is not passed, it will take effect immediately.
If the bill are passed, it will take effect immediately.
If the bill is passed, it will take effect immediately.
In the event that the bill is passed, it will come into effect immediately.
questions.e: If the bill is passed, it will take effect immediately. (in the event that > if.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The committee recommended to postpone the meeting.”?
o: The committee recommended postponing the meeting not.
The committee recommended to postpone the meeting.
The committee recommended postponing the meeting.
questions.e: The committee recommended postponing the meeting. (Recommend + gerund.)

questions.q: Which Rule is associated with Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) “You can't compare apples to oranges.” in the English reference?
o: Used when some work is finished, or for disconnection/cutting
Used for position on a surface
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 232: Rule “Comparison between dissimilar things” corresponds to Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) “You can't compare apples to oranges.”.

questions.q: Which Direct Speech is associated with Example “He said, "I have just finished." → He said that he had only finished.” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 227: Direct Speech “Just” corresponds to Example “He said, "I have just finished." → He said that he had only finished.”.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The policy nearly helped a million families.”?
o: The policy helped nearly an million families.
The policy helped nearly a million families.
The policy nearly helped a million families.
The policy helped nearly a million families not.
questions.e: The policy helped nearly a million families. (Nearly limits the number.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “At this point in time, we are in the process of conducting a review.”?
o: We are not now reviewing it. / We are conducting a review.
At this point in time, we are in the process of conducting a review.
We are now reviewing it. / We are conducting a review.
We is now reviewing it. / We are conducting a review.
questions.e: We are now reviewing it. / We are conducting a review. (Filler removed.)

questions.q: Which Type is associated with Example Word “can” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 230: Type “Modal Verb” corresponds to Example Word “can”.

questions.s: Present and past: the four forms of each
questions.q: Which sentence keeps a consistent tense?
o: He enters the hall, saw the notice and leaves immediately.
He enters the hall, sees the notice and left immediately.
He entered the hall, sees the notice and leaves immediately.
He entered the hall, saw the notice and left immediately.
questions.e: A completed past narrative stays in the past simple throughout.

questions.q: The bus remained ____ for an hour outside the terminal.
questions.e: Stationary means not moving; stationery means writing materials.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Poverty and the illiteracy are the two biggest problem facing the country.”?
o: Poverty and illiteracy is the two biggest problems facing the country.
Poverty and illiteracy are not the two biggest problems facing the country.
Poverty and the illiteracy are the two biggest problem facing the country.
Poverty and illiteracy are the two biggest problems facing the country.
questions.e: General abstract nouns take no article, and two requires a plural noun.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “To understand the crisis, accurate data is essential.”?
o: To understand the crisis, accurate data is essential.
To understand the crisis, we need accurate data.
than understand the crisis, we need accurate data.
To understand the crisis, we need accurate data not.
questions.e: To understand the crisis, we need accurate data. (Supply a doer for the infinitive phrase.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The final end result of the policy was a complete and total failure.”?
o: The final end result of the policy was a complete and total failure.
questions.e: The policy failed completely. (Redundant doublets cut.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “He is interested in to study public policy.”?
o: He is not interested in studying public policy.
He is interested in to study public policy.
He is interested in studying public policy.
He are interested in studying public policy.
questions.e: He is interested in studying public policy. (After a preposition → gerund.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “He is an honourable man and a university teacher who holds a MPhil degree.”?
o: He are an honourable man and a university teacher who holds an MPhil degree.
He is an honourable man and a university teacher who holds an MPhil degree.
He is an honourable man and a university teacher who holds a MPhil degree.
He is not an honourable man and a university teacher who holds an MPhil degree.
questions.e: Sound decides: silent h takes an, the y-sound of university takes a, and MPhil begins with the vowel sound e.

questions.q: Which Structure is associated with Tense “Past Continuous” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 244: Structure “subject + was/were + verb-ing” corresponds to Tense “Past Continuous”.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “She almost spent the entire budget on salaries.”?
o: She spent almost entire budget on salaries.
She spent almost the entire budget on salaries.
She almost spent the entire budget on salaries.
She spent almost the entire budget on salaries not.
questions.e: She spent almost the entire budget on salaries. (Almost limits the amount.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “After reviewing the budget, the decision was made to cut spending.”?
o: After reviewing the budget, the government decided to cut spending not.
After reviewing the budget, the government decided than cut spending.
After reviewing the budget, the government decided to cut spending.
After reviewing the budget, the decision was made to cut spending.
questions.e: After reviewing the budget, the government decided to cut spending. (The doer must follow the phrase.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The minister denied to have any knowledge of the deal.”?
o: The minister denied having any knowledge of the deal not.
The minister denied to have any knowledge of the deal.
The minister denied having any knowledge of the deal.
minister denied having any knowledge of the deal.
questions.e: The minister denied having any knowledge of the deal. (Deny + gerund.)

questions.q: Which Tense is associated with Structure “subject + has/have + past participle” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 244: Tense “Present Perfect” corresponds to Structure “subject + has/have + past participle”.

questions.q: Which Direct Speech is associated with Indirect Speech “Then” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 227: Direct Speech “Now” corresponds to Indirect Speech “Then”.

Running late, the commuters missed the bus.
Running late, the bus was missed by the commuters.
Running late, the commuters missed the bus not.

Reducing poverty is the main goal of the programme without.
Reducing poverty is the main goal of the programme.

questions.s: Capital letters, full stops and the everyday comma
questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “In the Spring of 2020 many School’s in the Province were closed.”?
o: In the spring of 2020, many schools in the province were closed.
In the Spring of 2020 many School’s in the Province were closed.
In the spring of 2020, many schools in the province were not closed.
In the spring of 2020, many schools in the province was closed.
questions.e: Seasons and common nouns take no capital; plurals take no apostrophe; the introductory phrase takes a comma.

questions.q: A tank contains milk and water in the ratio 2:3. After eight litres of water are added, the ratio becomes 1:2. What was the initial volume?
questions.e: Let milk = 2x and water = 3x. Then 2x/(3x+8) = 1/2, so x=8 and the initial volume is 5x=40 litres.

questions.q: A household earned Rs 1,000 and spent Rs 700. Its income rose by 20% while its expenditure rose by 15%. By what percentage did its savings rise?
questions.e: Original saving = Rs 300. New saving = 1,200 − 805 = Rs 395. The increase is 95/300 × 100 = 31⅔%.

questions.q: A can complete a job in 12 days and B in 18. After they work together for three days, A finishes the rest alone. How many more days does A need?
questions.e: In three days they do 3(1/12+1/18)=5/12. The remainder 7/12 takes A seven days.

questions.q: A divisor leaves remainder 7 when dividing 91 and also when dividing 133. What is the greatest possible divisor?
questions.e: The divisor must divide 91−7=84 and 133−7=126; their greatest common divisor is 42.

questions.q: One pipe fills a tank in 10 hours and another in 15 hours. An open drain empties it in 30 hours. If all three are open, how long does filling take?
questions.e: Net rate = 1/10+1/15−1/30=2/15 of a tank per hour; time = 15/2 hours.

questions.q: A meeting has four presentations. W follows X immediately; Y immediately precedes X; and Z is not first. Which presentation must be last?
questions.e: Y–X–W is a consecutive block; placing Z before it would put Z first, so the order is Y, X, W, Z.

questions.q: The mean of eight readings is 14. A reading recorded as 10 is corrected to 26. What is the corrected mean?
questions.e: The total increases by 16; the mean increases by 16/8=2, from 14 to 16.

questions.q: The ratio of teachers to learners is 2:35. If six teachers and 45 learners join, the ratio becomes 1:15. How many teachers were there originally?
questions.e: Let teachers be 2x and learners 35x. Then (2x+6)/(35x+45)=1/15, so 30x+90=35x+45, x=9 and teachers=18.

questions.q: The first shift produced 60% of a factory’s daily output, which was 240 units more than the second shift. How many units were produced that day?
questions.e: The difference between 60% and 40% is 20% of total output; 240 ÷ 0.20 = 1,200.

questions.q: The series reads 1, 4, 10, 19, 31. Which number should come next?
questions.e: The differences are 3, 6, 9 and 12; the next difference is 15, giving 31+15=46.

questions.q: The boys and girls in a class are in the ratio 5:4. When nine girls join, their numbers become equal. What was the original class size?
questions.e: The difference between the original groups is one part = 9, so the original nine parts total 81.

questions.q: The mean of nine readings is 26. One reading recorded as 41 should have been 23. What is the corrected mean?
questions.e: The recorded total is 234. Replacing 41 by 23 gives 216; 216/9 = 24.

questions.q: The sum of three consecutive odd positive integers is 75. What is the largest?
questions.e: Their middle value is 75/3=25, so the integers are 23, 25 and 27.

questions.q: What is the smaller angle between the hands of a clock at 2:20?
questions.e: The minute hand is at 120°. The hour hand is at 60°+10°=70°. The difference is 50°.

questions.q: The circumference of a circle is 44 cm. Using π=22/7, what is its area?
questions.e: 2πr=44 gives r=7 cm; area=(22/7)×49=154 cm².

questions.q: The product of two consecutive positive integers is 306. What is the smaller integer?
questions.e: 17×18=306, so the smaller integer is 17.

questions.q: What is the least positive integer that leaves remainder two when divided by five and remainder three when divided by seven?
questions.e: Numbers congruent to 2 mod 5 are 2,7,12,17,...; 17 leaves remainder 3 when divided by 7.

questions.q: Which number comes next: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, __?
questions.e: The terms are n(n+1): 1×2, 2×3, ..., so the next is 6×7=42.

questions.q: Eighteen pupils average 62 marks and twelve others average 77 marks. What is the mean for all thirty pupils?
Six parcels have an average weight of 50 kg. One parcel was entered as 68 kg instead of 86 kg. What is the corrected average?
questions.e: Correcting the entry adds 18 kg to the total; the mean increases by 18/6=3 kg to 53 kg.

questions.q: Five numbers are in ascending order: 14, 18, x, 25, 30. Their mean is 22. What is their median?
questions.e: Their total is 110; the four known numbers sum to 87, so x=23, the middle value.

questions.q: A student obtained 72 marks out of 90 on the first part. How many marks out of the remaining 30 are needed for 85% overall on a 120-mark test?
questions.e: The target is 0.85 × 120 = 102 marks, so 102 − 72 = 30 more marks are needed.

questions.q: A class has 18 boys averaging 64 marks and 12 girls averaging 74 marks. What is the class average?
A rectangular field is lengthened by 20% and narrowed by 10%. How does its area change?
questions.e: The area multiplier is 1.20 × 0.90 = 1.08, an 8% increase.

questions.q: Two groups have membership in the ratio 3:2. Ten people move from the first to the second; the ratio becomes 4:3. How many people were in the first group initially?
questions.e: (3x−10)/(2x+10)=4/3 gives 9x−30=8x+40, so x=70 and the first group had 3x=210 people.

questions.q: A 40 kg consignment at Rs 80 per kg is mixed with 60 kg at Rs 120 per kg. What is the cost per kilogram of the mixture?
questions.e: Weighted cost = (40×80 + 60×120)/100 = Rs 104 per kg.

questions.q: A mother is now three times as old as her daughter. Six years ago she was four times as old. How old is the daughter now?
questions.e: Write M=3D and M−6=4(D−6). Then 3D−6=4D−24, giving D=18.

questions.q: A fee is raised by 25%. By what percentage of the increased fee must it be reduced to restore the original amount?
questions.e: The required reduction is 25/125 = 20% of the increased fee.

questions.q: Two successive discounts of 10% and 20% are given on a marked price. What single discount has the same effect?
questions.e: The customer pays 0.90 × 0.80 = 0.72 of the marked price, a discount of 28%.

questions.q: A series begins 3, 8, 15, 24, 35. What is the next term?
questions.e: The increases are 5, 7, 9 and 11; the next increase is 13, giving 48.

questions.q: A cyclist covers the same distance at 30 km/h on the outward trip and 60 km/h on the return. What is the average speed for the complete trip?
questions.e: For equal distances the mean speed is 2×30×60/(30+60)=40 km/h.

questions.q: A boat covers 36 km downstream in three hours and 24 km upstream in four hours. What is the speed of the current?
questions.e: Downstream speed is 12 km/h and upstream speed is 6 km/h; current speed is (12−6)/2 = 3 km/h.

questions.q: For integer x, what is the least x satisfying 4x−7>9?
questions.e: 4x>16 implies x>4; the least integer solution is 5.

questions.q: Two quantities are in the ratio 4:5. Adding six to each makes their ratio 5:6. What was the smaller quantity?
questions.e: Let the quantities be 4x and 5x. Then 6(4x+6)=5(5x+6), giving x=6 and 4x=24.

questions.q: A rectangular plot has diagonal 13 m and one side 5 m. What is its perimeter?
questions.e: The other side is √(13²−5²)=12 m; perimeter = 2(5+12)=34 m.

questions.q: If x+y=13 and xy=36, what is x²+y²?
Six ordered observations are 7, 11, 14, x, 23 and 30. If their median is 18, what is x?
questions.e: (14+x)/2=18, so x=22, which is between 14 and 23 as required.

questions.q: A trapezium has parallel sides of 12 cm and 18 cm and a perpendicular height of 8 cm. What is its area?
A bag contains three green and two yellow counters. Two are drawn without replacement. What is the probability that their colours differ?
questions.e: Either green then yellow or yellow then green: (3/5)(2/4)+(2/5)(3/4)=3/5.

questions.q: A number divided by three, plus half the number after subtracting four, equals eight. What is the number?
questions.e: x/3+(x−4)/2=8. Multiplying by six gives 2x+3x−12=48, so x=12.

questions.q: An exterior angle of a triangle is 135°. One of its two remote interior angles is 50°. Find the other.
questions.e: An exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles; 135−50=85°.

questions.q: A two-digit number has digits summing to 11. Reversing its digits increases it by 27. What is the original number?
questions.e: If tens=t and units=u, t+u=11 and 9(u−t)=27, so u=7 and t=4.

questions.q: A population falls from 48,000 to 42,000. By what percentage did it decrease?
A fund spends 40% of its money on books and then 25% of the remainder on equipment. If Rs 270 is left, what was the original fund?
questions.e: The remaining share is 0.60 × 0.75 = 0.45; 270 ÷ 0.45 = Rs 600.

questions.q: A bag holds four red and five blue counters. Two are drawn without replacement. What is the probability that both are red?
questions.e: The probability is (4/9)×(3/8)=1/6.

questions.q: Increasing a vehicle’s speed by 20 km/h cuts the time for a 120 km route by one hour. What was its original speed?
questions.e: At 40 km/h it takes three hours; at 60 km/h it takes two, exactly one hour less.

questions.q: Among 60 candidates, 38 practised arithmetic, 35 practised English, and 20 practised both. How many practised neither?
questions.e: The union has 38+35−20=53 candidates; 60−53=7 practised neither.

questions.q: A rectangular tank is 10 cm by 6 cm at its base. How high is it if its volume is 480 cm³?
questions.e: Height = volume/base area = 480/(10×6)=8 cm.

questions.q: Two fair dice are rolled. What is the probability that their total is nine?
questions.e: The ordered pairs (3,6), (4,5), (5,4) and (6,3) are four of 36 equally likely outcomes: 1/9.

questions.q: Six workers can finish a job in 15 days. They all work for five days; two then leave. At the same rate per person, how many additional days will the remaining workers need?
questions.e: Total work is 6×15=90 worker-days; 30 are done, leaving 60. Four workers need 60/4=15 days.

questions.q: A bus covers 84 km in two hours, including a 15-minute stop. What is its average speed while moving?
questions.e: Moving time is 1¾ hours, so its moving speed is 84/(7/4)=48 km/h.

questions.q: A 180 m train takes nine seconds to pass a post at constant speed. How long will it take to clear a platform 220 m long?
questions.e: The train travels at 180/9=20 m/s. It must cover 180+220=400 m, requiring 20 seconds.

questions.q: The inner circumference of a circular race track is 440m. If the width of the track is 14m, what is the radius of the outer circle?
questions.e: With π=22/7, the inner radius is 440/(2π)=70 m. Adding the track width of 14 m gives an outer radius of 84 m.

questions.q: What is the sum of prime numbers less than 21?
questions.e: The primes below 21 are 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17 and 19; they total 77.

questions.q: What is the perimeter of a semi-circle lake having a radius of 700m?
questions.e: Perimeter of a semicircle includes its curved edge and diameter: π×700+1,400=3,600 m=3.6 km (π=22/7).

questions.q: What is the total surface area of a cylinder having a radius of 3.5 cm and height 5.5 cm?
questions.e: Total surface area is 2πr(r+h)=2×(22/7)×3.5×(3.5+5.5)=198 cm².

questions.q: When the equation y = x^2 + 8x - 5 is written in the form (x + a)^2 + b, then a is:
questions.e: Complete the square: x²+8x−5=(x+4)²−21. Hence a=4.

questions.q: How can the number 45 be divided into two parts such that four times one part is 9 less than 5 times the other?
questions.e: The two parts 21 and 24 total 45. Four times 24 is 96, nine less than five times 21, which is 105.

questions.q: A shopkeeper marks an item 25% above cost and allows an 8% discount on the marked price. What is the profit percentage?
questions.e: For cost 100, marked price is 125 and selling price is 125×0.92=115; profit is 15%.

questions.q: A 30-litre solution is 40% acid. How many litres of water must be added to make it 30% acid?
questions.e: There are 12 litres of acid. For this to be 30%, total volume must be 40 litres, so add 10 litres.

questions.q: How many mL of 0.1 M base neutralise 34 mL of 0.17 M monoprotic acid?
questions.e: At equivalence M_aV_a=M_bV_b, giving 57.8 mL.

questions.q: Resistors 9 Ω and 9 Ω are in parallel across 14 V. Total current is approximately
questions.e: R_eq=R1R2/(R1+R2), then I=V/R_eq≈3.11 A.

questions.q: A pollutant pool decays first-order at 0.044 yr−1 for 44 years. Fraction remaining is
questions.e: Fraction=e^(−rt)=0.1443.

questions.q: A thin converging lens has f=0.14 m and an object at 0.4 m. The real-image distance is approximately
questions.e: 1/f=1/u+1/v gives v≈0.22 m.

questions.q: A linkage test cross yields 1080 offspring at recombination fraction 0.33. Expected recombinant offspring are
questions.e: Recombinants=rN=0.33×1080≈356.

questions.q: For the perfectly inelastic collision of 6 kg at 5 m/s with stationary 5 kg, the kinetic-energy loss is
questions.e: Subtracting final kinetic energy from initial gives 34.09 J.

questions.q: A cubic cell has side 2.6 arbitrary units. Its surface-area-to-volume ratio is
questions.e: For a cube, SA:V=6a2/a3=6/a=2.308.

questions.q: A population of 1.37 million produces 1.17 kg waste/person-day. Annual waste is
questions.e: Population×per-capita rate×365 gives 585.06 thousand tonnes.

questions.q: Using a sidereal month of 27.3217 d and year of 365.256 d, the lunar synodic month is approximately
questions.e: 1/P_syn=1/P_sid−1/P_year gives 29.531 d.

questions.q: If the Sun converts 5.8×109 kg of mass to energy each second, power is approximately
A contaminant starts at 160 mg/L and decays with k=0.08 d−1 for 40 d. Final concentration is
An intervention is 89% effective against a baseline of 13900 infections. Expected residual infections are
questions.e: Residual=(1−effectiveness)×baseline=1529.

questions.q: A bacterial culture starts with 4400 cells and completes 4 binary-fission generations. Ignoring death, final count is
questions.e: Binary fission gives N=N02^g=70400.

questions.q: A mineral sample has mass 4.4 g and volume 1.18 cm3. Its density is
questions.e: Density=m/V=3.729 g/cm3.

questions.q: A carbon sink removes 3.65 GtC/yr for 53 years at constant rate. Total removal is
questions.e: Cumulative removal=rate×time=193.45 GtC.

questions.q: A weak monoprotic acid has C=0.01 M and Ka=0.00001. Using x≈√(KaC), its pH is about
questions.e: [H+]≈√(KaC), hence pH≈3.5.

questions.q: At heart rate 91 beats/min and stroke volume 122 mL/beat, cardiac output is
questions.e: Cardiac output=heart rate×stroke volume=11.1 L/min.

questions.q: Starting with 12200 kJ and efficiency 12.4% per transfer, energy after 4 transfers is
An ecosystem has GPP=1280 g C m−2 yr−1 and autotrophic respiration=540. NPP is
questions.e: NPP=GPP−R_a=740 g C m−2 yr−1.

questions.e: The second review concerned the Resilience and Sustainability Facility.

questions.q: What percentage of the global gender gap had been closed in the 2026 WEF report?
questions.e: The report gives a global figure of 69.2% for the 145 economies.

وہ حرف جو کسی چیز کو کسی اور سے تشبیہ دینے کے لیے ہو

What would strengthen the comparison?
o: Measure slopes and soils alongside tree cover
questions.e: Measuring other variables makes the effect of tree cover easier to assess.

questions.q:

o: The sites differed in other relevant ways
questions.e: Soil and slope are possible alternative explanations.

questions.q: Choose the sentence that is grammatically correct:

She has been living here since five years.
She lives here since five years.
She has been living here for five years.

The minister gave a great deal of information to the press not.
The minister gave many informations to the press.
The minister gave a great deal of information to the press.
questions.e: Information is uncountable: it takes no plural -s and no many.

questions.e: Because of is a preposition and needs a noun; because is a conjunction and takes a clause.

The government must address the deficit; otherwise the position will deteriorate sharply.
questions.e: Both halves are formal.

Covered in dust, the archivist found the missing file.

Neither the governor nor the ministers were not informed.

The new duty will affect small traders.
The new duty will effect small traders.

The principal reason for the delay were a lack of funds.

questions.q: The exterior angle of a triangle is 80 degrees and the interior opposite angles are in the ratio 1:3. The interior angles measure:
questions.e: The exterior angle equals the sum of the opposite interior angles. Split 80° in the ratio 1:3 to obtain 20° and 60°.

questions.q: The thickness of one sheet of paper is 5 x 10^-2 mm. What is the thickness of a book having 400 sheets of paper?
questions.e: Four hundred sheets at 0.05 mm per sheet are 20 mm thick, which equals 2 cm.

questions.q: The total number of cubic blocks is 50. To construct a solid cube with none left over, what is the minimum number that needs to be taken away?
questions.e: The largest perfect cube no greater than 50 is 27 (3³); 50−27=23 blocks must be removed.

questions.q: Five people P, Q, R, S and T stand in a row. P is immediately left of S, Q immediately left of R, and T is last. If P stands before Q, who must be third?
questions.e: The two adjacent pairs must be P–S then Q–R, followed by T: P, S, Q, R, T.

questions.q: A clock loses six minutes every hour. It is set correctly at noon. What time will it display when the actual time is 5 p.m.?
questions.e: Over five real hours it loses 5×6=30 minutes; the display shows 4:30 p.m.

questions.q: A walker travels 6 km east, 8 km north, 2 km west and 5 km south. What is the shortest distance from the finish to the starting point?
questions.e: The net movement is 4 km east and 3 km north, giving a straight-line distance of √(4²+3²)=5 km.

questions.q: A permit can be issued only if its fee has been paid. An applicant has not paid the fee. Which conclusion necessarily follows?
o: The permit cannot yet be issued
The permit has already been issued
questions.e: Payment is a necessary condition for issuance; without payment, issuance is not possible under the stated rule.

questions.q: Every archivist in an office is a researcher. Some researchers are historians. Which conclusion must be true?
questions.e: The first statement guarantees that every archivist is a researcher; the historians may or may not be archivists.

questions.q: After a 12% increase, a monthly allowance becomes Rs 5,600. What was it before the increase?
questions.e: The original amount is 5,600/1.12 = 5,000.

questions.q: Three boxes A, B and C contain one prize. A says “The prize is in B”; B says “The prize is not in B”; C says “The prize is not in A”. Exactly one statement is true. Where is the prize?
questions.e: If it is in A, only B’s statement is true. In B or C, two statements are true.

questions.q: Three tasks A, B and C are scheduled on Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday. A must precede B and C cannot be on Wednesday. Which task must be on Wednesday?
questions.e: A cannot be last because it precedes B, and C is excluded from Wednesday; therefore B must be last.

questions.q: Twelve learners average 68 marks and eight others average 83 marks. What is the mean for all twenty?
An item priced at Rs 800 is discounted by 15%, then its discounted price rises by 25%. What is the final price?
questions.e: 800×0.85×1.25 = 850; percentages apply to different bases.

questions.q: The difference of two integers is 36. The smaller integer is 60% smaller than the larger integer. What is the sum of the two?
questions.e: If the larger integer is L, the smaller is 0.4L. Their difference is 0.6L=36, so L=60, the smaller is 24 and the sum is 84.

questions.q: The total perimeter of a semicircle is 20.6 cm. What is the approximate radius of the semi-circle?
questions.e: The perimeter of a semicircle includes the arc and diameter: (π+2)r=20.6. With π≈3.14, r≈4 cm.

questions.q: What is k, given that 27^k = 9?
In a group of 50 people, 28 read newspaper A, 24 read newspaper B and 10 read both. How many read neither?
questions.e: Read at least one =28+24−10=42; neither=50−42=8.

questions.q: No licensed driver is under eighteen. Some trainees are under eighteen. Which conclusion must follow?
o: Some trainees are not licensed drivers
No trainee is a licensed driver
questions.e: The trainees known to be under eighteen cannot be licensed; therefore some trainees are not licensed drivers.

questions.q: All audited accounts are verified. No unverified document is admissible. An account is audited. What follows necessarily?
questions.e: The first premise directly entails that every audited account is verified.

questions.q: Four files J, K, L and M are arranged left to right. J is left of K; L is immediately right of K; M is not at an end. Which arrangement is possible?
questions.e: J–M–K–L satisfies J left of K, L immediately right of K, and M not at an end.

questions.q: A workshop schedules P, Q, R and S in four consecutive slots. Q is after P, R is before S, and P is not first. Which task must be first?
questions.e: Q cannot be first because it follows P; P is excluded; S cannot be first because R precedes it. Therefore R is first.

questions.q: A person faces north, turns 135° clockwise, then 90° anticlockwise. In which direction is the person facing?
questions.e: The net turn is 45° clockwise from north, which is north-east.

questions.q: A firm’s quarterly sales were 80, 100, 120 and 140 units. By what percentage did sales in the last two quarters exceed those in the first two?
questions.e: First two total 180; last two total 260; excess 80. Thus 80/180×100=44.4% approximately.

questions.q: If 1 March is a Tuesday in a non-leap year, what day is 1 April?
questions.e: March has 31 days, which shifts the weekday by three; Tuesday becomes Friday.

questions.q: Three times a number minus eight equals twice the number plus eleven. What is the number?
Two notebooks and three pens cost Rs 390; one notebook and two pens cost Rs 230. What is the price of a notebook?
questions.e: Doubling the second equation gives 2N+4P=460. Subtracting the first gives P=70; then N+140=230, so N=90.

questions.q: Find the missing term: 4, 7, 13, 25, 49, __.
questions.e: Each term is twice the preceding term minus one; 2×49−1=97.

questions.q: A sum becomes Rs 13,310 after three years at 10% compound interest annually. What was the principal?
From five candidates, how many different committees of two can be formed?
questions.e: The number is C(5,2)=5×4/2=10.

questions.q: A and B together finish a job in eight days. A alone needs twelve days. How long would B alone need?
questions.e: B’s rate is 1/8−1/12=1/24, so B needs 24 days.

questions.q: In a triangle, the second angle is twice the smallest and the third is three times the smallest. What is the largest angle?
questions.e: The angles contain six equal parts, so each part is 30° and the largest angle is 3×30°=90°.

questions.q: A 150-metre train moving at 54 km/h crosses a 300-metre platform in how many seconds?
questions.e: It covers 450 m at 54 km/h = 15 m/s; 450/15=30 seconds.

questions.q: Six years ago, a mother was five times her daughter’s age. In six years, she will be twice her daughter’s age. How old is the daughter now?
questions.e: Let current ages be M and D. M−6=5(D−6), M+6=2(D+6). Solving gives D=10.

questions.q: One card is drawn from cards numbered 1 to 20. What is the probability that its number is divisible by three or five?
questions.e: Multiples of 3: 6; of 5: 4; common multiple 15 counted twice: 6+4−1=9, so 9/20.

questions.q: Eight machines produce 1,200 units in five hours. At the same rate, how many units will twelve machines produce in three hours?
questions.e: One machine-hour produces 1,200/(8×5)=30 units; 12×3×30=1,080.

questions.q: A square and a rectangle have equal perimeter. The square has side 9 cm and the rectangle has length 11 cm. What is the rectangle’s width?
questions.e: The common perimeter is 36 cm. Thus 2(11+w)=36, giving w=7 cm.

questions.q: One pipe fills a tank in six hours and another in nine hours. A drain empties it in eighteen hours. With all three open, how long will filling take?
questions.e: Net rate = 1/6+1/9−1/18=2/9 tank per hour, so time is 9/2=4.5 hours.

questions.q: A tank is three-fifths full. After 24 litres are added it is nine-tenths full. What is its capacity?
questions.e: The added 24 litres equals 9/10−3/5=3/10 of capacity; capacity=24×10/3=80 litres.

questions.q: Three bells ring every 18, 24 and 30 minutes. If they ring together at 9:00 a.m., when will they next ring together?
questions.e: LCM(18,24,30)=360 minutes=6 hours, so the next common ringing is at 3:00 p.m.

questions.q: A can finish a task in 12 days and B in 18 days. They work together for three days; then B leaves. How many days have elapsed when A finishes the task?
questions.e: Together they complete 3(1/12+1/18)=5/12. A needs seven further days for the remaining 7/12; total 10.

questions.q: A library issued 120 books on Monday, 150 on Tuesday, 135 on Wednesday and 195 on Thursday. What percentage of the four-day total was issued on Thursday?
questions.e: The total is 600 books; 195/600×100=32.5%.

questions.q: In an election, 80% of registered voters cast ballots. Five percent of the ballots cast were invalid. Valid ballots were what percentage of registered voters?
questions.e: Valid ballots = 80% × 95% = 76% of registered voters.

o: صوت — وہ اسم جو کسی چیز کی کثرت یا مقدار ظاہر کرے۔

questions.q:
Read the passage: “A library stayed open later during examinations. Visits rose, yet the librarian noticed that the busiest evenings coincided with a nearby college closing its own reading room. She decided to compare several examination periods before changing permanent hours.”

Why did the librarian delay a permanent change?
o: The increase might partly reflect another reading room’s closure
The library had lost its books
questions.e: The nearby closure could explain part of the observed rise.

questions.q:
Read the passage: “A library stayed open later during examinations. Visits rose, yet the librarian noticed that the busiest evenings coincided with a nearby college closing its own reading room. She decided to compare several examination periods before changing permanent hours.”

What would comparing several examination periods help establish?
o: Whether the college will close permanently
questions.e: Further periods would show whether the observed demand is sustained.

questions.q: What does the idiom "To read the riot act" mean?
o: To organize a protest or demonstration.
To deliver a stern warning or reprimand.
To threaten someone with legal action.
To review a book about a riot.
questions.e: To read someone the riot act is to give them a stern warning or reprimand.

questions.q: What does the idiom "To put a spoke in one's wheel" mean?
o: To assist someone in their endeavors.
To obstruct or hinder someone's plans.
To engage in a friendly race.
questions.e: Putting a spoke in someone’s wheel obstructs their plans.

The reform will definitely solve poverty. (Hedge this claim.)

The report is not only lengthy but also it is repetitive.
The report is not only lengthy but also repetitive.
The report are not only lengthy but also repetitive.

The government, which had been under considerable pressure from various quarters, finally decided to reverse the decision it had earlier taken.
Under pressure, the government reversed its earlier decision.
questions.e: Every fact — the pressure, the reversal, the earlier decision — survives in nine words.

Citizens ___ have the right to information. (obligation/right)

He is not senior to me.

He are neither qualified nor experienced.
He is neither qualified nor experienced.

questions.q: Which sequence best follows claim → explanation → evidence → link?
questions.e: State it, explain it, prove it, then show why it matters.

Funding stopped, so the scheme lapsed in most districts.
The scheme lapsed in most districts when funding stopped.

The board recommended that he is transferred immediately.
The board recommended that he be transferred immediately not.
board recommended that he be transferred immediately.

Several reasons explain why the policy failed.
It is the case that several reasons explain the policy failure.
The reasons that explain the failure of the policy are several in number.
questions.e: The there-construction and the relative clause both disappear without loss.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “You must not bring your identity card if you have already registered.”?

You must not bring your identity card if you have already registered.
You need not bring your identity card if you have already registered.
You need not bring your identity card if you has already registered.
questions.e: Must not is a prohibition; the sentence means there is no obligation, which is need not.

questions.q: A, B and C share $112. B receives $12 less than A and C gets twice as much as B. How much does C get?

questions.q: ان اصطلاحات—مرک بِ تام، مرک بِ اضافی، مرک بِ توصیفی، مرک بِ عددی—میں درست اصطلاح اور تعریف کا جوڑا منتخب کریں۔
o: مرک بِ تام — ایسا مرکب جو مکمل مفہوم دے، یعنی جملہ مکمل ہو۔
مرک بِ عددی — دو اسم جن میں ایک دوسرے کی وضاحت کرے۔
مرک بِ توصیفی — عدد اور اسم پر مشتمل ترکیب۔
مرک بِ اضافی — صفت اور موصوف پر مشتمل ترکیب۔
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 214: مرک بِ تام — ایسا مرکب جو مکمل مفہوم دے، یعنی جملہ مکمل ہو۔

questions.q: ان اصطلاحات—کلمہ، مہمل، اسم، فعل—میں درست اصطلاح اور تعریف کا جوڑا منتخب کریں۔
o: مہمل — وہ لفظ جو کسی شخص، جگہ، چیز یا صفت کا نام ہو
اسم — وہ لفظ جو کسی کام یا حالت کو ظاہر کرے
فعل — ایسا لفظ جس کا کوئی مطلب نہ ہو اور نہ جملے میں استعمال کیا جا سکے۔
کلمہ — ایسا لفظ جس کا با معنی ہونا ضروری ہو اور وہ جملے میں استعمال ہو سکے۔
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 208: کلمہ — ایسا لفظ جس کا با معنی ہونا ضروری ہو اور وہ جملے میں استعمال ہو سکے۔

questions.q: محاورہ «کھری کھری سنانا» کا مطلب کیا ہے؟
questions.e: کھری کھری سنانا بے لاگ اور سخت باتیں کہنا ہے۔

questions.q: محاورہ «آڑے ہاتھوں لینا» کا مطلب کیا ہے؟
questions.e: آڑے ہاتھوں لینا سخت گرفت یا باز پرس کرنا ہے۔

questions.q: «مبہم» کے قریب ترین معنی کون سے ہیں؟
questions.e: مبہم کا مطلب غیر واضح ہے۔

questions.q: «صریح» کے قریب ترین معنی کون سے ہیں؟
questions.e: صریح ایسی بات ہے جو صاف اور واضح ہو۔

questions.q: _____ وہ کلمہ ہے جو کسی جاندار، بے جان چیز، جگہ یا شخص کے نام کو ظاہر کرے؟
وہ اسم جو نہ خود کسی کلمے سے لفظاً ہو اور نہ ہی اس سے کوئی لفظ نکلے _____ کہلاتا ہے۔
ان اصطلاحات—صفت، متعلقِ فعل، ضمیر، اسمِ نکرہ—میں درست اصطلاح اور تعریف کا جوڑا منتخب کریں۔
o: اسمِ نکرہ — وہ لفظ جو فعل کی کیفیت، وقت یا جگہ بتائے
ضمیر — جو کسی غیر معینّ چیز یا فرد پر دلالت کرے
متعلقِ فعل — وہ لفظ جو کسی اسم کی جگہ آتا ہے
صفت — وہ لفظ جو کسی اسم کی خوبی، برائی یا حالت بتائے
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 208: صفت — وہ لفظ جو کسی اسم کی خوبی، برائی یا حالت بتائے

questions.q: یہ تعریف کس اصطلاح کی ہے؟ “وہ اسم جس میں مصدر کی کیفیت یا اثر پایا جائے”
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 208: حاصل مصدر — وہ اسم جس میں مصدر کی کیفیت یا اثر پایا جائے

questions.q: ان اصطلاحات—متعدی، ناقص، معدولہ، فعل مفرد—میں درست اصطلاح اور تعریف کا جوڑا منتخب کریں۔
o: ناقص — وہ فعل جو ایک حالت سے دوسری حالت کی طرف منتقل ہونے کو ظاہر کرے۔
معدولہ — ایک ہی لفظ پر مشتمل فعل۔
فعل مفرد — وہ فعل جو جملے میں صرف اسناد (ربط) کے لیے آتا ہے اور مکمل معنی نہیں دیتا۔
متعدی — وہ فعل جو اپنے اثر کو کسی اور (مفعول) تک پہنچائے۔
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 210: متعدی — وہ فعل جو اپنے اثر کو کسی اور (مفعول) تک پہنچائے۔

questions.q: تعریف “مخصوص الفاظ میں زیر کی خاص صورت۔” اور مثال “انِھٰا (قرآنی طرز پر)” کس اصطلاح کو ظاہر کرتی ہیں؟
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 213: کهڑی زیر — مخصوص الفاظ میں زیر کی خاص صورت۔

questions.q: یہ تعریف کس اصطلاح کی ہے؟ “1. ایک جملہ دوسرے پر (مرکب مطلق ایک جملہ (مرکب ملتف .2 )منحصر نہ ہو )دوسرے پر منحصر ہو”
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 215: مرکب جملے کی اقسام — 1. ایک جملہ دوسرے پر (مرکب مطلق ایک جملہ (مرکب ملتف .2 )منحصر نہ ہو )دوسرے پر منحصر ہو

questions.q: “ضرب المثل” کی درست تعریف منتخب کریں۔
o: کسی چیز کو کسی دوسری چیز کے مشابہ قرار دینا جس میں دونوں کے درمیان کوئی مشترک خوبی ہو۔
ایک جملہ یا قول جو زندگی کے تجربات یا سچائیوں کو سادہ اور اثر دار انداز میں بیان کرتا ہے۔
لفظ کو اس کے غیر حقیقی مطلب میں استعمال کرنا، لیکن تشبیہ یا مشابہت کے بغیر۔
تشبیہ سے مبالغہ کرتے ہوئے مشبہ کا ذکر چھوڑ دینا اور صرف مشبہ بہ کو بطور حقیقت بیان کرنا۔
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 215: ضرب المثل — ایک جملہ یا قول جو زندگی کے تجربات یا سچائیوں کو سادہ اور اثر دار انداز میں بیان کرتا ہے۔

questions.q: “پیش” کی درست تعریف منتخب کریں۔
o: مخصوص الفاظ میں زیر کی خاص صورت۔
سیدھی لکیر جو مخصوص الفاظ میں زبر کی صورت میں آتی ہے۔
واؤ نما نشان، جس سے آواز گول ہوتی ہے۔
وہ عالمت جو ساکن حرف پر لگائی جاتی ہے، آواز رک جاتی ہے۔
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 213: پیش — واؤ نما نشان، جس سے آواز گول ہوتی ہے۔

questions.q: یہ تعریف کس اصطلاح کی ہے؟ “وہ فعل جس کا کرنے والا (فاعل) معلوم ہو اور ظاہر ہو۔”
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 211: فعل معروف (مفرد) — وہ فعل جس کا کرنے والا (فاعل) معلوم ہو اور ظاہر ہو۔

questions.q: ان اصطلاحات—ناقص، معدولہ، فعل مفرد، فعل مرکب—میں درست اصطلاح اور تعریف کا جوڑا منتخب کریں۔
o: معدولہ — ایک ہی لفظ پر مشتمل فعل۔
ناقص — وہ فعل جو جملے میں صرف اسناد (ربط) کے لیے آتا ہے اور مکمل معنی نہیں دیتا۔
فعل مرکب — وہ فعل جو ایک حالت سے دوسری حالت کی طرف منتقل ہونے کو ظاہر کرے۔
فعل مفرد — دو یا زیادہ الفاظ سے مل کر بننے والا فعل (جس میں ایک فعل + معاون لفظ ہو)
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 210: ناقص — وہ فعل جو جملے میں صرف اسناد (ربط) کے لیے آتا ہے اور مکمل معنی نہیں دیتا۔

questions.q:
Read the passage: “A city trialled two bus routes with equal fares. The express route saved time for passengers near the main road but required a long walk for those in smaller streets. The planners kept local stops while changing some buses to express service.”

What trade-off is described?
questions.e: The express route is quicker for some but less accessible for others.

questions.q:
Read the passage: “A city trialled two bus routes with equal fares. The express route saved time for passengers near the main road but required a long walk for those in smaller streets. The planners kept local stops while changing some buses to express service.”

Which concern shaped the mixed service?
o: A desire to increase every fare
Access for passengers away from the main road
The need to close all local stops
questions.e: Local stops protect access for passengers far from the express corridor.

questions.q: Identify the antonym of Turpitude.
questions.e: “Turpitude” means moral wrongdoing; “virtue” means moral goodness.

questions.q: Identify the antonym of Vituperate.
questions.e: To “vituperate” is to abuse verbally; to praise is the opposite action.

questions.q: Identify the antonym of Insouciant.
questions.e: “Insouciant” means free from concern; “anxious” expresses concern.

questions.q: Antonym of Ephemeral:
questions.e: “Ephemeral” means short-lived; “permanent” means lasting.

questions.q: Identify the antonym of Lionize.
questions.e: To “lionize” someone is to celebrate them; to “vilify” them is to denounce them.

questions.q: What is wrong with: “Which is why the appeal was dismissed”?
o: It has no subject of its own; it is a relative clause standing alone.
questions.e: Which cannot begin a free-standing sentence. Replace it with a subject such as That reasoning.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Having completed the inspection, the report was signed by the team leader.”?
o: Having completed inspection, the team leader signed the report.
Having completed the inspection, the team leader signed the report.
Having completed the inspection, the report was signed by the team leader.
Having completed the inspection, the team leader signed the report not.
questions.e: The report did not complete the inspection; the participle must attach to its real doer.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “After to complete the form, he submitted it.”?
o: After completing form, he submitted it.
After completing the form, he submitted it.
After to complete the form, he submitted it.
After completing the form, he submitted it not.
questions.e: Every preposition, after included, takes the -ing form.

questions.q: Which Type is associated with Definition “Compares two things” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 230: Type “Comparative Adjective” corresponds to Definition “Compares two things”.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The department not only failed to reply but also it ignored two reminders.”?
o: The department not only failed than reply but also ignored two reminders.
The department not only failed to reply but also ignored two reminders.
The department not only failed to reply but also it ignored two reminders.
The department not only failed to reply but also ignored two reminders not.
questions.e: Both halves now follow the subject directly, so the structures balance.

questions.q: Which Type is associated with Example “He said, "May God help us." → He prayed that God might help them.” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 228: Type “Prayer” corresponds to Example “He said, "May God help us." → He prayed that God might help them.”.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “We reached at the venue before the guests.”?
o: We reached venue before the guests.
We reached the venue before the guests.
We reached at the venue before the guests.
We reached the venue before the guests not.
questions.e: Reach is transitive; arrive takes at or in.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “She likes reading, writing and to travel.”?
o: She likes reading, writing and to travel.
She likes reading, writing and travelling not.
She likes reading, writing and travelling without.
She likes reading, writing and travelling.
questions.e: All three items after likes must take the same form.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “There is, according to the survey, three main causes of rural poverty.”?
o: There are, according to the survey, three main causes of rural poverty.
There are, according to the survey, three main causes of rural poverty without.
There are not, according to the survey, three main causes of rural poverty.
There is, according to the survey, three main causes of rural poverty.
questions.e: The subject is causes; the inserted phrase does not affect agreement.

questions.q: Which Rule is associated with Preposition “With” in the English reference?
o: Shows level or capacity of doing something
Shows relation like enmity, alliance, coordination
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 231: Rule “Shows relation like enmity, alliance, coordination” corresponds to Preposition “With”.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “His approach is different than mine.”?
o: His approach are different from mine.
His approach is not different from mine.
His approach is different than mine.
His approach is different from mine.
questions.e: Standard British usage is different from.

questions.q: Which Tense is associated with Passive Formula “Object + will/shall + have been + V3 + by + Subject” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 224: Tense “Future Perfect” corresponds to Passive Formula “Object + will/shall + have been + V3 + by + Subject”.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The officer was asked to submit the report and that he should appear in person.”?
o: The officer were asked to submit the report and to appear in person.
The officer was not asked to submit the report and to appear in person.
The officer was asked to submit the report and that he should appear in person.
The officer was asked to submit the report and to appear in person.
questions.e: Two infinitives balance; an infinitive and a that-clause do not.

questions.q: Which option is a complete sentence?
o: Because the deadline had already passed.
Since the deadline had already passed and no extension was granted.
questions.e: It has a subject and a finite verb and no subordinator holding it down.

questions.q: Which Rule is associated with Example Sentence “I saw a certain bird flying high. A certain man was looking for you.” in the English reference?
o: No article before names of people
Before a certain or specific unidentified thing
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 225: Rule “Before a certain or specific unidentified thing” corresponds to Example Sentence “I saw a certain bird flying high. A certain man was looking for you.”.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “After completing the inspection, a detailed report was submitted.”?
o: After completing the inspection, the team submitted a detailed report.
After completing the inspection, a detailed report was submitted.
After completing the inspection, the team submitted a detailed report not.
After completing the inspection, the team submitted an detailed report.
questions.e: The report did not complete the inspection. Name the doer immediately after the comma.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The committee recommended that the policy is revised.”?
o: committee recommended that the policy be revised.
The committee recommended that the policy be revised not.
The committee recommended that the policy is revised.
The committee recommended that the policy be revised.
questions.e: The committee recommended that the policy be revised. (Subjunctive after recommended that.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The report comprises of five chapters.”?
o: The report comprises of five chapters.
The report comprises five chapters not.
questions.e: Comprise takes no of; consist does.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The scheme is not only expensive but also it is unnecessary.”?
o: The scheme is not only expensive but also it is unnecessary.
The scheme is not not only expensive but also unnecessary.
The scheme are not only expensive but also unnecessary.
The scheme is not only expensive but also unnecessary.
questions.e: Two adjectives balance; an adjective and a clause do not.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The behaviour of the officials during the protests were widely criticised.”?
o: The behaviour of the officials during the protests was widely criticised.
The behaviour of the officials during the protests was widely criticised without.
The behaviour of the officials during the protests was not widely criticised.
The behaviour of the officials during the protests were widely criticised.
questions.e: Strip the phrases: behaviour … was criticised. Officials is inside a prepositional phrase and cannot control the verb.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The magistrate made the accused to appear and let the counsel to speak.”?
o: magistrate made the accused appear and let the counsel speak.
The magistrate made the accused appear and let the counsel speak not.
The magistrate made the accused to appear and let the counsel to speak.
The magistrate made the accused appear and let the counsel speak.
questions.e: Make and let take the bare infinitive in the active voice.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “As the weather was bad, so the match was cancelled.”?
o: As the weather were bad, the match was cancelled.
As the weather was not bad, the match was cancelled.
As the weather was bad, so the match was cancelled.
As the weather was bad, the match was cancelled.
questions.e: As and so both mark cause; only one may stay.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “If literacy improves, the country would prosper.”?
o: If literacy improves, the country would prosper.
If literacy improves, the country will not prosper.
If literacy improves, country will prosper.
If literacy improves, the country will prosper.
questions.e: If literacy improves, the country will prosper. (First conditional keep tenses matched.) Or fully hypothetical: If literacy improved, the country would prosper.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “She is married with an engineer.”?
o: She are married to an engineer.
She is not married to an engineer.
She is married with an engineer.
She is married to an engineer.
questions.e: Married takes to in English.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The accident was happened near the toll plaza.”?
o: accident happened near the toll plaza.
The accident happened near the toll plaza.
The accident was happened near the toll plaza.
The accident happened near the toll plaza not.
questions.e: Happen is intransitive and has no passive form.

questions.q: Which Tense is associated with Passive Formula “Object + is/am/are + being + V3 + by + Subject” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 224: Tense “Present Continuous” corresponds to Passive Formula “Object + is/am/are + being + V3 + by + Subject”.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “If the floods had not occurred, the economy will have grown.”?
o: If the floods had not occurred, the economy would has grown.
If the floods had not not occurred, the economy would have grown.
If the floods had not occurred, the economy will have grown.
If the floods had not occurred, the economy would have grown.
questions.e: If the floods had not occurred, the economy would have grown. (Third conditional.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The committee discussed about the new policy.”?
o: The committee discussed the new policy.
The committee discussed about the new policy.
The committee discussed the new policy not.
questions.e: Discuss is transitive and takes no preposition.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The report is being prepare by the sub-committee.”?
o: The report is being prepare by the sub-committee.
The report is being prepared by the sub-committee.
The report are being prepared by the sub-committee.
The report is not being prepared by the sub-committee.
questions.e: The passive always ends in a past participle.

questions.q: Which Connector Type is associated with Structure Pattern “Independent clause, coordinating conjunction, independent clause” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 234: Connector Type “Coordinating Conjunctions (FANBOYS)” corresponds to Structure Pattern “Independent clause, coordinating conjunction, independent clause”.

questions.q: Which Preposition is associated with Rule “Retreat or reversal movement” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 233: Preposition “From” corresponds to Rule “Retreat or reversal movement”.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The teacher, who taught us grammar, has retired, is coming today.”?
o: The teacher who taught us grammar has retired.
The teacher who taught us grammar have retired.
The teacher who taught us grammar has not retired.
The teacher, who taught us grammar, has retired, is coming today.
questions.e: Two competing main verbs. Decide which clause is the main one.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “If I was the chief secretary, I would decentralise authority.”?
o: If I was the chief secretary, I would decentralise authority.
If I were not the chief secretary, I would decentralise authority.
If I were the chief secretary, I would decentralise authority without.
If I were the chief secretary, I would decentralise authority.
questions.e: If I were the chief secretary, I would decentralise authority. (Subjunctive were.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The committee met on Tuesday, it adjourned without a decision.”?
o: The committee met on Tuesday, it adjourned without a decision.
The committee met on Tuesday, but it adjourned without a decision not.
The committee met on Tuesday, but it adjourned without an decision.
The committee met on Tuesday, but it adjourned without a decision.
questions.e: Two independent clauses cannot be joined by a comma alone.

questions.q: The commission reduced the syllabus; ____, it increased the number of papers.
questions.e: The second fact cuts against the first, so a contrast signal is needed.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “A notice has sent to all the candidates.”?
o: A notice have been sent to all the candidates.
A notice has been sent to all the candidates.
A notice has sent to all the candidates.
A notice has not been sent to all the candidates.
questions.e: The present perfect passive needs has been + participle.

questions.q: Which Tense is associated with Structure “subject + will/shall be + verb-ing” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 244: Tense “Future Continuous” corresponds to Structure “subject + will/shall be + verb-ing”.

questions.q: Which Preposition is associated with Rule “Longer residential stay” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 233: Preposition “In” corresponds to Rule “Longer residential stay”.

questions.s: Present and past: the four forms of each
questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “I am having a meeting yesterday when the power was failing.”?
o: I was not having a meeting yesterday when the power failed.
I am having a meeting yesterday when the power was failing.
I was having a meeting yesterday when the power failed.
I were having a meeting yesterday when the power failed.
questions.e: Have a meeting is an action, so the continuous is allowed, but the time is past; the short interruption takes the past simple.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Who broke the window? → By whom the window was broken?”?
o: Who broke the window? → By whom the window was broken?
Who broke the window? → By whom was the window broken?
Who broke the window? → By whom were the window broken?
Who broke the window? → By whom was not the window broken?
questions.e: A passive question keeps question word order: auxiliary before the subject.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Although the bill was passed, but it was never enforced.”?
o: Although the bill was passed, but it was never enforced.
Although the bill was passed, it was never enforced.
Although the bill were passed, it was never enforced.
