questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 211: فعل امر — وہ فعل جو حکم یا درخواست کے لیے بوال جائے۔

questions.q: تعریف “دو بامعنی الفاظ پر مشتمل، جہاں ایک دوسرے کی پیروی کرتا ہو۔” اور مثال “رونا دھونا، ہنسنا کھیلنا” کس اصطلاح کو ظاہر کرتی ہیں؟
o: مرک بِ عط فِ بیان و مبین
مرک بِ بدل و مبدل منہ
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 214: مرک بِ تابع و متبوع (موضوع) — دو بامعنی الفاظ پر مشتمل، جہاں ایک دوسرے کی پیروی کرتا ہو۔

questions.q: ان اصطلاحات—معدولہ، فعل مفرد، فعل مرکب، فعل معروف (مفرد)—میں درست اصطلاح اور تعریف کا جوڑا منتخب کریں۔
o: فعل معروف (مفرد) — ایک ہی لفظ پر مشتمل فعل۔
معدولہ — وہ فعل جو ایک حالت سے دوسری حالت کی طرف منتقل ہونے کو ظاہر کرے۔
فعل مفرد — دو یا زیادہ الفاظ سے مل کر بننے والا فعل (جس میں ایک فعل + معاون لفظ ہو)
فعل مرکب — وہ فعل جس کا کرنے والا (فاعل) معلوم ہو اور ظاہر ہو۔
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 210: معدولہ — وہ فعل جو ایک حالت سے دوسری حالت کی طرف منتقل ہونے کو ظاہر کرے۔

questions.q: ان اصطلاحات—لقب، کنیت، عرف، تخلص—میں درست اصطلاح اور تعریف کا جوڑا منتخب کریں۔
o: کنیت — وہ اسم جو کسی شخص کی پہچان یا عزت کے لئے غیر رسمی طور پر استعمال کیا جاتا ہے۔
لقب — وہ اسم جو کسی شخص کو کسی خاص خصوصیت یا حیثیت کی وجہ سے دیا جاتا ہے۔
تخلص — وہ اسم جو کسی شخص کے والد یا بچوں کی طرف اشارہ کرتا ہے۔
عرف — وہ اسم جو کسی شخص کا فرضی یا قلمی نام ہوتا ہے، جو شاعری یا ادبی کاموں میں استعمال ہوتا ہے۔
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 209: لقب — وہ اسم جو کسی شخص کو کسی خاص خصوصیت یا حیثیت کی وجہ سے دیا جاتا ہے۔

questions.q: یہ تعریف کس اصطلاح کی ہے؟ “وہ حرف جو شرط اور اس کے نتیجے کو ظاہر کرے”
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 211: حرف شرط و ۔ جزا — وہ حرف جو شرط اور اس کے نتیجے کو ظاہر کرے

questions.q: “فعل مجہول” کی درست تعریف منتخب کریں۔
o: وہ فعل جو ماضی میں مکمل ہو چکا ہو۔
وہ فعل جو آئندہ میں انجام پائے گا۔
وہ فعل جس میں کرنے والا (فاعل) معلوم نہ ہو یا ذکر نہ کیا گیا ہو۔
وہ فعل جو موجودہ وقت میں ہو رہا ہو۔
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 211: فعل مجہول — وہ فعل جس میں کرنے والا (فاعل) معلوم نہ ہو یا ذکر نہ کیا گیا ہو۔

questions.q:
Read the passage: “A council offered discounted waste collection in a pilot area. Fewer bags appeared beside roads, but some residents said collection had merely shifted dumping to nearby lanes. The council expanded its inspection to the surrounding streets.”

What was the council trying to check?
o: Whether the pilot had no participants
Whether waste bags had changed colour
Whether the problem moved rather than diminished
questions.e: Dumping may have shifted outside the pilot boundary.

questions.q:
Read the passage: “A council offered discounted waste collection in a pilot area. Fewer bags appeared beside roads, but some residents said collection had merely shifted dumping to nearby lanes. The council expanded its inspection to the surrounding streets.”

Which finding would weaken a claim of overall improvement?
o: More waste appearing in neighbouring lanes
Fewer bags on both pilot and neighbouring roads
questions.e: Displacement would undermine a claim of an overall reduction.

questions.q: He is so dull that he is insensible _____ the beauties of nature.
questions.e: The adjective “insensible” takes “to” when referring to a lack of awareness of something.

questions.q: We have been able to obtain no information _____ his whereabouts.
questions.e: “As to his whereabouts” means “regarding his whereabouts”; the other phrases do not fit after “information”.

questions.q: The committee ____ its recommendations last Thursday.
questions.e: A collective noun acting as one body takes a singular verb.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Item 6 compare like with like (Day 20)”?
o: Punjab’s economy are larger than Sindh’s / than that of Sindh.
Punjab’s economy is not larger than Sindh’s / than that of Sindh.
Punjab’s economy is larger than Sindh’s / than that of Sindh.
questions.e: Punjab’s economy is larger than Sindh’s / than that of Sindh. (Compare economies.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Item 9 parallelism (Day 15)”?
o: The plan aims to cut waste, improve services, and raise trust not.
The plan aims to cut waste, improve services, and raise trust.
The plan aims than cut waste, improve services, and raise trust.
questions.e: The plan aims to cut waste, improve services, and raise trust. (Three parallel infinitives.)

questions.s: Active Voice, Passive Voice, and Causatives
questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The school had its roof repaired. (Identify the structure.)”?
o: Causative: have something done the school caused the roof to be repaired.
The school had its roof repaired. (Identify the structure.)
Causative: have not something done the school caused the roof to be repaired.
Causative: has something done the school caused the roof to be repaired.
questions.e: Causative: have something done the school caused the roof to be repaired.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Item 7 affect/effect (Day 21)”?
o: The tax will not affect every household.
The tax will affect every household.
questions.e: The tax will affect every household. (affect = verb.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Item 8 colon (Day 14)”?
o: We must not reform three sectors: energy, water, and health.
We must reform three sectors: energy, water, and health without.
We must reform three sectors: energy, water, and health.
questions.e: We must reform three sectors: energy, water, and health. (Colon after a complete clause.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Each of the candidates have submitted their forms.”?
o: Each of the candidates has not submitted his or her form.
Each of the candidates have submitted their forms.
Each of the candidates has submitted his or her form.
Each of the candidates have submitted his or her form.
questions.e: Each of the candidates has submitted his or her form. (each is singular.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The policy lost it’s credibility within a year.”?
o: The policy lost its credibility within a year not.
The policy lost its credibility within an year.
The policy lost its credibility within a year.
The policy lost it’s credibility within a year.
questions.e: The policy lost its credibility within a year. (its = possessive, no apostrophe.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Item 1 conjunctive adverb punctuation (Day 17)”?
o: The plan was not sound; however, it was never funded.
The plan were sound; however, it was never funded.
The plan was sound; however, it was never funded.
questions.e: The plan was sound; however, it was never funded. (Semicolon + comma.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “It was the most perfect example of misgovernance.”?
o: It was not a perfect example of misgovernance.
It was the most perfect example of misgovernance.
It was a perfect example of misgovernance.
It were a perfect example of misgovernance.
questions.e: It was a perfect example of misgovernance. (perfect is absolute drop most.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Item 2 redundant subject pronoun (Day 18)”?
o: The government ignored the warning not.
questions.e: The government ignored the warning. (Redundant pronoun removed.)

questions.q: Which Rule is associated with Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) “He lives in Khan Street with his family.” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 232: Rule “General residence/location” corresponds to Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) “He lives in Khan Street with his family.”.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “He is living in Islamabad since 2015.”?
o: He has not been living in Islamabad since 2015.
He have been living in Islamabad since 2015.
He has been living in Islamabad since 2015.
He is living in Islamabad since 2015.
questions.e: He has been living in Islamabad since 2015. (Present perfect continuous with since.)

questions.q: Which Type is associated with Example Word “on, under” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 230: Type “Preposition of Place” corresponds to Example Word “on, under”.

questions.q: Which Indirect Speech is associated with Direct Speech “He said, "Are you coming?"” in the English reference?
o: She asked if I liked chocolate.
He asked if I was coming.
She asked what my name was.
He asked where I was going.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 227: Indirect Speech “He asked if I was coming.” corresponds to Direct Speech “He said, "Are you coming?"”.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Item 3 tense with since (Day 18)”?
o: He has not been working in this department since 2018.
He have been working in this department since 2018.
He has been working in this department since 2018.
questions.e: He has been working in this department since 2018. (Present perfect continuous.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Their going to announce the results tomorrow.”?
o: They’re going to announce the results tomorrow not.
Their going to announce the results tomorrow.
They’re going to announce the results tomorrow.
They’re going than announce the results tomorrow.
questions.e: They’re going to announce the results tomorrow. (their > they’re.)

questions.q: Which Type is associated with Sentence Example “He left because of the rain.” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 231: Type “Preposition of Reason” corresponds to Sentence Example “He left because of the rain.”.

questions.q: Which sentence hedges appropriately without becoming empty?
o: Enforcement has definitely and completely collapsed.
It may possibly perhaps be the case that enforcement has weakened.
The data suggest that enforcement has weakened.
questions.e: One hedge, one clear claim.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “She avoided to comment on the issue and denied to know anything about the file.”?
o: She avoided to comment on the issue and denied to know anything about the file.
She avoided commenting on the issue and denied knowing anything about the file.
She avoided commenting on issue and denied knowing anything about the file.
She avoided commenting on the issue and denied knowing anything about the file not.
questions.e: Both avoid and deny take the gerund.

questions.q: Which sentence is free of ambiguity?
o: The principal told the teacher that she had been promoted.
The principal informed the teacher of the teacher’s promotion.
She told her that she had been promoted.
The principal told her that she had been promoted.
questions.e: Only option B makes it certain who was promoted.

questions.q: Which Type is associated with Sentence Example “He can swim.” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 230: Type “Modal Verb” corresponds to Sentence Example “He can swim.”.

questions.q: Which Preposition is associated with Rule “Sitting beside something” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 231: Preposition “By” corresponds to Rule “Sitting beside something”.

questions.q: Which Type is associated with Sentence Example “She lives in France.” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 229: Type “Proper Noun” corresponds to Sentence Example “She lives in France.”.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The witness’ statement and the two accuseds’ confessions were read out.”?
o: The witness’s statement and the two accused’s confessions were not read out.
The witness’ statement and the two accuseds’ confessions were read out.
The witness’s statement and the two accused’s confessions were read out.
The witness’s statement and the two accused’s confessions was read out.
questions.e: Singular owner takes ’s; accused has no plural -s, so the possessive is regular.

questions.q: Which Type is associated with Definition “Shows physical or mental action” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 230: Type “Action Verb” corresponds to Definition “Shows physical or mental action”.

questions.q: Which Direct Speech is associated with Indirect Speech “Past Perfect Continuous” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 226: Direct Speech “Present Perfect Continuous” corresponds to Indirect Speech “Past Perfect Continuous”.

questions.q: Which Part of Speech is associated with Examples “Ouch! (Emotive - Pain)Hey! (Greeting)Um (Cognitive - Hesitation)” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 229: Part of Speech “Interjection” corresponds to Examples “Ouch! (Emotive - Pain)Hey! (Greeting)Um (Cognitive - Hesitation)”.

questions.s: Concision: saying it in fewer words
questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “It is important to note that the report was submitted late.”?
o: The report was not submitted late.
It is important to note that the report was submitted late.
questions.e: The opening phrase adds no information.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The minister implied from the report that enforcement had failed.”?
o: The minister inferred from the report that enforcement had not failed.
minister inferred from the report that enforcement had failed.
The minister inferred from the report that enforcement had failed.
The minister implied from the report that enforcement had failed.
questions.e: You infer from evidence; you imply in what you say.

questions.q: Which Structure is associated with Tense “Future Perfect” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 244: Structure “subject + will/shall have + past participle” corresponds to Tense “Future Perfect”.

questions.s: Concision: saying it in fewer words
questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “He repeated the instruction again and asked them to revert back.”?
o: He repeated the instruction and asked them to reply not.
He repeated the instruction and asked them than reply.
He repeated the instruction and asked them to reply.
He repeated the instruction again and asked them to revert back.
questions.e: Repeat already contains again; revert already contains back, and reply is the word actually meant.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “He is a very industrial student who works hard.”?
o: He is not a very industrious student who works hard.
He is a very industrial student who works hard.
He is a very industrious student who works hard.
He are a very industrious student who works hard.
questions.e: Industrious means hardworking; industrial relates to industry.

questions.q: Which Direct Speech is associated with Indirect Speech “Might” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 227: Direct Speech “May” corresponds to Indirect Speech “Might”.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Myself and my colleague attended the briefing.”?
o: Myself and my colleague attended the briefing.
My colleague and I attended the briefing not.
My colleague and I attended briefing.
My colleague and I attended the briefing.
questions.e: A reflexive pronoun cannot be the subject.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Kindly do the needful and revert back at the earliest.”?
o: Kindly take the necessary action and reply as soon as possible not.
Kindly take necessary action and reply as soon as possible.
Kindly take the necessary action and reply as soon as possible.
Kindly do the needful and revert back at the earliest.
questions.e: Neither expression is standard written English.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Between you and I, the decision was political.”?
o: Between you and I, the decision was political.
Between you and me, the decision was political.
Between you and me, the decision were political.
Between you and me, the decision was not political.
questions.e: Between is a preposition and takes the object form.

questions.q: Which Direct Speech is associated with Indirect Speech “He will say that he is ready.” in the English reference?
o: He said, "The sun rises in the east."
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 226: Direct Speech “He will say, "I am ready."” corresponds to Indirect Speech “He will say that he is ready.”.

questions.q: Which Rule is associated with Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) “The book is lying on the table.” in the English reference?
o: Used for position on a surface
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 231: Rule “Used for position on a surface” corresponds to Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) “The book is lying on the table.”.

questions.s: Concision: saying it in fewer words
questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Due to the fact that the funds were not released, the work was postponed.”?
o: Because the funds were not not released, the work was postponed.
Because the funds were not released, the work were postponed.
Because the funds were not released, the work was postponed.
Due to the fact that the funds were not released, the work was postponed.
questions.e: Due to the fact that is always replaceable by because.

questions.q: Which Rule is associated with Preposition “Behind” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 232: Rule “Hidden at the back” corresponds to Preposition “Behind”.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The committee announced their decision and published their report.”?
o: The committee announced their decision and published their report.
The committee announced its decision and published its report not.
committee announced its decision and published its report.
The committee announced its decision and published its report.
questions.e: A collective noun acting as one body takes it and its.

questions.q: Which Indirect Speech is associated with Direct Speech “She said, "Don't disturb me."” in the English reference?
o: He said that the sun rises in the east.
He will say that he is ready.
He says that he likes tea.
She requested not to disturb her.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 228: Indirect Speech “She requested not to disturb her.” corresponds to Direct Speech “She said, "Don't disturb me."”.

questions.s: Concision: saying it in fewer words
questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The committee made a decision to conduct an investigation into the matter.”?
o: The committee decided to investigate the matter.
The committee decided than investigate the matter.
The committee decided to investigate the matter not.
The committee made a decision to conduct an investigation into the matter.
questions.e: Two nominalisations become two verbs.

questions.q: Which sentence uses the reflexive correctly?
o: The officers reviewed the file theirselves.
The minister himself reviewed the file.
Please forward the file to myself.
questions.e: A reflexive may be used for emphasis beside the subject it echoes.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The new policy is not only ambitious but also it lacks any costing.”?
o: The new policy is not only ambitious but also it lacks any costing.
The new policy is not not only ambitious but also uncosted.
The new policy are not only ambitious but also uncosted.
The new policy is not only ambitious but also uncosted.
questions.e: Two adjectives balance after the correlative pair.

questions.q: District-office worksheet — A two-digit number has digit sum 1; reversing its digits reduces it by 9. What is the original number?
questions.e: Let the tens and units digits be x and y. Then x + y = 1 and 9(x − y) = 9; hence x = 1, y = 0.

questions.q: Warehouse planning case — A 79 m by 16 m rectangular courtyard has a uniform path 5 m wide inside its boundary. What area does the path cover?
questions.e: Path area = outer area − inner area = 1264 − 69×6 = 850 m².

questions.q: District-office worksheet — An investment grows to Rs 29376 in two years at 20% compound interest per year. What was the principal?
Scholarship-fund audit — A 78 m by 15 m rectangular courtyard has a uniform path 4 m wide inside its boundary. What area does the path cover?
questions.e: Path area = outer area − inner area = 1170 − 70×7 = 680 m².

questions.q: District-office worksheet — A vehicle covers two equal-distance legs at 102 km/h and 114 km/h. What is its average speed for the complete journey?
questions.e: For equal distances the harmonic mean applies: 2uv/(u + v) = 107.67 km/h.

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — An investment grows to Rs 16456 in two years at 10% compound interest per year. What was the principal?
Warehouse planning case — A two-digit number has digit sum 4; reversing its digits increases it by 18. What is the original number?
questions.e: Let the tens and units digits be x and y. Then x + y = 4 and 9(x − y) = -18; hence x = 1, y = 3.

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — A vehicle covers two equal-distance legs at 100 km/h and 110 km/h. What is its average speed for the complete journey?
questions.e: For equal distances the harmonic mean applies: 2uv/(u + v) = 104.76 km/h.

questions.q: District-office worksheet — On a coordinate grid, point Q lies 50 units east and 120 units north of point P. What is the straight-line distance PQ?
Relief-camp planning case — On a coordinate grid, point Q lies 27 units east and 36 units north of point P. What is the straight-line distance PQ?
questions.e: PQ = √(27² + 36²) = 45 units.

questions.q: District-office worksheet — An arithmetic sequence begins 54, 56, 58, … . What is the sum of its first 11 terms?
Relief-camp planning case — An arithmetic sequence begins 53, 61, 69, … . What is the sum of its first 10 terms?
Survey-unit review — A geometric sequence has first term 46 and common ratio 4. What is its 5th term?
Training-centre exercise — A geometric sequence has first term 47 and common ratio 2. What is its 6th term?
District-office worksheet — The roots of x² − 91x + 2068 = 0 differ by 3. What is the larger root?
questions.e: The quadratic factors as (x − 44)(x − 47); the larger root is 47.

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — The roots of x² − 88x + 1935 = 0 differ by 2. What is the larger root?
questions.e: The quadratic factors as (x − 43)(x − 45); the larger root is 45.

questions.q: Transport-depot calculation — A train 420 m long clears a 110 m platform in 18 seconds. What is its speed in km/h?
questions.e: The train covers 530 m. Its speed is (530)/18 m/s × 3.6 = 106 km/h.

questions.q: Health-programme report — A train 430 m long clears a 120 m platform in 19 seconds. What is its speed in km/h?
questions.e: The train covers 550 m. Its speed is (550)/19 m/s × 3.6 = 104.21 km/h.

questions.q: Transport-depot calculation — For two years at 15% per annum, by how much does compound interest exceed simple interest on Rs 400000?
Health-programme report — For two years at 20% per annum, by how much does compound interest exceed simple interest on Rs 410000?
Survey-unit review — After a 10% discount and then 5% sales tax, an equipment bill for a survey unit is Rs 58590. What was the listed price?
questions.e: If L is the list price, L × 90/100 × 105/100 = 58590, giving L = 62000.

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — After a 10% discount and then 5% sales tax, an equipment bill for a relief camp is Rs 62370. What was the listed price?
questions.e: If L is the list price, L × 90/100 × 105/100 = 62370, giving L = 66000.

questions.q: Transport-depot calculation — 78 passengers paid Rs 5220. An adult ticket cost Rs 70 and a child ticket Rs 50. How many adults travelled?
questions.e: If a is the adult count, 70a + 50(78 − a) = 5220, which gives a = 66.

questions.q: Health-programme report — 80 passengers paid Rs 5740. An adult ticket cost Rs 75 and a child ticket Rs 55. How many adults travelled?
questions.e: If a is the adult count, 75a + 55(80 − a) = 5740, which gives a = 67.

questions.q: Survey-unit review — A bag holds 31 red and 4 blue counters. Two are drawn without replacement. What is the probability that both are red?
questions.e: Multiply the changing probabilities: 31/35 × 30/34 = 78.15%.

questions.q: Training-centre exercise — A bag holds 32 red and 5 blue counters. Two are drawn without replacement. What is the probability that both are red?
questions.e: Multiply the changing probabilities: 32/37 × 31/36 = 74.47%.

questions.q: Training-centre exercise — Worker B takes 52 days for a task. Worker A is 25% more efficient than B. How many days would A need for the same task?
questions.e: Time varies inversely with efficiency, so A's time is 52 × 100/125 = 41.6 days.

questions.q: Survey-unit review — Worker B takes 51 days for a task. Worker A is 20% more efficient than B. How many days would A need for the same task?
questions.e: Time varies inversely with efficiency, so A's time is 51 × 100/120 = 42.5 days.

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — A invests Rs 36000 for 8 months and B invests Rs 9000 for 8 months. If their profit is Rs 3600, what is A's share?
questions.e: Profit follows capital-months. The weights are 288000:72000; A therefore receives Rs 2880.

questions.q: District-office worksheet — A invests Rs 37000 for 9 months and B invests Rs 10000 for 9 months. If their profit is Rs 4230, what is A's share?
questions.e: Profit follows capital-months. The weights are 333000:90000; A therefore receives Rs 3330.

questions.q: Warehouse planning case — Two batches assessed by a warehouse contain 63 and 17 candidates with mean scores 60 and 74. What is the combined mean?
questions.e: Use the weighted mean: (63 × 60 + 17 × 74) ÷ 80 = 62.98.

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — Two batches assessed by a relief camp contain 60 and 14 candidates with mean scores 57 and 71. What is the combined mean?
questions.e: Use the weighted mean: (60 × 57 + 14 × 71) ÷ 74 = 59.65.

questions.q: Transport-depot calculation — The mean of 15 observations in a report is 60. One entry, 50, is corrected to 80. What is the corrected mean?
questions.e: The total rises by 30; divided across 15 observations, the mean rises by 2 to 62.

questions.q: Health-programme report — The mean of 16 observations in a report is 61. One entry, 51, is corrected to 83. What is the corrected mean?
questions.e: The total rises by 32; divided across 16 observations, the mean rises by 2 to 63.

questions.q: Transport-depot calculation — A supplier wants a 30% profit on an item costing Rs 12800, even after allowing a 20% discount on its marked price. What marked price is required?

ایسا جملہ یا اظہار جس کا لغوی مطلب نہیں ہوتا، بلکہ ثقافتی یا لسانی پس منظر میں مخصوص معنی رکھتا ہے۔
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 215: سابقہ — وہ حرف یا جز جو لفظ کے شروع میں لگ کر اس کے معنی میں تبدیلی پیدا کرے۔

questions.q: “جملے کی تعریف” کی درست تعریف منتخب کریں۔
o: خبر + )جس کے بارے میں بات ہو(مبتدا )جو بات کی جائے(
ایسے الفاظ کا مجموعہ جو مکمل مفہوم دے۔
1. مرکب .2 )ایک ہی خیال(مفرد جملہ )دو یا زیادہ خیاالت جُڑے ہوں(جملہ
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 215: جملے کی تعریف — ایسے الفاظ کا مجموعہ جو مکمل مفہوم دے۔

questions.q: “فعل” کی درست تعریف منتخب کریں۔
o: وہ لفظ جو فعل کی کیفیت، وقت یا جگہ بتائے
وہ لفظ جو کسی کام یا حالت کو ظاہر کرے
وہ لفظ جو اکیلا مفہوم نہیں دیتا، بلکہ دوسرے الفاظ کو جوڑتا ہے
وہ لفظ جو کسی اسم کی خوبی، برائی یا حالت بتائے
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 208: فعل — وہ لفظ جو کسی کام یا حالت کو ظاہر کرے

questions.q:
Read the passage: “An archive scanned fragile letters so that researchers could view copies. Scanning improved access, but the curator kept the originals under controlled conditions because marks and paper texture were not always visible in a digital image.”

What is the curator’s position?
o: All letters should be displayed outdoors
Only digital records can be trusted
questions.e: The curator values access and preservation together.

questions.q:
Read the passage: “An archive scanned fragile letters so that researchers could view copies. Scanning improved access, but the curator kept the originals under controlled conditions because marks and paper texture were not always visible in a digital image.”

Why were the originals retained?
o: Digital copies cannot preserve every physical feature
questions.e: Certain physical details of the originals are not reproduced fully in scans.

questions.q: The two candidates differed on many points; the ____ was better prepared.
questions.e: Latter means the second of two; later refers to time.

questions.q: Which Type is associated with Example (Active) “Do not touch the wire.” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 224: Type “Negative Command” corresponds to Example (Active) “Do not touch the wire.”.

questions.q: Which Direct Speech is associated with Indirect Speech “Past Continuous” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 226: Direct Speech “Present Continuous” corresponds to Indirect Speech “Past Continuous”.

questions.q: Which Type is associated with Definition “Expresses request, wish or command” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 231: Type “Volitive Interjection” corresponds to Definition “Expresses request, wish or command”.

questions.q: Which Part of Speech is associated with Definition “Refers to a person, place, thing, or concept” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 229: Part of Speech “Noun” corresponds to Definition “Refers to a person, place, thing, or concept”.

questions.s: Concision: saying it in fewer words
questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “There are many candidates who fail because of poor time management.”?
o: Many candidates fail because of poor time management.
There are many candidates who fail because of poor time management.
Many candidates fail because of poor time management not.
Many candidates fail because of poor time management without.
questions.e: The there-construction hides the real subject.

questions.q: Which Part of Speech is associated with Explanation “Tells what the subject is doing” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 229: Part of Speech “Verb” corresponds to Explanation “Tells what the subject is doing”.

questions.q: Which Part of Speech is associated with Definition “Replaces a noun” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 229: Part of Speech “Pronoun” corresponds to Definition “Replaces a noun”.

questions.q: Which Direct Speech is associated with Indirect Speech “She asked if I liked chocolate.” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 227: Direct Speech “She said, "Do you like chocolate?"” corresponds to Indirect Speech “She asked if I liked chocolate.”.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The research findings was presented very clear to the audience.”?
o: The research findings were presented very clearly to the audience.
The research findings was presented very clear to the audience.
The research findings were not presented very clearly to the audience.
The research findings was presented very clearly to the audience.
questions.e: Two faults: findings is plural, so it takes were; and clear describes the verb presented, so it becomes clearly.

questions.s: Present and past: the four forms of each
questions.q: The novel ____ the collapse of a landed family in colonial Bengal.
questions.e: Discussion of a literary text uses the present simple.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “He is very intelligent boy but he behaves rudely with his teachers.”?
o: He is not a very intelligent boy, but he behaves rudely towards his teachers.
He is very intelligent boy but he behaves rudely with his teachers.
He is a very intelligent boy, but he behaves rudely towards his teachers.
He are a very intelligent boy, but he behaves rudely towards his teachers.
questions.e: A singular countable noun needs the article a. Behave takes towards, not with, when describing conduct to a person.

questions.q: Which Tense is associated with Active Formula “Subject + had + V3 + Object” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 224: Tense “Past Perfect” corresponds to Active Formula “Subject + had + V3 + Object”.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The government have issued many advices regarding the new tax.”?
o: The government has issued a great deal of advice regarding the new tax.
The government have issued many advices regarding the new tax.
The government has not issued a great deal of advice regarding the new tax.
The government have issued a great deal of advice regarding the new tax.
questions.e: Treat government as singular; advice is uncountable and cannot take many or a plural -s.

questions.q: Which Part of Speech is associated with Explanation “Shows if the noun is specific or non- specific” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 229: Part of Speech “Articles” corresponds to Explanation “Shows if the noun is specific or non- specific”.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Because of the roads were blocked, the convoy arrived lately.”?
o: Because the roads were not blocked, the convoy arrived late.
Because of the roads were blocked, the convoy arrived lately.
Because the roads were blocked, the convoy arrived late.
Because the roads was blocked, the convoy arrived late.
questions.e: Because introduces the clause. Late is the adverb of time; lately means “recently”.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Reforms are needed. Corruption is endemic. (Connect with given-new.)”?
o: Corruption are endemic. Tackling it demands serious reform.
Corruption is not endemic. Tackling it demands serious reform.
Reforms are needed. Corruption is endemic. (Connect with given-new.)
Corruption is endemic. Tackling it demands serious reform.
questions.e: Corruption is endemic. Tackling it demands serious reform. (Given problem first, new response last.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The proposal looks attractively but its financial implications are serious.”?
o: The proposal looks attractive, but its financial implications are serious.
The proposal looks attractively but its financial implications are serious.
The proposal looks attractive, but its financial implications are not serious.
The proposal looks attractive, but its financial implications is serious.
questions.e: Look is a linking verb here, so the adjective attractive follows; a comma precedes but joining two main clauses.

questions.q: Which Indirect Speech is associated with Direct Speech “She said, "What is your name?"” in the English reference?
o: She requested not to disturb her.
He says that he likes tea.
She asked what my name was.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 227: Indirect Speech “She asked what my name was.” corresponds to Direct Speech “She said, "What is your name?"”.

questions.q: Which Type is associated with Sentence Example “Hey! How are you?” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 231: Type “Greeting Interjection” corresponds to Sentence Example “Hey! How are you?”.

questions.q: Which Tense is associated with Example “She had written before I arrived.” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 244: Tense “Past Perfect” corresponds to Example “She had written before I arrived.”.

questions.q: Which Type is associated with Sentence Example “He walked to the shop.” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 231: Type “Preposition of Direction” corresponds to Sentence Example “He walked to the shop.”.

questions.q: Which Indirect Speech is associated with Direct Speech “Today” in the English reference?
o: The Previous Night / The Night Before
The Previous Day / The Day Before
The Next Day / The Following Day
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 227: Indirect Speech “That Day” corresponds to Direct Speech “Today”.

questions.q: Which Direct Speech is associated with Example “He said, "I will help you." → He said that he would help me.” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 227: Direct Speech “Will” corresponds to Example “He said, "I will help you." → He said that he would help me.”.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Inflation hurt the poor most. Prices rose sharply in 2023. (Reorder.)”?
o: Inflation hurt the poor most. Prices rose sharply in 2023. (Reorder.)
Prices rose sharply in 2023. This inflation hurt the poor most not.
Prices rose sharply in 2023. inflation hurt the poor most.
Prices rose sharply in 2023. This inflation hurt the poor most.
questions.e: Prices rose sharply in 2023. This inflation hurt the poor most. (Event first, consequence last.)

questions.q: Which Rule is associated with Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) “There is a lamp placed in the corner of the room.” in the English reference?
o: Shows relation like enmity, alliance, coordination
Shows transformation or change of state
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 231: Rule “Location inside a corner” corresponds to Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) “There is a lamp placed in the corner of the room.”.

questions.q: Which Type is associated with Sentence Example “I need some water.” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 230: Type “Uncountable Noun” corresponds to Sentence Example “I need some water.”.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “He was accused for embezzling public funds.”?
o: He was not accused of embezzling...
He was accused for embezzling public funds.
questions.e: He was accused of embezzling... (Preposition: accused of.)

questions.q: Which Example Sentence is associated with Rule “No article before hell, heaven, or God (used reverently)” in the English reference?
o: He is a teacher. She bought a university bag. (Note: "University" starts with a consonant sound /juː/)
He hopes to go to heaven. We must fear God.
A servant must obey his master. Anyone can become a leader.
I saw a certain bird flying high. A certain man was looking for you.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 225: Example Sentence “He hopes to go to heaven. We must fear God.” corresponds to Rule “No article before hell, heaven, or God (used reverently)”.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The committee met twice. This is a problem.”?
o: The committee met twice. This is a problem.
The committee met only twice in three years. This inactivity is the real problem.
The committee met only twice in three years. This inactivity are the real problem.
The committee met only twice in three years. This inactivity is not the real problem.
questions.e: A bare this refers to nothing precise; a summary noun fixes it.

questions.q: Which Structure is associated with Tense “Present Continuous” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 244: Structure “subject + is/am/are + verb-ing” corresponds to Tense “Present Continuous”.

questions.q: Which Connector Type is associated with Example “He was late; however, he completed the task.” in the English reference?
o: Noun Clause Introducers (That, What, Whether, If, etc.)
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 234: Connector Type “Conjunctive Adverbs” corresponds to Example “He was late; however, he completed the task.”.

questions.q: Which Preposition is associated with Rule “Confusion over "sat in/on" tree” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 233: Preposition “In / On” corresponds to Rule “Confusion over "sat in/on" tree”.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “When one prepares systematically, you retain more and we revise faster.”?
o: When candidates prepare systematically, they retain more and revise faster without.
When candidates prepare systematically, they retain more and revise faster.
When one prepares systematically, you retain more and we revise faster.
When candidates prepare systematically, they retain more and revise faster not.
questions.e: Three shifts of person inside one sentence.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “He said me that the file was missing.”?
o: He told me that the file were missing.
He told me that the file was not missing.
He said me that the file was missing.
He told me that the file was missing.
questions.e: Say does not take a person directly; tell does.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Walking into the hall, the silence struck the candidates.”?
o: Walking into the hall, the candidates were not struck by the silence.
Walking into the hall, the silence struck the candidates.
Walking into the hall, the candidates were struck by the silence.
Walking into the hall, the candidates was struck by the silence.
questions.e: Walking into the hall, the candidates were struck by the silence. (Dangling modifier.)

questions.q: Which Preposition is associated with Rule “Legal or moral state/status” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 232: Preposition “Of” corresponds to Rule “Legal or moral state/status”.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “She told that she would come the next day.”?
o: She said she would come the next day.
She said that she would come the next day.
She told that she would come the next day.
She said that she would not come the next day.
questions.e: Tell requires a person; without one, use say.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “There is less opportunities for graduates this year.”?
o: There are fewer opportunities for graduates.
There is less opportunities for graduates this year.
There are not fewer opportunities for graduates.
There is fewer opportunities for graduates.
questions.e: There are fewer opportunities for graduates. (fewer + agreement: opportunities are countable and plural.)

questions.q: Which Rule is associated with Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) “He goes to the office on foot every day.” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 233: Rule “Movement by foot” corresponds to Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) “He goes to the office on foot every day.”.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “He asked me that where was I going.”?
o: He asked me where I were going.
He asked me where I was not going.
He asked me that where was I going.
He asked me where I was going.
questions.e: A reported question drops that, drops the inversion and keeps statement order.

questions.s: Future forms and the sequence of tenses
questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “When the notification will be issued, we will start work.”?
o: When the notification is issued, we will start work.
When the notification are issued, we will start work.
When the notification is not issued, we will start work.
When the notification will be issued, we will start work.
questions.e: A time clause uses a present tense for future meaning.

questions.s: Future forms and the sequence of tenses
questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “He said that he is not interested in the post.”?
o: He said that he was not interested in the post.
He said that he were not interested in the post.
He said that he was not not interested in the post.
He said that he is not interested in the post.
questions.e: A past reporting verb pulls the reported clause into the past.

questions.q: Which sentence expresses an outside obligation rather than the speaker’s own?
o: You must submit the form by Friday.
You have to submit the form by Friday; it is a departmental rule.
You should submit the form by Friday.
You may submit the form by Friday.
questions.e: Have to points to an external rule; must usually carries the speaker’s own authority.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “She asked whether did I need any help.”?
o: She asked whether I needed any help without.
She asked whether I needed any help.
She asked whether did I need any help.
She asked whether I needed any help not.
questions.e: Did disappears and the main verb carries the backshifted tense.

questions.s: Future forms and the sequence of tenses
questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “If it will rain tomorrow, the ceremony will be cancelled.”?
o: If it rains tomorrow, the ceremony will be cancelled.
If it will rain tomorrow, the ceremony will be cancelled.
If it rains tomorrow, the ceremony will not be cancelled.
If it rains tomorrow, ceremony will be cancelled.
questions.e: The if-clause takes the present simple in a first conditional.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “He said that he will submit the report tomorrow.”?
o: He said he would submit the report the next day.
He said that he would not submit the report the next day.
He said that he will submit the report tomorrow.
He said that he would submit the report the next day.
questions.e: Will backshifts to would, and tomorrow becomes the next day.

questions.s: Future forms and the sequence of tenses
questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The train will leave at 6:40 every morning.”?
o: The train leaves at 6:40 every morning.
The train leaves at 6:40 every morning not.
The train will leave at 6:40 every morning.
questions.e: A timetable takes the present simple.

questions.q: District-office worksheet — The roots of x² − 30x + 216 = 0 differ by 6. What is the larger root?
questions.e: The quadratic factors as (x − 12)(x − 18); the larger root is 18.

questions.q: Health-programme report — The roots of x² − 24x + 140 = 0 differ by 4. What is the larger root?
questions.e: The quadratic factors as (x − 10)(x − 14); the larger root is 14.

questions.q: Scholarship-fund audit — A train 300 m long clears a 80 m platform in 17 seconds. What is its speed in km/h?
questions.e: The train covers 380 m. Its speed is (380)/17 m/s × 3.6 = 80.47 km/h.

questions.q: Warehouse planning case — A train 310 m long clears a 90 m platform in 18 seconds. What is its speed in km/h?
questions.e: The train covers 400 m. Its speed is (400)/18 m/s × 3.6 = 80 km/h.

questions.q: Scholarship-fund audit — The mean of 17 observations in a report is 80. One entry, 70, is corrected to 104. What is the corrected mean?
questions.e: The total rises by 34; divided across 17 observations, the mean rises by 2 to 82.

questions.q: Warehouse planning case — The mean of 18 observations in a report is 81. One entry, 71, is corrected to 107. What is the corrected mean?
questions.e: The total rises by 36; divided across 18 observations, the mean rises by 2 to 83.

questions.q: Transport-depot calculation — An arithmetic sequence begins 59, 66, 73, … . What is the sum of its first 16 terms?
Health-programme report — An arithmetic sequence begins 60, 68, 76, … . What is the sum of its first 17 terms?
Training-centre exercise — A bag holds 56 red and 8 blue counters. Two are drawn without replacement. What is the probability that both are red?
questions.e: Multiply the changing probabilities: 56/64 × 55/63 = 76.39%.

questions.q: Survey-unit review — A bag holds 55 red and 7 blue counters. Two are drawn without replacement. What is the probability that both are red?
questions.e: Multiply the changing probabilities: 55/62 × 54/61 = 78.53%.

questions.q: Scholarship-fund audit — A two-digit number has digit sum 11; reversing its digits increases it by 27. What is the original number?
questions.e: Let the tens and units digits be x and y. Then x + y = 11 and 9(x − y) = -27; hence x = 4, y = 7.

questions.q: Warehouse planning case — A two-digit number has digit sum 12; reversing its digits increases it by 36. What is the original number?
questions.e: Let the tens and units digits be x and y. Then x + y = 12 and 9(x − y) = -36; hence x = 4, y = 8.

questions.q: Health-programme report — A vehicle covers two equal-distance legs at 114 km/h and 130 km/h. What is its average speed for the complete journey?
questions.e: For equal distances the harmonic mean applies: 2uv/(u + v) = 121.48 km/h.

questions.q: Transport-depot calculation — A vehicle covers two equal-distance legs at 112 km/h and 126 km/h. What is its average speed for the complete journey?
questions.e: For equal distances the harmonic mean applies: 2uv/(u + v) = 118.59 km/h.

questions.q: Survey-unit review — A geometric sequence has first term 62 and common ratio 2. What is its 5th term?
Training-centre exercise — A geometric sequence has first term 63 and common ratio 3. What is its 6th term?
Transport-depot calculation — 42 passengers paid Rs 3040. An adult ticket cost Rs 80 and a child ticket Rs 60. How many adults travelled?
questions.e: If a is the adult count, 80a + 60(42 − a) = 3040, which gives a = 26.

questions.q: District-office worksheet — Worker B takes 16 days for a task. Worker A is 25% more efficient than B. How many days would A need for the same task?
questions.e: Time varies inversely with efficiency, so A's time is 16 × 100/125 = 12.8 days.

questions.q: Health-programme report — 44 passengers paid Rs 1860. An adult ticket cost Rs 50 and a child ticket Rs 30. How many adults travelled?
questions.e: If a is the adult count, 50a + 30(44 − a) = 1860, which gives a = 27.

questions.q: Scholarship-fund audit — Worker B takes 17 days for a task. Worker A is 50% more efficient than B. How many days would A need for the same task?
questions.e: Time varies inversely with efficiency, so A's time is 17 × 100/150 = 11.33 days.

questions.q: District-office worksheet — An investment grows to Rs 6336 in two years at 20% compound interest per year. What was the principal?
Relief-camp planning case — An investment grows to Rs 4840 in two years at 10% compound interest per year. What was the principal?
Survey-unit review — After a 10% discount and then 5% sales tax, an equipment bill for a survey unit is Rs 28350. What was the listed price?
questions.e: If L is the list price, L × 90/100 × 105/100 = 28350, giving L = 30000.

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — A invests Rs 68000 for 10 months and B invests Rs 6000 for 5 months. If their profit is Rs 7100, what is A's share?
questions.e: Profit follows capital-months. The weights are 680000:30000; A therefore receives Rs 6800.

questions.q: Health-programme report — A invests Rs 67000 for 9 months and B invests Rs 5000 for 4 months. If their profit is Rs 6230, what is A's share?
questions.e: Profit follows capital-months. The weights are 603000:20000; A therefore receives Rs 6030.

questions.q: Health-programme report — On a coordinate grid, point Q lies 448 units east and 1536 units north of point P. What is the straight-line distance PQ?
Transport-depot calculation — On a coordinate grid, point Q lies 504 units east and 945 units north of point P. What is the straight-line distance PQ?
Warehouse planning case — After a 30% discount and then 20% sales tax, an equipment bill for a warehouse is Rs 31080. What was the listed price?
questions.e: If L is the list price, L × 70/100 × 120/100 = 31080, giving L = 37000.

questions.q: Scholarship-fund audit — For two years at 15% per annum, by how much does compound interest exceed simple interest on Rs 600000?
Warehouse planning case — For two years at 20% per annum, by how much does compound interest exceed simple interest on Rs 610000?
Scholarship-fund audit — A 46 m by 16 m rectangular courtyard has a uniform path 4 m wide inside its boundary. What area does the path cover?
questions.e: Path area = outer area − inner area = 736 − 38×8 = 432 m².

questions.q: District-office worksheet — A 37 m by 18 m rectangular courtyard has a uniform path 3 m wide inside its boundary. What area does the path cover?
questions.e: Path area = outer area − inner area = 666 − 31×12 = 294 m².

questions.q: Survey-unit review — Two batches assessed by a survey unit contain 24 and 14 candidates with mean scores 54 and 74. What is the combined mean?
questions.e: Use the weighted mean: (24 × 54 + 14 × 74) ÷ 38 = 61.37.

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — Two batches assessed by a relief camp contain 68 and 13 candidates with mean scores 54 and 79. What is the combined mean?
questions.e: Use the weighted mean: (68 × 54 + 13 × 79) ÷ 81 = 58.01.

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — A can complete a project in 684 days and B in 1026 days. They work together for 342 days; B then leaves. How many days from the start will A take to finish the project?
questions.e: Together they complete 342 × (1/684 + 1/1026) = 5/6. A needs another 114 days for the remaining 1/6, totalling 456.

questions.q: Warehouse planning case — A boat's still-water speed is 69 km/h and the stream flows at 6 km/h. How long does a 14175 km upstream and 14175 km downstream round trip take?
District-office worksheet — A can complete a project in 696 days and B in 1044 days. They work together for 348 days; B then leaves. How many days from the start will A take to finish the project?
questions.e: Together they complete 348 × (1/696 + 1/1044) = 5/6. A needs another 116 days for the remaining 1/6, totalling 464.

questions.q: Scholarship-fund audit — A boat's still-water speed is 68 km/h and the stream flows at 5 km/h. How long does a 9198 km upstream and 9198 km downstream round trip take?
District-office worksheet — Two triangles are similar. A side of 4 cm in the smaller corresponds to 16 cm in the larger. If another smaller side is 7 cm, what is its corresponding larger side?
questions.e: The scale factor is 16/4 = 4; therefore 7 × 4 = 28 cm.

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — Two triangles are similar. A side of 3 cm in the smaller corresponds to 15 cm in the larger. If another smaller side is 12 cm, what is its corresponding larger side?
questions.e: The scale factor is 15/3 = 5; therefore 12 × 5 = 60 cm.

questions.q: Training-centre exercise — Two runners start together in opposite directions on a 560 m circular track at 80 m/s and 62.22 m/s. After how many seconds do they first meet?
questions.e: In opposite directions their relative speed is 142.22 m/s, so time is 560 ÷ 142.22 = 3.94 seconds.

questions.q: Survey-unit review — Two runners start together in opposite directions on a 540 m circular track at 90 m/s and 67.5 m/s. After how many seconds do they first meet?
questions.e: In opposite directions their relative speed is 157.5 m/s, so time is 540 ÷ 157.5 = 3.43 seconds.

questions.q: Survey-unit review — a survey unit must select 5 representatives from 19 eligible people. If order does not matter, how many different committees are possible?
Training-centre exercise — a training centre must select 2 representatives from 20 eligible people. If order does not matter, how many different committees are possible?
Transport-depot calculation — A bus leaves a transport depot at 92 km/h. 3 hours later, a car follows on the same route at 104 km/h. How long after the car starts will it catch the bus?
questions.e: The bus has a 276 km lead. Relative speed is 12 km/h, so catch-up time is 23 hours.

questions.q: Scholarship-fund audit — A bus leaves a scholarship fund at 32 km/h. 3 hours later, a car follows on the same route at 44 km/h. How long after the car starts will it catch the bus?
questions.e: The bus has a 96 km lead. Relative speed is 12 km/h, so catch-up time is 8 hours.

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — A tank contains 470 litres of a 25% solution. 94 litres of the mixture are removed and replaced by water. What is the new concentration?
questions.e: Removing one-fifth of a uniform mixture removes one-fifth of its solute. The remaining concentration is 25% × 4/5 = 20%.

questions.q: District-office worksheet — A tank contains 480 litres of a 30% solution. 96 litres of the mixture are removed and replaced by water. What is the new concentration?
questions.e: Removing one-fifth of a uniform mixture removes one-fifth of its solute. The remaining concentration is 30% × 4/5 = 24%.

questions.q: District-office worksheet — A quarterly table for a district office records 530, 285, and 125 completed cases in three months. What percentage of the three-month total was completed in the first month?
questions.e: The total is 940; the first-month share is 530/940 × 100 = 56.38%.

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — A quarterly table for a relief camp records 520, 280, and 120 completed cases in three months. What percentage of the three-month total was completed in the first month?
questions.e: The total is 920; the first-month share is 520/920 × 100 = 56.52%.

questions.q: Survey-unit review — Two pipes can fill a tank in 252 and 378 minutes, while a leak can empty it in 756 minutes. If all three remain open, when will the tank fill?
questions.e: Net rate = 1/252 + 1/378 − 1/756 = 1/189, so the tank fills in 189 minutes.

questions.q: Training-centre exercise — Two pipes can fill a tank in 264 and 396 minutes, while a leak can empty it in 792 minutes. If all three remain open, when will the tank fill?
questions.e: Net rate = 1/264 + 1/396 − 1/792 = 1/198, so the tank fills in 198 minutes.

questions.q: District-office worksheet — A supplier wants a 25% profit on an item costing Rs 2400, even after allowing a 25% discount on its marked price. What marked price is required?
questions.e: Required selling price is 2400 × 125/100. Since that is 75% of the marked price, divide it by 0.75.

questions.q: Warehouse planning case — A supplier wants a 40% profit on an item costing Rs 4000, even after allowing a 30% discount on its marked price. What marked price is required?
questions.e: Required selling price is 4000 × 140/100. Since that is 70% of the marked price, divide it by 0.7.

questions.q: Health-programme report — a health programme divides 602 files between teams A and B in the ratio 6:8. How many additional files must A receive for the new ratio A:B to become 12:8?
questions.e: The original shares are 258 and 344. To make A's share 516, it needs 516 − 258 = 258 more files.

questions.q: Transport-depot calculation — a transport depot divides 504 files between teams A and B in the ratio 5:7. How many additional files must A receive for the new ratio A:B to become 10:7?
questions.e: The original shares are 210 and 294. To make A's share 420, it needs 420 − 210 = 210 more files.

questions.q: Warehouse planning case — What is the least number greater than 2862 that leaves remainder 52 when divided by both 53 and 54, given that 53 and 54 are coprime?
questions.e: A common remainder means N − 52 is a multiple of lcm(53, 54) = 2862. The least eligible N is 2862 + 52 = 2914.

questions.q: Scholarship-fund audit — What is the least number greater than 2756 that leaves remainder 51 when divided by both 52 and 53, given that 52 and 53 are coprime?
questions.e: A common remainder means N − 51 is a multiple of lcm(52, 53) = 2756. The least eligible N is 2756 + 51 = 2807.
