questions.q: Which sentence describes a fixed arrangement?
o: We will meet the registrar sometime.
We are meeting the registrar at eleven tomorrow.
questions.e: The present continuous with a stated time marks a fixed arrangement.

questions.q: Which Direct Speech is associated with Rule “He said, "I have finished." → He said that he had finished.” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 226: Direct Speech “Present Perfect” corresponds to Rule “He said, "I have finished." → He said that he had finished.”.

questions.q: Which Direct Speech is associated with Indirect Speech “The Previous Night / The Night Before” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 227: Direct Speech “Last night” corresponds to Indirect Speech “The Previous Night / The Night Before”.

questions.q: Which Type is associated with Example Word “book” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 229: Type “Common Noun” corresponds to Example Word “book”.

questions.s: Future forms and the sequence of tenses
questions.q: The teacher explained that light ____ faster than sound.
questions.e: A scientific truth keeps the present tense after a past reporting verb.

questions.q: Which Indirect Speech is associated with Direct Speech “Just” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 227: Indirect Speech “Only” corresponds to Direct Speech “Just”.

questions.q: Which Preposition is associated with Rule “Disagreement with an idea” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 232: Preposition “To” corresponds to Rule “Disagreement with an idea”.

questions.q: Which Tense is associated with Example (Active) “They had completed the task.” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 224: Tense “Past Perfect” corresponds to Example (Active) “They had completed the task.”.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Because the data was outdated, therefore the projections were wrong.”?
o: Because the data were outdated, the projections were wrong.
Because the data was outdated, the projections were wrong.
Because the data was outdated, therefore the projections were wrong.
Because the data was not outdated, the projections were wrong.
questions.e: Because already supplies the cause; therefore duplicates it.

questions.q: How long ____ you ____ for the result?
questions.e: How long with an activity continuing to now takes the present perfect continuous.

questions.q: Which Type is associated with Passive Formula “Let not + Object + be + V3” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 224: Type “Negative Command” corresponds to Passive Formula “Let not + Object + be + V3”.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Keeping a list of all my mistakes from every test.”?
o: Keeping one page per error type, with the rule written in my own words not.
Keeping one page per error type, with rule written in my own words.
Keeping one page per error type, with the rule written in my own words.
Keeping a list of all my mistakes from every test.
questions.e: A log sorted by rule can be revised; a chronological list cannot.

questions.q: Which Example Sentence is associated with Rule “Before consonant sounds (not just consonants)” in the English reference?
o: A servant must obey his master. Anyone can become a leader.
I saw a certain bird flying high. A certain man was looking for you.
He is a teacher. She bought a university bag. (Note: "University" starts with a consonant sound /juː/)
I met Ahmed yesterday. Fatima is my sister.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 225: Example Sentence “He is a teacher. She bought a university bag. (Note: "University" starts with a consonant sound /juː/)” corresponds to Rule “Before consonant sounds (not just consonants)”.

questions.q: Which Indirect Speech is associated with Direct Speech “Now” in the English reference?
o: The Previous Day / The Day Before
The Next Day / The Following Day
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 227: Indirect Speech “Then” corresponds to Direct Speech “Now”.

questions.q: Which Type is associated with Example Word “water” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 230: Type “Uncountable Noun” corresponds to Example Word “water”.

questions.q: Which Indirect Speech is associated with Direct Speech “Present Indefinite” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 226: Indirect Speech “Past Indefinite” corresponds to Direct Speech “Present Indefinite”.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “He served tea to the guests in plastic cups.”?
o: He served tea in plastic cups than the guests.
He served tea in plastic cups to the guests.
He served tea to the guests in plastic cups.
He served tea in plastic cups to the guests not.
questions.e: He served tea in plastic cups to the guests. (The tea was in cups, not the guests.)

questions.q: The file ____ on the table where the clerk had left it.
questions.e: Lie (to rest) has the past form lay; laid belongs to lay (to place something).

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Her handwriting is not so good like her sister.”?
o: Her handwriting is not so good like her sister.
Her handwriting is not not so good as her sister’s.
Her handwriting are not so good as her sister’s.
Her handwriting is not so good as her sister’s.
questions.e: Not so … as is the pattern, and the possessive makes both sides handwriting.

questions.q: Which Type is associated with Definition “Refers back to subject” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 230: Type “Reflexive Pronoun” corresponds to Definition “Refers back to subject”.

questions.q: Which Type is associated with Example Word “my, his” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 230: Type “Possessive Adjective” corresponds to Example Word “my, his”.

questions.q: Which Connector Type is associated with Example “Because he was ill, he stayed home. He stayed home because he was ill.” in the English reference?
o: Noun Clause Introducers (That, What, Whether, If, etc.)
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 234: Connector Type “Subordinating Conjunctions (Adverb Clause)” corresponds to Example “Because he was ill, he stayed home. He stayed home because he was ill.”.

questions.q: Which Rule is associated with Example Sentence “He caught the measles last month. She was diagnosed with the mumps.” in the English reference?
o: No article before hell, heaven, or God (used reverently)
Exception: article the is used with "devil"
Exceptions: article the is used with measles, mumps
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 225: Rule “Exceptions: article the is used with measles, mumps” corresponds to Example Sentence “He caught the measles last month. She was diagnosed with the mumps.”.

questions.q: The accused was released from ____ prison after ____ appeal succeeded.
questions.e: In or from prison as an inmate takes no article; the appeal is the specific one mentioned.

questions.q: Which Type is associated with Sentence Example “He won by luck.” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 231: Type “Preposition of Manner” corresponds to Sentence Example “He won by luck.”.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “He is interested in politics, history and to study law.”?
o: He is interested in politics, history and to study law.
He is interested in politics, history and law.
He are interested in politics, history and law.
He is not interested in politics, history and law.
questions.e: After in, all three items must be nouns.

questions.q: Which Type is associated with Example Word “Hey!” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 231: Type “Greeting Interjection” corresponds to Example Word “Hey!”.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Teaching is more demanding than to administer.”?
o: Teaching are more demanding than administering.
Teaching is more demanding than administering.
Teaching is more demanding than to administer.
Teaching is not more demanding than administering.
questions.e: Both sides of a comparison take the same form.

questions.q: Which Type is associated with Example (Passive) “Let the door be closed.” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 224: Type “Order/Command” corresponds to Example (Passive) “Let the door be closed.”.

questions.q: Which Connector Type is associated with Example “My friend, who is a doctor, is coming. People who work hard succeed.” in the English reference?
o: Noun Clause Introducers (That, What, Whether, If, etc.)
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 234: Connector Type “Relative Pronouns (Adjective Clause)” corresponds to Example “My friend, who is a doctor, is coming. People who work hard succeed.”.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The PM said, ’We are facing a severe economic crisis.’”?
o: The PM said that they were not facing a severe economic crisis.
The PM said, ’We are facing a severe economic crisis.’
The PM said that they were facing a severe economic crisis.
The PM said that they was facing a severe economic crisis.
questions.e: The PM said that they were facing a severe economic crisis.

questions.q: Which Rule is associated with Example Sentence “He read The Quran daily. She studied The Republic by Plato.” in the English reference?
o: Use the with names of famous books
Use the with a class of animals, birds, or objects
Use the with a class of people
Use the with books, journals, and buildings
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 225: Rule “Use the with names of famous books” corresponds to Example Sentence “He read The Quran daily. She studied The Republic by Plato.”.

questions.q: Which Tense is associated with Active Formula “Subject + V2 + Object” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 224: Tense “Past Indefinite” corresponds to Active Formula “Subject + V2 + Object”.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “He said, ’I will resign tomorrow.’”?
o: He said that he would not resign the following day.
He said that he would resign the following day.
He said he would resign the following day.
questions.e: He said that he would resign the following day.

questions.q: Which Type is associated with Example Word “because, if” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 231: Type “Subordinating Conjunction” corresponds to Example Word “because, if”.

questions.q: The accounts ____ externally every year, as the rules require.
questions.e: Present simple passive: are + participle.

questions.q: Which Rule is associated with Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) “We stopped at Dubai on our way to Saudi Arabia.” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 233: Rule “Temporary or transit stop” corresponds to Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) “We stopped at Dubai on our way to Saudi Arabia.”.

questions.q: Which Rule is associated with Preposition “Of / For / To” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 233: Rule “Desire/longing related to personality” corresponds to Preposition “Of / For / To”.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The judge said, ’The accused is guilty.’”?
o: The judge said that the accused was not guilty.
The judge said that the accused were guilty.
The judge said that the accused was guilty.
The judge said, ’The accused is guilty.’
questions.e: The judge said that the accused was guilty.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Each of the candidate have been informed about their result by the commission.”?
o: Each of the candidate have been informed about their result by the commission.
Each of the candidates has been informed of the result by the commission.
Each of the candidates have been informed of the result by the commission.
Each of the candidates has not been informed of the result by the commission.
questions.e: Each of + plural noun, singular verb and singular reference; inform takes of before a thing.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “She is admired for her honesty, her courage, and because she works hard.”?
o: She are admired for her honesty, her courage, and her diligence.
She is not admired for her honesty, her courage, and her diligence.
She is admired for her honesty, her courage, and because she works hard.
She is admired for her honesty, her courage, and her diligence.
questions.e: She is admired for her honesty, her courage, and her diligence. (Three matched noun phrases.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Item 5 article (Day 12)”?
o: Corruption is not the biggest threat to development.
Corruption is the biggest threat to development.
Corruption are the biggest threat to development.
questions.e: Corruption is the biggest threat to development. (No article before the abstract general noun development.)

questions.q: Warehouse planning case — A invests Rs 63000 for 10 months and B invests Rs 8000 for 7 months. If their profit is Rs 6860, what is A's share?
questions.e: Profit follows capital-months. The weights are 630000:56000; A therefore receives Rs 6300.

questions.q: Transport-depot calculation — A vehicle covers two equal-distance legs at 80 km/h and 94 km/h. What is its average speed for the complete journey?
questions.e: For equal distances the harmonic mean applies: 2uv/(u + v) = 86.44 km/h.

questions.q: District-office worksheet — A invests Rs 53000 for 10 months and B invests Rs 5000 for 4 months. If their profit is Rs 5500, what is A's share?
questions.e: Profit follows capital-months. The weights are 530000:20000; A therefore receives Rs 5300.

questions.q: Health-programme report — A vehicle covers two equal-distance legs at 82 km/h and 98 km/h. What is its average speed for the complete journey?
questions.e: For equal distances the harmonic mean applies: 2uv/(u + v) = 89.29 km/h.

questions.q: Survey-unit review — A 80 m by 17 m rectangular courtyard has a uniform path 2 m wide inside its boundary. What area does the path cover?
questions.e: Path area = outer area − inner area = 1360 − 76×13 = 372 m².

questions.q: Training-centre exercise — A 81 m by 18 m rectangular courtyard has a uniform path 3 m wide inside its boundary. What area does the path cover?
questions.e: Path area = outer area − inner area = 1458 − 75×12 = 558 m².

questions.q: Transport-depot calculation — 52 passengers paid Rs 2660. An adult ticket cost Rs 55 and a child ticket Rs 35. How many adults travelled?
questions.e: If a is the adult count, 55a + 35(52 − a) = 2660, which gives a = 42.

questions.q: Scholarship-fund audit — 81 passengers paid Rs 3670. An adult ticket cost Rs 50 and a child ticket Rs 30. How many adults travelled?
questions.e: If a is the adult count, 50a + 30(81 − a) = 3670, which gives a = 62.

questions.q: Health-programme report — The roots of x² − 57x + 806 = 0 differ by 5. What is the larger root?
questions.e: The quadratic factors as (x − 26)(x − 31); the larger root is 31.

questions.q: Warehouse planning case — For two years at 20% per annum, by how much does compound interest exceed simple interest on Rs 450000?
Transport-depot calculation — The roots of x² − 54x + 725 = 0 differ by 4. What is the larger root?
questions.e: The quadratic factors as (x − 25)(x − 29); the larger root is 29.

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — A geometric sequence has first term 42 and common ratio 3. What is its 5th term?
Scholarship-fund audit — For two years at 15% per annum, by how much does compound interest exceed simple interest on Rs 440000?
District-office worksheet — A geometric sequence has first term 43 and common ratio 4. What is its 6th term?
District-office worksheet — On a coordinate grid, point Q lies 10 units east and 24 units north of point P. What is the straight-line distance PQ?
questions.e: PQ = √(10² + 24²) = 26 units.

questions.q: Health-programme report — An investment grows to Rs 58500 in two years at 50% compound interest per year. What was the principal?
Warehouse planning case — On a coordinate grid, point Q lies 28 units east and 96 units north of point P. What is the straight-line distance PQ?
Training-centre exercise — An investment grows to Rs 36288 in two years at 20% compound interest per year. What was the principal?
District-office worksheet — An arithmetic sequence begins 6, 9, 12, … . What is the sum of its first 11 terms?
Warehouse planning case — An arithmetic sequence begins 8, 13, 18, … . What is the sum of its first 13 terms?

questions.q:
Read the passage: “A river agency reported fewer pollution incidents after installing monitoring stations. It also admitted that earlier records came from occasional visits and might have missed short spills. The director warned against treating the two counts as a clean before-and-after comparison.”

Which improvement would make a later trend more credible?
o: Apply a consistent monitoring method over time
questions.e: A consistent measurement method supports comparisons across periods.

questions.q:
Read the passage: “A river agency reported fewer pollution incidents after installing monitoring stations. It also admitted that earlier records came from occasional visits and might have missed short spills. The director warned against treating the two counts as a clean before-and-after comparison.”

What makes the comparison uncertain?
o: The two periods used different detection methods
questions.e: Occasional visits and continuous stations may detect different numbers of incidents.

questions.q: Which Type is associated with Sentence Example “This house is bigger than mine.” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 230: Type “Comparative Adjective” corresponds to Sentence Example “This house is bigger than mine.”.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “He neither apologised nor did he explain.”?
o: He neither apologised nor did he explain.
He neither apologised nor explained without.
He neither apologised nor explained not.
questions.e: He neither apologised nor explained. (Two matched past-tense verbs after neither ... nor.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Writing essays is more demanding than to attempt the precis.”?
o: Writing essays is not more demanding than attempting the precis.
Writing essays is more demanding than to attempt the precis.
Writing essays is more demanding than attempting the precis.
Writing essays are more demanding than attempting the precis.
questions.e: Writing essays is more demanding than attempting the precis. (Gerund vs. gerund.)

questions.q: Which Part of Speech is associated with Definition “Modifies nouns (specific or general)” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 229: Part of Speech “Articles” corresponds to Definition “Modifies nouns (specific or general)”.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The plan is both ambitious and it costs a lot.”?
o: The plan are both ambitious and expensive.
The plan is both ambitious and expensive.
The plan is both ambitious and it costs a lot.
The plan is not both ambitious and expensive.
questions.e: The plan is both ambitious and expensive. (Two adjectives after both ... and.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “We came, we saw, and conquering followed.”?
o: We came, we saw, and conquering followed.
We came, we saw, we conquered.
We came, we saw, we conquered without.
We came, we saw, we conquered not.
questions.e: We came, we saw, we conquered. (Three matched clauses.)

questions.q: Which Direct Speech is associated with Indirect Speech “Past Indefinite” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 226: Direct Speech “Present Indefinite” corresponds to Indirect Speech “Past Indefinite”.

questions.q: Which Direct Speech is associated with Example “He said, "I can swim." → He said that he could swim.” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 227: Direct Speech “Can” corresponds to Example “He said, "I can swim." → He said that he could swim.”.

questions.q: Which Type is associated with Example Word “mine, yours” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 230: Type “Possessive Pronoun” corresponds to Example Word “mine, yours”.

questions.q: Which Part of Speech is associated with Explanation “Gives more information about a noun” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 229: Part of Speech “Adjective” corresponds to Explanation “Gives more information about a noun”.

questions.q: Which Type is associated with Reporting Verb “Cursed” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 228: Type “Curse” corresponds to Reporting Verb “Cursed”.

questions.q: Which Type is associated with Reporting Verb “Wondered” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 228: Type “Wonder” corresponds to Reporting Verb “Wondered”.

questions.q: Which Direct Speech is associated with Example “He said, "I must finish it." → He said that he had to finish it.” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 227: Direct Speech “Must” corresponds to Example “He said, "I must finish it." → He said that he had to finish it.”.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The new tax will effect small traders badly.”?
o: The new tax will not affect small traders badly.
The new tax will effect small traders badly.
The new tax will affect small traders badly.
new tax will affect small traders badly.
questions.e: Affect is the verb; effect as a verb means to bring about.

questions.q: Which Type is associated with Sentence Example “He hurt himself.” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 230: Type “Reflexive Pronoun” corresponds to Sentence Example “He hurt himself.”.

questions.q: Which Preposition is associated with Rule “Comparison between similar things” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 233: Preposition “With” corresponds to Rule “Comparison between similar things”.

questions.q: Which Rule is associated with Preposition “Into” in the English reference?
o: Shows relation like enmity, alliance, coordination
Shows level or capacity of doing something
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 231: Rule “Movement from outside to inside” corresponds to Preposition “Into”.

questions.q: Which Preposition is associated with Rule “Hidden at the back” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 232: Preposition “Behind” corresponds to Rule “Hidden at the back”.

questions.q: Which Preposition is associated with Rule “Shows relation like enmity, alliance, coordination” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 231: Preposition “With” corresponds to Rule “Shows relation like enmity, alliance, coordination”.

questions.q: Which Rule is associated with Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) “I applied to the university last week.” in the English reference?
o: Applied to a person or institution
Applied for a thing or purpose
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 232: Rule “Applied to a person or institution” corresponds to Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) “I applied to the university last week.”.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “He spoke confident about the success of the policy.”?
o: He spoke confident about the success of the policy.
He spoke confidently about the success of the policy.
He spoke confidently about success of the policy.
He spoke confidently about the success of the policy not.
questions.e: He spoke confidently about the success of the policy. (Adverb modifies spoke.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The committee have postponed their decision until next week.”?
o: The committee have postponed their decision until next week.
The committee has not postponed its decision until next week.
The committee have postponed its decision until next week.
The committee has postponed its decision until next week.
questions.e: The committee has postponed its decision until next week. (Collective noun = singular.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Every officer and every clerk were required to attend.”?
o: Every officer and every clerk were required to attend.
Every officer and every clerk was required to attend.
Every officer and every clerk was required to attend without.
Every officer and every clerk was not required to attend.
questions.e: Every officer and every clerk was required to attend. (Every … and every takes a singular verb.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The data clearly shows that literacy have improved.”?
o: The data clearly shows that literacy have improved.
The data clearly shows that literacy has not improved.
The data clearly shows that literacy has improved without.
The data clearly shows that literacy has improved.
questions.e: The data clearly shows that literacy has improved. (Literacy is singular.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Each of the provinces have its own assembly.”?
o: Each of the provinces have its own assembly.
Each of the provinces has its own assembly.
Each of the provinces has its own assembly without.
Each of the provinces has not its own assembly.
questions.e: Each of the provinces has its own assembly. (Each is singular.)

questions.q: Which sentence uses the present perfect correctly?
o: The commission has met three times yesterday.
The commission has met three times in 2019.
The commission has met three times last month.
The commission has met three times this month.
questions.e: This month is an unfinished period, so the present perfect fits.

questions.q: Which Tense is associated with Active Formula “Subject + is/am/are + V1+ing + Object” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 224: Tense “Present Continuous” corresponds to Active Formula “Subject + is/am/are + V1+ing + Object”.

questions.q: Which Tense is associated with Structure “subject + base verb (s/es for third-person singular)” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 244: Tense “Present Simple” corresponds to Structure “subject + base verb (s/es for third-person singular)”.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Neither the report nor the minutes was circulated.”?
o: Neither the report nor the minutes was circulated.
questions.e: ...nor the minutes were circulated. (Agreement with nearer subject Day 4.)

questions.q: The new duty had a significant effect ____ import volumes.
questions.e: Effect on is the fixed partnership; affect is the verb.

questions.q: Which Tense is associated with Example “She was writing at noon.” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 244: Tense “Past Continuous” corresponds to Example “She was writing at noon.”.

questions.q: Which Type is associated with Definition “Joins dependent clause” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 231: Type “Subordinating Conjunction” corresponds to Definition “Joins dependent clause”.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “He is the officer who we recommended for the post.”?
o: He are the officer whom we recommended for the post.
He is not the officer whom we recommended for the post.
He is the officer who we recommended for the post.
He is the officer whom we recommended for the post.
questions.e: We recommended him, so the object form whom is required.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The govt didn’t do much about it. (Fix the register.)”?
o: government took little action on it.
The government took little action on it not.
The govt didn’t do much about it. (Fix the register.)
The government took little action on it.
questions.e: The government took little action on it. (Register Day 24.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The teacher told the student that he had made a mistake.”?
o: The teacher told the student that the student had made an mistake.
The teacher told the student that the student had made a mistake.
The teacher told the student that he had made a mistake.
The teacher told the student that the student had not made a mistake.
questions.e: He could refer to either person; repetition removes the ambiguity.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Due to the fact that funds were short, the scheme was cancelled. (Tighten.)”?
o: Because funds were short, the scheme were cancelled.
Because funds were short, the scheme was cancelled.
Due to the fact that funds were short, the scheme was cancelled. (Tighten.)
Because funds were not short, the scheme was cancelled.
questions.e: Because funds were short, the scheme was cancelled. (Concision Day 25.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The quality of the roads in the northern districts have deteriorated sharply.”?
o: The quality of the roads in the northern districts has deteriorated sharply.
The quality of the roads in the northern districts have deteriorated sharply.
The quality of the roads in the northern districts has not deteriorated sharply.
The quality of the roads in the northern districts has deteriorated sharply without.
questions.e: Head noun quality is singular; the two prepositional phrases are irrelevant to agreement.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Having considered all the evidence and heard both parties at length.”?
o: Having considered all the evidence and heard both parties at length, the tribunal reserved its judgement not.
Having considered all the evidence and heard both parties at length.
Having considered all the evidence and heard both parties at length, the tribunal reserved its judgement.
Having considered all evidence and heard both parties at length, the tribunal reserved its judgement.
questions.e: A participle phrase is not a sentence; attach a main clause.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Neither of the two proposals were acceptable to the board.”?
o: Neither of the two proposals was not acceptable to the board.
Neither of the two proposals were acceptable to the board.
Neither of the two proposals was acceptable to the board.
Neither of the two proposals was acceptable to the board without.
questions.e: Neither is singular even when followed by a plural noun.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “There is several reasons why the scheme did not attract applicants.”?
o: There are several reasons why the scheme did not attract applicants.
There is several reasons why the scheme did not attract applicants.
There are not several reasons why the scheme did not attract applicants.
There are several reasons why the scheme did not attract applicants without.
questions.e: The subject is reasons, which comes after the verb.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “By the time aid arrived, thousands already died.”?
o: By the time aid arrived, thousands had already died.
By time aid arrived, thousands had already died.
By the time aid arrived, thousands had not already died.
By the time aid arrived, thousands already died.
questions.e: By the time aid arrived, thousands had already died. (Sequence earlier past takes past perfect.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Which explains why the scheme collapsed.”?
o: This history explains why the scheme collapsed.
Which explains why the scheme collapsed.
This history explains why the scheme collapsed not.
history explains why the scheme collapsed.
questions.e: A relative clause standing alone is a fragment; give it a subject and a finite verb.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Neither the minister nor his aides was present at the briefing.”?
o: Neither the minister nor his aides was present at the briefing.
questions.e: ...nor his aides were present. (Agreement: verb agrees with the nearer subject, aides.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “He is one of those leaders who always keeps his word.”?
o: ...who always keeps his word > keep his word not.
He is one of those leaders who always keeps his word.
...who always keeps his word > keep his word.
...who always keeps his word > keep his word without.
questions.e: ...who always keeps his word > keep his word. (Agreement: the verb agrees with leaders.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The committee have submitted their report yesterday.”?
o: The committee submitted their report yesterday not.
The committee submitted their report yesterday.
The committee have submitted their report yesterday.
questions.e: The committee submitted their report yesterday. (Tense: yesterday needs the simple past, not present perfect.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The policy was ambitious, the budget was inadequate, the result was failure.”?
o: The policy was ambitious, the budget was inadequate, the result was failure.
The policy was ambitious, the budget was inadequate, and the result was failure.
The policy were ambitious, the budget was inadequate, and the result was failure.
The policy was not ambitious, the budget was inadequate, and the result was failure.
questions.e: The policy was ambitious, the budget was inadequate, and the result was failure. (Series of clauses needs a conjunction before the last item.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Combine: The subsidy ended. Prices rose sharply.”?
o: Combine: The subsidy ended. Prices rose sharply.
When the subsidy ended, prices rose sharply.
When subsidy ended, prices rose sharply.
When the subsidy ended, prices rose sharply not.
questions.e: When the subsidy ended, prices rose sharply. (Complex sentence; adverb clause of time.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Because the judiciary acted independently, public confidence increased.”?
o: Correct as written complex sentence, adverb clause of reason first, comma after it not.
Correct as written complex sentence, adverb clause of reason first, comma after it without.
Correct as written complex sentence, adverb clause of reason first, comma after it.
Because the judiciary acted independently, public confidence increased.
questions.e: Correct as written complex sentence, adverb clause of reason first, comma after it.

questions.q: District-office worksheet — 79 passengers paid Rs 5960. An adult ticket cost Rs 80 and a child ticket Rs 60. How many adults travelled?
questions.e: If a is the adult count, 80a + 60(79 − a) = 5960, which gives a = 61.

questions.q: Health-programme report — 85 passengers paid Rs 6600. An adult ticket cost Rs 80 and a child ticket Rs 60. How many adults travelled?
questions.e: If a is the adult count, 80a + 60(85 − a) = 6600, which gives a = 75.

questions.q: Health-programme report — A bag holds 34 red and 7 blue counters. Two are drawn without replacement. What is the probability that both are red?
questions.e: Multiply the changing probabilities: 34/41 × 33/40 = 68.41%.

questions.q: Transport-depot calculation — A bag holds 33 red and 6 blue counters. Two are drawn without replacement. What is the probability that both are red?
questions.e: Multiply the changing probabilities: 33/39 × 32/38 = 71.26%.

questions.q: Training-centre exercise — A 73 m by 21 m rectangular courtyard has a uniform path 3 m wide inside its boundary. What area does the path cover?
questions.e: Path area = outer area − inner area = 1533 − 67×15 = 528 m².

questions.q: Scholarship-fund audit — The roots of x² − 127x + 4026 = 0 differ by 5. What is the larger root?
questions.e: The quadratic factors as (x − 61)(x − 66); the larger root is 66.

questions.q: Survey-unit review — A 72 m by 20 m rectangular courtyard has a uniform path 2 m wide inside its boundary. What area does the path cover?
questions.e: Path area = outer area − inner area = 1440 − 68×16 = 352 m².

questions.q: Warehouse planning case — The roots of x² − 130x + 4216 = 0 differ by 6. What is the larger root?
questions.e: The quadratic factors as (x − 62)(x − 68); the larger root is 68.

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — A geometric sequence has first term 66 and common ratio 3. What is its 5th term?
District-office worksheet — The mean of 12 observations in a report is 39. One entry, 29, is corrected to 53. What is the corrected mean?
questions.e: The total rises by 24; divided across 12 observations, the mean rises by 2 to 41.

questions.q: Health-programme report — A geometric sequence has first term 17 and common ratio 2. What is its 8th term?
Relief-camp planning case — The mean of 20 observations in a report is 38. One entry, 28, is corrected to 68. What is the corrected mean?
questions.e: The total rises by 40; divided across 20 observations, the mean rises by 2 to 40.

questions.q: Survey-unit review — A invests Rs 16000 for 8 months and B invests Rs 10000 for 9 months. If their profit is Rs 2180, what is A's share?
questions.e: Profit follows capital-months. The weights are 128000:90000; A therefore receives Rs 1280.

questions.q: Training-centre exercise — A invests Rs 17000 for 9 months and B invests Rs 11000 for 10 months. If their profit is Rs 2630, what is A's share?
questions.e: Profit follows capital-months. The weights are 153000:110000; A therefore receives Rs 1530.

questions.q: Scholarship-fund audit — A vehicle covers two equal-distance legs at 120 km/h and 134 km/h. What is its average speed for the complete journey?
questions.e: For equal distances the harmonic mean applies: 2uv/(u + v) = 126.61 km/h.

questions.q: Warehouse planning case — A vehicle covers two equal-distance legs at 122 km/h and 138 km/h. What is its average speed for the complete journey?
questions.e: For equal distances the harmonic mean applies: 2uv/(u + v) = 129.51 km/h.

questions.q: Transport-depot calculation — A two-digit number has digit sum 7; reversing its digits increases it by 27. What is the original number?
questions.e: Let the tens and units digits be x and y. Then x + y = 7 and 9(x − y) = -27; hence x = 2, y = 5.

questions.q: Health-programme report — A two-digit number has digit sum 8; reversing its digits increases it by 36. What is the original number?
questions.e: Let the tens and units digits be x and y. Then x + y = 8 and 9(x − y) = -36; hence x = 2, y = 6.

questions.q: Health-programme report — For two years at 20% per annum, by how much does compound interest exceed simple interest on Rs 90000?
Transport-depot calculation — For two years at 15% per annum, by how much does compound interest exceed simple interest on Rs 80000?
Survey-unit review — An investment grows to Rs 30008 in two years at 10% compound interest per year. What was the principal?
Transport-depot calculation — An investment grows to Rs 10000 in two years at 25% compound interest per year. What was the principal?
Scholarship-fund audit — On a coordinate grid, point Q lies 152 units east and 285 units north of point P. What is the straight-line distance PQ?
Warehouse planning case — On a coordinate grid, point Q lies 140 units east and 480 units north of point P. What is the straight-line distance PQ?
Warehouse planning case — An arithmetic sequence begins 48, 51, 54, … . What is the sum of its first 13 terms?
Scholarship-fund audit — An arithmetic sequence begins 47, 49, 51, … . What is the sum of its first 12 terms?
Warehouse planning case — A train 550 m long clears a 150 m platform in 20 seconds. What is its speed in km/h?
questions.e: The train covers 700 m. Its speed is (700)/20 m/s × 3.6 = 126 km/h.

questions.q: Scholarship-fund audit — A train 540 m long clears a 140 m platform in 19 seconds. What is its speed in km/h?
questions.e: The train covers 680 m. Its speed is (680)/19 m/s × 3.6 = 128.84 km/h.

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — Worker B takes 23 days for a task. Worker A is 20% more efficient than B. How many days would A need for the same task?
questions.e: Time varies inversely with efficiency, so A's time is 23 × 100/120 = 19.17 days.

questions.q: District-office worksheet — Worker B takes 24 days for a task. Worker A is 25% more efficient than B. How many days would A need for the same task?
questions.e: Time varies inversely with efficiency, so A's time is 24 × 100/125 = 19.2 days.

questions.q: Survey-unit review — Two runners start together in opposite directions on a 1500 m circular track at 375 m/s and 250 m/s. After how many seconds do they first meet?
questions.e: In opposite directions their relative speed is 625 m/s, so time is 1500 ÷ 625 = 2.4 seconds.

questions.q: Training-centre exercise — Two runners start together in opposite directions on a 1520 m circular track at 304 m/s and 217.14 m/s. After how many seconds do they first meet?
questions.e: In opposite directions their relative speed is 521.14 m/s, so time is 1520 ÷ 521.14 = 2.92 seconds.

questions.q: Training-centre exercise — Two pipes can fill a tank in 648 and 972 minutes, while a leak can empty it in 1944 minutes. If all three remain open, when will the tank fill?
questions.e: Net rate = 1/648 + 1/972 − 1/1944 = 1/486, so the tank fills in 486 minutes.

کل: 51 ایسے حروف جن کے ساتھ "ال" لگانے پر "ل" واضح پڑھی جاتی ہے
متحرک: جس حرف پر حرکت (زبر، زیر، پیش) ہو۔ساکن: جس پر کوئی حرکت نہ ہو بلکہ جزم ہو۔
وہ حروف جن پر کوئی نقطہ نہیں 52 ہوتا۔ کل
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 213: حرو فِ مهملہ — وہ حروف جن پر کوئی نقطہ نہیں 52 ہوتا۔ کل

questions.q: “اسمِ فاعل” کی درست تعریف منتخب کریں۔
o: جو کسی کام کا نشانہ بننے والے پر دلالت کرے
جو کسی گروہ یا مجموعے پر دلالت کرے
جو کسی معاوضے، اجرت یا مزدوری کے لیے استعمال ہو
جو کسی کام کو کرنے والے پر دلالت کرے (مصدر سے بنا ہو)
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 208: اسمِ فاعل — جو کسی کام کو کرنے والے پر دلالت کرے (مصدر سے بنا ہو)

questions.q: یہ تعریف کس اصطلاح کی ہے؟ “جو کسی گروہ یا مجموعے پر دلالت کرے”
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 209: اسمِ جمع — جو کسی گروہ یا مجموعے پر دلالت کرے

questions.q: یہ تعریف کس اصطلاح کی ہے؟ “وہ مسدر جس کا فعل فاعل اور مفعول دونوں کو چاہیے، یعنی اس کا اثر دوسرے پر بھی پڑتا ہے۔”
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 210: متعدی — وہ مسدر جس کا فعل فاعل اور مفعول دونوں کو چاہیے، یعنی اس کا اثر دوسرے پر بھی پڑتا ہے۔

questions.q: یہ تعریف کس اصطلاح کی ہے؟ “جو کافی پہلے ہو چکا ہو۔”
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 211: ماضی بعید — جو کافی پہلے ہو چکا ہو۔

questions.q: یہ تعریف کس اصطلاح کی ہے؟ “جو سوال یا بات کے جواب میں استعمال ہو۔”
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 212: حرفِ جواب — جو سوال یا بات کے جواب میں استعمال ہو۔

questions.q:
Read the passage: “Farmers in one area planted a drought-tolerant crop after a dry season. It yielded less during a wet trial year but prevented serious losses when rainfall was poor. The advisory service discussed risk across several years rather than a single season’s yield.”

What is the implied trade-off?
o: Potential maximum yield against protection from drought losses
questions.e: The crop may yield less in wet conditions but reduce losses in dry ones.

questions.q:
Read the passage: “Farmers in one area planted a drought-tolerant crop after a dry season. It yielded less during a wet trial year but prevented serious losses when rainfall was poor. The advisory service discussed risk across several years rather than a single season’s yield.”

Why consider several years?
o: The crop’s advantage appears under particular weather conditions
A single yield reveals every future result
The trial year had no harvest
questions.e: Performance differs across wet and dry years.

questions.s: Verb Tense System and Sequence of Tenses
questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The minister announces the budget last week.”?
o: minister announced the budget last week.
The minister announced the budget last week.
The minister announces the budget last week.
The minister announced the budget last week not.
questions.e: The minister announced the budget last week. (Finished past time marker → simple past.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Although Pakistan has abundant resources.”?
o: Although Pakistan have abundant resources, it struggles to convert them into growth.
Although Pakistan has abundant resources, it struggles to convert them into growth.
Although Pakistan has not abundant resources, it struggles to convert them into growth.
questions.e: Although Pakistan has abundant resources, it struggles to convert them into growth. (Fragment completed with an independent clause.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The reform passed easily, it was never implemented.”?
o: The reform passed easily, but it were never implemented.
The reform passed easily, but it was not never implemented.
The reform passed easily, it was never implemented.
The reform passed easily, but it was never implemented.
questions.e: The reform passed easily, but it was never implemented. (Comma splice fixed with a conjunction.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “A new policy has introduced by the ministry last month.”?
o: A new policy was not introduced by the ministry last month.
A new policy were introduced by the ministry last month.
A new policy was introduced by the ministry last month.
A new policy has introduced by the ministry last month.
questions.e: The policy did not introduce anything, so the passive is right; last month is a finished time, so the tense is the past simple.

questions.q: Which Type is associated with Sentence Example “This is my car.” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 230: Type “Possessive Adjective” corresponds to Sentence Example “This is my car.”.

questions.q: Which Preposition is associated with Rule “Movement of clock/time” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 232: Preposition “Forward / Back” corresponds to Rule “Movement of clock/time”.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “I got attested my documents and then I submitted them.”?
o: I had not my documents attested and then submitted them.
I had my documents attested and then submitted them without.
I had my documents attested and then submitted them.
I got attested my documents and then I submitted them.
questions.e: Causative word order is have/get + object + past participle.

questions.q: Which Direct Speech is associated with Indirect Speech “That” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 227: Direct Speech “This” corresponds to Indirect Speech “That”.

questions.q: Which paragraph opening is a true topic sentence?
o: There are many problems with enforcement.
Enforcement, not legislation, is the binding constraint.
In 2019, the smog emergency was declared.
questions.e: It states one arguable claim the paragraph can support.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The proposal is being consider by the finance division at present.”?
o: The proposal is being considered by the finance division at present.
The proposal are being considered by the finance division at present.
The proposal is not being considered by the finance division at present.
The proposal is being consider by the finance division at present.
questions.e: Every passive ends in a past participle.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “It was said by the spokesperson that the inquiry will be completed by June.”?
o: The spokesperson said that the inquiry would not be completed by June.
spokesperson said that the inquiry would be completed by June.
The spokesperson said that the inquiry would be completed by June.
It was said by the spokesperson that the inquiry will be completed by June.
questions.e: The agent is known and relevant, so the active is better; the reported clause backshifts to would.

questions.q: Which sentence uses ellipsis correctly for concision?
o: The first proposal was costly; the second, less so.
The first proposal was costly; the second proposal was less costly than the first proposal.
The first proposal was costly, the second was costly less.
The first proposal costly; second less.
questions.e: The repeated words are understood and need not be written.

questions.q: Which is the weaker use of a connector?
o: The funds lapsed, so the work stopped.
Because the funds lapsed, the work stopped.
The funds lapsed. The work therefore stopped.
The funds lapsed. Moreover, the work stopped.
questions.e: Moreover claims addition where the real relationship is cause and effect.

questions.q: Which Preposition is associated with Rule “Shows indulgence or involvement in something” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 231: Preposition “With” corresponds to Rule “Shows indulgence or involvement in something”.

questions.q: Which Type is associated with Example Word “always” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 230: Type “Adverb of Frequency” corresponds to Example Word “always”.

questions.q: Which Type is associated with Sentence Example “That house is mine.” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 230: Type “Demonstrative Adjective” corresponds to Sentence Example “That house is mine.”.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The report, along with its annexes, were tabled in the house.”?
o: The report, along with its annexes, were tabled.
The report, along with its annexes, was not tabled.
The report, along with its annexes, were tabled in the house.
The report, along with its annexes, was tabled.
questions.e: The report, along with its annexes, was tabled. (Agreement: the subject is report, singular.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The cabinet comprised of fifteen ministers.”?
o: The cabinet comprised of fifteen ministers.
The cabinet comprised fifteen ministers not.
questions.e: The cabinet comprised fifteen ministers. (comprise, never comprised of.)

questions.q: Which Type is associated with Example Word “chair” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 229: Type “Concrete Noun” corresponds to Example Word “chair”.

questions.q: Which Structure is associated with Tense “Past Perfect” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 244: Structure “subject + had + past participle” corresponds to Tense “Past Perfect”.

questions.q: Which Preposition is associated with Rule “Location beneath something natural” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 231: Preposition “Under” corresponds to Rule “Location beneath something natural”.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The crisis resulted into mass unemployment.”?
o: The crisis resulted into mass unemployment.
The crisis resulted in mass unemployment not.
The crisis resulted in mass unemployment.
questions.e: The crisis resulted in mass unemployment. (result in.)

questions.q: Which Type is associated with Definition “Describes when action happens” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 230: Type “Adverb of Time” corresponds to Definition “Describes when action happens”.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The report consists in three chapters.”?
o: The report consists in three chapters.
The report consists of three chapters.
The report consists of three chapters not.
questions.e: The report consists of three chapters. (consist of is fixed.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Economic growth depends from political stability.”?
o: Economic growth depends from political stability.
Economic growth depends on political stability.
Economic growth depends on political stability without.
Economic growth depends on political stability not.
questions.e: Economic growth depends on political stability. (depend on.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The government must comply to international law.”?
o: The government must comply to international law.
The government must not comply with international law.
government must comply with international law.
The government must comply with international law.
questions.e: The government must comply with international law. (comply with.)

questions.q: Which Rule is associated with Preposition “In” in the English reference?
o: Shows relation like enmity, alliance, coordination
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 231: Rule “Location inside a corner” corresponds to Preposition “In”.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “She is capable to lead the team.”?
o: She is capable to lead the team.
She is capable of leading the team.
She are capable of leading the team.
She is not capable of leading the team.
questions.e: She is capable of leading the team. (capable of + gerund.)

questions.q: Which Type is associated with Example Word “and, but” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 231: Type “Coordinating Conjunction” corresponds to Example Word “and, but”.

questions.q: Which Indirect Speech is associated with Direct Speech “Present Perfect Continuous” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 226: Indirect Speech “Past Perfect Continuous” corresponds to Direct Speech “Present Perfect Continuous”.

questions.q: Which Rule is associated with Example Sentence “President Lincoln abolished slavery. Doctor Ali is on leave today.” in the English reference?
o: No article before titles (when used with names)
No article before cities and countries (general rule)
No article before abstract nouns (general idea)
No article before common diseases (except a few)
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 225: Rule “No article before titles (when used with names)” corresponds to Example Sentence “President Lincoln abolished slavery. Doctor Ali is on leave today.”.

questions.q: Which Direct Speech is associated with Indirect Speech “She requested not to disturb her.” in the English reference?
o: He said, "The sun rises in the east."
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 228: Direct Speech “She said, "Don't disturb me."” corresponds to Indirect Speech “She requested not to disturb her.”.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “I have completed my graduation in 2019 and I am preparing for CSS since then.”?
o: I have completed my graduation in 2019 and I am preparing for CSS since then.
I completed my graduation in 2019 and have not been preparing for CSS since then.
I completed my graduation in 2019 and has been preparing for CSS since then.
I completed my graduation in 2019 and have been preparing for CSS since then.
questions.e: A dated event takes the past simple; since then with a continuing activity takes the present perfect continuous.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “When the auditors reached the office, the staff already destroyed the records.”?
o: When auditors reached the office, the staff had already destroyed the records.
When the auditors reached the office, the staff had not already destroyed the records.
When the auditors reached the office, the staff already destroyed the records.
When the auditors reached the office, the staff had already destroyed the records.
questions.e: The destruction came first, so it takes the past perfect.

questions.q: Which Direct Speech is associated with Rule “He said, "I went to Lahore." → He said that he had gone to Lahore.” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 226: Direct Speech “Past Indefinite” corresponds to Rule “He said, "I went to Lahore." → He said that he had gone to Lahore.”.

questions.q: Which Indirect Speech is associated with Direct Speech “He says, "I like tea."” in the English reference?
o: He says that he likes tea.
He will say that he is ready.
He said that the sun rises in the east.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 226: Indirect Speech “He says that he likes tea.” corresponds to Direct Speech “He says, "I like tea."”.

questions.q: Which Rule is associated with Example Sentence “Man is mortal. Woman has always played a vital role.” in the English reference?
o: No article before hell, heaven, or God (used reverently)
Exception: article the is used with "devil"
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 225: Rule “No article before man/woman (used generally)” corresponds to Example Sentence “Man is mortal. Woman has always played a vital role.”.

questions.s: Modifiers: put the describing words where they belong
questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “She nearly drove her children to school every day.”?
o: She drove her children to school nearly every day.
She nearly drove her children to school every day.
She drove her children to school nearly every day not.
She drove her children than school nearly every day.
questions.e: Nearly describes the frequency, not the driving.

questions.q: Which Rule is associated with Example Sentence “He visited the United States. She works in the Netherlands.” in the English reference?
o: Use the with provinces, mountain ranges, rivers, oceans
Use the with countries having "States", "Kingdom", or plurals
Use the when speaking of a known person or thing
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 225: Rule “Use the with countries having "States", "Kingdom", or plurals” corresponds to Example Sentence “He visited the United States. She works in the Netherlands.”.

questions.q: The candidate worked ____ throughout the year but ____ took a day of leave.
questions.e: Hard means with effort; hardly means almost not. The sentence needs one of each, in that order.

questions.q: Which sentence is correct?
questions.e: Appear is a linking verb, so the adjective convincing follows it.

questions.q: Which sentence uses well correctly?
o: She performed well in the interview.
She performed good in the interview.
She performed a good in the interview.
She performed goodly in the interview.
questions.e: Performed is an action verb, so it needs the adverb well, not the adjective good.

questions.q: The policy was ____ criticised by independent economists.
questions.e: The word describes the participle criticised, so an adverb is required.

questions.q: Which Preposition is associated with Rule “Movement by foot” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 233: Preposition “On” corresponds to Rule “Movement by foot”.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The course teaches reading, writing, and how to speak well.”?
o: The course teaches reading, writing, and speaking.
course teaches reading, writing, and speaking.
The course teaches reading, writing, and speaking not.
The course teaches reading, writing, and how to speak well.
questions.e: The course teaches reading, writing, and speaking. (Three gerunds.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The number of accidents have increased.”?
o: The number of accidents has increased without.
The number of accidents has not increased.
The number of accidents have increased.
The number of accidents has increased.
questions.e: The number of means one figure and is singular; a number of means many and is plural.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “He is one of those officers who never admits a mistake.”?
o: He is one of those officers who never admits a mistake.
He is not one of those officers who never admit a mistake.
He are one of those officers who never admit a mistake.
He is one of those officers who never admit a mistake.
questions.e: Who stands for officers, so the verb is plural.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Mathematics are a difficult subject for many candidates.”?
o: Mathematics is a difficult subject for many candidates without.
Mathematics is not a difficult subject for many candidates.
Mathematics are a difficult subject for many candidates.
Mathematics is a difficult subject for many candidates.
questions.e: As the name of a discipline, mathematics is singular.

questions.q: Health-programme report — A train 670 m long clears a 90 m platform in 10 seconds. What is its speed in km/h?
questions.e: The train covers 760 m. Its speed is (760)/10 m/s × 3.6 = 273.6 km/h.

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — On a coordinate grid, point Q lies 99 units east and 132 units north of point P. What is the straight-line distance PQ?
Transport-depot calculation — A train 660 m long clears a 80 m platform in 20 seconds. What is its speed in km/h?
questions.e: The train covers 740 m. Its speed is (740)/20 m/s × 3.6 = 133.2 km/h.

questions.q: Health-programme report — On a coordinate grid, point Q lies 224 units east and 768 units north of point P. What is the straight-line distance PQ?
Survey-unit review — For two years at 10% per annum, by how much does compound interest exceed simple interest on Rs 220000?
Training-centre exercise — For two years at 12% per annum, by how much does compound interest exceed simple interest on Rs 230000?
Survey-unit review — An investment grows to Rs 2904 in two years at 10% compound interest per year. What was the principal?
Training-centre exercise — An investment grows to Rs 4032 in two years at 20% compound interest per year. What was the principal?
Transport-depot calculation — A bag holds 41 red and 7 blue counters. Two are drawn without replacement. What is the probability that both are red?
questions.e: Multiply the changing probabilities: 41/48 × 40/47 = 72.7%.

questions.q: Survey-unit review — The roots of x² − 128x + 4095 = 0 differ by 2. What is the larger root?
questions.e: The quadratic factors as (x − 63)(x − 65); the larger root is 65.

questions.q: Health-programme report — A bag holds 42 red and 8 blue counters. Two are drawn without replacement. What is the probability that both are red?
questions.e: Multiply the changing probabilities: 42/50 × 41/49 = 70.29%.

questions.q: Training-centre exercise — The roots of x² − 131x + 4288 = 0 differ by 3. What is the larger root?
questions.e: The quadratic factors as (x − 64)(x − 67); the larger root is 67.

questions.q: Scholarship-fund audit — A 22 m by 14 m rectangular courtyard has a uniform path 4 m wide inside its boundary. What area does the path cover?
questions.e: Path area = outer area − inner area = 308 − 14×6 = 224 m².

questions.q: Health-programme report — A 27 m by 19 m rectangular courtyard has a uniform path 5 m wide inside its boundary. What area does the path cover?
questions.e: Path area = outer area − inner area = 513 − 17×9 = 360 m².

questions.q: Health-programme report — A two-digit number has digit sum 7; reversing its digits reduces it by 9. What is the original number?
questions.e: Let the tens and units digits be x and y. Then x + y = 7 and 9(x − y) = 9; hence x = 4, y = 3.

questions.q: Transport-depot calculation — A two-digit number has digit sum 6; reversing its digits reduces it by 18. What is the original number?
questions.e: Let the tens and units digits be x and y. Then x + y = 6 and 9(x − y) = 18; hence x = 4, y = 2.

questions.q: Training-centre exercise — A geometric sequence has first term 23 and common ratio 2. What is its 6th term?
Survey-unit review — A geometric sequence has first term 22 and common ratio 4. What is its 5th term?
Transport-depot calculation — 94 passengers paid Rs 6650. An adult ticket cost Rs 75 and a child ticket Rs 55. How many adults travelled?
questions.e: If a is the adult count, 75a + 55(94 − a) = 6650, which gives a = 74.

questions.q: Training-centre exercise — An arithmetic sequence begins 58, 64, 70, … . What is the sum of its first 15 terms?
Relief-camp planning case — 87 passengers paid Rs 4130. An adult ticket cost Rs 50 and a child ticket Rs 30. How many adults travelled?
questions.e: If a is the adult count, 50a + 30(87 − a) = 4130, which gives a = 76.

questions.q: Survey-unit review — An arithmetic sequence begins 57, 62, 67, … . What is the sum of its first 14 terms?
Transport-depot calculation — A invests Rs 34000 for 6 months and B invests Rs 7000 for 6 months. If their profit is Rs 2460, what is A's share?
questions.e: Profit follows capital-months. The weights are 204000:42000; A therefore receives Rs 2040.

questions.q: Survey-unit review — A invests Rs 48000 for 10 months and B invests Rs 7000 for 6 months. If their profit is Rs 5220, what is A's share?
questions.e: Profit follows capital-months. The weights are 480000:42000; A therefore receives Rs 4800.

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — A vehicle covers two equal-distance legs at 116 km/h and 126 km/h. What is its average speed for the complete journey?
questions.e: For equal distances the harmonic mean applies: 2uv/(u + v) = 120.79 km/h.

questions.q: District-office worksheet — A vehicle covers two equal-distance legs at 118 km/h and 130 km/h. What is its average speed for the complete journey?
questions.e: For equal distances the harmonic mean applies: 2uv/(u + v) = 123.71 km/h.

questions.q: Transport-depot calculation — Worker B takes 45 days for a task. Worker A is 50% more efficient than B. How many days would A need for the same task?
questions.e: Time varies inversely with efficiency, so A's time is 45 × 100/150 = 30 days.

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — Worker B takes 47 days for a task. Worker A is 20% more efficient than B. How many days would A need for the same task?
questions.e: Time varies inversely with efficiency, so A's time is 47 × 100/120 = 39.17 days.

questions.q: Transport-depot calculation — The mean of 18 observations in a report is 36. One entry, 26, is corrected to 62. What is the corrected mean?
questions.e: The total rises by 36; divided across 18 observations, the mean rises by 2 to 38.

questions.q: Health-programme report — The mean of 19 observations in a report is 37. One entry, 27, is corrected to 65. What is the corrected mean?
questions.e: The total rises by 38; divided across 19 observations, the mean rises by 2 to 39.

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — Two pipes can fill a tank in 204 and 306 minutes, while a leak can empty it in 612 minutes. If all three remain open, when will the tank fill?
questions.e: Net rate = 1/204 + 1/306 − 1/612 = 1/153, so the tank fills in 153 minutes.

questions.q: Five candidates—Sana, Sara, Shahid, Sobia, Talha—are interviewed once each. Sana is before Sara; Sara is immediately before Shahid; Talha is after Sobia; and Sobia is after Shahid. Which order is possible?
questions.e: The fixed block is Sara–Shahid; Sana must precede it, and Shahid must be followed in order by Sobia and Talha.

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — a relief camp divides 608 files between teams A and B in the ratio 3:5. How many additional files must A receive for the new ratio A:B to become 6:5?
questions.e: The original shares are 228 and 380. To make A's share 456, it needs 456 − 228 = 228 more files.

questions.q: Five candidates—Fiza, Hania, Haris, Hassan, Hina—are interviewed once each. Fiza is before Hania; Hania is immediately before Haris; Hina is after Hassan; and Hassan is after Haris. Which order is possible?
questions.e: The fixed block is Hania–Haris; Fiza must precede it, and Haris must be followed in order by Hassan and Hina.

questions.q: Health-programme report — a health programme divides 266 files between teams A and B in the ratio 6:8. How many additional files must A receive for the new ratio A:B to become 12:8?
questions.e: The original shares are 114 and 152. To make A's share 228, it needs 228 − 114 = 114 more files.

questions.q: Transport-depot calculation — Two pipes can fill a tank in 180 and 270 minutes, while a leak can empty it in 540 minutes. If all three remain open, when will the tank fill?
questions.e: Net rate = 1/180 + 1/270 − 1/540 = 1/135, so the tank fills in 135 minutes.

questions.q: Transport-depot calculation — A quarterly table for a transport depot records 340, 190, and 120 completed cases in three months. What percentage of the three-month total was completed in the first month?
questions.e: The total is 650; the first-month share is 340/650 × 100 = 52.31%.

questions.q: Health-programme report — A quarterly table for a health programme records 350, 195, and 125 completed cases in three months. What percentage of the three-month total was completed in the first month?
questions.e: The total is 670; the first-month share is 350/670 × 100 = 52.24%.

questions.q: Health-programme report — Two triangles are similar. A side of 10 cm in the smaller corresponds to 50 cm in the larger. If another smaller side is 4 cm, what is its corresponding larger side?
questions.e: The scale factor is 50/10 = 5; therefore 4 × 5 = 20 cm.

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — Two triangles are similar. A side of 3 cm in the smaller corresponds to 9 cm in the larger. If another smaller side is 6 cm, what is its corresponding larger side?
questions.e: The scale factor is 9/3 = 3; therefore 6 × 3 = 18 cm.

questions.q: Training-centre exercise — A tank contains 120 litres of a 30% solution. 24 litres of the mixture are removed and replaced by water. What is the new concentration?
questions.e: Removing one-fifth of a uniform mixture removes one-fifth of its solute. The remaining concentration is 30% × 4/5 = 24%.

questions.q: Survey-unit review — A tank contains 110 litres of a 25% solution. 22 litres of the mixture are removed and replaced by water. What is the new concentration?
questions.e: Removing one-fifth of a uniform mixture removes one-fifth of its solute. The remaining concentration is 25% × 4/5 = 20%.

questions.q: District-office worksheet — A can complete a project in 408 days and B in 612 days. They work together for 204 days; B then leaves. How many days from the start will A take to finish the project?
questions.e: Together they complete 204 × (1/408 + 1/612) = 5/6. A needs another 68 days for the remaining 1/6, totalling 272.

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — A can complete a project in 396 days and B in 594 days. They work together for 198 days; B then leaves. How many days from the start will A take to finish the project?
questions.e: Together they complete 198 × (1/396 + 1/594) = 5/6. A needs another 66 days for the remaining 1/6, totalling 264.

questions.e: Required selling price is 42400 × 140/100. Since that is 70% of the marked price, divide it by 0.7.

questions.q: Health-programme report — Two runners start together in opposite directions on a 1560 m circular track at 222.86 m/s and 173.33 m/s. After how many seconds do they first meet?
questions.e: In opposite directions their relative speed is 396.19 m/s, so time is 1560 ÷ 396.19 = 3.94 seconds.

questions.q: Training-centre exercise — Two runners start together in opposite directions on a 400 m circular track at 100 m/s and 66.67 m/s. After how many seconds do they first meet?
questions.e: In opposite directions their relative speed is 166.67 m/s, so time is 400 ÷ 166.67 = 2.4 seconds.

questions.q: Health-programme report — A bus leaves a health programme at 69 km/h. 4 hours later, a car follows on the same route at 82 km/h. How long after the car starts will it catch the bus?
questions.e: The bus has a 276 km lead. Relative speed is 13 km/h, so catch-up time is 21.23 hours.

questions.q: Training-centre exercise — A bus leaves a training centre at 59 km/h. 2 hours later, a car follows on the same route at 74 km/h. How long after the car starts will it catch the bus?

questions.q: District-office worksheet — What is the least number greater than 1892 that leaves remainder 42 when divided by both 43 and 44, given that 43 and 44 are coprime?
questions.e: A common remainder means N − 42 is a multiple of lcm(43, 44) = 1892. The least eligible N is 1892 + 42 = 1934.

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — What is the least number greater than 1806 that leaves remainder 41 when divided by both 42 and 43, given that 42 and 43 are coprime?
questions.e: A common remainder means N − 41 is a multiple of lcm(42, 43) = 1806. The least eligible N is 1806 + 41 = 1847.

questions.q: District-office worksheet — In a survey, 53 chose only A, 22 only B, 16 only C, 7 chose A and B only, 4 A and C only, 2 B and C only, and 2 chose all three. How many chose at least one?
questions.e: The seven disjoint regions are added once: 53+22+16+7+4+2+2 = 106.
