o: فعل مضارع — وہ فعل جو ماضی میں مکمل ہو چکا ہو۔
فعل مستقبل — وہ فعل جو حال یا مستقبل دونوں پر دلالت کرے، اکثر شرطیہ یا عمومی جملوں میں آتا ہے۔
فعل ماضی — وہ فعل جو آئندہ میں انجام پائے گا۔
فعل حال — وہ فعل جو موجودہ وقت میں ہو رہا ہو۔
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 211: فعل حال — وہ فعل جو موجودہ وقت میں ہو رہا ہو۔

questions.q: ان اصطلاحات—مہمل، اسم، فعل، حرف—میں درست اصطلاح اور تعریف کا جوڑا منتخب کریں۔
o: مہمل — ایسا لفظ جس کا کوئی مطلب نہ ہو اور نہ جملے میں استعمال کیا جا سکے۔
اسم — وہ لفظ جو کسی کام یا حالت کو ظاہر کرے
فعل — وہ لفظ جو اکیلا مفہوم نہیں دیتا، بلکہ دوسرے الفاظ کو جوڑتا ہے
حرف — وہ لفظ جو کسی شخص، جگہ، چیز یا صفت کا نام ہو
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 208: مہمل — ایسا لفظ جس کا کوئی مطلب نہ ہو اور نہ جملے میں استعمال کیا جا سکے۔

questions.q: یہ تعریف کس اصطلاح کی ہے؟ “ایک بے معنی لفظ اور ایک بامعنی لفظ پر مشتمل۔”
o: مرک بِ بدل و مبدل منہ
مرک بِ عط فِ بیان و مبین
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 214: مرک بِ تابع و متبوع (مہمل) — ایک بے معنی لفظ اور ایک بامعنی لفظ پر مشتمل۔

questions.q: تعریف “وہ حرف جو کسی چیز کو باقیوں سے الگ کرے” اور مثال “سوائے، ما عدا، بجز” کس اصطلاح کو ظاہر کرتی ہیں؟
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 211: ۔ حرف استثنا — وہ حرف جو کسی چیز کو باقیوں سے الگ کرے

questions.q: یہ تعریف کس اصطلاح کی ہے؟ “وہ فعل جو ماضی میں مکمل ہو چکا ہو۔”
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 211: فعل ماضی — وہ فعل جو ماضی میں مکمل ہو چکا ہو۔

questions.q:
Read the passage: “A town translated its emergency notices into three languages. Translators agreed on most words, but one technical term had a meaning that varied by community. Officials tested draft notices with speakers from each area before printing them.”

Why test the notices with local speakers?
o: A literal translation might be misunderstood in some communities
The notices were to remain secret
No one could read the notices
questions.e: The term could convey different meanings in different communities.

questions.q:
Read the passage: “A town translated its emergency notices into three languages. Translators agreed on most words, but one technical term had a meaning that varied by community. Officials tested draft notices with speakers from each area before printing them.”

What principle does the testing illustrate?
o: Notices should use one language only
questions.e: The purpose is effective communication, not word-for-word conversion alone.

questions.q: Which Type is associated with Example (Active) “Kindly follow the rules.” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 224: Type “Advice (Kindly)” corresponds to Example (Active) “Kindly follow the rules.”.

questions.q: Which Type is associated with Example Word “quickly” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 230: Type “Adverb of Manner” corresponds to Example Word “quickly”.

questions.q: Which Direct Speech is associated with Indirect Speech “The Previous Day / The Day Before” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 227: Direct Speech “Yesterday” corresponds to Indirect Speech “The Previous Day / The Day Before”.

questions.q: Which Direct Speech is associated with Indirect Speech “Had to” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 227: Direct Speech “Must” corresponds to Indirect Speech “Had to”.

questions.q: Which Part of Speech is associated with Definition “Indicates quantity, possession, or position” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 229: Part of Speech “Determiners” corresponds to Definition “Indicates quantity, possession, or position”.

questions.q: Which Type is associated with Definition “Shows ability, possibility, or permission” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 230: Type “Modal Verb” corresponds to Definition “Shows ability, possibility, or permission”.

questions.q: Which Type is associated with Example Word “honesty” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 229: Type “Abstract Noun” corresponds to Example Word “honesty”.

questions.q: Which Type is associated with Definition “Refers to a group of people or things” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 229: Type “Collective Noun” corresponds to Definition “Refers to a group of people or things”.

questions.q: Which Indirect Speech is associated with Direct Speech “Will” in the English reference?
o: She asked if I liked chocolate.
He asked if I was coming.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 227: Indirect Speech “Would” corresponds to Direct Speech “Will”.

questions.q: Which Indirect Speech is associated with Direct Speech “Present Perfect” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 226: Indirect Speech “Past Perfect” corresponds to Direct Speech “Present Perfect”.

questions.q: Which group of words is a fragment?
o: The deadline, which passed last Monday, was final.
Since the deadline passed last Monday.
questions.e: Since makes the clause dependent, so it cannot stand alone.

questions.q: Which Rule is associated with Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) “He sat by the door, waiting for her.” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 231: Rule “Sitting beside something” corresponds to Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) “He sat by the door, waiting for her.”.

questions.q: Which Preposition is associated with Rule “Shows transformation or change of state” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 231: Preposition “Into” corresponds to Rule “Shows transformation or change of state”.

questions.q: Which Direct Speech is associated with Indirect Speech “Only” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 227: Direct Speech “Just” corresponds to Indirect Speech “Only”.

questions.q: Which possessive is correct for a report belonging jointly to Ali and Sara?
questions.e: Joint ownership marks only the last name.

questions.q: Which Type is associated with Example Word “to, into” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 231: Type “Preposition of Direction” corresponds to Example Word “to, into”.

questions.q: Which Preposition is associated with Rule “Comparison between dissimilar things” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 232: Preposition “To” corresponds to Rule “Comparison between dissimilar things”.

questions.q: Which Rule is associated with Preposition “To” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 232: Rule “Used for benefit or harm” corresponds to Preposition “To”.

questions.s: Capital letters, full stops and the everyday comma
questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Its important to note that the committee submitted it’s report late.”?
o: It’s important to note that the committee submitted its report late.
It’s important than note that the committee submitted its report late.
It’s important to note that the committee submitted its report late not.
Its important to note that the committee submitted it’s report late.
questions.e: It’s = it is; its = belonging to it. The sentence has them the wrong way round.

questions.s: Capital letters, full stops and the everyday comma
questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The Ministry issued three notification’s in one week.”?
o: The ministry issued three notifications in one week.
The Ministry issued three notification’s in one week.
The ministry issued three notifications in one week not.
ministry issued three notifications in one week.
questions.e: An apostrophe never forms a plural.

questions.q: Which is the minimum correction of “The quality of the answers were disappointing”?
o: The quality of the answers was disappointing.
The answers were disappointing in quality.
The answers disappointed in their quality.
questions.e: One verb form is at fault; nothing else moves.

questions.s: Capital letters, full stops and the everyday comma
questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “He asked me that where I was going?”?
o: He asked me that where I was going?
He asked me where I was not going.
He asked me where I were going.
He asked me where I was going.
questions.e: An indirect question drops that, keeps statement word order and ends with a full stop.

questions.q: Which sentence contains NO error?
o: The committee have announced its decision.
The committee has announced their decision.
The committee has announced its decision.
The committee have announced their decision.
questions.e: Singular verb and singular pronoun, consistently.

questions.q: Which is the minimum correction of “He suggested to postpone the meeting”?
o: He proposed that the meeting be postponed.
He wanted to postpone the meeting.
He said the meeting should be postponed.
questions.e: Only the form after suggested is wrong; one word changes.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Each of the officers have submitted a report.”?
o: Each of the officers have submitted a report.
Each of the officers has submitted a report.
Each of the officers has submitted a report without.
Each of the officers has not submitted a report.
questions.e: Each is always singular, whatever noun follows it.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Neither the teachers nor the principal were present.”?
o: Neither the teachers nor the principal was present without.
Neither the teachers nor the principal was present.
Neither the teachers nor the principal were present.
Neither the teachers nor the principal was not present.
questions.e: With neither … nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject, principal.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The list of the shortlisted candidates were displayed.”?
o: The list of the shortlisted candidates was displayed without.
The list of the shortlisted candidates was displayed.
The list of the shortlisted candidates were displayed.
The list of the shortlisted candidates was not displayed.
questions.e: The head noun is list, which is singular.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “This proposal is more better than the last one.”?
o: This proposal is more better than the last one.
This proposal is not better than the last one.
This proposal are better than the last one.
This proposal is better than the last one.
questions.e: This proposal is better than the last one. (Double comparative drop more.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The committee it submitted its report on time.”?
o: committee submitted its report on time.
The committee submitted its report on time not.
The committee it submitted its report on time.
The committee submitted its report on time.
questions.e: The committee submitted its report on time. (Redundant subject pronoun removed.)

questions.q: Which Example Sentence is associated with Rule “In the general sense of "any"” in the English reference?
o: I met Ahmed yesterday. Fatima is my sister.
Gold is a precious metal. Iron is used in construction.
President Lincoln abolished slavery. Doctor Ali is on leave today.
A servant must obey his master. Anyone can become a leader.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 225: Example Sentence “A servant must obey his master. Anyone can become a leader.” corresponds to Rule “In the general sense of "any"”.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The country is facing inflation from a long time.”?
o: The country have been facing inflation for a long time.
The country has not been facing inflation for a long time.
The country is facing inflation from a long time.
The country has been facing inflation for a long time.
questions.e: The country has been facing inflation for a long time. (for a duration + present perfect.)

questions.q: Which Tense is associated with Active Formula “Subject + will/shall + V1 + Object” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 224: Tense “Future Indefinite” corresponds to Active Formula “Subject + will/shall + V1 + Object”.

questions.q: Which Preposition is associated with Rule “Temporary or transit stop” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 233: Preposition “At” corresponds to Rule “Temporary or transit stop”.

questions.s: Modifiers: put the describing words where they belong
questions.q: Which sentence places the modifier correctly?
o: The department almost has released all the funds.
Almost the department has released all the funds.
The department has released almost all the funds.
The department has almost released all the funds.
questions.e: Almost limits the quantity, so it belongs beside all the funds.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The federation (comprises / is comprised of) four provinces.”?
o: The federation (comprises / is comprised of) four provinces.
The federation comprises four provinces not.
questions.e: The federation comprises four provinces. (comprise, never comprised of.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “This is the most cleanest water available in the region.”?
o: This is the cleanest water available in the region.
This are the cleanest water available in the region.
This is not the cleanest water available in the region.
This is the most cleanest water available in the region.
questions.e: This is the cleanest water available in the region. (Drop most before a superlative form.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Punjab’s population is larger than Sindh.”?
o: Punjab’s population is larger than Sindh’s / than that of Sindh.
Punjab’s population are larger than Sindh’s / than that of Sindh.
Punjab’s population is not larger than Sindh’s / than that of Sindh.
Punjab’s population is larger than Sindh.
questions.e: Punjab’s population is larger than Sindh’s / than that of Sindh. (Compare populations.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Of the two candidates, she is the most qualified.”?
o: Of the two candidates, she is the more qualified.
Of the two candidates, she is the most qualified.
Of the two candidates, she is not the more qualified.
Of the two candidates, she are the more qualified.
questions.e: Of the two candidates, she is the more qualified. (Two items comparative.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The judgement was a real surprising to the legal community.”?
o: The judgement was not a real surprise to the legal community.
The judgement was a real surprising to the legal community.
The judgement was a real surprise to the legal community.
The judgement were a real surprise to the legal community.
questions.e: The judgement was a real surprise to the legal community. (Use the noun surprise, not the adjective.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The reforms were implemented quick and without consultation.”?
o: The reforms were not implemented quickly and without consultation.
The reforms were implemented quick and without consultation.
The reforms were implemented quickly and without consultation.
The reforms was implemented quickly and without consultation.
questions.e: The reforms were implemented quickly and without consultation. (Adverb modifies the verb.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Neither of the proposals are practical in the current fiscal climate.”?
o: Neither of the proposals is practical in the current fiscal climate.
Neither of the proposals are practical in the current fiscal climate.
Neither of the proposals is not practical in the current fiscal climate.
Neither of the proposals is practical in the current fiscal climate without.
questions.e: Neither of the proposals is practical in the current fiscal climate. (Neither is singular.)

questions.s: Active Voice, Passive Voice, and Causatives
questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The police arrested twelve suspects. (Make passive and judge if useful.)”?
o: Twelve suspects was arrested by the police.
Twelve suspects were not arrested by the police.
The police arrested twelve suspects. (Make passive and judge if useful.)
Twelve suspects were arrested by the police.
questions.e: Twelve suspects were arrested by the police. (Useful only if the suspects are the focus; otherwise keep active.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “He was accused for corruption.”?
o: He was not accused of corruption.
questions.e: He was accused of corruption. (accused of.)

questions.s: Active Voice, Passive Voice, and Causatives
questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Reforms have been promised by every government since 1990. (Make active.)”?
o: Reforms have been promised by every government since 1990. (Make active.)
Every government since 1990 has not promised reforms.
Every government since 1990 have promised reforms.
Every government since 1990 has promised reforms.
questions.e: Every government since 1990 has promised reforms. (Active assigns clear responsibility.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “We must cut down on wasteful expenditure. (Make more formal.)”?
o: We must reduce wasteful expenditure without.
We must cut down on wasteful expenditure. (Make more formal.)
We must not reduce wasteful expenditure.
questions.e: We must reduce wasteful expenditure. (reduce is more formal.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The committee will look into the allegations. (Make more formal.)”?
o: The committee will investigate the allegations.
The committee will look into the allegations. (Make more formal.)
The committee will not investigate the allegations.
questions.e: The committee will investigate the allegations. (single formal verb.)

questions.s: Active Voice, Passive Voice, and Causatives
questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “It was decided by the government to raise taxes. (Improve.)”?
o: The government decided than raise taxes.
The government decided to raise taxes not.
It was decided by the government to raise taxes. (Improve.)
The government decided to raise taxes.
questions.e: The government decided to raise taxes. (Active is shorter and assigns responsibility.)

questions.s: Active Voice, Passive Voice, and Causatives
questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Mistakes in the audit were made by the junior staff. (Make active.)”?
o: Mistakes in the audit were made by the junior staff. (Make active.)
The junior staff made mistakes in the audit not.
junior staff made mistakes in the audit.
The junior staff made mistakes in the audit.
questions.e: The junior staff made mistakes in the audit. (Active names the actor directly.)

questions.q: Training-centre exercise — A invests Rs 9000 for 6 months and B invests Rs 10000 for 9 months. If their profit is Rs 1440, what is A's share?
questions.e: Profit follows capital-months. The weights are 54000:90000; A therefore receives Rs 540.

questions.q: Transport-depot calculation — An arithmetic sequence begins 51, 57, 63, … . What is the sum of its first 16 terms?
Scholarship-fund audit — A invests Rs 46000 for 8 months and B invests Rs 5000 for 4 months. If their profit is Rs 3880, what is A's share?
questions.e: Profit follows capital-months. The weights are 368000:20000; A therefore receives Rs 3680.

questions.q: Health-programme report — An arithmetic sequence begins 12, 14, 16, … . What is the sum of its first 17 terms?
Relief-camp planning case — A geometric sequence has first term 18 and common ratio 3. What is its 5th term?
Survey-unit review — A geometric sequence has first term 6 and common ratio 3. What is its 5th term?
Transport-depot calculation — A two-digit number has digit sum 6; reversing its digits reduces it by 54. What is the original number?
questions.e: Let the tens and units digits be x and y. Then x + y = 6 and 9(x − y) = 54; hence x = 6, y = 0.

questions.q: District-office worksheet — A train 450 m long clears a 140 m platform in 10 seconds. What is its speed in km/h?
questions.e: The train covers 590 m. Its speed is (590)/10 m/s × 3.6 = 212.4 km/h.

questions.q: Health-programme report — A two-digit number has digit sum 7; reversing its digits reduces it by 45. What is the original number?
questions.e: Let the tens and units digits be x and y. Then x + y = 7 and 9(x − y) = 45; hence x = 6, y = 1.

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — A train 440 m long clears a 130 m platform in 20 seconds. What is its speed in km/h?
questions.e: The train covers 570 m. Its speed is (570)/20 m/s × 3.6 = 102.6 km/h.

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — A 76 m by 13 m rectangular courtyard has a uniform path 2 m wide inside its boundary. What area does the path cover?
questions.e: Path area = outer area − inner area = 988 − 72×9 = 340 m².

questions.q: District-office worksheet — A 77 m by 14 m rectangular courtyard has a uniform path 3 m wide inside its boundary. What area does the path cover?
questions.e: Path area = outer area − inner area = 1078 − 71×8 = 510 m².

questions.q: District-office worksheet — A bag holds 52 red and 4 blue counters. Two are drawn without replacement. What is the probability that both are red?
questions.e: Multiply the changing probabilities: 52/56 × 51/55 = 86.1%.

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — A bag holds 51 red and 10 blue counters. Two are drawn without replacement. What is the probability that both are red?
questions.e: Multiply the changing probabilities: 51/61 × 50/60 = 69.67%.

questions.q: Scholarship-fund audit — On a coordinate grid, point Q lies 24 units east and 45 units north of point P. What is the straight-line distance PQ?
questions.e: PQ = √(24² + 45²) = 51 units.

questions.q: District-office worksheet — For two years at 12% per annum, by how much does compound interest exceed simple interest on Rs 30000?
Training-centre exercise — On a coordinate grid, point Q lies 70 units east and 168 units north of point P. What is the straight-line distance PQ?
Scholarship-fund audit — For two years at 15% per annum, by how much does compound interest exceed simple interest on Rs 40000?
Relief-camp planning case — 77 passengers paid Rs 5435. An adult ticket cost Rs 75 and a child ticket Rs 55. How many adults travelled?
questions.e: If a is the adult count, 75a + 55(77 − a) = 5435, which gives a = 60.

questions.q: Warehouse planning case — 83 passengers paid Rs 4165. An adult ticket cost Rs 55 and a child ticket Rs 35. How many adults travelled?
questions.e: If a is the adult count, 55a + 35(83 − a) = 4165, which gives a = 63.

questions.q: Transport-depot calculation — An investment grows to Rs 5000 in two years at 25% compound interest per year. What was the principal?
Health-programme report — An investment grows to Rs 8100 in two years at 50% compound interest per year. What was the principal?
Health-programme report — Worker B takes 78 days for a task. Worker A is 100% more efficient than B. How many days would A need for the same task?
questions.e: Time varies inversely with efficiency, so A's time is 78 × 100/200 = 39 days.

questions.q: Transport-depot calculation — Worker B takes 77 days for a task. Worker A is 50% more efficient than B. How many days would A need for the same task?
questions.e: Time varies inversely with efficiency, so A's time is 77 × 100/150 = 51.33 days.

questions.q: Scholarship-fund audit — The roots of x² − 94x + 2205 = 0 differ by 4. What is the larger root?
questions.e: The quadratic factors as (x − 45)(x − 49); the larger root is 49.

questions.q: Warehouse planning case — The roots of x² − 97x + 2346 = 0 differ by 5. What is the larger root?
questions.e: The quadratic factors as (x − 46)(x − 51); the larger root is 51.

questions.q: Survey-unit review — The mean of 18 observations in a report is 90. One entry, 80, is corrected to 116. What is the corrected mean?
questions.e: The total rises by 36; divided across 18 observations, the mean rises by 2 to 92.

questions.q: Training-centre exercise — The mean of 19 observations in a report is 91. One entry, 81, is corrected to 119. What is the corrected mean?
questions.e: The total rises by 38; divided across 19 observations, the mean rises by 2 to 93.

questions.q: District-office worksheet — A vehicle covers two equal-distance legs at 22 km/h and 34 km/h. What is its average speed for the complete journey?
questions.e: For equal distances the harmonic mean applies: 2uv/(u + v) = 26.71 km/h.

questions.q: Health-programme report — A vehicle covers two equal-distance legs at 50 km/h and 66 km/h. What is its average speed for the complete journey?
questions.e: For equal distances the harmonic mean applies: 2uv/(u + v) = 56.9 km/h.

questions.q: Transport-depot calculation — a transport depot divides 888 files between teams A and B in the ratio 5:7. How many additional files must A receive for the new ratio A:B to become 10:7?
questions.e: The original shares are 370 and 518. To make A's share 740, it needs 740 − 370 = 370 more files.

questions.q: Scholarship-fund audit — a scholarship fund divides 840 files between teams A and B in the ratio 5:7. How many additional files must A receive for the new ratio A:B to become 10:7?
questions.e: The original shares are 350 and 490. To make A's share 700, it needs 700 − 350 = 350 more files.

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — What is the least number greater than 1190 that leaves remainder 33 when divided by both 34 and 35, given that 34 and 35 are coprime?
questions.e: A common remainder means N − 33 is a multiple of lcm(34, 35) = 1190. The least eligible N is 1190 + 33 = 1223.

questions.q: District-office worksheet — After a 20% discount and then 10% sales tax, an equipment bill for a district office is Rs 44880. What was the listed price?
questions.e: If L is the list price, L × 80/100 × 110/100 = 44880, giving L = 51000.

questions.q: Health-programme report — Two pipes can fill a tank in 768 and 1152 minutes, while a leak can empty it in 2304 minutes. If all three remain open, when will the tank fill?
questions.e: Net rate = 1/768 + 1/1152 − 1/2304 = 1/576, so the tank fills in 576 minutes.

questions.q: Warehouse planning case — What is the least number greater than 2070 that leaves remainder 44 when divided by both 45 and 46, given that 45 and 46 are coprime?
questions.e: A common remainder means N − 44 is a multiple of lcm(45, 46) = 2070. The least eligible N is 2070 + 44 = 2114.

questions.q: Transport-depot calculation — Two pipes can fill a tank in 756 and 1134 minutes, while a leak can empty it in 2268 minutes. If all three remain open, when will the tank fill?
questions.e: Net rate = 1/756 + 1/1134 − 1/2268 = 1/567, so the tank fills in 567 minutes.

questions.q: Health-programme report — After a 30% discount and then 20% sales tax, an equipment bill for a health programme is Rs 34440. What was the listed price?
questions.e: If L is the list price, L × 70/100 × 120/100 = 34440, giving L = 41000.

questions.q: Scholarship-fund audit — A bus leaves a scholarship fund at 80 km/h. 3 hours later, a car follows on the same route at 92 km/h. How long after the car starts will it catch the bus?
questions.e: The bus has a 240 km lead. Relative speed is 12 km/h, so catch-up time is 20 hours.

questions.q: Warehouse planning case — A bus leaves a warehouse at 81 km/h. 4 hours later, a car follows on the same route at 94 km/h. How long after the car starts will it catch the bus?
questions.e: The bus has a 324 km lead. Relative speed is 13 km/h, so catch-up time is 24.92 hours.

questions.q: Transport-depot calculation — Two triangles are similar. A side of 9 cm in the smaller corresponds to 54 cm in the larger. If another smaller side is 9 cm, what is its corresponding larger side?

تملیکی — ملکیت ظاہر کرے (کسی چیز کا مالک کون ہے)
ظرفی — کسی اسم کی تخصیص (محدود دائرہ) بیان کرے
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 214: تملیکی — ملکیت ظاہر کرے (کسی چیز کا مالک کون ہے)

questions.q: تعریف “دو یا زائد الفاظ کو "و" یا کسی اور حرفِ عطف سے مالیا جائے۔” اور مثال “ماں اور باپ، علم و ادب” کس اصطلاح کو ظاہر کرتی ہیں؟
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 214: مرک بِ عطفی — دو یا زائد الفاظ کو "و" یا کسی اور حرفِ عطف سے مالیا جائے۔

questions.q: “نسبتی” کی درست تعریف منتخب کریں۔
o: وہ صفت جو کسی چیز یا شخص کا تعلق یا نسبت ظاہر کرے۔
وہ صفت جو کسی ضمیر کے ذریعے کسی اسم کی طرف اشارہ کرے۔
وہ صفت جو کسی چیز کی مقدار یا پیمانہ ظاہر کرے۔
وہ صفت جو کسی چیز کی تعداد ظاہر کرے۔
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 210: نسبتی — وہ صفت جو کسی چیز یا شخص کا تعلق یا نسبت ظاہر کرے۔

questions.q:
Read the passage: “An agency rated projects by the number of people reached. A small remote clinic scored poorly, even though its patients had no nearby alternative. The agency revised the score to consider both reach and the availability of other services.”

What weakness did the original rating have?
o: It ignored whether people had alternatives
questions.e: A low number reached can conceal high need where alternatives are absent.

questions.q:
Read the passage: “An agency rated projects by the number of people reached. A small remote clinic scored poorly, even though its patients had no nearby alternative. The agency revised the score to consider both reach and the availability of other services.”

What does the revision attempt to balance?
o: Scale of benefit and severity of unmet need
questions.e: The revised score considers both numbers reached and access to substitutes.

questions.q: Which Type is associated with Example Word “this, that” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 230: Type “Demonstrative Pronoun” corresponds to Example Word “this, that”.

questions.q: Which Direct Speech is associated with Indirect Speech “Go” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 227: Direct Speech “Come” corresponds to Indirect Speech “Go”.

questions.q: Which Type is associated with Definition “Shows ownership” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 230: Type “Possessive Pronoun” corresponds to Definition “Shows ownership”.

questions.q: Which Rule is associated with Preposition “At” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 231: Rule “Used for working position” corresponds to Preposition “At”.

questions.q: Which Type is associated with Sentence Example “Shh! Be quiet.” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 231: Type “Volitive Interjection” corresponds to Sentence Example “Shh! Be quiet.”.

questions.q: Which Type is associated with Reporting Verb “Requested” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 228: Type “Request” corresponds to Reporting Verb “Requested”.

questions.q: Which Indirect Speech is associated with Direct Speech “He said, "Where are you going?"” in the English reference?
o: She asked what my name was.
He asked where I was going.
She requested not to disturb her.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 227: Indirect Speech “He asked where I was going.” corresponds to Direct Speech “He said, "Where are you going?"”.

questions.q: Which Type is associated with Definition “Describes intensity” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 230: Type “Adverb of Degree” corresponds to Definition “Describes intensity”.

questions.q: Which Type is associated with Reporting Verb “Ordered” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 228: Type “Order” corresponds to Reporting Verb “Ordered”.

questions.q: Which Type is associated with Sentence Example “He ate three apples.” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 229: Type “Countable Noun” corresponds to Sentence Example “He ate three apples.”.

questions.q: Which Direct Speech is associated with Example “He said, "Come here." → He told me to go there.” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 227: Direct Speech “Come” corresponds to Example “He said, "Come here." → He told me to go there.”.

questions.q: Which Type is associated with Sentence Example “He is the laziest student.” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 230: Type “Superlative Adjective” corresponds to Sentence Example “He is the laziest student.”.

questions.q: Which Rule is associated with Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) “He stood before the judge in silence.” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 232: Rule “Standing in front of something” corresponds to Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) “He stood before the judge in silence.”.

questions.q: Which Preposition is associated with Rule “Effectiveness or appropriateness” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 232: Preposition “To” corresponds to Rule “Effectiveness or appropriateness”.

questions.s: Active Voice, Passive Voice, and Causatives
questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The committee approved the proposal. (Make passive.)”?
o: The proposal was not approved by the committee.
The committee approved the proposal. (Make passive.)
The proposal was approved by the committee.
The proposal were approved by the committee.
questions.e: The proposal was approved by the committee. (Useful if the proposal is the topic.)

questions.q: Which Preposition is associated with Rule “Specific time” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 232: Preposition “At” corresponds to Rule “Specific time”.

questions.q: In Articles, which Example Sentence corresponds to Rule “With musical instruments”?
o: He is the Shakespeare of our times.
I read the Dawn every morning.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 225: Rule “With musical instruments” corresponds to Example Sentence “He plays the piano beautifully.”.

questions.q: Find the error: “The government will analyze (A) the programme (B) and publish (C) its defence (D) of the policy.”
questions.e: The rest of the sentence uses British spelling, so analyse is required. Keep one system throughout.

questions.q: In Articles, which Example Sentence corresponds to Rule “Use the with provinces, mountain ranges, rivers, oceans”?
o: He lives in the Punjab. They climbed the Himalayas. We swam in the Atlantic Ocean.
The United Nations passed a new resolution. The World Bank approved the loan.
The man you saw was my teacher. The pen on the desk is mine.
He read The Quran daily. She studied The Republic by Plato.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 225: Rule “Use the with provinces, mountain ranges, rivers, oceans” corresponds to Example Sentence “He lives in the Punjab. They climbed the Himalayas. We swam in the Atlantic Ocean.”.

questions.q: In Twelve-Tense Reference, which Structure corresponds to Tense “Past Perfect”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 244: Tense “Past Perfect” corresponds to Structure “subject + had + past participle”.

questions.q: In Sentences, Clauses and Phrases, which Rule corresponds to Preposition “Of / For / To”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 233: Preposition “Of / For / To” corresponds to Rule “Desire/longing related to personality”.

questions.q: Find the error: “He is responsible for planning (A), for budgeting (B) and to monitor (C) the annual programme (D).”
questions.e: The third item must be for monitoring.

questions.q: Neither the chairman nor the members ____ willing to sign.
questions.e: With neither … nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject, members.

questions.q: Find the error: “Decision (A) to postpone the examination (B) was announced (C) on Friday (D).”
questions.e: A singular countable noun cannot stand alone as a subject. Write “The decision”.

questions.q: In “The board declared the contract void”, what is void?
questions.e: Void describes the object contract, so it is an object complement.

questions.q: In Active and Passive Voice, which Example (Active) corresponds to Tense “Present Continuous”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 224: Tense “Present Continuous” corresponds to Example (Active) “They are playing cricket.”.

questions.q: Find the error: “Candidates must either submit (A) the original degree (B) or they should attach (C) an attested copy (D).”
questions.e: Either … or must join like with like: “or attach an attested copy”.

questions.q: In Sentences, Clauses and Phrases, which Example corresponds to Connector Type “Coordinating Conjunctions (FANBOYS)”?
o: Because he was ill, he stayed home. He stayed home because he was ill.
My friend, who is a doctor, is coming. People who work hard succeed.
He plays cricket, and she plays football.
He was late; however, he completed the task.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 234: Connector Type “Coordinating Conjunctions (FANBOYS)” corresponds to Example “He plays cricket, and she plays football.”.

questions.q: In Twelve-Tense Reference, which Example corresponds to Tense “Past Perfect Continuous”?
o: She will have written by noon.
She had been writing for an hour.
She will be writing at noon.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 244: Tense “Past Perfect Continuous” corresponds to Example “She had been writing for an hour.”.

questions.q: Find the error: “The report was clear (A), concise (B) and it was well argued (C) throughout (D).”
questions.e: The third item becomes a clause. Write simply “well argued”.

questions.q: His performance in the interview was not so impressive ____ his written papers.
questions.e: Not so … as is the fixed pattern of negative equality.

questions.q: In Twelve-Tense Reference, which Structure corresponds to Tense “Present Continuous”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 244: Tense “Present Continuous” corresponds to Structure “subject + is/am/are + verb-ing”.

questions.q: Find the error: “The scheme aims to raise incomes (A), to improve nutrition (B) and reducing (C) rural indebtedness (D).”
questions.e: The third item must match the first two: to reduce.

questions.q: Find the error: “The number of vacancies advertised (A) this year (B) are lower (C) than last year (D).”
questions.e: The number of is a single figure and takes is.

questions.q: Find the error: “The salary of a lecturer (A) is much lower (B) than a deputy secretary (C) in the same grade (D).”
questions.e: Compare salary with salary: “than that of a deputy secretary”.

questions.q: Either the secretary or his deputies ____ to attend the briefing.
questions.e: The nearer subject, deputies, is plural.

questions.q: Find the error: “Each of the provinces (A) have submitted (B) their own (C) education plan (D).”
questions.e: Each is singular: has submitted, and correspondingly its own.

questions.q: Find the error: “The training improves (A) drafting, presentation (B) and how to manage time (C) under pressure (D).”
questions.e: Two nouns and a clause do not balance: write “time management”.

questions.q: In Twelve-Tense Reference, which Tense corresponds to Structure “subject + will/shall + base verb”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 244: Structure “subject + will/shall + base verb” corresponds to Tense “Future Simple”.

questions.q: In Twelve-Tense Reference, which Example corresponds to Tense “Future Perfect”?
o: She has been writing for an hour.
She will have written by noon.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 244: Tense “Future Perfect” corresponds to Example “She will have written by noon.”.

questions.q: In Articles, which Example Sentence corresponds to Rule “Exception: article the is used with "devil"”?
o: He lives in the Punjab. They climbed the Himalayas. We swam in the Atlantic Ocean.
He visited the United States. She works in the Netherlands.
The moon looks beautiful tonight. The sun rises in the east.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 225: Rule “Exception: article the is used with "devil"” corresponds to Example Sentence “He behaves like the devil.”.

questions.q: Find the error: “She is one of the (A) most brilliant candidate (B) the academy (C) has produced (D).”
questions.e: One of the + superlative requires a plural noun: candidates.

questions.q: In Sentences, Clauses and Phrases, which Preposition corresponds to Rule “Confusion over "sat in/on" tree”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 233: Rule “Confusion over "sat in/on" tree” corresponds to Preposition “In / On”.

questions.q: In Active and Passive Voice, which Example (Active) corresponds to Type “Negative Command”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 224: Type “Negative Command” corresponds to Example (Active) “Do not touch the wire.”.

questions.q: For Sentences, Clauses and Phrases, which Sentence Type–Definition / Explanation association is accurate?
o: Compound Sentence — A sentence with one independent clause and one or more dependent clauses.
Simple Sentence — A sentence with only one independent clause. It expresses a complete thought.
Compound- Complex Sentence — A sentence with two or more independent clauses, joined by a coordinating conjunction, conjunctive adverb, or semicolon.
Complex Sentence — A sentence that has two or I more independent clauses and at least one dependent clause.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 233: Sentence Type “Simple Sentence” corresponds to Definition / Explanation “A sentence with only one independent clause. It expresses a complete thought.”.

questions.q: For Active and Passive Voice, which Tense–Passive Formula association is accurate?
o: Past Indefinite — Object + will/shall + be + V3 + by + Subject
Future Indefinite — Object + is/am/are + being + V3 + by + Subject
Present Continuous — Object + was/were + V3 + by + Subject
Present Indefinite — Object + is/am/are + V3 + by + Subject
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 224: Tense “Present Indefinite” corresponds to Passive Formula “Object + is/am/are + V3 + by + Subject”.

questions.q: Find the error: “The committee, after discussing about the issue (A) for two hours (B), decided to postpone (C) the decision (D).”
questions.e: Discuss takes no preposition: “after discussing the issue”.

questions.q: Find the error: “The impact of rising fuel prices (A) on household budgets (B) have been (C) severe this year (D).”
questions.e: The head noun is impact, so the verb must be has been.

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — An investment grows to Rs 24200 in two years at 10% compound interest per year. What was the principal?
Health-programme report — An investment grows to Rs 44100 in two years at 50% compound interest per year. What was the principal?
Training-centre exercise — A geometric sequence has first term 55 and common ratio 4. What is its 6th term?
Survey-unit review — A geometric sequence has first term 54 and common ratio 3. What is its 5th term?
Survey-unit review — For two years at 10% per annum, by how much does compound interest exceed simple interest on Rs 380000?
Training-centre exercise — For two years at 12% per annum, by how much does compound interest exceed simple interest on Rs 390000?
Relief-camp planning case — A bag holds 43 red and 9 blue counters. Two are drawn without replacement. What is the probability that both are red?
questions.e: Multiply the changing probabilities: 43/52 × 42/51 = 68.1%.

questions.q: District-office worksheet — A bag holds 44 red and 10 blue counters. Two are drawn without replacement. What is the probability that both are red?
questions.e: Multiply the changing probabilities: 44/54 × 43/53 = 66.11%.

questions.q: District-office worksheet — 48 passengers paid Rs 2500. An adult ticket cost Rs 60 and a child ticket Rs 40. How many adults travelled?
questions.e: If a is the adult count, 60a + 40(48 − a) = 2500, which gives a = 29.

questions.q: Warehouse planning case — 57 passengers paid Rs 3915. An adult ticket cost Rs 75 and a child ticket Rs 55. How many adults travelled?
questions.e: If a is the adult count, 75a + 55(57 − a) = 3915, which gives a = 39.

questions.q: Warehouse planning case — A 71 m by 19 m rectangular courtyard has a uniform path 5 m wide inside its boundary. What area does the path cover?
questions.e: Path area = outer area − inner area = 1349 − 61×9 = 800 m².

questions.q: Scholarship-fund audit — A 70 m by 18 m rectangular courtyard has a uniform path 4 m wide inside its boundary. What area does the path cover?
questions.e: Path area = outer area − inner area = 1260 − 62×10 = 640 m².

questions.q: Transport-depot calculation — A vehicle covers two equal-distance legs at 48 km/h and 62 km/h. What is its average speed for the complete journey?
questions.e: For equal distances the harmonic mean applies: 2uv/(u + v) = 54.11 km/h.

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — A vehicle covers two equal-distance legs at 52 km/h and 62 km/h. What is its average speed for the complete journey?
questions.e: For equal distances the harmonic mean applies: 2uv/(u + v) = 56.56 km/h.

questions.q: Transport-depot calculation — The roots of x² − 40x + 391 = 0 differ by 6. What is the larger root?
questions.e: The quadratic factors as (x − 17)(x − 23); the larger root is 23.

questions.q: Health-programme report — The roots of x² − 38x + 360 = 0 differ by 2. What is the larger root?
questions.e: The quadratic factors as (x − 18)(x − 20); the larger root is 20.

questions.q: Training-centre exercise — An arithmetic sequence begins 34, 37, 40, … . What is the sum of its first 15 terms?
Survey-unit review — On a coordinate grid, point Q lies 159 units east and 212 units north of point P. What is the straight-line distance PQ?
Training-centre exercise — On a coordinate grid, point Q lies 270 units east and 648 units north of point P. What is the straight-line distance PQ?
Training-centre exercise — The mean of 14 observations in a report is 59. One entry, 49, is corrected to 77. What is the corrected mean?
questions.e: The total rises by 28; divided across 14 observations, the mean rises by 2 to 61.

questions.q: Survey-unit review — An arithmetic sequence begins 25, 33, 41, … . What is the sum of its first 14 terms?
Survey-unit review — The mean of 19 observations in a report is 82. One entry, 72, is corrected to 110. What is the corrected mean?
questions.e: The total rises by 38; divided across 19 observations, the mean rises by 2 to 84.

questions.q: Health-programme report — A two-digit number has digit sum 8; reversing its digits increases it by 18. What is the original number?
questions.e: Let the tens and units digits be x and y. Then x + y = 8 and 9(x − y) = -18; hence x = 3, y = 5.

questions.q: Transport-depot calculation — A two-digit number has digit sum 7; reversing its digits increases it by 9. What is the original number?
questions.e: Let the tens and units digits be x and y. Then x + y = 7 and 9(x − y) = -9; hence x = 3, y = 4.

questions.q: Scholarship-fund audit — A train 700 m long clears a 120 m platform in 13 seconds. What is its speed in km/h?
questions.e: The train covers 820 m. Its speed is (820)/13 m/s × 3.6 = 227.08 km/h.

questions.q: Warehouse planning case — A train 710 m long clears a 130 m platform in 14 seconds. What is its speed in km/h?
questions.e: The train covers 840 m. Its speed is (840)/14 m/s × 3.6 = 216 km/h.

questions.q: Health-programme report — A invests Rs 27000 for 9 months and B invests Rs 7000 for 6 months. If their profit is Rs 2850, what is A's share?
questions.e: Profit follows capital-months. The weights are 243000:42000; A therefore receives Rs 2430.

questions.q: Transport-depot calculation — A invests Rs 26000 for 8 months and B invests Rs 6000 for 5 months. If their profit is Rs 2380, what is A's share?
questions.e: Profit follows capital-months. The weights are 208000:30000; A therefore receives Rs 2080.

questions.q: Survey-unit review — Worker B takes 19 days for a task. Worker A is 20% more efficient than B. How many days would A need for the same task?
questions.e: Time varies inversely with efficiency, so A's time is 19 × 100/120 = 15.83 days.

questions.q: Training-centre exercise — Worker B takes 44 days for a task. Worker A is 25% more efficient than B. How many days would A need for the same task?
questions.e: Time varies inversely with efficiency, so A's time is 44 × 100/125 = 35.2 days.

questions.q: Warehouse planning case — A tank contains 660 litres of a 40% solution. 132 litres of the mixture are removed and replaced by water. What is the new concentration?
questions.e: Removing one-fifth of a uniform mixture removes one-fifth of its solute. The remaining concentration is 40% × 4/5 = 32%.

questions.q: Training-centre exercise — A tank contains 360 litres of a 30% solution. 72 litres of the mixture are removed and replaced by water. What is the new concentration?
questions.e: Removing one-fifth of a uniform mixture removes one-fifth of its solute. The remaining concentration is 30% × 4/5 = 24%.

questions.q: Survey-unit review — What is the least number greater than 930 that leaves remainder 29 when divided by both 30 and 31, given that 30 and 31 are coprime?
questions.e: A common remainder means N − 29 is a multiple of lcm(30, 31) = 930. The least eligible N is 930 + 29 = 959.

questions.q: District-office worksheet — Two batches assessed by a district office contain 69 and 14 candidates with mean scores 55 and 80. What is the combined mean?
questions.e: Use the weighted mean: (69 × 55 + 14 × 80) ÷ 83 = 59.22.

questions.q: Health-programme report — Two batches assessed by a health programme contain 75 and 11 candidates with mean scores 50 and 73. What is the combined mean?
questions.e: Use the weighted mean: (75 × 50 + 11 × 73) ÷ 86 = 52.94.

questions.q: Training-centre exercise — What is the least number greater than 992 that leaves remainder 30 when divided by both 31 and 32, given that 31 and 32 are coprime?
questions.e: A common remainder means N − 30 is a multiple of lcm(31, 32) = 992. The least eligible N is 992 + 30 = 1022.

questions.q: District-office worksheet — Two pipes can fill a tank in 24 and 36 minutes, while a leak can empty it in 72 minutes. If all three remain open, when will the tank fill?
questions.e: Net rate = 1/24 + 1/36 − 1/72 = 1/18, so the tank fills in 18 minutes.

questions.q: District-office worksheet — After a 20% discount and then 10% sales tax, an equipment bill for a district office is Rs 16720. What was the listed price?
questions.e: If L is the list price, L × 80/100 × 110/100 = 16720, giving L = 19000.

questions.q: Health-programme report — After a 30% discount and then 20% sales tax, an equipment bill for a health programme is Rs 14280. What was the listed price?
questions.e: If L is the list price, L × 70/100 × 120/100 = 14280, giving L = 17000.

questions.q: Warehouse planning case — Two runners start together in opposite directions on a 680 m circular track at 85 m/s and 68 m/s. After how many seconds do they first meet?
questions.e: In opposite directions their relative speed is 153 m/s, so time is 680 ÷ 153 = 4.44 seconds.

questions.q: District-office worksheet — Two runners start together in opposite directions on a 640 m circular track at 106.67 m/s and 80 m/s. After how many seconds do they first meet?
questions.e: In opposite directions their relative speed is 186.67 m/s, so time is 640 ÷ 186.67 = 3.43 seconds.

questions.q: Training-centre exercise — A bus leaves a training centre at 67 km/h. 2 hours later, a car follows on the same route at 78 km/h. How long after the car starts will it catch the bus?
questions.e: The bus has a 134 km lead. Relative speed is 11 km/h, so catch-up time is 12.18 hours.

questions.q: Survey-unit review — A bus leaves a survey unit at 66 km/h. 1 hours later, a car follows on the same route at 76 km/h. How long after the car starts will it catch the bus?
questions.e: The bus has a 66 km lead. Relative speed is 10 km/h, so catch-up time is 6.6 hours.

questions.q: Transport-depot calculation — A supplier wants a 30% profit on an item costing Rs 25600, even after allowing a 20% discount on its marked price. What marked price is required?
questions.e: Required selling price is 25600 × 130/100. Since that is 80% of the marked price, divide it by 0.8.

questions.q: Health-programme report — A supplier wants a 40% profit on an item costing Rs 26400, even after allowing a 30% discount on its marked price. What marked price is required?
questions.e: Required selling price is 26400 × 140/100. Since that is 70% of the marked price, divide it by 0.7.

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — A boat's still-water speed is 50 km/h and the stream flows at 2 km/h. How long does a 4992 km upstream and 4992 km downstream round trip take?
District-office worksheet — A boat's still-water speed is 51 km/h and the stream flows at 3 km/h. How long does a 7776 km upstream and 7776 km downstream round trip take?

Five candidates—Maryam, Mehak, Muneeb, Nadia, Noman—are interviewed once each. Maryam is before Mehak; Mehak is immediately before Muneeb; Noman is after Nadia; and Nadia is after Muneeb. Which order is possible?
questions.e: The fixed block is Mehak–Muneeb; Maryam must precede it, and Muneeb must be followed in order by Nadia and Noman.

questions.q: Five candidates—Mehak, Muneeb, Nadia, Noman, Omar—are interviewed once each. Mehak is before Muneeb; Muneeb is immediately before Nadia; Omar is after Noman; and Noman is after Nadia. Which order is possible?
questions.e: The fixed block is Muneeb–Nadia; Mehak must precede it, and Nadia must be followed in order by Noman and Omar.

questions.q: District-office worksheet — a district office divides 130 files between teams A and B in the ratio 4:6. How many additional files must A receive for the new ratio A:B to become 8:6?
questions.e: The original shares are 52 and 78. To make A's share 104, it needs 104 − 52 = 52 more files.

questions.q: Scholarship-fund audit — a scholarship fund divides 168 files between teams A and B in the ratio 5:7. How many additional files must A receive for the new ratio A:B to become 10:7?
questions.e: The original shares are 70 and 98. To make A's share 140, it needs 140 − 70 = 70 more files.

questions.q: District-office worksheet — A quarterly table for a district office records 610, 325, and 120 completed cases in three months. What percentage of the three-month total was completed in the first month?
questions.e: The total is 1055; the first-month share is 610/1055 × 100 = 57.82%.

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — A quarterly table for a relief camp records 600, 320, and 115 completed cases in three months. What percentage of the three-month total was completed in the first month?
questions.e: The total is 1035; the first-month share is 600/1035 × 100 = 57.97%.

questions.q: Scholarship-fund audit — In a survey, 38 chose only A, 20 only B, 10 only C, 7 chose A and B only, 5 A and C only, 2 B and C only, and 1 chose all three. How many chose at least one?
questions.e: The seven disjoint regions are added once: 38+20+10+7+5+2+1 = 83.

questions.q: Warehouse planning case — In a survey, 39 chose only A, 21 only B, 11 only C, 8 chose A and B only, 6 A and C only, 3 B and C only, and 2 chose all three. How many chose at least one?
questions.e: The seven disjoint regions are added once: 39+21+11+8+6+3+2 = 90.

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — Two triangles are similar. A side of 3 cm in the smaller corresponds to 18 cm in the larger. If another smaller side is 5 cm, what is its corresponding larger side?
questions.e: The scale factor is 18/3 = 6; therefore 5 × 6 = 30 cm.

questions.q: District-office worksheet — Two triangles are similar. A side of 4 cm in the smaller corresponds to 24 cm in the larger. If another smaller side is 8 cm, what is its corresponding larger side?
questions.e: The scale factor is 24/4 = 6; therefore 8 × 6 = 48 cm.

questions.q: Training-centre exercise — A can complete a project in 552 days and B in 828 days. They work together for 276 days; B then leaves. How many days from the start will A take to finish the project?
questions.e: Together they complete 276 × (1/552 + 1/828) = 5/6. A needs another 92 days for the remaining 1/6, totalling 368.

questions.q: Which Indirect Speech is associated with Direct Speech “Present Continuous” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 226: Indirect Speech “Past Continuous” corresponds to Direct Speech “Present Continuous”.

questions.q: Which Direct Speech is associated with Rule “He said, "I was writing." → He said that he had been writing.” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 226: Direct Speech “Past Continuous” corresponds to Rule “He said, "I was writing." → He said that he had been writing.”.

questions.q: Which Rule is associated with Preposition “Forward / Back” in the English reference?
o: Used when some work is finished, or for disconnection/cutting
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 232: Rule “Movement of clock/time” corresponds to Preposition “Forward / Back”.

questions.q: Which Type is associated with Reporting Verb “Prayed” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 228: Type “Prayer” corresponds to Reporting Verb “Prayed”.

questions.q: Which Rule is associated with Preposition “On” in the English reference?
o: Used for position on a surface
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 231: Rule “Used for position on a surface” corresponds to Preposition “On”.

questions.q: In Twelve-Tense Reference, which Example corresponds to Tense “Present Perfect Continuous”?
o: She has been writing for an hour.
She had written before I arrived.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 244: Tense “Present Perfect Continuous” corresponds to Example “She has been writing for an hour.”.

questions.q: In Prepositions, which Sentence Example corresponds to Type “Cognitive Interjection”?
o: He left because of the rain.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 231: Type “Cognitive Interjection” corresponds to Sentence Example “Um... I'm not sure.”.

questions.q: In Sentences, Clauses and Phrases, which Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) corresponds to Rule “Desire/longing related to personality”?
o: He sat in the tree, hidden by leaves. He sat on the branch and started whistling.
I stayed in Dubai for five days.
He is ambitious of fame. She has ambition for power. He aspires to greatness.
The army retrogressed from the battlefield. They had to retreat from enemy lines.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 233: Rule “Desire/longing related to personality” corresponds to Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) “He is ambitious of fame. She has ambition for power. He aspires to greatness.”.

questions.q: In Prepositions, which Definition corresponds to Type “Preposition of Reason”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 231: Type “Preposition of Reason” corresponds to Definition “Shows reason”.

questions.s: Capital letters, full stops and the everyday comma
questions.q: Find the error: “In 1947 (A) Pakistan (B) gained independence, (C) and adopted a new flag (D).”
questions.e: “adopted a new flag” has no subject of its own, so no comma is needed before and.

questions.q: ____ the funds been released on time, the project would have finished within budget.
questions.e: Inverting had replaces if in a formal third conditional.

questions.q: In Sentences, Clauses and Phrases, which Rule corresponds to Preposition “By”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 233: Preposition “By” corresponds to Rule “Non-specific vehicle travel”.

questions.s: Modifiers: put the describing words where they belong
questions.q: Find the error: “He said he would (A) only sign the file (B) after the legal branch (C) had cleared it (D).”
questions.e: The limit is on the timing, not the act: “he would sign the file only after the legal branch had cleared it”.

questions.q: Find the error: “It is essential that every candidate carries (A) a valid identity card (B) and reports (C) an hour early (D).”
questions.e: It is essential that takes the subjunctive: carry, and correspondingly report.

questions.q: In Active and Passive Voice, which Passive Formula corresponds to Tense “Present Perfect Continuous ❌”?
o: Object + will/shall + be + V3 + by + Subject
Object + is/am/are + being + V3 + by + Subject
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 224: Tense “Present Perfect Continuous ❌” corresponds to Passive Formula “Not Possible”.

questions.q: In Sentences, Clauses and Phrases, which Preposition corresponds to Rule “Movement by foot”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 233: Rule “Movement by foot” corresponds to Preposition “On”.

questions.q: Find the error: “Candidates will can apply (A) online from Monday (B) until the closing date (C) in March (D).”
questions.e: Two modals cannot combine. Write “will be able to apply”.

questions.s: Capital letters, full stops and the everyday comma
questions.q: Find the error: “The report, which was tabled in March (A), recommend (B) three reforms (C) to the licensing regime (D).”
questions.e: The subject is report, which is singular, so the verb is recommends. The clause in commas does not control the verb.

questions.q: You ____ paid the fine; the notice had already been withdrawn.
questions.e: Need not have + participle means the action was done but was unnecessary.

questions.q: Find the error: “Even though the notification was issued (A), but the department (B) did not act (C) on it for six months (D).”
questions.e: Even though already marks the contrast; delete but.

questions.s: Concision: saying it in fewer words
questions.q: Find the wordy phrase: “The department will act (A) at this point in time (B) to reduce (C) the backlog (D).”
questions.e: At this point in time means now.

questions.q: In Active and Passive Voice, which Passive Formula corresponds to Type “Advice (Kindly)”?
o: You are advised to + V1 + Object
You are requested to + V1 + Object
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 224: Type “Advice (Kindly)” corresponds to Passive Formula “You are advised to + V1 + Object”.

questions.q: If she had accepted the posting, she ____ in Gilgit now.
questions.e: A past condition with a present result is a mixed conditional: would + bare infinitive.

questions.q: Find the error: “Despite of (A) repeated reminders (B), the department (C) failed to respond (D).”
questions.e: Despite takes no of; in spite of is the three-word alternative.

questions.q: Find the error: “The chairman (A) spoke confident (B) about the reforms (C) that his department had introduced (D).”
questions.e: Confident describes the verb spoke, so it must be the adverb confidently.

questions.s: Concision: saying it in fewer words
questions.q: Find the redundancy: “The committee reviewed (A) the past history (B) of the dispute (C) before deciding (D).”
questions.e: History is already past.

questions.q: Find the error: “During (A) the committee was in session (B), the press (C) waited outside (D).”
questions.e: During takes a noun; before a clause use while.

questions.q: A significant ____ of complaints was received by the ombudsman.
questions.e: Complaints are countable, so number is correct. Amount belongs with uncountable nouns.

questions.q: In Articles, which Rule corresponds to Example Sentence “A servant must obey his master. Anyone can become a leader.”?
o: No article before names of people
No article before titles (when used with names)
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 225: Example Sentence “A servant must obey his master. Anyone can become a leader.” corresponds to Rule “In the general sense of "any"”.

questions.s: Concision: saying it in fewer words
questions.q: Replace “in the event that the appeal is dismissed”.
o: when there is an appeal dismissal event
at the time of the dismissal of the appeal
questions.e: If carries the whole meaning in one word.

questions.q: Find the error: “Several equipments (A) were purchased (B) without (C) proper approval (D).”
questions.e: Equipment is uncountable. Write “several items of equipment” or simply “equipment”.

questions.q: In Sentences, Clauses and Phrases, which Clause Structure corresponds to Sentence Type “Complex Sentence”?
o: One Independent Clause + One or More Dependent Clauses
Two or More ndependent Clauses + One or More Dependent Clauses
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 234: Sentence Type “Complex Sentence” corresponds to Clause Structure “One Independent Clause + One or More Dependent Clauses”.

questions.s: Concision: saying it in fewer words
questions.q: Find the redundancy: “The file was returned back (A) to the section (B) on the following (C) Monday (D).”
questions.e: Return already contains the idea of back.

questions.q: Find the error: “He could not attend (A) the hearing because of (B) he was (C) out of the country (D).”
questions.e: Because of takes a noun phrase. Before the clause “he was out of the country”, use because.

questions.s: Concision: saying it in fewer words
questions.q: Find the redundancy: “Each and every candidate (A) must bring (B) an original (C) identity card (D).”
questions.e: Each and every says the same thing twice.

questions.q: In Twelve-Tense Reference, which Structure corresponds to Tense “Past Perfect Continuous”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 244: Tense “Past Perfect Continuous” corresponds to Structure “subject + had been + verb-ing”.

questions.q: In which sentence is fund used as a verb?
o: Donors will fund the second phase.
questions.e: In option B, fund carries the action after the modal will, so it is a verb.

questions.q: In Sentences, Clauses and Phrases, which Preposition corresponds to Rule “Comparison between similar things”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 233: Rule “Comparison between similar things” corresponds to Preposition “With”.

questions.q: In Articles, which Example Sentence corresponds to Rule “No article before cities and countries (general rule)”?
o: He caught the measles last month. She was diagnosed with the mumps.
I live in Multan. He visited Pakistan last year.
Honesty is the best policy. Love conquers all.
He is suffering from malaria. She has diabetes.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 225: Rule “No article before cities and countries (general rule)” corresponds to Example Sentence “I live in Multan. He visited Pakistan last year.”.

questions.q: In Twelve-Tense Reference, which Tense corresponds to Structure “subject + past form”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 244: Structure “subject + past form” corresponds to Tense “Past Simple”.

questions.q: Survey-unit review — A vehicle covers two equal-distance legs at 124 km/h and 134 km/h. What is its average speed for the complete journey?
questions.e: For equal distances the harmonic mean applies: 2uv/(u + v) = 128.81 km/h.

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — A train 520 m long clears a 120 m platform in 17 seconds. What is its speed in km/h?
questions.e: The train covers 640 m. Its speed is (640)/17 m/s × 3.6 = 135.53 km/h.

questions.q: Warehouse planning case — A invests Rs 31000 for 8 months and B invests Rs 11000 for 10 months. If their profit is Rs 3580, what is A's share?

questions.q: District-office worksheet — A train 530 m long clears a 130 m platform in 18 seconds. What is its speed in km/h?

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — A bag holds 35 red and 8 blue counters. Two are drawn without replacement. What is the probability that both are red?
questions.e: Multiply the changing probabilities: 35/43 × 34/42 = 65.89%.

questions.q: District-office worksheet — A bag holds 36 red and 9 blue counters. Two are drawn without replacement. What is the probability that both are red?
questions.e: Multiply the changing probabilities: 36/45 × 35/44 = 63.64%.

questions.q: Transport-depot calculation — 47 passengers paid Rs 2090. An adult ticket cost Rs 50 and a child ticket Rs 30. How many adults travelled?
questions.e: If a is the adult count, 50a + 30(47 − a) = 2090, which gives a = 34.

questions.q: Health-programme report — 49 passengers paid Rs 2415. An adult ticket cost Rs 55 and a child ticket Rs 35. How many adults travelled?
questions.e: If a is the adult count, 55a + 35(49 − a) = 2415, which gives a = 35.

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — The mean of 13 observations in a report is 94. One entry, 84, is corrected to 110. What is the corrected mean?
questions.e: The total rises by 26; divided across 13 observations, the mean rises by 2 to 96.

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — In a survey, 68 chose only A, 24 only B, 13 only C, 7 chose A and B only, 3 A and C only, 2 B and C only, and 1 chose all three. How many chose at least one?
questions.e: The seven disjoint regions are added once: 68+24+13+7+3+2+1 = 118.

questions.q: District-office worksheet — In a survey, 69 chose only A, 25 only B, 14 only C, 8 chose A and B only, 4 A and C only, 3 B and C only, and 2 chose all three. How many chose at least one?
questions.e: The seven disjoint regions are added once: 69+25+14+8+4+3+2 = 125.

questions.q: Five candidates—Asad, Ayesha, Basit, Bilal, Dania—are interviewed once each. Asad is before Ayesha; Ayesha is immediately before Basit; Dania is after Bilal; and Bilal is after Basit. Which order is possible?
questions.e: The fixed block is Ayesha–Basit; Asad must precede it, and Basit must be followed in order by Bilal and Dania.

questions.q: Five candidates—Ayesha, Basit, Bilal, Dania, Danish—are interviewed once each. Ayesha is before Basit; Basit is immediately before Bilal; Danish is after Dania; and Dania is after Bilal. Which order is possible?
questions.e: The fixed block is Basit–Bilal; Ayesha must precede it, and Bilal must be followed in order by Dania and Danish.

questions.q: Training-centre exercise — After a 20% discount and then 10% sales tax, an equipment bill for a training centre is Rs 55440. What was the listed price?
questions.e: If L is the list price, L × 80/100 × 110/100 = 55440, giving L = 63000.

questions.q: Transport-depot calculation — After a 25% discount and then 12.5% sales tax, an equipment bill for a transport depot is Rs 54000. What was the listed price?
questions.e: If L is the list price, L × 75/100 × 112.5/100 = 54000, giving L = 64000.

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — What is the least number greater than 342 that leaves remainder 17 when divided by both 18 and 19, given that 18 and 19 are coprime?
questions.e: A common remainder means N − 17 is a multiple of lcm(18, 19) = 342. The least eligible N is 342 + 17 = 359.

questions.q: District-office worksheet — What is the least number greater than 380 that leaves remainder 18 when divided by both 19 and 20, given that 19 and 20 are coprime?
questions.e: A common remainder means N − 18 is a multiple of lcm(19, 20) = 380. The least eligible N is 380 + 18 = 398.

questions.q: Training-centre exercise — a training centre divides 730 files between teams A and B in the ratio 4:6. How many additional files must A receive for the new ratio A:B to become 8:6?
questions.e: The original shares are 292 and 438. To make A's share 584, it needs 584 − 292 = 292 more files.

questions.q: Survey-unit review — a survey unit divides 576 files between teams A and B in the ratio 3:5. How many additional files must A receive for the new ratio A:B to become 6:5?
questions.e: The original shares are 216 and 360. To make A's share 432, it needs 432 − 216 = 216 more files.

questions.e: In opposite directions their relative speed is 294.6 m/s, so time is 1160 ÷ 294.6 = 3.94 seconds.

questions.q: Scholarship-fund audit — Two runners start together in opposite directions on a 1140 m circular track at 190 m/s and 142.5 m/s. After how many seconds do they first meet?

questions.q: Scholarship-fund audit — Two triangles are similar. A side of 5 cm in the smaller corresponds to 30 cm in the larger. If another smaller side is 11 cm, what is its corresponding larger side?
questions.e: The scale factor is 30/5 = 6; therefore 11 × 6 = 66 cm.

questions.q: Training-centre exercise — Two triangles are similar. A side of 8 cm in the smaller corresponds to 16 cm in the larger. If another smaller side is 4 cm, what is its corresponding larger side?
questions.e: The scale factor is 16/8 = 2; therefore 4 × 2 = 8 cm.

questions.q: Training-centre exercise — A supplier wants a 25% profit on an item costing Rs 24800, even after allowing a 25% discount on its marked price. What marked price is required?
questions.e: Required selling price is 24800 × 125/100. Since that is 75% of the marked price, divide it by 0.75.

questions.q: Survey-unit review — A supplier wants a 20% profit on an item costing Rs 43200, even after allowing a 20% discount on its marked price. What marked price is required?
questions.e: Required selling price is 43200 × 120/100. Since that is 80% of the marked price, divide it by 0.8.

questions.q: District-office worksheet — Two pipes can fill a tank in 504 and 756 minutes, while a leak can empty it in 1512 minutes. If all three remain open, when will the tank fill?
questions.e: Net rate = 1/504 + 1/756 − 1/1512 = 1/378, so the tank fills in 378 minutes.

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — Two pipes can fill a tank in 492 and 738 minutes, while a leak can empty it in 1476 minutes. If all three remain open, when will the tank fill?
questions.e: Net rate = 1/492 + 1/738 − 1/1476 = 1/369, so the tank fills in 369 minutes.

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — A can complete a project in 780 days and B in 1170 days. They work together for 390 days; B then leaves. How many days from the start will A take to finish the project?
questions.e: Together they complete 390 × (1/780 + 1/1170) = 5/6. A needs another 130 days for the remaining 1/6, totalling 520.

questions.q: Scholarship-fund audit — Two batches assessed by a scholarship fund contain 30 and 11 candidates with mean scores 60 and 80. What is the combined mean?
questions.e: Use the weighted mean: (30 × 60 + 11 × 80) ÷ 41 = 65.37.

questions.q: Warehouse planning case — A tank contains 500 litres of a 40% solution. 100 litres of the mixture are removed and replaced by water. What is the new concentration?
questions.e: Removing one-fifth of a uniform mixture removes one-fifth of its solute. The remaining concentration is 40% × 4/5 = 32%.

questions.q: Scholarship-fund audit — A tank contains 490 litres of a 35% solution. 98 litres of the mixture are removed and replaced by water. What is the new concentration?
questions.e: Removing one-fifth of a uniform mixture removes one-fifth of its solute. The remaining concentration is 35% × 4/5 = 28%.

questions.q: District-office worksheet — Two batches assessed by a district office contain 37 and 18 candidates with mean scores 56 and 74. What is the combined mean?

questions.q: Health-programme report — A can complete a project in 768 days and B in 1152 days. They work together for 384 days; B then leaves. How many days from the start will A take to finish the project?

questions.q: Warehouse planning case — A quarterly table for a warehouse records 710, 375, and 125 completed cases in three months. What percentage of the three-month total was completed in the first month?

questions.q: Training-centre exercise — A quarterly table for a training centre records 410, 225, and 110 completed cases in three months. What percentage of the three-month total was completed in the first month?

questions.q: District-office worksheet — A bus leaves a district office at 87 km/h. 2 hours later, a car follows on the same route at 100 km/h. How long after the car starts will it catch the bus?
questions.e: The bus has a 174 km lead. Relative speed is 13 km/h, so catch-up time is 13.38 hours.

questions.q:
Read the passage: “A public garden planted fast-growing trees. Shade increased quickly, but the same species became vulnerable to one disease. The gardeners decided that future planting should include several species even if shade grew more slowly.”

What prompted the change in planting?
o: All trees grew at the same rate
Dependence on one species created a shared risk
questions.e: A single disease could threaten many trees of the same species.

questions.q:
Read the passage: “A public garden planted fast-growing trees. Shade increased quickly, but the same species became vulnerable to one disease. The gardeners decided that future planting should include several species even if shade grew more slowly.”

What trade-off did the gardeners accept?

Slower shade growth in exchange for diversity
Less diversity for more immediate shade
questions.e: They prioritised resilience over the fastest possible shade.

His explanation was adequate to the situation. The policy is adverse to public interest. This environment is conducive to learning. The solution is suited to our needs.
He hid behind the door when he saw the teacher coming.
He stood before the judge in silence.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 232: Rule “Used for benefit or harm” corresponds to Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) “Regular exercise is beneficial to health. Loud music is detrimental to concentration. Smoking is injurious to health.”.

questions.q: In Articles, which Example Sentence corresponds to Rule “No article before metals”?

President Lincoln abolished slavery. Doctor Ali is on leave today.
Gold is a precious metal. Iron is used in construction.
Honesty is the best policy. Love conquers all.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 225: Rule “No article before metals” corresponds to Example Sentence “Gold is a precious metal. Iron is used in construction.”.

questions.q: For Active and Passive Voice, which Type–Passive Formula association is accurate?

questions.e: Repository English reference, page 224: Type “Order/Command” corresponds to Passive Formula “Let + Object + be + V3”.

questions.q: For Sentences, Clauses and Phrases, which Connector Type–Structure Pattern association is accurate?

Subordinating Conjunctions (Adverb Clause) — Independent clause, nonessential dependent clause, clause or Independent clause essential dependent clause clause
Relative Pronouns (Adjective Clause) — Independent clause; conjunctive adverb, independent clause
Coordinating Conjunctions (FANBOYS) — Independent clause, coordinating conjunction, independent clause
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 234: Connector Type “Coordinating Conjunctions (FANBOYS)” corresponds to Structure Pattern “Independent clause, coordinating conjunction, independent clause”.

Introduce a dependent clause describing a noun

Join two independent clauses in compound sentences
