questions.q: Survey-unit review — A two-digit number has digit sum 5; reversing its digits increases it by 9. What is the original number?
questions.e: Let the tens and units digits be x and y. Then x + y = 5 and 9(x − y) = -9; hence x = 2, y = 3.

questions.q: Scholarship-fund audit — A two-digit number has digit sum 2; reversing its digits reduces it by 18. What is the original number?

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — Worker B takes 79 days for a task. Worker A is 20% more efficient than B. How many days would A need for the same task?

questions.e: Net rate = 1/84 + 1/126 − 1/252 = 1/63, so the tank fills in 63 minutes.

questions.q: Training-centre exercise — Two runners start together in opposite directions on a 1200 m circular track at 300 m/s and 200 m/s. After how many seconds do they first meet?
questions.e: In opposite directions their relative speed is 500 m/s, so time is 1200 ÷ 500 = 2.4 seconds.

questions.q: Transport-depot calculation — What is the least number greater than 600 that leaves remainder 23 when divided by both 24 and 25, given that 24 and 25 are coprime?
questions.e: A common remainder means N − 23 is a multiple of lcm(24, 25) = 600. The least eligible N is 600 + 23 = 623.

questions.q: Health-programme report — What is the least number greater than 650 that leaves remainder 24 when divided by both 25 and 26, given that 25 and 26 are coprime?
questions.e: A common remainder means N − 24 is a multiple of lcm(25, 26) = 650. The least eligible N is 650 + 24 = 674.

questions.q: Transport-depot calculation — A can complete a project in 180 days and B in 270 days. They work together for 90 days; B then leaves. How many days from the start will A take to finish the project?
questions.e: Together they complete 90 × (1/180 + 1/270) = 5/6. A needs another 30 days for the remaining 1/6, totalling 120.

questions.q: Health-programme report — A can complete a project in 192 days and B in 288 days. They work together for 96 days; B then leaves. How many days from the start will A take to finish the project?

questions.q:
Read the passage: “An evaluation compared two training groups. Volunteers chose the new course, while those in the old course were assigned by their employers. The evaluator said higher scores in the new group could reflect motivation as well as teaching.”

Which design would better isolate the course’s effect?
o: Assign comparable participants to courses at random
Allow only top scorers to volunteer
questions.e: Random assignment reduces selection differences between groups.

questions.q:
Read the passage: “An evaluation compared two training groups. Volunteers chose the new course, while those in the old course were assigned by their employers. The evaluator said higher scores in the new group could reflect motivation as well as teaching.”

Why are the higher scores inconclusive?
o: The groups may have differed before training began
Every participant had the same motivation
Scores cannot be compared at all
questions.e: Self-selection may create a motivational difference unrelated to teaching.

questions.q:
Read the passage: “A village installed a water meter at its main tank. The measured outflow exceeded the total recorded at households. Engineers investigated leaks but also checked whether every household meter was working before estimating the loss.”

Why check household meters?
o: Faulty readings could mimic or exaggerate a leak
questions.e: A measurement error can explain part of the difference.

questions.q:
Read the passage: “A village installed a water meter at its main tank. The measured outflow exceeded the total recorded at households. Engineers investigated leaks but also checked whether every household meter was working before estimating the loss.”

What does the difference between the two totals establish on its own?
o: That all household meters are accurate
The exact location of every leak
questions.e: The difference alone does not identify its cause.

questions.q: Which Type is associated with Definition “Can be counted” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 229: Type “Countable Noun” corresponds to Definition “Can be counted”.

questions.q: Which Part of Speech is associated with Definition “Describes action, occurrence, or state” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 229: Part of Speech “Verb” corresponds to Definition “Describes action, occurrence, or state”.

questions.q: In Prepositions, which Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) corresponds to Rule “Used for effort, feeling, state”?
o: He persisted in his efforts. She found satisfaction in helping others. He was disappointed in the result.
He applied for a job in the bank.
I applied to the university last week.
She is married to a doctor. He is engaged to his cousin.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 232: Rule “Used for effort, feeling, state” corresponds to Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) “He persisted in his efforts. She found satisfaction in helping others. He was disappointed in the result.”.

questions.q: In Twelve-Tense Reference, which Structure corresponds to Tense “Future Simple”?
o: subject + base verb (s/es for third-person singular)
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 244: Tense “Future Simple” corresponds to Structure “subject + will/shall + base verb”.

questions.q: In Prepositions, which Preposition corresponds to Rule “Sitting beside something”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 231: Rule “Sitting beside something” corresponds to Preposition “By”.

questions.q: In Twelve-Tense Reference, which Structure corresponds to Tense “Future Perfect Continuous”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 244: Tense “Future Perfect Continuous” corresponds to Structure “subject + will/shall have been + verb-ing”.

questions.q: In Articles, which Example Sentence corresponds to Rule “Before a certain or specific unidentified thing”?
o: Gold is a precious metal. Iron is used in construction.
I saw a certain bird flying high. A certain man was looking for you.
A servant must obey his master. Anyone can become a leader.
I met Ahmed yesterday. Fatima is my sister.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 225: Rule “Before a certain or specific unidentified thing” corresponds to Example Sentence “I saw a certain bird flying high. A certain man was looking for you.”.

questions.q: In Active and Passive Voice, which Passive Formula corresponds to Type “Order/Command”?
o: You are advised to + V1 + Object
You are requested to + V1 + Object
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 224: Type “Order/Command” corresponds to Passive Formula “Let + Object + be + V3”.

questions.q: In Prepositions, which Example Word corresponds to Type “Greeting Interjection”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 231: Type “Greeting Interjection” corresponds to Example Word “Hey!”.

questions.q: In Prepositions, which Example Word corresponds to Type “Emotive Interjection”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 231: Type “Emotive Interjection” corresponds to Example Word “Ouch!”.

questions.q: In Sentences, Clauses and Phrases, which Definition / Explanation corresponds to Sentence Type “Compound Sentence”?
o: A sentence that has two or I more independent clauses and at least one dependent clause.
A sentence with one independent clause and one or more dependent clauses.
A sentence with two or more independent clauses, joined by a coordinating conjunction, conjunctive adverb, or semicolon.
A sentence with only one independent clause. It expresses a complete thought.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 233: Sentence Type “Compound Sentence” corresponds to Definition / Explanation “A sentence with two or more independent clauses, joined by a coordinating conjunction, conjunctive adverb, or semicolon.”.

questions.q: In Parts of Speech, which Sentence Example corresponds to Type “Interrogative Pronoun”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 230: Type “Interrogative Pronoun” corresponds to Sentence Example “Who called you?”.

questions.q: In Prepositions, which Preposition corresponds to Rule “Standing in front of something”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 232: Rule “Standing in front of something” corresponds to Preposition “Before”.

questions.q: In Direct and Indirect Speech, which Reporting Verb corresponds to Type “Prayer”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 228: Type “Prayer” corresponds to Reporting Verb “Prayed”.

questions.q: In Parts of Speech, which Definition corresponds to Type “Demonstrative Pronoun”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 230: Type “Demonstrative Pronoun” corresponds to Definition “Points to specific things”.

questions.q: In Direct and Indirect Speech, which Direct Speech corresponds to Indirect Speech “The Previous Day / The Day Before”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 227: Indirect Speech “The Previous Day / The Day Before” corresponds to Direct Speech “Yesterday”.

questions.q: In Parts of Speech, which Examples corresponds to Part of Speech “Pronoun”?
o: jump (Action - Regular Verb)sing (Action - Irregular Verb)is (State - Linking Verb)
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 229: Part of Speech “Pronoun” corresponds to Examples “I (Personal - Person)That (Demonstrative - Thing)Who (Interrogative - Person)”.

questions.q: Convert to the passive: “Close the gate at sunset.”
o: The gate was closed at sunset.
The gate is closed at sunset by you.
Let the gate be closed at sunset.
questions.e: An imperative becomes “Let … be + participle” or “… should be + participle”.

questions.q: Convert to the passive: “The registrar had issued the notice.”
o: The notice was issued by the registrar.
The notice had issued by the registrar.
The notice had been issued by the registrar.
The notice has been issued by the registrar.
questions.e: Past perfect active becomes had been + participle.

questions.q: Find the error: “The draft policy (A) has circulated (B) to all provincial departments (C) for comment (D).”
questions.e: The draft did not circulate anything: it needs the passive has been circulated.

questions.q: In Direct and Indirect Speech, which Direct Speech corresponds to Indirect Speech “She asked what my name was.”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 227: Indirect Speech “She asked what my name was.” corresponds to Direct Speech “She said, "What is your name?"”.

questions.q: Find the error: “The report shows (A) that the scheme’s effect (B) on rural incomes (C) was continual and unbroken (D).”
questions.e: Continual means repeated with breaks, so it contradicts unbroken. Use continuous.

questions.q: In Sentences, Clauses and Phrases, which Explanation / Usage corresponds to Connector Type “Relative Pronouns (Adjective Clause)”?
o: Introduce a dependent clause describing a noun
Join two independent clauses, showing relationship (cause, contrast, result, etc.)
Join two independent clauses in compound sentences
Used as subject or object in a sentence
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 234: Connector Type “Relative Pronouns (Adjective Clause)” corresponds to Explanation / Usage “Introduce a dependent clause describing a noun”.

questions.q: In Direct and Indirect Speech, which Direct Speech corresponds to Indirect Speech “The Following Week”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 227: Indirect Speech “The Following Week” corresponds to Direct Speech “Next week”.

questions.q: From the minister’s silence the press ____ that a decision had already been taken.
questions.e: The listener infers; the speaker implies.

questions.q: For Sentences, Clauses and Phrases, which Preposition–Rule association is accurate?
o: In / On — Desire/longing related to personality
Of / For / To — Retreat or reversal movement
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 233: Preposition “With” corresponds to Rule “Comparison between similar things”.

questions.q: In Direct and Indirect Speech, which Direct Speech corresponds to Indirect Speech “Past Continuous”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 226: Indirect Speech “Past Continuous” corresponds to Direct Speech “Present Continuous”.

questions.q: Find the error: “The committee comprises of (A) seven members (B), three of whom (C) are officials (D).”
questions.e: Comprise takes no of. Write “comprises seven members” or “is composed of seven members”.

questions.q: Find the error: “By whom (A) the decision (B) was taken (C) remains unclear (D).”
questions.e: The passive question requires inversion: “By whom the decision was taken” works only as an embedded clause; as a direct question it must be “By whom was the decision taken?”

questions.q: It ____ that the department ignored the earlier warnings.
questions.e: The impersonal passive of a reporting verb is it is + participle + that.

questions.q: Find the error: “The judgment was a historical (A) moment for (B) the protection of (C) fundamental rights (D).”
questions.e: A moment of importance in history is historic; historical merely means relating to the past.

questions.q: In Active and Passive Voice, which Passive Formula corresponds to Tense “Future Perfect”?
o: Object + will/shall + have been + V3 + by + Subject
Object + will/shall + be + V3 + by + Subject
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 224: Tense “Future Perfect” corresponds to Passive Formula “Object + will/shall + have been + V3 + by + Subject”.

questions.q: In Twelve-Tense Reference, which Tense corresponds to Structure “subject + has/have + past participle”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 244: Structure “subject + has/have + past participle” corresponds to Tense “Present Perfect”.

questions.q: Candidates should ____ précis writing daily; regular ____ is essential.
questions.e: In British usage practise is the verb and practice the noun.

questions.q: In Sentences, Clauses and Phrases, which Example corresponds to Sentence Type “Simple Sentence”?
o: A. When it rained, we stayed inside. B. We stayed inside when it rained. C. My car, which is red, is fast. D. The man who called is my friend.
Although it rained, we went outside, and we enjoyed the walk.
A. He studied, and he passed. B. He studied; therefore, he passed. C. He studied; he passed.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 233: Sentence Type “Simple Sentence” corresponds to Example “She reads books.”.

questions.q: In Articles, which Example Sentence corresponds to Rule “With newspapers”?
o: He is a teacher. She bought a university bag. (Note: "University" starts with a consonant sound /juː/)
I read the Dawn every morning.
He is the Shakespeare of our times.
He saw an owl in the tree. She is an honest girl.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 225: Rule “With newspapers” corresponds to Example Sentence “I read the Dawn every morning.”.

questions.q: In Active and Passive Voice, which Passive Formula corresponds to Tense “Past Continuous”?
o: Object + has/have + been + V3 + by + Subject
Object + was/were + being + V3 + by + Subject
Object + had been + V3 + by + Subject
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 224: Tense “Past Continuous” corresponds to Passive Formula “Object + was/were + being + V3 + by + Subject”.

questions.q: In Articles, which Rule corresponds to Example Sentence “Man is mortal. Woman has always played a vital role.”?
o: No article before hell, heaven, or God (used reverently)
Before a certain or specific unidentified thing
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 225: Example Sentence “Man is mortal. Woman has always played a vital role.” corresponds to Rule “No article before man/woman (used generally)”.

questions.q: For Sentences, Clauses and Phrases, which Connector Type–Example association is accurate?
o: Conjunctive Adverbs — Because he was ill, he stayed home. He stayed home because he was ill.
Coordinating Conjunctions (FANBOYS) — He plays cricket, and she plays football.
Relative Pronouns (Adjective Clause) — He was late; however, he completed the task.
Subordinating Conjunctions (Adverb Clause) — My friend, who is a doctor, is coming. People who work hard succeed.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 234: Connector Type “Coordinating Conjunctions (FANBOYS)” corresponds to Example “He plays cricket, and she plays football.”.

questions.q: In Twelve-Tense Reference, which Example corresponds to Tense “Past Perfect”?
o: She had been writing for an hour.
She had written before I arrived.
She will be writing at noon.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 244: Tense “Past Perfect” corresponds to Example “She had written before I arrived.”.

questions.q: In Active and Passive Voice, which Example (Active) corresponds to Tense “Present Indefinite”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 224: Tense “Present Indefinite” corresponds to Example (Active) “He writes a letter.”.

questions.q: Find the error: “In Iqbal’s poetry (A), he argues (B) that the self (C) is dynamic (D).”
questions.e: He cannot refer back to the possessive Iqbal’s. Write “In his poetry, Iqbal argues …”.

questions.q: In Twelve-Tense Reference, which Tense corresponds to Structure “subject + was/were + verb-ing”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 244: Structure “subject + was/were + verb-ing” corresponds to Tense “Past Continuous”.

questions.q: In Articles, which Example Sentence corresponds to Rule “Use the with a class of animals, birds, or objects”?
o: The lion is a dangerous animal. The eagle soars high. The computer has changed the world.
The rich must help the poor. The elderly need care.
I visited the Eiffel Tower. He reads the Economist every week. She works in the Parliament House.
He is the best player on the team.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 225: Rule “Use the with a class of animals, birds, or objects” corresponds to Example Sentence “The lion is a dangerous animal. The eagle soars high. The computer has changed the world.”.

questions.q: In Articles, which Example Sentence corresponds to Rule “Use the with books, journals, and buildings”?
o: He is the best player on the team.
I visited the Eiffel Tower. He reads the Economist every week. She works in the Parliament House.
She was the first to arrive.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 225: Rule “Use the with books, journals, and buildings” corresponds to Example Sentence “I visited the Eiffel Tower. He reads the Economist every week. She works in the Parliament House.”.

questions.q: Find the error: “An honest officer (A) who refuses (B) bribes is more rarer (C) than we admit (D).”
questions.e: Rarer is already comparative; more is a double marker.

questions.q: Find the error: “The government announced (A) their new housing policy (B) without consulting (C) the provinces (D).”
questions.e: Government as one body takes its, not their.

questions.q: Find the error: “She had wrote (A) three chapters (B) before the deadline (C) was extended (D).”
questions.e: The past perfect takes the participle written: had written.

questions.q: Transport-depot calculation — A geometric sequence has first term 8 and common ratio 2. What is its 7th term?
Training-centre exercise — A geometric sequence has first term 39 and common ratio 3. What is its 6th term?
Relief-camp planning case — A vehicle covers two equal-distance legs at 84 km/h and 94 km/h. What is its average speed for the complete journey?
questions.e: For equal distances the harmonic mean applies: 2uv/(u + v) = 88.72 km/h.

questions.q: District-office worksheet — A vehicle covers two equal-distance legs at 86 km/h and 98 km/h. What is its average speed for the complete journey?
questions.e: For equal distances the harmonic mean applies: 2uv/(u + v) = 91.61 km/h.

questions.q: Health-programme report — A 35 m by 16 m rectangular courtyard has a uniform path 5 m wide inside its boundary. What area does the path cover?
questions.e: Path area = outer area − inner area = 560 − 25×6 = 410 m².

questions.q: Transport-depot calculation — A 34 m by 15 m rectangular courtyard has a uniform path 4 m wide inside its boundary. What area does the path cover?

جو دو الفاظ یا جملوں کو مالنے کے لیے استعمال ہو۔
جو کسی کو پکارنے کے لیے استعمال ہو۔
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 211: حرفِ اتصال — جو دو الفاظ یا جملوں کو مالنے کے لیے استعمال ہو۔

questions.q: یہ تعریف کس اصطلاح کی ہے؟ “وہ فعل جو موجودہ وقت میں ہو رہا ہو۔”
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 211: فعل حال — وہ فعل جو موجودہ وقت میں ہو رہا ہو۔

questions.q: ان اصطلاحات—حرو فِ مهملہ، حرو فِ شمسیة، حرو فِ قمریة، متحرک اور ساکن میں فرق—میں درست اصطلاح اور تعریف کا جوڑا منتخب کریں۔
o: حرو فِ مهملہ — وہ حروف جن پر کوئی نقطہ نہیں 52 ہوتا۔ کل
حرو فِ شمسیة — کل: 51 ایسے حروف جن کے ساتھ "ال" لگانے پر "ل" واضح پڑھی جاتی ہے
حرو فِ قمریة — متحرک: جس حرف پر حرکت (زبر، زیر، پیش) ہو۔ساکن: جس پر کوئی حرکت نہ ہو بلکہ جزم ہو۔
متحرک اور ساکن میں فرق — کل: 51 ایسے حروف جن کے ساتھ "ال" لگانے پر "ل" کا تلفظ نہیں ہوتا
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 213: حرو فِ مهملہ — وہ حروف جن پر کوئی نقطہ نہیں 52 ہوتا۔ کل

questions.q: یہ تعریف کس اصطلاح کی ہے؟ “مسند (خبر) +مسند علیہ (مبتدا)”
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 215: بڑے جزو — مسند (خبر) +مسند علیہ (مبتدا)

questions.q: یہ تعریف کس اصطلاح کی ہے؟ “جو کسی کام کو کرنے والے پر دلالت کرے (مصدر سے بنا ہو)”
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 208: اسمِ فاعل — جو کسی کام کو کرنے والے پر دلالت کرے (مصدر سے بنا ہو)

questions.q: تعریف “وہ اسم جو کسی چیز یا فعل کے لیے آلہ یا اوزار کو ظاہر کرے۔” اور مثال “قلم، قینچی، چھری” کس اصطلاح کو ظاہر کرتی ہیں؟
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 209: آلہ — وہ اسم جو کسی چیز یا فعل کے لیے آلہ یا اوزار کو ظاہر کرے۔

questions.q: تعریف “ایسا مرکب جو مکمل مفہوم دے، یعنی جملہ مکمل ہو۔” اور مثال “علی اسکول گیا، بچہ کھیل رہا ہے۔” کس اصطلاح کو ظاہر کرتی ہیں؟
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 214: مرک بِ تام — ایسا مرکب جو مکمل مفہوم دے، یعنی جملہ مکمل ہو۔

questions.q: تعریف “عدد اور اسم پر مشتمل ترکیب۔” اور مثال “تین لڑکے، پانچ کتابیں” کس اصطلاح کو ظاہر کرتی ہیں؟
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 214: مرک بِ عددی — عدد اور اسم پر مشتمل ترکیب۔

questions.q: یہ تعریف کس اصطلاح کی ہے؟ “وہ صفت جو کسی چیز کی تعداد ظاہر کرے۔”
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 210: عددی — وہ صفت جو کسی چیز کی تعداد ظاہر کرے۔

questions.q: ان اصطلاحات—ماضی تمنائی / شرطی، ۔ حرف علت، ۔ حرف عطف، حرف تردید—میں درست اصطلاح اور تعریف کا جوڑا منتخب کریں۔
o: ۔ حرف علت — وہ حرف جو دو الفاظ یا جملوں کو مالئے
۔ حرف عطف — وہ حرف جو کسی شے کے ہونے یا نہ ہونے میں شک ظاہر کرے
حرف تردید — وہ حرف جو کسی سبب یا علت کو ظاہر کرے
ماضی تمنائی / شرطی — ایسا ماضی جو خواہش یا شرط کے اظہار کے لیے ہو، حقیقت میں واقع نہ ہوا ہو
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 211: ماضی تمنائی / شرطی — ایسا ماضی جو خواہش یا شرط کے اظہار کے لیے ہو، حقیقت میں واقع نہ ہوا ہو

questions.q: “مرک بِ تابع و متبوع (مہمل)” کی درست تعریف منتخب کریں۔
o: ایک اسم دوسرے کا بدل بنے۔
دو بامعنی الفاظ پر مشتمل، جہاں ایک دوسرے کی پیروی کرتا ہو۔
ایک بے معنی لفظ اور ایک بامعنی لفظ پر مشتمل۔
اسم کی مزید وضاحت کرنے والا دوسرا اسم۔
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 214: مرک بِ تابع و متبوع (مہمل) — ایک بے معنی لفظ اور ایک بامعنی لفظ پر مشتمل۔

questions.q: ان اصطلاحات—اسمِ مفعول، اسمِ جمع، اسمِ معاوضہ، اسمِ حالیہّ—میں درست اصطلاح اور تعریف کا جوڑا منتخب کریں۔
o: اسمِ معاوضہ — جو فاعل یا مفعول کی حالت یا کیفیت کو ظاہر کرے
اسمِ جمع — جو کسی معاوضے، اجرت یا مزدوری کے لیے استعمال ہو
اسمِ مفعول — جو کسی کام کا نشانہ بننے والے پر دلالت کرے
اسمِ حالیہّ — جو کسی گروہ یا مجموعے پر دلالت کرے
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 208: اسمِ مفعول — جو کسی کام کا نشانہ بننے والے پر دلالت کرے

questions.q:
Read the passage: “A local market reported more registered traders after fees were reduced. Some traders explained that they had been operating before the change but had never registered. Officials separated newly registered businesses from genuinely new businesses.”

What would overstate growth in business activity?
o: Reporting both registration and operation dates
Asking when each trader began operating
Counting every new registration as a new business
questions.e: New registrations are not necessarily new economic activity.

questions.q:
Read the passage: “A local market reported more registered traders after fees were reduced. Some traders explained that they had been operating before the change but had never registered. Officials separated newly registered businesses from genuinely new businesses.”

Why make that distinction?
o: A registered trader cannot have operated before
Registration can rise without the same rise in actual businesses
questions.e: Some existing traders may simply have entered the records.

questions.q: In Sentences, Clauses and Phrases, which Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) corresponds to Rule “Travel using private vehicles”?
o: He goes to the office on foot every day.
She arrived in a car. He was taken in an ambulance. They rode in a taxi.
He compared one type of mango with another.
People in our city travel mostly by train.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 233: Rule “Travel using private vehicles” corresponds to Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) “She arrived in a car. He was taken in an ambulance. They rode in a taxi.”.

questions.q: In Prepositions, which Sentence Example corresponds to Type “Preposition of Manner”?
o: I stayed home because I was sick.
You can have either tea or coffee.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 231: Type “Preposition of Manner” corresponds to Sentence Example “He won by luck.”.

questions.q: In Parts of Speech, which Sentence Example corresponds to Type “Common Noun”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 229: Type “Common Noun” corresponds to Sentence Example “I read a book.”.

questions.q: He performed better in the interview than ____.
questions.e: Complete the comparison: better than I did. The subject form is needed.

questions.q: In Direct and Indirect Speech, which Indirect Speech corresponds to Direct Speech “Must”?
o: He asked where I was going.
He asked if I was coming.
She asked if I liked chocolate.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 227: Direct Speech “Must” corresponds to Indirect Speech “Had to”.

questions.q: Find the error: “The population of Karachi (A) is greater (B) than Lahore (C) by several million (D).”
questions.e: Compare like with like: “than that of Lahore”. Two words are inserted, and nothing else moves.

questions.q: In Prepositions, which Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) corresponds to Rule “Comparison between dissimilar things”?
o: The power was cut off during the storm. He jumped off the wall.
You can't compare apples to oranges.
She is sitting at the desk, writing a letter.
The book is lying on the table.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 232: Rule “Comparison between dissimilar things” corresponds to Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) “You can't compare apples to oranges.”.

questions.q: For Parts of Speech, which Part of Speech–Definition association is accurate?
o: Verb — Describes a noun or pronoun
Pronoun — Describes action, occurrence, or state
Noun — Refers to a person, place, thing, or concept
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 229: Part of Speech “Noun” corresponds to Definition “Refers to a person, place, thing, or concept”.

questions.q: In Direct and Indirect Speech, which Example corresponds to Type “Wonder”?
o: He said, "What a beautiful view!" → He wondered that it was a VERY beautiful view.
He said, "Hurrah! We won the match." → He exclaimed with joy that they had won the match.
He said, "Alas! He is dead." → He exclaimed with sorrow that he was dead.
He said, "May you live long!" → He wished that I might live long.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 228: Type “Wonder” corresponds to Example “He said, "What a beautiful view!" → He wondered that it was a VERY beautiful view.”.

questions.q: Find the error: “Neither the clerk (A) nor the officers (B) was aware (C) of the change (D).”
questions.e: Nor points the verb at the nearer subject, officers, so were is required.

questions.q: In Direct and Indirect Speech, which Reporting Verb corresponds to Type “Proposal”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 228: Type “Proposal” corresponds to Reporting Verb “Proposed”.

questions.q: In Parts of Speech, which Definition corresponds to Type “Adverb of Time”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 230: Type “Adverb of Time” corresponds to Definition “Describes when action happens”.

questions.q: In Prepositions, which Preposition corresponds to Rule “Used for working position”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 231: Rule “Used for working position” corresponds to Preposition “At”.

questions.q: In Direct and Indirect Speech, which Direct Speech corresponds to Indirect Speech “She requested not to disturb her.”?
o: He said, "The sun rises in the east."
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 228: Indirect Speech “She requested not to disturb her.” corresponds to Direct Speech “She said, "Don't disturb me."”.

questions.q: Find the error: “She has been working (A) in this department (B) since the last (C) five years (D).”
questions.e: A duration takes for, not since the last: “for the last five years”.

questions.q: In Parts of Speech, which Example Word corresponds to Type “Linking Verb”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 230: Type “Linking Verb” corresponds to Example Word “is”.

questions.q: In Parts of Speech, which Definition corresponds to Part of Speech “Verb”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 229: Part of Speech “Verb” corresponds to Definition “Describes action, occurrence, or state”.

questions.q: Two corrections are possible for “If I would have known, I would have informed you.” Which changes fewer words?
o: If I had known, I would have informed you.
Had I known, I would have informed you.
Knowing that, I would have informed you.
I would have informed you if I had been aware.
questions.e: Replacing would have with had changes two words and keeps the structure.

questions.q: In Direct and Indirect Speech, which Direct Speech corresponds to Indirect Speech “He says that he likes tea.”?
o: He said, "The sun rises in the east."
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 226: Indirect Speech “He says that he likes tea.” corresponds to Direct Speech “He says, "I like tea."”.

questions.q: Find the error: “The number of applications (A) received this year (B) have exceeded (C) all previous records (D).”
questions.e: Pass 1: the head noun is number, which is singular — has exceeded.

questions.q: In Prepositions, which Rule corresponds to Preposition “Before”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 232: Preposition “Before” corresponds to Rule “Standing in front of something”.

questions.q: In Prepositions, which Sentence Example corresponds to Type “Coordinating Conjunction”?
o: I stayed home because I was sick.
You can have either tea or coffee.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 231: Type “Coordinating Conjunction” corresponds to Sentence Example “I like tea and coffee.”.

questions.q: In Articles, which Example Sentence corresponds to Rule “No article before common diseases (except a few)”?
o: Man is mortal. Woman has always played a vital role.
He caught the measles last month. She was diagnosed with the mumps.
He is suffering from malaria. She has diabetes.
He hopes to go to heaven. We must fear God.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 225: Rule “No article before common diseases (except a few)” corresponds to Example Sentence “He is suffering from malaria. She has diabetes.”.

questions.q: In Sentences, Clauses and Phrases, which Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) corresponds to Rule “Comparison between similar things”?
o: He is ambitious of fame. She has ambition for power. He aspires to greatness.
The army retrogressed from the battlefield. They had to retreat from enemy lines.
He sat in the tree, hidden by leaves. He sat on the branch and started whistling.
He compared one type of mango with another.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 233: Rule “Comparison between similar things” corresponds to Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) “He compared one type of mango with another.”.

questions.q: In Sentences, Clauses and Phrases, which Preposition corresponds to Rule “Retreat or reversal movement”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 233: Rule “Retreat or reversal movement” corresponds to Preposition “From”.

questions.q: In Twelve-Tense Reference, which Tense corresponds to Structure “subject + is/am/are + verb-ing”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 244: Structure “subject + is/am/are + verb-ing” corresponds to Tense “Present Continuous”.

questions.q: In Sentences, Clauses and Phrases, which Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) corresponds to Rule “Temporary or transit stop”?
o: He came on a bus. She travels on a train daily. They flew on a plane.
We stopped at Dubai on our way to Saudi Arabia.
He goes to the office on foot every day.
She arrived in a car. He was taken in an ambulance. They rode in a taxi.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 233: Rule “Temporary or transit stop” corresponds to Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) “We stopped at Dubai on our way to Saudi Arabia.”.

questions.q: In Active and Passive Voice, which Passive Formula corresponds to Tense “Past Indefinite”?
o: Object + is/am/are + being + V3 + by + Subject
Object + was/were + being + V3 + by + Subject
Object + will/shall + be + V3 + by + Subject
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 224: Tense “Past Indefinite” corresponds to Passive Formula “Object + was/were + V3 + by + Subject”.

questions.q: In Articles, which Example Sentence corresponds to Rule “Before consonant sounds (not just consonants)”?
o: A servant must obey his master. Anyone can become a leader.
I saw a certain bird flying high. A certain man was looking for you.
He is a teacher. She bought a university bag. (Note: "University" starts with a consonant sound /juː/)
I met Ahmed yesterday. Fatima is my sister.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 225: Rule “Before consonant sounds (not just consonants)” corresponds to Example Sentence “He is a teacher. She bought a university bag. (Note: "University" starts with a consonant sound /juː/)”.

questions.q: In Sentences, Clauses and Phrases, which Structure Pattern corresponds to Connector Type “Coordinating Conjunctions (FANBOYS)”?
o: Dependent clause, independent clause or Independent clause dependent clause
Independent clause; conjunctive adverb, independent clause
Independent clause, coordinating conjunction, independent clause
Independent clause, nonessential dependent clause, clause or Independent clause essential dependent clause clause
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 234: Connector Type “Coordinating Conjunctions (FANBOYS)” corresponds to Structure Pattern “Independent clause, coordinating conjunction, independent clause”.

questions.q: In Articles, which Example Sentence corresponds to Rule “No article before hell, heaven, or God (used reverently)”?
o: He visited the United States. She works in the Netherlands.
The moon looks beautiful tonight. The sun rises in the east.
He hopes to go to heaven. We must fear God.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 225: Rule “No article before hell, heaven, or God (used reverently)” corresponds to Example Sentence “He hopes to go to heaven. We must fear God.”.

questions.q: Find the error: “The scissors used in the laboratory (A) is kept (B) in the second drawer (C) of the cupboard (D).”
questions.e: Scissors is a two-part noun and takes a plural verb: are kept. Write “a pair of scissors is” if you need the singular.

questions.q: In Active and Passive Voice, which Passive Formula corresponds to Type “Request (Please)”?
o: You are requested to + V1 + Object
You are advised to + V1 + Object
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 224: Type “Request (Please)” corresponds to Passive Formula “You are requested to + V1 + Object”.

questions.q: In Twelve-Tense Reference, which Example corresponds to Tense “Present Continuous”?
o: She has been writing for an hour.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 244: Tense “Present Continuous” corresponds to Example “She is writing now.”.

questions.q: In Active and Passive Voice, which Active Formula corresponds to Tense “Future Indefinite”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 224: Tense “Future Indefinite” corresponds to Active Formula “Subject + will/shall + V1 + Object”.

questions.q: Find the error: “The inquiry was thorough (A), nevertheless (B) its findings (C) were ignored (D).”
questions.e: The comma should be a semicolon: “thorough; nevertheless, its findings …”.

questions.q: Find the error: “Having examined the file (A) and interviewed the staff (B) over three days (C) in the regional office (D).”
questions.e: There is no main clause anywhere. The whole group is a fragment and needs a subject and finite verb.

questions.q: In Articles, which Example Sentence corresponds to Rule “With proper nouns used in a descriptive sense”?
o: I saw a certain bird flying high. A certain man was looking for you.
He is a teacher. She bought a university bag. (Note: "University" starts with a consonant sound /juː/)
He saw an owl in the tree. She is an honest girl.
He is the Shakespeare of our times.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 225: Rule “With proper nouns used in a descriptive sense” corresponds to Example Sentence “He is the Shakespeare of our times.”.

questions.q: In Active and Passive Voice, which Active Formula corresponds to Tense “Future Continuous ❌”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 224: Tense “Future Continuous ❌” corresponds to Active Formula “Not Possible”.

questions.q: In Articles, which Rule corresponds to Example Sentence “I live in Multan. He visited Pakistan last year.”?
o: No article before cities and countries (general rule)
No article before abstract nouns (general idea)
No article before common diseases (except a few)
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 225: Example Sentence “I live in Multan. He visited Pakistan last year.” corresponds to Rule “No article before cities and countries (general rule)”.

questions.q: Find the error: “The department denied the allegation (A) the press (B) published the documents (C) the next morning (D).”
questions.e: Two independent clauses are fused. Put a full stop or semicolon after allegation.

questions.q: In Twelve-Tense Reference, which Tense corresponds to Structure “subject + base verb (s/es for third-person singular)”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 244: Structure “subject + base verb (s/es for third-person singular)” corresponds to Tense “Present Simple”.

questions.q: In Active and Passive Voice, which Example (Active) corresponds to Type “Request (Please)”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 224: Type “Request (Please)” corresponds to Example (Active) “Please help me.”.

questions.q: Find the error: “The magistrate (A) reached a judicial (B) decision that everyone (C) accepted as fair (D).”
questions.e: A wise decision is judicious. Judicial simply means relating to a court, which adds nothing about the quality of the decision.

questions.q: An ____ economist warned that a collapse was ____.
questions.e: Eminent means distinguished; imminent means about to happen.

questions.q: Find the error: “Having examined the accounts (A), a number of irregularities (B) were detected (C) by the auditors (D).”
questions.e: The irregularities did not examine the accounts. The auditors did, so the auditors must follow the comma.

questions.q: Find the spelling error: “The committee (A) recommended (B) seperate (C) accommodation (D) for the two groups.”
questions.e: The correct spelling is separate — there is a rat in the middle of it.

questions.q: Find the error: “The principle of the college (A) addressed the students (B) on the importance (C) of discipline (D).”
questions.e: The head of a college is the principal; a principle is a rule.

questions.q: Health-programme report — A vehicle covers two equal-distance legs at 34 km/h and 50 km/h. What is its average speed for the complete journey?
questions.e: For equal distances the harmonic mean applies: 2uv/(u + v) = 40.48 km/h.

questions.q: Scholarship-fund audit — An arithmetic sequence begins 39, 47, 55, … . What is the sum of its first 12 terms?
Transport-depot calculation — A vehicle covers two equal-distance legs at 32 km/h and 46 km/h. What is its average speed for the complete journey?
questions.e: For equal distances the harmonic mean applies: 2uv/(u + v) = 37.74 km/h.

questions.q: Warehouse planning case — An arithmetic sequence begins 40, 42, 44, … . What is the sum of its first 13 terms?
Scholarship-fund audit — The roots of x² − 80x + 1591 = 0 differ by 6. What is the larger root?
questions.e: The quadratic factors as (x − 37)(x − 43); the larger root is 43.

questions.q: Warehouse planning case — The roots of x² − 78x + 1520 = 0 differ by 2. What is the larger root?
questions.e: The quadratic factors as (x − 38)(x − 40); the larger root is 40.

questions.q: Training-centre exercise — A bag holds 48 red and 7 blue counters. Two are drawn without replacement. What is the probability that both are red?
questions.e: Multiply the changing probabilities: 48/55 × 47/54 = 75.96%.

questions.q: Scholarship-fund audit — A train 460 m long clears a 150 m platform in 11 seconds. What is its speed in km/h?
questions.e: The train covers 610 m. Its speed is (610)/11 m/s × 3.6 = 199.64 km/h.

questions.q: Training-centre exercise — A train 570 m long clears a 80 m platform in 11 seconds. What is its speed in km/h?
questions.e: The train covers 650 m. Its speed is (650)/11 m/s × 3.6 = 212.73 km/h.

questions.q: Transport-depot calculation — A two-digit number has digit sum 15; reversing its digits increases it by 27. What is the original number?
questions.e: Let the tens and units digits be x and y. Then x + y = 15 and 9(x − y) = -27; hence x = 6, y = 9.

questions.q: Health-programme report — A two-digit number has digit sum 7; reversing its digits reduces it by 63. What is the original number?
questions.e: Let the tens and units digits be x and y. Then x + y = 7 and 9(x − y) = 63; hence x = 7, y = 0.

questions.q: Survey-unit review — 64 passengers paid Rs 2880. An adult ticket cost Rs 50 and a child ticket Rs 30. How many adults travelled?
questions.e: If a is the adult count, 50a + 30(64 − a) = 2880, which gives a = 48.

questions.q: Transport-depot calculation — A 82 m by 19 m rectangular courtyard has a uniform path 4 m wide inside its boundary. What area does the path cover?
questions.e: Path area = outer area − inner area = 1558 − 74×11 = 744 m².

questions.q: Training-centre exercise — 66 passengers paid Rs 3290. An adult ticket cost Rs 55 and a child ticket Rs 35. How many adults travelled?
questions.e: If a is the adult count, 55a + 35(66 − a) = 3290, which gives a = 49.

questions.q: Health-programme report — A 83 m by 20 m rectangular courtyard has a uniform path 5 m wide inside its boundary. What area does the path cover?
questions.e: Path area = outer area − inner area = 1660 − 73×10 = 930 m².

جمع — جو عورت یا مادہ پر دلالت کرے
مذکر — جو مرد یا نر پر دلالت کرے
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 208: مذکر — جو مرد یا نر پر دلالت کرے

questions.q: “اسمِ اشارہ” کی درست تعریف منتخب کریں۔
o: وہ اسم جو کسی شخص کو کسی خاص خصوصیت یا حیثیت کی وجہ سے دیا جاتا ہے۔
وہ اسم جو کسی شخص کو عزت یا احترام سے پکارنے کے لئے استعمال ہوتا ہے۔
وہ اسم جو کسی جملے یا فقرے کے ساتھ منسلک ہوتا ہو اور مکمل معنی تب تک نہیں دیتا جب تک کہ دوسرا جملہ اس کے ساتھ نہ ہو۔
وہ اسم جو کسی چیز یا شخص کی طرف اشارہ کرتا ہو۔
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 209: اسمِ اشارہ — وہ اسم جو کسی چیز یا شخص کی طرف اشارہ کرتا ہو۔

questions.q: تعریف “اسم اور اسمِ اشارہ پر مشتمل ترکیب۔” اور مثال “یہ کتاب، وہ مکان” کس اصطلاح کو ظاہر کرتی ہیں؟
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 214: مرک بِ اشارہ — اسم اور اسمِ اشارہ پر مشتمل ترکیب۔

questions.q: تعریف “وہ فعل جو حکم یا درخواست کے لیے بوال جائے۔” اور مثال “بیٹھو، آؤ، سنو” کس اصطلاح کو ظاہر کرتی ہیں؟
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 211: فعل امر — وہ فعل جو حکم یا درخواست کے لیے بوال جائے۔

questions.q: “مکبر” کی درست تعریف منتخب کریں۔
o: وہ اسم جو کسی چیز کو بڑا یا اہم ظاہر کرے۔
وہ اسم جو کسی چیز یا فعل کے لیے آلہ یا اوزار کو ظاہر کرے۔
وہ اسم جو وقت کو ظاہر کرے۔
وہ اسم جو جگہ یا مقام کو ظاہر کرے۔
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 209: مکبر — وہ اسم جو کسی چیز کو بڑا یا اہم ظاہر کرے۔

questions.q: تعریف “سیدھی لکیر جو مخصوص الفاظ میں زبر کی صورت میں آتی ہے۔” اور مثال “عَلٰی، الِٰہ، رُبمَّٰا” کس اصطلاح کو ظاہر کرتی ہیں؟
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 213: کهڑی زبر — سیدھی لکیر جو مخصوص الفاظ میں زبر کی صورت میں آتی ہے۔

questions.q: ان اصطلاحات—اسمِ علم، ضمیر، اسمِ اشارہ، اسمِ موصول—میں درست اصطلاح اور تعریف کا جوڑا منتخب کریں۔
o: اسمِ موصول — وہ اسم جو کسی شخص یا چیز کی جگہ پر آتا ہے۔
اسمِ علم — وہ اسم جو کسی خاص شخص، مقام، یا چیز کا نام ہو۔
ضمیر — وہ اسم جو کسی چیز یا شخص کی طرف اشارہ کرتا ہو۔
اسمِ اشارہ — وہ اسم جو کسی جملے یا فقرے کے ساتھ منسلک ہوتا ہو اور مکمل معنی تب تک نہیں دیتا جب تک کہ دوسرا جملہ اس کے ساتھ نہ ہو۔
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 209: اسمِ علم — وہ اسم جو کسی خاص شخص، مقام، یا چیز کا نام ہو۔

questions.q: تعریف “وہ فعل جس میں کرنے والا (فاعل) معلوم نہ ہو یا ذکر نہ کیا گیا ہو۔” اور مثال “خط لکھا گیا۔” کس اصطلاح کو ظاہر کرتی ہیں؟
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 211: فعل مجہول — وہ فعل جس میں کرنے والا (فاعل) معلوم نہ ہو یا ذکر نہ کیا گیا ہو۔

questions.q: یہ تعریف کس اصطلاح کی ہے؟ “نحوِ تفصیلی: قواعد کی تفصیل نحوِ ترکیبی: جملے کی ترکیب کا مطالعہ”
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 214: نحو کی اقسام — نحوِ تفصیلی: قواعد کی تفصیل نحوِ ترکیبی: جملے کی ترکیب کا مطالعہ

questions.q: یہ تعریف کس اصطلاح کی ہے؟ “ایسا اندازِ بیان جس میں کوئی بات بالواسطہ کہی جائے مگر اس کا مطلب سمجھا جائے۔”
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 216: کنایہ — ایسا اندازِ بیان جس میں کوئی بات بالواسطہ کہی جائے مگر اس کا مطلب سمجھا جائے۔

questions.q: تعریف “جو کسی معینّ چیز یا فرد پر دلالت کرے” اور مثال “علی، قرآن، پاکستان” کس اصطلاح کو ظاہر کرتی ہیں؟
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 208: اسمِ معرفہ — جو کسی معینّ چیز یا فرد پر دلالت کرے

questions.q: تعریف “جو خوشی یا وسع تِ دل کے اظہار کے لیے ہو۔” اور مثال “واہ، سبحان ہللا، ماشاء ہللا” کس اصطلاح کو ظاہر کرتی ہیں؟
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 212: حرفِ انبساط — جو خوشی یا وسع تِ دل کے اظہار کے لیے ہو۔

questions.q:
Read the passage: “A university offered recorded lessons to students with long commutes. Most watched them, but attendance at discussion sessions remained uneven. The teacher concluded that easier access to lectures had solved only part of the learning problem.”

Which conclusion follows best?
o: Access to material does not guarantee active participation
questions.e: The two outcomes did not improve equally.

questions.q:
Read the passage: “A university offered recorded lessons to students with long commutes. Most watched them, but attendance at discussion sessions remained uneven. The teacher concluded that easier access to lectures had solved only part of the learning problem.”

What remained unresolved?
questions.e: Recorded lectures did not make discussion attendance consistent.

questions.q: In Prepositions, which Definition corresponds to Type “Preposition of Direction”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 231: Type “Preposition of Direction” corresponds to Definition “Shows movement”.

questions.q: In Parts of Speech, which Definition corresponds to Type “Concrete Noun”?
o: Refers to things you can touch or see
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 229: Type “Concrete Noun” corresponds to Definition “Refers to things you can touch or see”.

questions.q: In Prepositions, which Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) corresponds to Rule “Location beneath something natural”?
o: They rested under the tree. The kids played under the sun. I slept under the open sky.
There is a lamp placed in the corner of the room.
He fell into the ditch while running.
The book was translated into French. The kingdom was divided into provinces.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 231: Rule “Location beneath something natural” corresponds to Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) “They rested under the tree. The kids played under the sun. I slept under the open sky.”.

questions.q: In Parts of Speech, which Sentence Example corresponds to Type “Adverb of Degree”?
o: The book is on the table.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 230: Type “Adverb of Degree” corresponds to Sentence Example “She is very tired.”.

questions.q: In Parts of Speech, which Sentence Example corresponds to Type “Comparative Adjective”?
o: This house is bigger than mine.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 230: Type “Comparative Adjective” corresponds to Sentence Example “This house is bigger than mine.”.

questions.q: In Parts of Speech, which Definition corresponds to Type “Possessive Pronoun”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 230: Type “Possessive Pronoun” corresponds to Definition “Shows ownership”.

questions.q: In Direct and Indirect Speech, which Reporting Verb corresponds to Type “Sorrow”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 228: Type “Sorrow” corresponds to Reporting Verb “Exclaimed with Sorrow”.

questions.q: In Parts of Speech, which Sentence Example corresponds to Type “Phrasal Verb”?
o: This house is bigger than mine.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 230: Type “Phrasal Verb” corresponds to Sentence Example “He gave up smoking.”.

questions.q: In Direct and Indirect Speech, which Example corresponds to Type “Request”?
o: He said, "Close the door." → He ordered to close the door.
He said, "Please help me." → He requested to help him.
He said, "Hurrah! We won the match." → He exclaimed with joy that they had won the match.
He said, "What a beautiful view!" → He wondered that it was a VERY beautiful view.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 228: Type “Request” corresponds to Example “He said, "Please help me." → He requested to help him.”.

questions.q: In Prepositions, which Preposition corresponds to Rule “Used for position on a surface”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 231: Rule “Used for position on a surface” corresponds to Preposition “On”.

questions.q: In Direct and Indirect Speech, which Indirect Speech corresponds to Direct Speech “He will say, "I am ready."”?
o: He said that the sun rises in the east.
He will say that he is ready.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 226: Direct Speech “He will say, "I am ready."” corresponds to Indirect Speech “He will say that he is ready.”.

questions.q: In Prepositions, which Definition corresponds to Type “Volitive Interjection”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 231: Type “Volitive Interjection” corresponds to Definition “Expresses request, wish or command”.

questions.q: In Direct and Indirect Speech, which Example corresponds to Direct Speech “This”?
o: He said, "I have just finished." → He said that he had only finished.
He said, "I met him two days ago." → He said that he had met him two days before.
He said, "These flowers are beautiful." → He said that those flowers were beautiful.
He said, "I like this book." → He said that he liked that book.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 227: Direct Speech “This” corresponds to Example “He said, "I like this book." → He said that he liked that book.”.

questions.q: In Direct and Indirect Speech, which Reporting Verb corresponds to Type “Wonder”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 228: Type “Wonder” corresponds to Reporting Verb “Wondered”.

questions.q: In Sentences, Clauses and Phrases, which Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) corresponds to Rule “Movement by foot”?
o: He compared one type of mango with another.
People in our city travel mostly by train.
He goes to the office on foot every day.
He is ambitious of fame. She has ambition for power. He aspires to greatness.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 233: Rule “Movement by foot” corresponds to Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) “He goes to the office on foot every day.”.

questions.q: In Prepositions, which Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) corresponds to Rule “Legal or moral state/status”?
o: He hid behind the door when he saw the teacher coming.
He was convicted of theft. She is guilty of lying. The child is innocent of any wrongdoing.
Regular exercise is beneficial to health. Loud music is detrimental to concentration. Smoking is injurious to health.
His explanation was adequate to the situation. The policy is adverse to public interest. This environment is conducive to learning. The solution is suited to our needs.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 232: Rule “Legal or moral state/status” corresponds to Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) “He was convicted of theft. She is guilty of lying. The child is innocent of any wrongdoing.”.

questions.q: In Twelve-Tense Reference, which Example corresponds to Tense “Future Perfect Continuous”?
o: She has been writing for an hour.
She will have been writing for two hours.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 244: Tense “Future Perfect Continuous” corresponds to Example “She will have been writing for two hours.”.

questions.q: Find the error: “The Pakistan (A) is a member (B) of the United Nations (C) and the Commonwealth (D).”
questions.e: A single-word country name takes no article; organisation names with of or plural forms do.

questions.q: In Articles, which Rule corresponds to Example Sentence “He is suffering from malaria. She has diabetes.”?
o: No article before common diseases (except a few)
No article before hell, heaven, or God (used reverently)
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 225: Example Sentence “He is suffering from malaria. She has diabetes.” corresponds to Rule “No article before common diseases (except a few)”.

questions.q: It was ____ honour to serve on ____ committee that drafted the policy.
questions.e: Honour has a silent h; the relative clause identifies which committee.

questions.q: Find the error: “He is one of (A) the most competent officer (B) in the division (C) this year (D).”
questions.e: One of the + superlative requires a plural noun: officers.

questions.q: In Sentences, Clauses and Phrases, which Explanation / Usage corresponds to Connector Type “Coordinating Conjunctions (FANBOYS)”?
o: Join two independent clauses, showing relationship (cause, contrast, result, etc.)
Join two independent clauses in compound sentences
Introduce a dependent clause describing a noun
Introduce a dependent clause in complex sentences
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 234: Connector Type “Coordinating Conjunctions (FANBOYS)” corresponds to Explanation / Usage “Join two independent clauses in compound sentences”.

questions.q: In Sentences, Clauses and Phrases, which Rule corresponds to Preposition “At”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 233: Preposition “At” corresponds to Rule “Temporary or transit stop”.

questions.q: ____ poor in ____ rural areas have little access to credit.
questions.e: The + adjective names a class of people; rural areas in a general sense takes no article.

questions.q: For Twelve-Tense Reference, which Structure–Tense association is accurate?
o: subject + has/have + past participle — Present Perfect Continuous
subject + has/have been + verb-ing — Present Continuous
subject + base verb (s/es for third-person singular) — Present Simple
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 244: Structure “subject + base verb (s/es for third-person singular)” corresponds to Tense “Present Simple”.

questions.q: In Sentences, Clauses and Phrases, which Example corresponds to Connector Type “Conjunctive Adverbs”?
o: What he said shocked everyone. I believe that honesty matters.
He was late; however, he completed the task.
Because he was ill, he stayed home. He stayed home because he was ill.
My friend, who is a doctor, is coming. People who work hard succeed.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 234: Connector Type “Conjunctive Adverbs” corresponds to Example “He was late; however, he completed the task.”.

questions.q: Find the error: “The unemployment (A) among young graduates (B) has risen (C) sharply since 2019 (D).”
questions.e: Unemployment here is a general abstract noun and takes no article.

questions.q: In Sentences, Clauses and Phrases, which Example corresponds to Connector Type “Noun Clause Introducers (That, What, Whether, If, etc.)”?
o: Because he was ill, he stayed home. He stayed home because he was ill.
He was late; however, he completed the task.
He plays cricket, and she plays football.
What he said shocked everyone. I believe that honesty matters.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 234: Connector Type “Noun Clause Introducers (That, What, Whether, If, etc.)” corresponds to Example “What he said shocked everyone. I believe that honesty matters.”.

questions.q: In Articles, which Example Sentence corresponds to Rule “No article before titles (when used with names)”?
o: President Lincoln abolished slavery. Doctor Ali is on leave today.
He is suffering from malaria. She has diabetes.
Honesty is the best policy. Love conquers all.
I live in Multan. He visited Pakistan last year.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 225: Rule “No article before titles (when used with names)” corresponds to Example Sentence “President Lincoln abolished slavery. Doctor Ali is on leave today.”.

questions.q: Find the error: “Having reviewed the file (A), a decision (B) was taken (C) to close the case (D).”
questions.e: A decision did not review the file. The minimum repair names the doer: “the officer took a decision”.

questions.s: Capital letters, full stops and the everyday comma
questions.q: Find the error: “The Summer of 2022 (A) brought record flooding (B) to southern Punjab (C) and Sindh (D).”
questions.e: Seasons are not capitalised: “The summer of 2022”.

questions.q: In Active and Passive Voice, which Example (Active) corresponds to Tense “Present Perfect”?
o: She will have completed the project.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 224: Tense “Present Perfect” corresponds to Example (Active) “She has completed the project.”.

questions.q: In Active and Passive Voice, which Passive Formula corresponds to Tense “Past Perfect”?
o: Object + will/shall + have been + V3 + by + Subject
Object + had been + V3 + by + Subject
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 224: Tense “Past Perfect” corresponds to Passive Formula “Object + had been + V3 + by + Subject”.

questions.q: In Twelve-Tense Reference, which Example corresponds to Tense “Future Simple”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 244: Tense “Future Simple” corresponds to Example “She will write tomorrow.”.

questions.q: In Active and Passive Voice, which Passive Formula corresponds to Tense “Present Continuous”?
o: Object + has/have + been + V3 + by + Subject
Object + was/were + being + V3 + by + Subject
Object + is/am/are + being + V3 + by + Subject
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 224: Tense “Present Continuous” corresponds to Passive Formula “Object + is/am/are + being + V3 + by + Subject”.

questions.q: For Articles, which Example Sentence–Rule association is accurate?
o: He is a teacher. She bought a university bag. (Note: "University" starts with a consonant sound /juː/) — Before consonant sounds (not just consonants)
I saw a certain bird flying high. A certain man was looking for you. — In the general sense of "any"
A servant must obey his master. Anyone can become a leader. — No article before names of people
I met Ahmed yesterday. Fatima is my sister. — Before a certain or specific unidentified thing
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 225: Example Sentence “He is a teacher. She bought a university bag. (Note: "University" starts with a consonant sound /juː/)” corresponds to Rule “Before consonant sounds (not just consonants)”.

questions.q: In Articles, which Example Sentence corresponds to Rule “With ordinal numbers”?
o: She was the first to arrive.
I read the Dawn every morning.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 225: Rule “With ordinal numbers” corresponds to Example Sentence “She was the first to arrive.”.

questions.q: In Articles, which Example Sentence corresponds to Rule “With superlatives”?
o: He is the best player on the team.
She was the first to arrive.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 225: Rule “With superlatives” corresponds to Example Sentence “He is the best player on the team.”.

questions.q: In Twelve-Tense Reference, which Structure corresponds to Tense “Present Perfect Continuous”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 244: Tense “Present Perfect Continuous” corresponds to Structure “subject + has/have been + verb-ing”.

questions.q: Find the shift: “A candidate who prepares systematically (A) will find that you retain more (B) and that your revision (C) becomes faster (D).”
questions.e: The third-person subject shifts to the second person. Keep he, she, they or the candidate throughout.

questions.q: In Active and Passive Voice, which Example (Passive) corresponds to Type “Order/Command”?
o: You are advised to follow the rules.
Let not the wire be touched.
You are requested to help me.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 224: Type “Order/Command” corresponds to Example (Passive) “Let the door be closed.”.

questions.q: Most of the evidence ____ inconclusive.
questions.e: Most takes its number from evidence, which is uncountable and singular.

questions.q: Find the error: “Every officer and every clerk (A) in the division (B) were issued (C) a new identity card (D).”
questions.e: Every before joined subjects forces a singular verb: was issued.

questions.q: Attached to the application ____ three certificates.
questions.e: The subject, certificates, follows the verb and is plural.

questions.q: In Twelve-Tense Reference, which Structure corresponds to Tense “Past Continuous”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 244: Tense “Past Continuous” corresponds to Structure “subject + was/were + verb-ing”.

questions.q: In Active and Passive Voice, which Example (Active) corresponds to Type “Advice (Kindly)”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 224: Type “Advice (Kindly)” corresponds to Example (Active) “Kindly follow the rules.”.

questions.q: She managed ____ the file before the office closed.
questions.e: Manage takes a to-infinitive.

questions.q: ____ the tribunal reserved its judgement, the parties waited outside.
questions.e: A clause follows, so a subordinator is needed; during and despite take nouns.

questions.q: Training-centre exercise — A vehicle covers two equal-distance legs at 78 km/h and 90 km/h. What is its average speed for the complete journey?
questions.e: For equal distances the harmonic mean applies: 2uv/(u + v) = 83.57 km/h.

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — 51 passengers paid Rs 2760. An adult ticket cost Rs 60 and a child ticket Rs 40. How many adults travelled?
questions.e: If a is the adult count, 60a + 40(51 − a) = 2760, which gives a = 36.

questions.q: Transport-depot calculation — A 58 m by 17 m rectangular courtyard has a uniform path 4 m wide inside its boundary. What area does the path cover?
questions.e: Path area = outer area − inner area = 986 − 50×9 = 536 m².

questions.q: District-office worksheet — A 61 m by 20 m rectangular courtyard has a uniform path 3 m wide inside its boundary. What area does the path cover?
questions.e: Path area = outer area − inner area = 1220 − 55×14 = 450 m².

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — A train 360 m long clears a 140 m platform in 12 seconds. What is its speed in km/h?
questions.e: The train covers 500 m. Its speed is (500)/12 m/s × 3.6 = 150 km/h.

questions.q: District-office worksheet — A train 370 m long clears a 150 m platform in 13 seconds. What is its speed in km/h?
questions.e: The train covers 520 m. Its speed is (520)/13 m/s × 3.6 = 144 km/h.

questions.q: Training-centre exercise — The mean of 20 observations in a report is 83. One entry, 73, is corrected to 113. What is the corrected mean?
questions.e: The total rises by 40; divided across 20 observations, the mean rises by 2 to 85.

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — The mean of 18 observations in a report is 54. One entry, 44, is corrected to 80. What is the corrected mean?
questions.e: The total rises by 36; divided across 18 observations, the mean rises by 2 to 56.

questions.q: Survey-unit review — A bag holds 39 red and 5 blue counters. Two are drawn without replacement. What is the probability that both are red?
questions.e: Multiply the changing probabilities: 39/44 × 38/43 = 78.33%.

questions.q: Training-centre exercise — A bag holds 40 red and 6 blue counters. Two are drawn without replacement. What is the probability that both are red?
questions.e: Multiply the changing probabilities: 40/46 × 39/45 = 75.36%.

questions.q: Scholarship-fund audit — A geometric sequence has first term 20 and common ratio 2. What is its 7th term?
Warehouse planning case — A geometric sequence has first term 21 and common ratio 3. What is its 8th term?
Transport-depot calculation — For two years at 15% per annum, by how much does compound interest exceed simple interest on Rs 640000?
Transport-depot calculation — Worker B takes 29 days for a task. Worker A is 50% more efficient than B. How many days would A need for the same task?
questions.e: Time varies inversely with efficiency, so A's time is 29 × 100/150 = 19.33 days.

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — For two years at 10% per annum, by how much does compound interest exceed simple interest on Rs 660000?
District-office worksheet — A two-digit number has digit sum 10; reversing its digits increases it by 54. What is the original number?
questions.e: Let the tens and units digits be x and y. Then x + y = 10 and 9(x − y) = -54; hence x = 2, y = 8.

questions.q: Survey-unit review — A two-digit number has digit sum 13; reversing its digits increases it by 27. What is the original number?
questions.e: Let the tens and units digits be x and y. Then x + y = 13 and 9(x − y) = -27; hence x = 5, y = 8.

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — The roots of x² − 140x + 4891 = 0 differ by 6. What is the larger root?
questions.e: The quadratic factors as (x − 67)(x − 73); the larger root is 73.

questions.q: Survey-unit review — The roots of x² − 20x + 91 = 0 differ by 6. What is the larger root?
questions.e: The quadratic factors as (x − 7)(x − 13); the larger root is 13.

questions.q: Survey-unit review — A vehicle covers two equal-distance legs at 108 km/h and 118 km/h. What is its average speed for the complete journey?
questions.e: For equal distances the harmonic mean applies: 2uv/(u + v) = 112.78 km/h.

questions.q: Survey-unit review — A can complete a project in 60 days and B in 90 days. They work together for 30 days; B then leaves. How many days from the start will A take to finish the project?
questions.e: Together they complete 30 × (1/60 + 1/90) = 5/6. A needs another 10 days for the remaining 1/6, totalling 40.

questions.q: Training-centre exercise — A can complete a project in 72 days and B in 108 days. They work together for 36 days; B then leaves. How many days from the start will A take to finish the project?

questions.q: Health-programme report — Two runners start together in opposite directions on a 1240 m circular track at 206.67 m/s and 155 m/s. After how many seconds do they first meet?
questions.e: In opposite directions their relative speed is 361.67 m/s, so time is 1240 ÷ 361.67 = 3.43 seconds.

questions.q: Scholarship-fund audit — Two triangles are similar. A side of 5 cm in the smaller corresponds to 25 cm in the larger. If another smaller side is 8 cm, what is its corresponding larger side?

questions.q: Warehouse planning case — Two triangles are similar. A side of 6 cm in the smaller corresponds to 36 cm in the larger. If another smaller side is 9 cm, what is its corresponding larger side?

questions.q: Transport-depot calculation — Two batches assessed by a transport depot contain 34 and 15 candidates with mean scores 53 and 71. What is the combined mean?
questions.e: Use the weighted mean: (34 × 53 + 15 × 71) ÷ 49 = 58.51.

questions.q: Survey-unit review — In a survey, 80 chose only A, 23 only B, 16 only C, 4 chose A and B only, 3 A and C only, 2 B and C only, and 1 chose all three. How many chose at least one?
questions.e: The seven disjoint regions are added once: 80+23+16+4+3+2+1 = 129.

questions.q: Health-programme report — Two batches assessed by a health programme contain 35 and 16 candidates with mean scores 54 and 72. What is the combined mean?

questions.q: Transport-depot calculation — What is the least number greater than 4160 that leaves remainder 63 when divided by both 64 and 65, given that 64 and 65 are coprime?
questions.e: A common remainder means N − 63 is a multiple of lcm(64, 65) = 4160. The least eligible N is 4160 + 63 = 4223.

questions.q: Health-programme report — What is the least number greater than 306 that leaves remainder 16 when divided by both 17 and 18, given that 17 and 18 are coprime?
questions.e: A common remainder means N − 16 is a multiple of lcm(17, 18) = 306. The least eligible N is 306 + 16 = 322.
