حرفِ تنبیہ — جو خواہش یا آرزو ظاہر کرے۔
حرفِ تعجب — جو حیرت یا تعجب ظاہر کرے۔
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 212: حرفِ تعجب — جو حیرت یا تعجب ظاہر کرے۔

questions.q: ان اصطلاحات—فعل امر، فعل نہی، ماضی قریب، ماضی بعید—میں درست اصطلاح اور تعریف کا جوڑا منتخب کریں۔
o: فعل نہی — جو ابھی ابھی وقوع پذیر ہوا ہو۔
فعل امر — وہ فعل جو حکم یا درخواست کے لیے بوال جائے۔
ماضی بعید — وہ فعل جو منع یا روکنے کے لیے استعمال ہو۔
ماضی قریب — جو کافی پہلے ہو چکا ہو۔
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 211: فعل امر — وہ فعل جو حکم یا درخواست کے لیے بوال جائے۔

questions.q: تعریف “جو مرد یا نر پر دلالت کرے” اور مثال “لڑکا، گھوڑا” کس اصطلاح کو ظاہر کرتی ہیں؟
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 208: مذکر — جو مرد یا نر پر دلالت کرے

questions.q: ان اصطلاحات—اسمِ معرفہ، مذکر، مؤنث، واحد—میں درست اصطلاح اور تعریف کا جوڑا منتخب کریں۔
o: مذکر — جو عورت یا مادہ پر دلالت کرے
اسمِ معرفہ — جو کسی معینّ چیز یا فرد پر دلالت کرے
واحد — جو مرد یا نر پر دلالت کرے
مؤنث — جو ایک چیز یا فرد پر دلالت کرے
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 208: اسمِ معرفہ — جو کسی معینّ چیز یا فرد پر دلالت کرے

questions.q: ان اصطلاحات—زیر، پیش، کهڑی زبر، کهڑی زیر—میں درست اصطلاح اور تعریف کا جوڑا منتخب کریں۔
o: پیش — سیدھی لکیر جو مخصوص الفاظ میں زبر کی صورت میں آتی ہے۔
کهڑی زبر — مخصوص الفاظ میں زیر کی خاص صورت۔
کهڑی زیر — واؤ نما نشان، جس سے آواز گول ہوتی ہے۔
زیر — نیچے کی چھوٹی لکیر جو آواز کو نیچے التی ہے۔
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 213: زیر — نیچے کی چھوٹی لکیر جو آواز کو نیچے التی ہے۔

questions.q: ان اصطلاحات—ضمیر، اسمِ نکرہ، اسمِ معرفہ، مذکر—میں درست اصطلاح اور تعریف کا جوڑا منتخب کریں۔
o: اسمِ معرفہ — جو مرد یا نر پر دلالت کرے
مذکر — جو کسی غیر معینّ چیز یا فرد پر دلالت کرے
ضمیر — وہ لفظ جو کسی اسم کی جگہ آتا ہے
اسمِ نکرہ — جو کسی معینّ چیز یا فرد پر دلالت کرے
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 208: ضمیر — وہ لفظ جو کسی اسم کی جگہ آتا ہے

questions.q: “ماضی تمنائی / شرطی” کی درست تعریف منتخب کریں۔
o: وہ حرف جو دو الفاظ یا جملوں کو مالئے
وہ حرف جو کسی شے کے ہونے یا نہ ہونے میں شک ظاہر کرے
ایسا ماضی جو خواہش یا شرط کے اظہار کے لیے ہو، حقیقت میں واقع نہ ہوا ہو
وہ حرف جو کسی سبب یا علت کو ظاہر کرے
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 211: ماضی تمنائی / شرطی — ایسا ماضی جو خواہش یا شرط کے اظہار کے لیے ہو، حقیقت میں واقع نہ ہوا ہو

questions.q: تعریف “وہ اسم جو کسی خاص شخص، مقام، یا چیز کا نام ہو۔” اور مثال “علی، پاکستان، لاہور” کس اصطلاح کو ظاہر کرتی ہیں؟
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 209: اسمِ علم — وہ اسم جو کسی خاص شخص، مقام، یا چیز کا نام ہو۔

questions.q: ان اصطلاحات—تشبیہ، استعارہ، مجازِ مرسل، کنایہ—میں درست اصطلاح اور تعریف کا جوڑا منتخب کریں۔
o: مجازِ مرسل — ایسا اندازِ بیان جس میں کوئی بات بالواسطہ کہی جائے مگر اس کا مطلب سمجھا جائے۔
کنایہ — تشبیہ سے مبالغہ کرتے ہوئے مشبہ کا ذکر چھوڑ دینا اور صرف مشبہ بہ کو بطور حقیقت بیان کرنا۔
تشبیہ — کسی چیز کو کسی دوسری چیز کے مشابہ قرار دینا جس میں دونوں کے درمیان کوئی مشترک خوبی ہو۔
استعارہ — لفظ کو اس کے غیر حقیقی مطلب میں استعمال کرنا، لیکن تشبیہ یا مشابہت کے بغیر۔
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 215: تشبیہ — کسی چیز کو کسی دوسری چیز کے مشابہ قرار دینا جس میں دونوں کے درمیان کوئی مشترک خوبی ہو۔

questions.q: “مجازِ مرسل” کی درست تعریف منتخب کریں۔
o: ایسے الفاظ کا مجموعہ جو مکمل مفہوم دے۔
ایسا اندازِ بیان جس میں کوئی بات بالواسطہ کہی جائے مگر اس کا مطلب سمجھا جائے۔
لفظ کو اس کے غیر حقیقی مطلب میں استعمال کرنا، لیکن تشبیہ یا مشابہت کے بغیر۔
خبر + )جس کے بارے میں بات ہو(مبتدا )جو بات کی جائے(
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 215: مجازِ مرسل — لفظ کو اس کے غیر حقیقی مطلب میں استعمال کرنا، لیکن تشبیہ یا مشابہت کے بغیر۔

questions.q:
Read the passage: “A coastal community agreed to seasonal fishing limits. Catches fell during the restriction, and some residents called the rule a failure. The committee said the test was whether catches and fish stocks recovered over several seasons.”

Why did the committee reject an immediate verdict?
o: The rule applied to no fishing boats
The intended benefits take longer to assess
questions.e: The policy’s aim is recovery across seasons, not a high catch during the restriction.

questions.q:
Read the passage: “A coastal community agreed to seasonal fishing limits. Catches fell during the restriction, and some residents called the rule a failure. The committee said the test was whether catches and fish stocks recovered over several seasons.”

What evidence would best evaluate the stated goal?
o: Fish-stock and catch trends over several seasons
Only the first restricted week’s sales
questions.e: The stated goal concerns medium-term recovery.

questions.q: In Twelve-Tense Reference, which Structure corresponds to Tense “Present Simple”?
o: subject + base verb (s/es for third-person singular)
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 244: Tense “Present Simple” corresponds to Structure “subject + base verb (s/es for third-person singular)”.

questions.q: In Active and Passive Voice, which Example (Passive) corresponds to Type “Request (Please)”?
o: You are requested to help me.
Let not the wire be touched.
You are advised to follow the rules.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 224: Type “Request (Please)” corresponds to Example (Passive) “You are requested to help me.”.

questions.q: In Prepositions, which Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) corresponds to Rule “To finish or overcome something”?
o: You can't compare apples to oranges.
She pulled through the illness. He saw through the deception.
The clock's arms moved forward by one hour. Last night, we moved the clocks back for winter time.
They laughed at his joke. She was shocked at the news. The crowd sneered at the performer. He was horrified at the scene. The bullies jeered at him.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 232: Rule “To finish or overcome something” corresponds to Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) “She pulled through the illness. He saw through the deception.”.

questions.q: In Direct and Indirect Speech, which Rule corresponds to Direct Speech “Past Indefinite”?
o: He said, "I play chess." → He said that he played chess.
He said, "I was writing." → He said that he had been writing.
He said, "I went to Lahore." → He said that he had gone to Lahore.
He said, "I am reading." → He said that he was reading.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 226: Direct Speech “Past Indefinite” corresponds to Rule “He said, "I went to Lahore." → He said that he had gone to Lahore.”.

questions.q: In Direct and Indirect Speech, which Indirect Speech corresponds to Direct Speech “He said, "Are you coming?"”?
o: He asked if I was coming.
She asked if I liked chocolate.
He asked where I was going.
She asked what my name was.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 227: Direct Speech “He said, "Are you coming?"” corresponds to Indirect Speech “He asked if I was coming.”.

questions.q: In Direct and Indirect Speech, which Indirect Speech corresponds to Direct Speech “She said, "What is your name?"”?
o: He says that he likes tea.
She requested not to disturb her.
She asked what my name was.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 227: Direct Speech “She said, "What is your name?"” corresponds to Indirect Speech “She asked what my name was.”.

questions.q: In Parts of Speech, which Definition corresponds to Type “Descriptive Adjective”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 230: Type “Descriptive Adjective” corresponds to Definition “Describes quality”.

questions.q: In Parts of Speech, which Definition corresponds to Type “Adverb of Frequency”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 230: Type “Adverb of Frequency” corresponds to Definition “Describes how often action happens”.

questions.q: In Parts of Speech, which Definition corresponds to Type “Auxiliary Verb”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 230: Type “Auxiliary Verb” corresponds to Definition “Helps main verb in tense”.

questions.q: In Articles, which Rule corresponds to Example Sentence “Honesty is the best policy. Love conquers all.”?
o: No article before abstract nouns (general idea)
No article before common diseases (except a few)
No article before hell, heaven, or God (used reverently)
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 225: Example Sentence “Honesty is the best policy. Love conquers all.” corresponds to Rule “No article before abstract nouns (general idea)”.

questions.q: In Parts of Speech, which Example Word corresponds to Type “Abstract Noun”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 229: Type “Abstract Noun” corresponds to Example Word “honesty”.

questions.q: In Parts of Speech, which Definition corresponds to Type “Preposition of Place”?
o: Refers to a group of people or things
Refers to specific names of people, places, or things
Refers to general people, places, or things
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 230: Type “Preposition of Place” corresponds to Definition “Shows location”.

questions.q: In Sentences, Clauses and Phrases, which Rule corresponds to Preposition “On”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 233: Preposition “On” corresponds to Rule “Travel using public/shared transport”.

questions.q: In Prepositions, which Preposition corresponds to Rule “Used for effort, feeling, state”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 232: Rule “Used for effort, feeling, state” corresponds to Preposition “In”.

questions.q: In Direct and Indirect Speech, which Rule corresponds to Direct Speech “Past Continuous”?
o: He said, "I am reading." → He said that he was reading.
He said, "I have finished." → He said that he had finished.
He said, "I was writing." → He said that he had been writing.
He said, "I play chess." → He said that he played chess.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 226: Direct Speech “Past Continuous” corresponds to Rule “He said, "I was writing." → He said that he had been writing.”.

questions.q: In Sentences, Clauses and Phrases, which Clause Structure corresponds to Sentence Type “Compound Sentence”?
o: Two or More ndependent Clauses + One or More Dependent Clauses
One Independent Clause + One or More Dependent Clauses
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 233: Sentence Type “Compound Sentence” corresponds to Clause Structure “Two Independent Clauses”.

questions.q: In Articles, which Rule corresponds to Example Sentence “I met Ahmed yesterday. Fatima is my sister.”?
o: No article before names of people
No article before titles (when used with names)
No article before cities and countries (general rule)
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 225: Example Sentence “I met Ahmed yesterday. Fatima is my sister.” corresponds to Rule “No article before names of people”.

questions.q: In Direct and Indirect Speech, which Indirect Speech corresponds to Direct Speech “Tomorrow”?
o: The Next Day / The Following Day
The Previous Day / The Day Before
The Previous Night / The Night Before
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 227: Direct Speech “Tomorrow” corresponds to Indirect Speech “The Next Day / The Following Day”.

questions.q: In Prepositions, which Preposition corresponds to Rule “Shows transformation or change of state”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 231: Rule “Shows transformation or change of state” corresponds to Preposition “Into”.

questions.q: In Prepositions, which Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) corresponds to Rule “Used when some work is finished, or for disconnection/cutting”?
o: She is sitting at the desk, writing a letter.
He sat by the door, waiting for her.
The power was cut off during the storm. He jumped off the wall.
The book is lying on the table.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 231: Rule “Used when some work is finished, or for disconnection/cutting” corresponds to Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) “The power was cut off during the storm. He jumped off the wall.”.

questions.q: In Prepositions, which Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) corresponds to Rule “Used for working position”?
o: They rested under the tree. The kids played under the sun. I slept under the open sky.
There is a lamp placed in the corner of the room.
She is sitting at the desk, writing a letter.
He sat by the door, waiting for her.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 231: Rule “Used for working position” corresponds to Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) “She is sitting at the desk, writing a letter.”.

questions.q: For Sentences, Clauses and Phrases, which Rule–Preposition association is accurate?
o: Confusion over "sat in/on" tree — Of / For / To
Retreat or reversal movement — In / On
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 233: Rule “Comparison between similar things” corresponds to Preposition “With”.

questions.q: In Sentences, Clauses and Phrases, which Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) corresponds to Rule “Retreat or reversal movement”?
o: The army retrogressed from the battlefield. They had to retreat from enemy lines.
We stopped at Dubai on our way to Saudi Arabia.
I stayed in Dubai for five days.
He sat in the tree, hidden by leaves. He sat on the branch and started whistling.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 233: Rule “Retreat or reversal movement” corresponds to Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) “The army retrogressed from the battlefield. They had to retreat from enemy lines.”.

questions.q: In Sentences, Clauses and Phrases, which Definition / Explanation corresponds to Sentence Type “Simple Sentence”?
o: A sentence that has two or I more independent clauses and at least one dependent clause.
A sentence with one independent clause and one or more dependent clauses.
A sentence with two or more independent clauses, joined by a coordinating conjunction, conjunctive adverb, or semicolon.
A sentence with only one independent clause. It expresses a complete thought.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 233: Sentence Type “Simple Sentence” corresponds to Definition / Explanation “A sentence with only one independent clause. It expresses a complete thought.”.

questions.s: Modifiers: put the describing words where they belong
questions.q: Find the error: “The scheme, after several years of delay and three separate inquiries into its finances (A), was (B) finally (C) abandoned (D).”
questions.e: The long insertion separates the subject from its verb. Move it: “After several years of delay and three separate inquiries into its finances, the scheme was finally abandoned.”

questions.q: For Articles, which Rule–Example Sentence association is accurate?
o: In the general sense of "any" — He is a teacher. She bought a university bag. (Note: "University" starts with a consonant sound /juː/)
Before vowel sounds (not just vowels) — He saw an owl in the tree. She is an honest girl.
Before consonant sounds (not just consonants) — I saw a certain bird flying high. A certain man was looking for you.
Before a certain or specific unidentified thing — A servant must obey his master. Anyone can become a leader.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 225: Rule “Before vowel sounds (not just vowels)” corresponds to Example Sentence “He saw an owl in the tree. She is an honest girl.”.

questions.q: In Twelve-Tense Reference, which Tense corresponds to Structure “subject + had + past participle”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 244: Structure “subject + had + past participle” corresponds to Tense “Past Perfect”.

questions.s: Modifiers: put the describing words where they belong
questions.q: Find the error: “To qualify for the scholarship (A), a minimum of sixty per cent marks (B) is required (C) in the last degree (D).”
questions.e: Marks do not qualify for a scholarship. Write “a candidate must obtain a minimum of sixty per cent”.

questions.s: Modifiers: put the describing words where they belong
questions.q: Find the error: “Driving through the flooded district (A), the damaged bridges (B) were clearly visible (C) from the road (D).”
questions.e: Bridges do not drive. Name the traveller: “we could clearly see the damaged bridges”.

questions.q: In Active and Passive Voice, which Active Formula corresponds to Tense “Past Perfect Continuous ❌”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 224: Tense “Past Perfect Continuous ❌” corresponds to Active Formula “Not Possible”.

questions.s: Modifiers: put the describing words where they belong
questions.q: Find the error: “The report criticised the contractor (A) for the delay (B) which ran to (C) four hundred pages (D).”
questions.e: The relative clause describes the report, not the delay. Move it: “The report, which ran to four hundred pages, criticised …”.

questions.q: In Articles, which Example Sentence corresponds to Rule “Exceptions: article the is used with measles, mumps”?
o: Man is mortal. Woman has always played a vital role.
He hopes to go to heaven. We must fear God.
He caught the measles last month. She was diagnosed with the mumps.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 225: Rule “Exceptions: article the is used with measles, mumps” corresponds to Example Sentence “He caught the measles last month. She was diagnosed with the mumps.”.

questions.q: In Active and Passive Voice, which Active Formula corresponds to Tense “Present Indefinite”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 224: Tense “Present Indefinite” corresponds to Active Formula “Subject + V1 + Object”.

questions.q: In Articles, which Example Sentence corresponds to Rule “Use the with international organizations”?
o: The man you saw was my teacher. The pen on the desk is mine.
He read The Quran daily. She studied The Republic by Plato.
The lion is a dangerous animal. The eagle soars high. The computer has changed the world.
The United Nations passed a new resolution. The World Bank approved the loan.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 225: Rule “Use the with international organizations” corresponds to Example Sentence “The United Nations passed a new resolution. The World Bank approved the loan.”.

questions.q: In Twelve-Tense Reference, which Structure corresponds to Tense “Future Perfect”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 244: Tense “Future Perfect” corresponds to Structure “subject + will/shall have + past participle”.

questions.q: In Twelve-Tense Reference, which Tense corresponds to Structure “subject + will/shall be + verb-ing”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 244: Structure “subject + will/shall be + verb-ing” corresponds to Tense “Future Continuous”.

questions.q: In Twelve-Tense Reference, which Example corresponds to Tense “Present Simple”?
o: She has been writing for an hour.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 244: Tense “Present Simple” corresponds to Example “She writes daily.”.

questions.q: Prices ____ steadily since the imposition of the new duty.
questions.e: Since requires a perfect tense, and rise is the intransitive verb.

questions.q: Find the error: “The government has announced (A) the relief package (B) in March (C) of last year (D).”
questions.e: A stated finished time requires the past simple: announced.

questions.q: In Active and Passive Voice, which Example (Active) corresponds to Tense “Past Continuous”?
o: She will have completed the project.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 224: Tense “Past Continuous” corresponds to Example (Active) “He was reading a book.”.

questions.q: Find the error: “The department is reviewing (A) the eligibility rules (B) since the last recruitment cycle (C) ended (D).”
questions.e: Since requires the present perfect continuous: has been reviewing.

questions.q: For Active and Passive Voice, which Type–Example (Passive) association is accurate?
o: Negative Command — You are requested to help me.
Advice (Kindly) — Let not the wire be touched.
Request (Please) — You are advised to follow the rules.
Order/Command — Let the door be closed.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 224: Type “Order/Command” corresponds to Example (Passive) “Let the door be closed.”.

questions.q: Find the error: “If the tribunal would have examined (A) the evidence carefully (B), it would have reached (C) a different conclusion (D).”
questions.e: The if-clause of a third conditional takes the past perfect: had examined.

questions.q: He ____ the file; he was on leave all week.
questions.e: Can’t have + participle expresses a confident denial about the past.

questions.q: Report: “Do not touch the exhibits,” the guide warned us.
o: The guide warned us that we do not touch the exhibits.
The guide warned us to not touching the exhibits.
The guide warned us not to touch the exhibits.
The guide warned us that do not touch the exhibits.
questions.e: A negative command becomes not to + infinitive.

questions.q: Find the error: “The minister told (A) that the subsidy (B) would continue (C) until December (D).”
questions.e: Tell needs a person: told the House, told reporters — or use said that.

questions.q: Report: “Have you seen the notification?” the clerk asked.
o: The clerk asked whether I had seen the notification.
The clerk asked have I seen the notification.
The clerk asked whether had I seen the notification.
The clerk asked that whether I had seen the notification.
questions.e: Yes-or-no questions take if or whether and statement order.

questions.q: “You must submit it today.” → He said that I ____ submit it that day.
questions.e: Must backshifts to had to when it expresses obligation.

questions.q: Training-centre exercise — On a coordinate grid, point Q lies 190 units east and 456 units north of point P. What is the straight-line distance PQ?
Survey-unit review — On a coordinate grid, point Q lies 111 units east and 148 units north of point P. What is the straight-line distance PQ?
Warehouse planning case — The roots of x² − 50x + 616 = 0 differ by 6. What is the larger root?
questions.e: The quadratic factors as (x − 22)(x − 28); the larger root is 28.

questions.q: Scholarship-fund audit — The roots of x² − 47x + 546 = 0 differ by 5. What is the larger root?
questions.e: The quadratic factors as (x − 21)(x − 26); the larger root is 26.

questions.q: Scholarship-fund audit — 55 passengers paid Rs 3510. An adult ticket cost Rs 70 and a child ticket Rs 50. How many adults travelled?
questions.e: If a is the adult count, 70a + 50(55 − a) = 3510, which gives a = 38.

questions.q: Warehouse planning case — 88 passengers paid Rs 4940. An adult ticket cost Rs 60 and a child ticket Rs 40. How many adults travelled?
questions.e: If a is the adult count, 60a + 40(88 − a) = 4940, which gives a = 71.

questions.q: District-office worksheet — A invests Rs 61000 for 8 months and B invests Rs 6000 for 5 months. If their profit is Rs 5180, what is A's share?
questions.e: Profit follows capital-months. The weights are 488000:30000; A therefore receives Rs 4880.

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — A invests Rs 60000 for 7 months and B invests Rs 5000 for 4 months. If their profit is Rs 4400, what is A's share?
questions.e: Profit follows capital-months. The weights are 420000:20000; A therefore receives Rs 4200.

questions.q: تعریف “وہ فعل جس کا کرنے والا (فاعل) معلوم ہو اور ظاہر ہو۔” اور مثال “علی نے خط لکھا۔” کس اصطلاح کو ظاہر کرتی ہیں؟
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 211: فعل معروف (مفرد) — وہ فعل جس کا کرنے والا (فاعل) معلوم ہو اور ظاہر ہو۔

questions.q: ان اصطلاحات—الزم، متعدی، ذاتی / تفصیلی، نسبتی—میں درست اصطلاح اور تعریف کا جوڑا منتخب کریں۔
o: الزم — وہ مسدر جس کا فعل صرف فاعل کو چاہیے، یعنی اس کا اثر صرف کرنے والے پر ہوتا ہے۔
نسبتی — وہ مسدر جس کا فعل فاعل اور مفعول دونوں کو چاہیے، یعنی اس کا اثر دوسرے پر بھی پڑتا ہے۔
ذاتی / تفصیلی — وہ صفت جو کسی چیز یا شخص کا تعلق یا نسبت ظاہر کرے۔
متعدی — وہ صفت جو کسی چیز کی ذاتی خوبی یا خامی ظاہر کرے۔
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 210: الزم — وہ مسدر جس کا فعل صرف فاعل کو چاہیے، یعنی اس کا اثر صرف کرنے والے پر ہوتا ہے۔

questions.q: یہ تعریف کس اصطلاح کی ہے؟ “وہ فعل جو فاعل پر ختم ہو جائے اور مفعول کی ضرورت نہ ہو۔”
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 210: الزم — وہ فعل جو فاعل پر ختم ہو جائے اور مفعول کی ضرورت نہ ہو۔

questions.q: “فعل مستقبل” کی درست تعریف منتخب کریں۔
o: وہ فعل جو آئندہ میں انجام پائے گا۔
وہ فعل جو منع یا روکنے کے لیے استعمال ہو۔
وہ فعل جو حکم یا درخواست کے لیے بوال جائے۔
وہ فعل جو حال یا مستقبل دونوں پر دلالت کرے، اکثر شرطیہ یا عمومی جملوں میں آتا ہے۔
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 211: فعل مستقبل — وہ فعل جو آئندہ میں انجام پائے گا۔

questions.q: تعریف “جو کسی غیر معینّ چیز یا فرد پر دلالت کرے” اور مثال “کتاب، لڑکا، شہر” کس اصطلاح کو ظاہر کرتی ہیں؟
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 208: اسمِ نکرہ — جو کسی غیر معینّ چیز یا فرد پر دلالت کرے

questions.q: “اسمِ مفعول” کی درست تعریف منتخب کریں۔
o: جو کسی معاوضے، اجرت یا مزدوری کے لیے استعمال ہو
جو فاعل یا مفعول کی حالت یا کیفیت کو ظاہر کرے
جو کسی کام کا نشانہ بننے والے پر دلالت کرے
جو کسی گروہ یا مجموعے پر دلالت کرے
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 208: اسمِ مفعول — جو کسی کام کا نشانہ بننے والے پر دلالت کرے

questions.q: “تخصیصی” کی درست تعریف منتخب کریں۔
o: کسی اسم کی تخصیص (محدود دائرہ) بیان کرے
ایک لفظ دوسرے کا مادہ ہو (جس سے وہ بنا ہو)
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 214: تخصیصی — کسی اسم کی تخصیص (محدود دائرہ) بیان کرے

questions.q: یہ تعریف کس اصطلاح کی ہے؟ “متحرک: جس حرف پر حرکت (زبر، زیر، پیش) ہو۔ساکن: جس پر کوئی حرکت نہ ہو بلکہ جزم ہو۔”
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 213: متحرک اور ساکن میں فرق — متحرک: جس حرف پر حرکت (زبر، زیر، پیش) ہو۔ساکن: جس پر کوئی حرکت نہ ہو بلکہ جزم ہو۔

questions.q: “اسمِ نکرہ” کی درست تعریف منتخب کریں۔
o: جو کسی غیر معینّ چیز یا فرد پر دلالت کرے
جو کسی معینّ چیز یا فرد پر دلالت کرے
جو مرد یا نر پر دلالت کرے
جو عورت یا مادہ پر دلالت کرے
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 208: اسمِ نکرہ — جو کسی غیر معینّ چیز یا فرد پر دلالت کرے

questions.q: یہ تعریف کس اصطلاح کی ہے؟ “دو اسم یا الفاظ اس طرح جُڑ جائیں کہ الگ نہ کیے جا سکیں۔”
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 214: مرک بِ امتزاجی — دو اسم یا الفاظ اس طرح جُڑ جائیں کہ الگ نہ کیے جا سکیں۔

questions.q: “الزم” کی درست تعریف منتخب کریں۔
o: وہ مسدر جس کا فعل صرف فاعل کو چاہیے، یعنی اس کا اثر صرف کرنے والے پر ہوتا ہے۔
وہ مسدر جس کا فعل فاعل اور مفعول دونوں کو چاہیے، یعنی اس کا اثر دوسرے پر بھی پڑتا ہے۔
وہ صفت جو کسی چیز کی ذاتی خوبی یا خامی ظاہر کرے۔
وہ صفت جو کسی چیز یا شخص کا تعلق یا نسبت ظاہر کرے۔
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 210: الزم — وہ مسدر جس کا فعل صرف فاعل کو چاہیے، یعنی اس کا اثر صرف کرنے والے پر ہوتا ہے۔

questions.q:
Read the passage: “A city planted trees near a heat sensor. Its readings fell, but a second sensor in a shaded lane had been cooler even before planting. Researchers compared each site with its own earlier readings rather than comparing only the two sites.”

What would most directly show the change at the planted site?
o: Its reading before and after planting under comparable conditions
Only a reading from the shaded lane
The number of trees in another city
The cost of the heat sensor
questions.e: A before-and-after comparison at the same site addresses the change.

questions.q:
Read the passage: “A city planted trees near a heat sensor. Its readings fell, but a second sensor in a shaded lane had been cooler even before planting. Researchers compared each site with its own earlier readings rather than comparing only the two sites.”

Why compare each site with its earlier readings?
o: The sensors had no earlier records
The sites began with different temperature conditions
questions.e: A baseline difference makes a simple between-site comparison misleading.

questions.q: In Parts of Speech, which Example Word corresponds to Type “Personal Pronoun”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 230: Type “Personal Pronoun” corresponds to Example Word “I, he, she”.

questions.q: For Parts of Speech, which Part of Speech–Explanation association is accurate?
o: Verb — Gives more information about a noun
Pronoun — Tells what the subject is doing
Noun — Identifies what the sentence is about
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 229: Part of Speech “Noun” corresponds to Explanation “Identifies what the sentence is about”.

questions.q: In Parts of Speech, which Definition corresponds to Type “Phrasal Verb”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 230: Type “Phrasal Verb” corresponds to Definition “Verb + preposition”.

questions.q: In Direct and Indirect Speech, which Example corresponds to Direct Speech “Yesterday”?
o: He said, "I am here." → He said that he was there.
He said, "I will visit next week." → He said that he would visit the following week.
He said, "I was there last night." → He said that he had been there the previous night.
He said, "I saw him yesterday." → He said that he had seen him the previous day.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 227: Direct Speech “Yesterday” corresponds to Example “He said, "I saw him yesterday." → He said that he had seen him the previous day.”.

questions.q: In Direct and Indirect Speech, which Direct Speech corresponds to Indirect Speech “Before”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 227: Indirect Speech “Before” corresponds to Direct Speech “Ago”.

questions.q: In Prepositions, which Definition corresponds to Type “Correlative Conjunction”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 231: Type “Correlative Conjunction” corresponds to Definition “Used in pairs”.

questions.q: In Direct and Indirect Speech, which Rule corresponds to Direct Speech “Present Indefinite”?
o: He said, "I am reading." → He said that he was reading.
He said, "I have finished." → He said that he had finished.
He said, "I have been working." → He said that he had been working.
He said, "I play chess." → He said that he played chess.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 226: Direct Speech “Present Indefinite” corresponds to Rule “He said, "I play chess." → He said that he played chess.”.

questions.q: In Prepositions, which Preposition corresponds to Rule “Specific time”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 232: Rule “Specific time” corresponds to Preposition “At”.

questions.q: In Sentences, Clauses and Phrases, which Clause Structure corresponds to Sentence Type “Simple Sentence”?
o: One Independent Clause + One or More Dependent Clauses
Two or More ndependent Clauses + One or More Dependent Clauses
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 233: Sentence Type “Simple Sentence” corresponds to Clause Structure “One Independent Clause”.

questions.q: In Prepositions, which Rule corresponds to Preposition “Through”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 232: Preposition “Through” corresponds to Rule “To finish or overcome something”.

questions.q: In Parts of Speech, which Sentence Example corresponds to Type “Auxiliary Verb”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 230: Type “Auxiliary Verb” corresponds to Sentence Example “I have finished.”.

questions.q: In Parts of Speech, which Sentence Example corresponds to Type “Linking Verb”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 230: Type “Linking Verb” corresponds to Sentence Example “He is tall.”.

questions.q: In Sentences, Clauses and Phrases, which Structure Pattern corresponds to Connector Type “Conjunctive Adverbs”?
o: Independent clause; conjunctive adverb, independent clause
Dependent clause, independent clause or Independent clause dependent clause
Independent clause, nonessential dependent clause, clause or Independent clause essential dependent clause clause
Depends on placement in the sentence (no special punctuation rule)
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 234: Connector Type “Conjunctive Adverbs” corresponds to Structure Pattern “Independent clause; conjunctive adverb, independent clause”.

questions.q: In Prepositions, which Preposition corresponds to Rule “Used when some work is finished, or for disconnection/cutting”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 231: Rule “Used when some work is finished, or for disconnection/cutting” corresponds to Preposition “Off”.

questions.q: In Prepositions, which Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) corresponds to Rule “General residence/location”?
o: The train departs at dawn. The meeting starts at 3 AM.
He lives in Khan Street with his family.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 232: Rule “General residence/location” corresponds to Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) “He lives in Khan Street with his family.”.

questions.q: In Direct and Indirect Speech, which Example corresponds to Direct Speech “Will”?
o: He said, "I will go today." → He said that he would go that day.
He said, "I will help you." → He said that he would help me.
He said, "I must finish it." → He said that he had to finish it.
He said, "I am busy now." → He said that he was busy then.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 227: Direct Speech “Will” corresponds to Example “He said, "I will help you." → He said that he would help me.”.

questions.q: In Direct and Indirect Speech, which Reporting Verb corresponds to Type “Advice”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 228: Type “Advice” corresponds to Reporting Verb “Advised”.

questions.q: In Sentences, Clauses and Phrases, which Explanation / Usage corresponds to Connector Type “Conjunctive Adverbs”?
o: Join two independent clauses, showing relationship (cause, contrast, result, etc.)
Used as subject or object in a sentence
Introduce a dependent clause describing a noun
Introduce a dependent clause in complex sentences
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 234: Connector Type “Conjunctive Adverbs” corresponds to Explanation / Usage “Join two independent clauses, showing relationship (cause, contrast, result, etc.)”.

questions.q: In Active and Passive Voice, which Active Formula corresponds to Tense “Present Perfect”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 224: Tense “Present Perfect” corresponds to Active Formula “Subject + has/have + V3 + Object”.

questions.q: For Sentences, Clauses and Phrases, which Sentence Type–Example association is accurate?
o: Compound- Complex Sentence — A. He studied, and he passed. B. He studied; therefore, he passed. C. He studied; he passed.
Complex Sentence — Although it rained, we went outside, and we enjoyed the walk.
Compound Sentence — A. When it rained, we stayed inside. B. We stayed inside when it rained. C. My car, which is red, is fast. D. The man who called is my friend.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 233: Sentence Type “Simple Sentence” corresponds to Example “She reads books.”.

questions.q: In Twelve-Tense Reference, which Tense corresponds to Structure “subject + has/have been + verb-ing”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 244: Structure “subject + has/have been + verb-ing” corresponds to Tense “Present Perfect Continuous”.

questions.q: In Active and Passive Voice, which Example (Active) corresponds to Type “Order/Command”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 224: Type “Order/Command” corresponds to Example (Active) “Close the door.”.

questions.q: In Sentences, Clauses and Phrases, which Structure Pattern corresponds to Connector Type “Relative Pronouns (Adjective Clause)”?
o: Independent clause, coordinating conjunction, independent clause
Independent clause; conjunctive adverb, independent clause
Independent clause, nonessential dependent clause, clause or Independent clause essential dependent clause clause
Depends on placement in the sentence (no special punctuation rule)
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 234: Connector Type “Relative Pronouns (Adjective Clause)” corresponds to Structure Pattern “Independent clause, nonessential dependent clause, clause or Independent clause essential dependent clause clause”.

questions.q: In Active and Passive Voice, which Passive Formula corresponds to Tense “Future Indefinite”?
o: Object + will/shall + be + V3 + by + Subject
Object + was/were + being + V3 + by + Subject
Object + is/am/are + being + V3 + by + Subject
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 224: Tense “Future Indefinite” corresponds to Passive Formula “Object + will/shall + be + V3 + by + Subject”.

questions.q: In Active and Passive Voice, which Example (Active) corresponds to Tense “Past Perfect”?
o: She will have completed the project.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 224: Tense “Past Perfect” corresponds to Example (Active) “They had completed the task.”.

questions.q: Find the error: “Because of (A) the applicant had submitted (B) the wrong form (C), the request was rejected (D).”
questions.e: A full clause follows, so because is required, not because of.

questions.q: In “The report shows that enforcement has failed”, the that-clause works as
questions.e: It answers “shows what?”, so it is a noun clause working as the object.

questions.q: Find the error: “The villages, that were worst affected (A) by the floods (B), received relief (C) three weeks late (D).”
questions.e: Use which after a comma. That never introduces a non-defining clause.

questions.q: Find the error: “Even though (A) the department issued a clarification (B), but the confusion (C) continued for weeks (D).”
questions.e: Even though and but both mark contrast. Delete but.

questions.q: Find the error: “As the rains failed (A), so the wheat output (B) fell by (C) nine per cent (D).”
questions.e: As already marks the cause; so must go.

questions.q: She said that she ____ the file the previous day.
questions.e: A past simple in direct speech backshifts to the past perfect.

questions.q: Find the error: “He asked me (A) that when (B) the results would (C) be announced (D).”
questions.e: A reported wh-question takes no that: “asked me when the results would be announced”.

questions.q: Report: “Please lend me your notes,” he said to her.
o: He requested her to lend him her notes.
He said her to lend him her notes.
He told her that please lend him her notes.
He requested her that she lends him her notes.
questions.e: A polite request becomes request/ask + person + to + infinitive.

questions.q: Find the error: “The witness said (A) that he had seen (B) the accused here (C) the previous evening (D).”
questions.e: Here becomes there when the report is made elsewhere.

questions.q: In Articles, which Rule corresponds to Example Sentence “President Lincoln abolished slavery. Doctor Ali is on leave today.”?
o: No article before common diseases (except a few)
No article before abstract nouns (general idea)
No article before cities and countries (general rule)
No article before titles (when used with names)
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 225: Example Sentence “President Lincoln abolished slavery. Doctor Ali is on leave today.” corresponds to Rule “No article before titles (when used with names)”.

questions.q: In Articles, which Rule corresponds to Example Sentence “Gold is a precious metal. Iron is used in construction.”?
o: No article before cities and countries (general rule)
No article before abstract nouns (general idea)
No article before titles (when used with names)
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 225: Example Sentence “Gold is a precious metal. Iron is used in construction.” corresponds to Rule “No article before metals”.

questions.q: In Articles, which Example Sentence corresponds to Rule “Use the with heavenly bodies”?
o: He lives in the Punjab. They climbed the Himalayas. We swam in the Atlantic Ocean.
The United Nations passed a new resolution. The World Bank approved the loan.
The moon looks beautiful tonight. The sun rises in the east.
He visited the United States. She works in the Netherlands.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 225: Rule “Use the with heavenly bodies” corresponds to Example Sentence “The moon looks beautiful tonight. The sun rises in the east.”.

questions.q: In Active and Passive Voice, which Active Formula corresponds to Tense “Past Perfect”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 224: Tense “Past Perfect” corresponds to Active Formula “Subject + had + V3 + Object”.

questions.q: Find the error: “The minister emphasised on (A) the need for (B) transparency (C) in public procurement (D).”
questions.e: Emphasise is transitive: “emphasised the need”. Lay stress on is the phrase that takes on.

questions.q: Find the error: “She has been married with (A) a serving officer (B) for the last (C) eight years (D).”
questions.e: Married takes to.

questions.q: There is no easy solution ____ the energy crisis.
questions.e: Solution takes to.

questions.q: Find the error: “The inquiry committee (A) investigated into (B) the allegations (C) for three months (D).”
questions.e: Investigate is transitive and takes no into.

questions.q: Find the error: “The number of applications received (A) by the commission (B) have risen (C) sharply this year (D).”
questions.e: The head noun is number, which is singular: “has risen”.

questions.q: Improving literacy rates in rural districts ____ sustained funding.
questions.e: The whole -ing phrase is one singular subject.

questions.q: Find the error: “While travelling to Islamabad (A), the briefcase containing the file (B) was lost (C) by the deputy secretary (D).”
questions.e: The briefcase was not travelling. Rewrite: “While travelling to Islamabad, the deputy secretary lost the briefcase …”

questions.q: Find the error: “There has been (A) numerous complaints (B) about the quality (C) of drinking water (D).”
questions.e: The subject is complaints, so the verb must be “There have been”.

questions.q: In Articles, which Example Sentence corresponds to Rule “Use the with a class of people”?
o: I visited the Eiffel Tower. He reads the Economist every week. She works in the Parliament House.
He is the best player on the team.
She was the first to arrive.
The rich must help the poor. The elderly need care.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 225: Rule “Use the with a class of people” corresponds to Example Sentence “The rich must help the poor. The elderly need care.”.

questions.q: Find the error: “The chairman invited (A) the secretary and I (B) to attend (C) the briefing (D).”
questions.e: Delete “the secretary and”: “invited me”. The object form is required.

questions.q: District-office worksheet — A 45 m by 15 m rectangular courtyard has a uniform path 3 m wide inside its boundary. What area does the path cover?
questions.e: Path area = outer area − inner area = 675 − 39×9 = 324 m².

questions.q: Health-programme report — A 59 m by 18 m rectangular courtyard has a uniform path 5 m wide inside its boundary. What area does the path cover?
questions.e: Path area = outer area − inner area = 1062 − 49×8 = 670 m².

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — An arithmetic sequence begins 69, 72, 75, … . What is the sum of its first 10 terms?
Health-programme report — A geometric sequence has first term 57 and common ratio 3. What is its 8th term?
Transport-depot calculation — A geometric sequence has first term 56 and common ratio 2. What is its 7th term?
Relief-camp planning case — The roots of x² − 121x + 3658 = 0 differ by 3. What is the larger root?
questions.e: The quadratic factors as (x − 59)(x − 62); the larger root is 62.

questions.q: Transport-depot calculation — The roots of x² − 120x + 3591 = 0 differ by 6. What is the larger root?
questions.e: The quadratic factors as (x − 57)(x − 63); the larger root is 63.

questions.q: Warehouse planning case — A invests Rs 7000 for 9 months and B invests Rs 8000 for 7 months. If their profit is Rs 1190, what is A's share?
questions.e: Profit follows capital-months. The weights are 63000:56000; A therefore receives Rs 630.

questions.q: Scholarship-fund audit — A invests Rs 6000 for 8 months and B invests Rs 7000 for 6 months. If their profit is Rs 900, what is A's share?
questions.e: Profit follows capital-months. The weights are 48000:42000; A therefore receives Rs 480.

questions.q: Warehouse planning case — A two-digit number has digit sum 12; reversing its digits increases it by 54. What is the original number?
questions.e: Let the tens and units digits be x and y. Then x + y = 12 and 9(x − y) = -54; hence x = 3, y = 9.

questions.q: Scholarship-fund audit — A two-digit number has digit sum 11; reversing its digits increases it by 45. What is the original number?
questions.e: Let the tens and units digits be x and y. Then x + y = 11 and 9(x − y) = -45; hence x = 3, y = 8.

questions.q: Warehouse planning case — An investment grows to Rs 26100 in two years at 50% compound interest per year. What was the principal?
Scholarship-fund audit — An investment grows to Rs 17500 in two years at 25% compound interest per year. What was the principal?
Relief-camp planning case — The mean of 19 observations in a report is 46. One entry, 36, is corrected to 74. What is the corrected mean?
questions.e: The total rises by 38; divided across 19 observations, the mean rises by 2 to 48.

questions.q: District-office worksheet — The mean of 20 observations in a report is 47. One entry, 37, is corrected to 77. What is the corrected mean?
questions.e: The total rises by 40; divided across 20 observations, the mean rises by 2 to 49.

questions.q: Survey-unit review — 95 passengers paid Rs 6350. An adult ticket cost Rs 70 and a child ticket Rs 50. How many adults travelled?
questions.e: If a is the adult count, 70a + 50(95 − a) = 6350, which gives a = 80.

questions.q: Training-centre exercise — For two years at 12% per annum, by how much does compound interest exceed simple interest on Rs 70000?
Survey-unit review — For two years at 10% per annum, by how much does compound interest exceed simple interest on Rs 60000?
Training-centre exercise — 76 passengers paid Rs 4720. An adult ticket cost Rs 65 and a child ticket Rs 45. How many adults travelled?
questions.e: If a is the adult count, 65a + 45(76 − a) = 4720, which gives a = 65.

questions.q: Survey-unit review — A train 640 m long clears a 150 m platform in 18 seconds. What is its speed in km/h?
questions.e: The train covers 790 m. Its speed is (790)/18 m/s × 3.6 = 158 km/h.

questions.q: Warehouse planning case — A train 630 m long clears a 140 m platform in 17 seconds. What is its speed in km/h?
questions.e: The train covers 770 m. Its speed is (770)/17 m/s × 3.6 = 163.06 km/h.

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — Worker B takes 39 days for a task. Worker A is 20% more efficient than B. How many days would A need for the same task?

questions.q:
Read the passage: “An office adopted a rule requiring two signatures for purchases. Errors fell, but urgent small orders were delayed. Managers kept two approvals for large purchases and introduced a recorded exception for minor urgent ones.”

What conflict did managers address?
questions.e: Extra checks reduce mistakes but can slow urgent purchases.

questions.q:
Read the passage: “An office adopted a rule requiring two signatures for purchases. Errors fell, but urgent small orders were delayed. Managers kept two approvals for large purchases and introduced a recorded exception for minor urgent ones.”

What feature makes the exception accountable?
o: It applies to all large orders
questions.e: A recorded exception can be reviewed.

questions.q: In Parts of Speech, which Definition corresponds to Type “Abstract Noun”?
o: Refers to things you can touch or see
Refers to ideas, feelings, or qualities
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 229: Type “Abstract Noun” corresponds to Definition “Refers to ideas, feelings, or qualities”.

questions.q: In Direct and Indirect Speech, which Example corresponds to Type “Sorrow”?
o: He said, "May God help us." → He prayed that God might help them.
He said, "May you fail!" → He cursed that I might fail.
He said, "Alas! He is dead." → He exclaimed with sorrow that he was dead.
He said, "May you live long!" → He wished that I might live long.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 228: Type “Sorrow” corresponds to Example “He said, "Alas! He is dead." → He exclaimed with sorrow that he was dead.”.

questions.q: In Sentences, Clauses and Phrases, which Definition / Explanation corresponds to Sentence Type “Complex Sentence”?
o: A sentence with only one independent clause. It expresses a complete thought.
A sentence with two or more independent clauses, joined by a coordinating conjunction, conjunctive adverb, or semicolon.
A sentence with one independent clause and one or more dependent clauses.
A sentence that has two or I more independent clauses and at least one dependent clause.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 234: Sentence Type “Complex Sentence” corresponds to Definition / Explanation “A sentence with one independent clause and one or more dependent clauses.”.

questions.q: In Prepositions, which Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) corresponds to Rule “Disagreement with a person”?
o: She is married to a doctor. He is engaged to his cousin.
I applied to the university last week.
He persisted in his efforts. She found satisfaction in helping others. He was disappointed in the result.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 232: Rule “Disagreement with a person” corresponds to Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) “He disagreed with his manager.”.

questions.q: In Prepositions, which Preposition corresponds to Rule “Location inside a corner”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 231: Rule “Location inside a corner” corresponds to Preposition “In”.

questions.q: In Direct and Indirect Speech, which Indirect Speech corresponds to Direct Speech “Can”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 227: Direct Speech “Can” corresponds to Indirect Speech “Could”.

questions.q: In Prepositions, which Preposition corresponds to Rule “Hidden at the back”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 232: Rule “Hidden at the back” corresponds to Preposition “Behind”.

questions.q: In Direct and Indirect Speech, which Indirect Speech corresponds to Direct Speech “Here”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 227: Direct Speech “Here” corresponds to Indirect Speech “There”.

questions.q: For Prepositions, which Type–Example Word association is accurate?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 231: Type “Preposition of Direction” corresponds to Example Word “to, into”.

questions.q: In Prepositions, which Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) corresponds to Rule “Location inside a corner”?
o: He fell into the ditch while running.
The book was translated into French. The kingdom was divided into provinces.
He quarreled with his brother. Our country allied with its neighbor. They coordinated with the police.
There is a lamp placed in the corner of the room.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 231: Rule “Location inside a corner” corresponds to Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) “There is a lamp placed in the corner of the room.”.

questions.q: In Direct and Indirect Speech, which Direct Speech corresponds to Indirect Speech “The Previous Night / The Night Before”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 227: Indirect Speech “The Previous Night / The Night Before” corresponds to Direct Speech “Last night”.

questions.q: In Direct and Indirect Speech, which Indirect Speech corresponds to Direct Speech “This morning”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 227: Direct Speech “This morning” corresponds to Indirect Speech “That morning”.

questions.q: In Parts of Speech, which Sentence Example corresponds to Type “Possessive Adjective”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 230: Type “Possessive Adjective” corresponds to Sentence Example “This is my car.”.

questions.q: In Parts of Speech, which Definition corresponds to Type “Action Verb”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 230: Type “Action Verb” corresponds to Definition “Shows physical or mental action”.

questions.q: In Active and Passive Voice, which Passive Formula corresponds to Tense “Future Continuous ❌”?
o: Object + has/have + been + V3 + by + Subject
Object + had been + V3 + by + Subject
Object + will/shall + have been + V3 + by + Subject
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 224: Tense “Future Continuous ❌” corresponds to Passive Formula “Not Possible”.

questions.q: In Parts of Speech, which Definition corresponds to Type “Preposition of Time”?
o: Refers to specific names of people, places, or things
Refers to general people, places, or things
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 230: Type “Preposition of Time” corresponds to Definition “Shows time”.

questions.q: In Parts of Speech, which Explanation corresponds to Part of Speech “Noun”?
o: Tells what the subject is doing
Gives more information about a noun
Identifies what the sentence is about
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 229: Part of Speech “Noun” corresponds to Explanation “Identifies what the sentence is about”.

questions.q: In Articles, which Example Sentence corresponds to Rule “Use the with names of famous books”?
o: He read The Quran daily. She studied The Republic by Plato.
I visited the Eiffel Tower. He reads the Economist every week. She works in the Parliament House.
The rich must help the poor. The elderly need care.
The lion is a dangerous animal. The eagle soars high. The computer has changed the world.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 225: Rule “Use the with names of famous books” corresponds to Example Sentence “He read The Quran daily. She studied The Republic by Plato.”.

questions.q: In Active and Passive Voice, which Active Formula corresponds to Tense “Past Continuous”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 224: Tense “Past Continuous” corresponds to Active Formula “Subject + was/were + V1+ing + Object”.

questions.q: In Sentences, Clauses and Phrases, which Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) corresponds to Rule “Non-specific vehicle travel”?
o: People in our city travel mostly by train.
He compared one type of mango with another.
He is ambitious of fame. She has ambition for power. He aspires to greatness.
The army retrogressed from the battlefield. They had to retreat from enemy lines.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 233: Rule “Non-specific vehicle travel” corresponds to Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) “People in our city travel mostly by train.”.

questions.q: In Sentences, Clauses and Phrases, which Preposition corresponds to Rule “Travel using private vehicles”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 233: Rule “Travel using private vehicles” corresponds to Preposition “In”.

questions.q: In Sentences, Clauses and Phrases, which Example corresponds to Sentence Type “Compound- Complex Sentence”?
o: A. He studied, and he passed. B. He studied; therefore, he passed. C. He studied; he passed.
Although it rained, we went outside, and we enjoyed the walk.
A. When it rained, we stayed inside. B. We stayed inside when it rained. C. My car, which is red, is fast. D. The man who called is my friend.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 234: Sentence Type “Compound- Complex Sentence” corresponds to Example “Although it rained, we went outside, and we enjoyed the walk.”.

o: Dependent clause, independent clause or Independent clause dependent clause
Independent clause, coordinating conjunction, independent clause
Depends on placement in the sentence (no special punctuation rule)
Independent clause, nonessential dependent clause, clause or Independent clause essential dependent clause clause

questions.q: For Active and Passive Voice, which Type–Example (Active) association is accurate?
o: Advice (Kindly) — Do not touch the wire.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 224: Type “Order/Command” corresponds to Example (Active) “Close the door.”.

questions.q: In Active and Passive Voice, which Example (Passive) corresponds to Type “Negative Command”?
o: You are requested to help me.
You are advised to follow the rules.
Let not the wire be touched.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 224: Type “Negative Command” corresponds to Example (Passive) “Let not the wire be touched.”.

o: Object + will/shall + be + V3 + by + Subject
Object + is/am/are + being + V3 + by + Subject
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 224: Tense “Present Indefinite” corresponds to Passive Formula “Object + is/am/are + V3 + by + Subject”.

questions.q: In Twelve-Tense Reference, which Tense corresponds to Structure “subject + will/shall have been + verb-ing”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 244: Structure “subject + will/shall have been + verb-ing” corresponds to Tense “Future Perfect Continuous”.

questions.q: In Articles, which Example Sentence corresponds to Rule “No article before abstract nouns (general idea)”?
o: Man is mortal. Woman has always played a vital role.
Honesty is the best policy. Love conquers all.
He is suffering from malaria. She has diabetes.
He caught the measles last month. She was diagnosed with the mumps.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 225: Rule “No article before abstract nouns (general idea)” corresponds to Example Sentence “Honesty is the best policy. Love conquers all.”.

questions.q: Find the error: “Myself and two colleagues (A) prepared the draft (B) over three days (C) in the secretariat (D).”
questions.e: A reflexive cannot be a subject: “Two colleagues and I prepared …”.

questions.q: She is the scholar ____ work on land reform is most often cited.
questions.e: Possession requires whose; who’s means who is.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The policy was announced in March. The provinces were not consulted by the ministry. Implementation began in June.”?
o: The policy was announced in March. The provinces were not consulted by the ministry. Implementation began in June.
The policy was announced in March without consulting the provinces. Implementation nevertheless began in June.
The policy were announced in March without consulting the provinces. Implementation nevertheless began in June.
The policy was not announced in March without consulting the provinces. Implementation nevertheless began in June.
questions.e: Voice held steady and the logical turn signalled.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Firstly, the data are incomplete. Secondly, the method was untested. Thirdly, the conclusion is overstated. Fourthly, the annexures are missing.”?
o: The data are incomplete and the method untested; the conclusion are therefore overstated.
The data are incomplete and the method untested; the conclusion is therefore overstated.
Firstly, the data are incomplete. Secondly, the method was untested. Thirdly, the conclusion is overstated. Fourthly, the annexures are missing.
The data are not incomplete and the method untested; the conclusion is therefore overstated.
questions.e: Numbering is not cohesion. Show the relationship instead of counting.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “He is neither qualified for the post or interested in it, moreover he has applied twice.”?
o: He is neither qualified for the post nor interested in it; moreover, he have applied twice.
He is not neither qualified for the post nor interested in it; moreover, he has applied twice.
He is neither qualified for the post or interested in it, moreover he has applied twice.
He is neither qualified for the post nor interested in it; moreover, he has applied twice.
questions.e: Neither pairs with nor, and moreover takes a semicolon before and a comma after.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “A new scheme was launched in 2019. Rural credit was the target of it. It failed.”?
o: In 2019 the government launched an new scheme targeting rural credit. The scheme failed within two years.
In 2019 the government launched a new scheme targeting rural credit. The scheme failed within two years.
A new scheme was launched in 2019. Rural credit was the target of it. It failed.
In 2019 the government launched a new scheme targeting rural credit. The scheme failed within two years not.
questions.e: Given–new ordering and a lexical link replace three disconnected statements.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Despite of the warnings and because of the roads were blocked, the convoy was delayed.”?
o: Despite the warnings, and because the roads were blocked, the convoy were delayed.
Despite the warnings, and because the roads were blocked, the convoy was delayed.
Despite of the warnings and because of the roads were blocked, the convoy was delayed.
Despite the warnings, and because the roads were not blocked, the convoy was delayed.
questions.e: Despite takes no of; because introduces the clause.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Although the government announced the package, but no funds were released, therefore the work stopped.”?
o: Although the government announced the package, no funds was released; the work therefore stopped.
Although the government announced the package, no funds were not released; the work therefore stopped.
Although the government announced the package, but no funds were released, therefore the work stopped.
Although the government announced the package, no funds were released; the work therefore stopped.
questions.e: Delete but after although, and give the conclusion its own punctuation.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “It was decided by the cabinet that the project would be abandoned. (Improve the voice.)”?
o: The cabinet decided than abandon the project.
The cabinet decided to abandon the project.
It was decided by the cabinet that the project would be abandoned. (Improve the voice.)
The cabinet decided to abandon the project not.
questions.e: The cabinet decided to abandon the project. (Active voice Day 9.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “During the assembly was debating the bill, the opposition walked out, due to they were not given time.”?
o: While the assembly were debating the bill, the opposition walked out because it had not been given time.
While the assembly was not debating the bill, the opposition walked out because it had not been given time.
During the assembly was debating the bill, the opposition walked out, due to they were not given time.
While the assembly was debating the bill, the opposition walked out because it had not been given time.
questions.e: While before a clause, because before a clause, and a consistent singular pronoun for opposition.

questions.s: Concision: saying it in fewer words
questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Due to the fact that there was a shortage of funds, the department made a decision to postpone the project.”?
o: Because of a shortage of funds, the department decided to postpone the project.
Because of a shortage of funds, the department decided than postpone the project.
Because of a shortage of funds, the department decided to postpone the project not.
Due to the fact that there was a shortage of funds, the department made a decision to postpone the project.
questions.e: One wordy connector and one nominalisation removed; nothing is lost.

questions.s: Concision: saying it in fewer words
questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “There are many experts who are of the opinion that the reforms have not been successful in achieving their objectives.”?
o: Many experts believe the reforms have failed to achieve their objectives.
Many experts believe the reforms has failed to achieve their objectives.
Many experts believe the reforms have not failed to achieve their objectives.
There are many experts who are of the opinion that the reforms have not been successful in achieving their objectives.
questions.e: The there-construction and two noun phrases become verbs.

questions.s: Concision: saying it in fewer words
questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “It is important to note that each and every applicant must submit his application prior to the closing date.”?
o: Every applicant must apply before the closing date.
It is important to note that each and every applicant must submit his application prior to the closing date.
Every applicant must not apply before the closing date.
Every applicant must apply before closing date.
questions.e: Throat-clearing, redundancy and a nominalisation all go.

questions.s: Concision: saying it in fewer words
questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The committee carried out an examination of the accounts and subsequent to that it gave consideration to the auditor’s recommendations.”?
o: The committee examined the accounts and then considered the auditor’s recommendations.
committee examined the accounts and then considered the auditor’s recommendations.
The committee examined the accounts and then considered the auditor’s recommendations not.
The committee carried out an examination of the accounts and subsequent to that it gave consideration to the auditor’s recommendations.
questions.e: Two nominalisations become verbs; subsequent to that becomes then.

questions.s: Concision: saying it in fewer words
questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “In my personal opinion, I think that the final conclusion of the report is basically correct.”?
o: I think the report’s conclusion is correct.
In my personal opinion, I think that the final conclusion of the report is basically correct.
I think the report’s conclusion is not correct.
I think the report’s conclusion are correct.
questions.e: Four redundancies removed without touching the claim.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “He returned to the home after the school and played the football till the evening.”?
o: He returned home after school and played football till evening.
He returned home after school and played football till the evening not.
He returned to the home after the school and played the football till the evening.
He returned home after school and played football till the evening.
questions.e: Home, school and games take no article; in the evening keeps it.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The reform failed. It was underfunded. It lacked support. (Combine with variety and one short emphatic sentence.)”?
o: Underfunded and unsupported, the reform was not doomed. It collapsed.
Underfunded and unsupported, the reform were doomed. It collapsed.
Underfunded and unsupported, the reform was doomed. It collapsed.
The reform failed. It was underfunded. It lacked support. (Combine with variety and one short emphatic sentence.)
questions.e: Underfunded and unsupported, the reform was doomed. It collapsed. (Variety + short emphatic close Day 28.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Build given–new flow: Inflation rose sharply. Household budgets came under pressure. Public anger increased.”?
o: Inflation rose sharply. This rise squeezed household budgets, and that pressure intensified public anger.
Inflation rose sharply. rise squeezed household budgets, and that pressure intensified public anger.
Inflation rose sharply. This rise squeezed household budgets, and that pressure intensified public anger not.
Build given–new flow: Inflation rose sharply. Household budgets came under pressure. Public anger increased.
questions.e: Inflation rose sharply. This rise squeezed household budgets, and that pressure intensified public anger. (Linear progression.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Fix register: The policy was, honestly, a total mess and nobody knew what to do.”?
o: The policy was seriously flawed, and officials lacked a coherent response.
The policy were seriously flawed, and officials lacked a coherent response.
The policy was not seriously flawed, and officials lacked a coherent response.
Fix register: The policy was, honestly, a total mess and nobody knew what to do.
questions.e: The policy was seriously flawed, and officials lacked a coherent response. (Measured formal register.)

questions.q: Which Rule is associated with Example Sentence “He lives in the Punjab. They climbed the Himalayas. We swam in the Atlantic Ocean.” in the English reference?
o: Use the with provinces, mountain ranges, rivers, oceans
Use the with names of famous books
Use the when speaking of a known person or thing
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 225: Rule “Use the with provinces, mountain ranges, rivers, oceans” corresponds to Example Sentence “He lives in the Punjab. They climbed the Himalayas. We swam in the Atlantic Ocean.”.

questions.q: Transport-depot calculation — A invests Rs 58000 for 10 months and B invests Rs 10000 for 9 months. If their profit is Rs 6700, what is A's share?
questions.e: Profit follows capital-months. The weights are 580000:90000; A therefore receives Rs 5800.

questions.q: Health-programme report — A invests Rs 59000 for 6 months and B invests Rs 11000 for 10 months. If their profit is Rs 4640, what is A's share?
questions.e: Profit follows capital-months. The weights are 354000:110000; A therefore receives Rs 3540.

questions.q: Transport-depot calculation — The mean of 12 observations in a report is 84. One entry, 74, is corrected to 98. What is the corrected mean?
questions.e: The total rises by 24; divided across 12 observations, the mean rises by 2 to 86.

questions.q: Warehouse planning case — A two-digit number has digit sum 11; reversing its digits reduces it by 9. What is the original number?
questions.e: Let the tens and units digits be x and y. Then x + y = 11 and 9(x − y) = 9; hence x = 6, y = 5.

questions.q: Training-centre exercise — A two-digit number has digit sum 5; reversing its digits reduces it by 27. What is the original number?
questions.e: Let the tens and units digits be x and y. Then x + y = 5 and 9(x − y) = 27; hence x = 4, y = 1.

questions.q: District-office worksheet — The mean of 19 observations in a report is 55. One entry, 45, is corrected to 83. What is the corrected mean?
questions.e: The total rises by 38; divided across 19 observations, the mean rises by 2 to 57.

questions.q: Survey-unit review — A geometric sequence has first term 30 and common ratio 3. What is its 5th term?
Training-centre exercise — A geometric sequence has first term 31 and common ratio 4. What is its 6th term?
Relief-camp planning case — The roots of x² − 41x + 418 = 0 differ by 3. What is the larger root?
questions.e: The quadratic factors as (x − 19)(x − 22); the larger root is 22.

questions.q: District-office worksheet — The roots of x² − 44x + 480 = 0 differ by 4. What is the larger root?
questions.e: The quadratic factors as (x − 20)(x − 24); the larger root is 24.

questions.q: Scholarship-fund audit — Worker B takes 41 days for a task. Worker A is 50% more efficient than B. How many days would A need for the same task?
questions.e: Time varies inversely with efficiency, so A's time is 41 × 100/150 = 27.33 days.

questions.q: Warehouse planning case — Worker B takes 42 days for a task. Worker A is 100% more efficient than B. How many days would A need for the same task?
questions.e: Time varies inversely with efficiency, so A's time is 42 × 100/200 = 21 days.
