o: مرک بِ توصیفی — عدد اور اسم پر مشتمل ترکیب۔
مرک بِ اضافی — دو اسم جن میں ایک دوسرے کی وضاحت کرے۔
مرک بِ امتزاجی — صفت اور موصوف پر مشتمل ترکیب۔
مرک بِ عددی — دو اسم یا الفاظ اس طرح جُڑ جائیں کہ الگ نہ کیے جا سکیں۔
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 214: مرک بِ اضافی — دو اسم جن میں ایک دوسرے کی وضاحت کرے۔

questions.q: تعریف “وہ اسم جو کسی شخص کے والد یا بچوں کی طرف اشارہ کرتا ہے۔” اور مثال “ابو علی، ام محمد” کس اصطلاح کو ظاہر کرتی ہیں؟
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 209: کنیت — وہ اسم جو کسی شخص کے والد یا بچوں کی طرف اشارہ کرتا ہے۔

questions.q: یہ تعریف کس اصطلاح کی ہے؟ “وہ فعل جو جملے میں صرف اسناد (ربط) کے لیے آتا ہے اور مکمل معنی نہیں دیتا۔”
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 210: ناقص — وہ فعل جو جملے میں صرف اسناد (ربط) کے لیے آتا ہے اور مکمل معنی نہیں دیتا۔

questions.q: تعریف “وہ حرف یا جز جو لفظ کے آخر میں لگ کر اس کے معنی میں تبدیلی پیدا کرے” اور مثال “عقل + مند = عقلمند” کس اصطلاح کو ظاہر کرتی ہیں؟
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 215: الحقہ — وہ حرف یا جز جو لفظ کے آخر میں لگ کر اس کے معنی میں تبدیلی پیدا کرے

questions.q: یہ تعریف کس اصطلاح کی ہے؟ “وہ لفظ جو کسی اسم کی جگہ آتا ہے”
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 208: ضمیر — وہ لفظ جو کسی اسم کی جگہ آتا ہے

questions.q: تعریف “جو تعریف و تحسین کے لیے استعمال ہو۔” اور مثال “سبحان ہللا، واہ واہ، کیا بات ہے” کس اصطلاح کو ظاہر کرتی ہیں؟
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 212: حرفِ تحسین — جو تعریف و تحسین کے لیے استعمال ہو۔

questions.q: “حرو فِ علت” کی درست تعریف منتخب کریں۔
o: وہ حروف جن پر نقطے ہوتے ہیں 52 کل
وہ حروف جن پر کوئی نقطہ نہیں 52 ہوتا۔ کل
کل: 51 ایسے حروف جن کے ساتھ "ال" لگانے پر "ل" کا تلفظ نہیں ہوتا
وہ حروف جن میں نرمی ہو، آواز کو لمبا کرتے ہیں یا کمزور تلفظ رکھتے ہیں
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 212: حرو فِ علت — وہ حروف جن میں نرمی ہو، آواز کو لمبا کرتے ہیں یا کمزور تلفظ رکھتے ہیں

questions.q: ان اصطلاحات—اشباع، امالہ، ادغام، محذوف—میں درست اصطلاح اور تعریف کا جوڑا منتخب کریں۔
o: ادغام — وہ حرف یا حرکت جو موجود تو ہو مگر تلفظ میں نہ آئے۔
امالہ — دو ہم آواز حروف کو مال کر ایک ساتھ پڑھنا یا لکھنا۔
اشباع — حرکت کو لمبا کر کے پڑھنا
محذوف — امال کے لحاظ سے کسی لفظ میں الف یا ی کو بڑی ے میں تبدیل کرنا۔
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 213: اشباع — حرکت کو لمبا کر کے پڑھنا

questions.q: “حرف تشبیہ” کی درست تعریف منتخب کریں۔
o: جو کسی چیز کی خصوصیت یا شمولیت کو ظاہر کرے۔
وہ حرف جو کسی چیز کو کسی اور سے تشبیہ دینے کے لیے ہو
وہ حرف جو اسم پر داخل ہو کر اسے مجرور کرتا ہے، اور رابطے یا نسبت کو ظاہر کرتا ہے۔
جو دو الفاظ یا جملوں کو مالنے کے لیے استعمال ہو۔
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 211: حرف تشبیہ — وہ حرف جو کسی چیز کو کسی اور سے تشبیہ دینے کے لیے ہو

questions.q: یہ تعریف کس اصطلاح کی ہے؟ “وہ اسم جو کسی شخص کو کسی خاص خصوصیت یا حیثیت کی وجہ سے دیا جاتا ہے۔”
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 209: لقب — وہ اسم جو کسی شخص کو کسی خاص خصوصیت یا حیثیت کی وجہ سے دیا جاتا ہے۔

questions.q: یہ تعریف کس اصطلاح کی ہے؟ “ایسا لفظ جس کا کوئی مطلب نہ ہو اور نہ جملے میں استعمال کیا جا سکے۔”
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 208: مہمل — ایسا لفظ جس کا کوئی مطلب نہ ہو اور نہ جملے میں استعمال کیا جا سکے۔

questions.q: تعریف “حرف کو دہُرا اور زور سے ادا کرنے کی عالمت۔” اور مثال “شد،ّ مد،ّ مح بّ، لّٰلا” کس اصطلاح کو ظاہر کرتی ہیں؟
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 213: تشدید — حرف کو دہُرا اور زور سے ادا کرنے کی عالمت۔

questions.q:
Read the passage: “An app marked an answer correct only if it matched an exact phrase. Several equivalent explanations were rejected. The developers introduced a review process for answers expressing the same idea in different words.”

What problem did the exact-match rule create?
o: It prevented any answer being submitted
It could reject a substantively correct answer
questions.e: Equivalent explanations can differ in wording.

questions.q:
Read the passage: “An app marked an answer correct only if it matched an exact phrase. Several equivalent explanations were rejected. The developers introduced a review process for answers expressing the same idea in different words.”

Why add human review?
o: To judge meaning when phrasing differs
To require longer answers from everyone
questions.e: Review can assess whether differently worded responses express the same idea.

questions.q: In Prepositions, which Preposition corresponds to Rule “Effectiveness or appropriateness”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 232: Rule “Effectiveness or appropriateness” corresponds to Preposition “To”.

questions.q: In Parts of Speech, which Examples corresponds to Part of Speech “Adjective”?
o: and (Coordinating - joins swimming and hiking)because (Subordinating - shows reason)either...or (Correlative - shows choice)
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 229: Part of Speech “Adjective” corresponds to Examples “red (Descriptive - Color)bigger (Comparative - Size)laziest (Superlative - Quality)”.

questions.q: In Direct and Indirect Speech, which Indirect Speech corresponds to Direct Speech “Today”?
o: The Previous Day / The Day Before
The Next Day / The Following Day
The Previous Night / The Night Before
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 227: Direct Speech “Today” corresponds to Indirect Speech “That Day”.

questions.q: In Direct and Indirect Speech, which Reporting Verb corresponds to Type “Request”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 228: Type “Request” corresponds to Reporting Verb “Requested”.

questions.q: In Prepositions, which Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) corresponds to Rule “Used for position on a surface”?
o: He sat by the door, waiting for her.
She is sitting at the desk, writing a letter.
The book is lying on the table.
They rested under the tree. The kids played under the sun. I slept under the open sky.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 231: Rule “Used for position on a surface” corresponds to Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) “The book is lying on the table.”.

questions.q: In Parts of Speech, which Explanation corresponds to Part of Speech “Pronoun”?
o: Explains how, when, where, or to what extent an action happens
Tells what the subject is doing
Gives more information about a noun
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 229: Part of Speech “Pronoun” corresponds to Explanation “Used to avoid repetition”.

questions.q: In Prepositions, which Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) corresponds to Rule “Applied for a thing or purpose”?
o: They laughed at his joke. She was shocked at the news. The crowd sneered at the performer. He was horrified at the scene. The bullies jeered at him.
The clock's arms moved forward by one hour. Last night, we moved the clocks back for winter time.
She pulled through the illness. He saw through the deception.
He applied for a job in the bank.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 232: Rule “Applied for a thing or purpose” corresponds to Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) “He applied for a job in the bank.”.

questions.q: In Direct and Indirect Speech, which Example corresponds to Type “Joy”?
o: He said, "Alas! He is dead." → He exclaimed with sorrow that he was dead.
He said, "May you live long!" → He wished that I might live long.
He said, "May God help us." → He prayed that God might help them.
He said, "Hurrah! We won the match." → He exclaimed with joy that they had won the match.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 228: Type “Joy” corresponds to Example “He said, "Hurrah! We won the match." → He exclaimed with joy that they had won the match.”.

questions.q: For Prepositions, which Type–Sentence Example association is accurate?
o: Preposition of Manner — I like tea and coffee.
Preposition of Reason — He won by luck.
Preposition of Direction — He walked to the shop.
Coordinating Conjunction — He left because of the rain.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 231: Type “Preposition of Direction” corresponds to Sentence Example “He walked to the shop.”.

questions.q: In Parts of Speech, which Examples corresponds to Part of Speech “Determiners”?
o: book (Thing - Common Noun)France (Place - Proper Noun)band (Group of People - Collective Noun)
the (Definite - Specific noun)a (Indefinite - General noun)an (Indefinite - General noun)
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 229: Part of Speech “Determiners” corresponds to Examples “this (Demonstrative)my (Possessive)many (Quantifier)”.

questions.q: In Parts of Speech, which Sentence Example corresponds to Type “Descriptive Adjective”?
o: This house is bigger than mine.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 230: Type “Descriptive Adjective” corresponds to Sentence Example “She is beautiful.”.

questions.q: In Direct and Indirect Speech, which Indirect Speech corresponds to Direct Speech “He says, "I like tea."”?
o: He says that he likes tea.
He will say that he is ready.
He said that the sun rises in the east.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 226: Direct Speech “He says, "I like tea."” corresponds to Indirect Speech “He says that he likes tea.”.

questions.q: In Direct and Indirect Speech, which Indirect Speech corresponds to Direct Speech “Present Perfect”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 226: Direct Speech “Present Perfect” corresponds to Indirect Speech “Past Perfect”.

questions.q: In Parts of Speech, which Example Word corresponds to Type “Possessive Adjective”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 230: Type “Possessive Adjective” corresponds to Example Word “my, his”.

questions.q: In Prepositions, which Rule corresponds to Preposition “Of”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 232: Preposition “Of” corresponds to Rule “Legal or moral state/status”.

questions.q: In Sentences, Clauses and Phrases, which Example corresponds to Sentence Type “Compound Sentence”?
o: A. When it rained, we stayed inside. B. We stayed inside when it rained. C. My car, which is red, is fast. D. The man who called is my friend.
Although it rained, we went outside, and we enjoyed the walk.
A. He studied, and he passed. B. He studied; therefore, he passed. C. He studied; he passed.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 233: Sentence Type “Compound Sentence” corresponds to Example “A. He studied, and he passed. B. He studied; therefore, he passed. C. He studied; he passed.”.

questions.q: In Active and Passive Voice, which Active Formula corresponds to Tense “Future Perfect Continuous ❌”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 224: Tense “Future Perfect Continuous ❌” corresponds to Active Formula “Not Possible”.

questions.q: For Active and Passive Voice, which Tense–Example (Active) association is accurate?
o: Present Indefinite — He writes a letter.
Past Indefinite — He will finish the work.
Future Indefinite — They are playing cricket.
Present Continuous — They built a house.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 224: Tense “Present Indefinite” corresponds to Example (Active) “He writes a letter.”.

questions.q: In Sentences, Clauses and Phrases, which Rule corresponds to Preposition “In / On”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 233: Preposition “In / On” corresponds to Rule “Confusion over "sat in/on" tree”.

questions.q: In Sentences, Clauses and Phrases, which Example corresponds to Connector Type “Relative Pronouns (Adjective Clause)”?
o: He was late; however, he completed the task.
My friend, who is a doctor, is coming. People who work hard succeed.
What he said shocked everyone. I believe that honesty matters.
He plays cricket, and she plays football.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 234: Connector Type “Relative Pronouns (Adjective Clause)” corresponds to Example “My friend, who is a doctor, is coming. People who work hard succeed.”.

questions.q: For Sentences, Clauses and Phrases, which Sentence Type–Clause Structure association is accurate?
o: Complex Sentence — Two or More ndependent Clauses + One or More Dependent Clauses
Compound Sentence — One Independent Clause + One or More Dependent Clauses
Compound- Complex Sentence — Two Independent Clauses
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 233: Sentence Type “Simple Sentence” corresponds to Clause Structure “One Independent Clause”.

questions.q: In Sentences, Clauses and Phrases, which Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) corresponds to Rule “Travel using public/shared transport”?
o: He came on a bus. She travels on a train daily. They flew on a plane.
People in our city travel mostly by train.
He goes to the office on foot every day.
She arrived in a car. He was taken in an ambulance. They rode in a taxi.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 233: Rule “Travel using public/shared transport” corresponds to Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) “He came on a bus. She travels on a train daily. They flew on a plane.”.

questions.q: In Active and Passive Voice, which Example (Active) corresponds to Tense “Future Perfect”?
o: She will have completed the project.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 224: Tense “Future Perfect” corresponds to Example (Active) “She will have completed the project.”.

questions.q: In Active and Passive Voice, which Passive Formula corresponds to Tense “Present Perfect”?
o: Object + had been + V3 + by + Subject
Object + will/shall + have been + V3 + by + Subject
Object + has/have + been + V3 + by + Subject
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 224: Tense “Present Perfect” corresponds to Passive Formula “Object + has/have + been + V3 + by + Subject”.

questions.q: In Twelve-Tense Reference, which Structure corresponds to Tense “Future Continuous”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 244: Tense “Future Continuous” corresponds to Structure “subject + will/shall be + verb-ing”.

questions.s: Timed simulation across the whole syllabus
questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Each of the provinces have submitted their plan, but the number of plans that has been examined are very small.”?
o: Each of the provinces has submitted its plan, but the number of plans that have been examined is very small.
Each of the provinces have submitted its plan, but the number of plans that have been examined is very small.
Each of the provinces has not submitted its plan, but the number of plans that have been examined is very small.
Each of the provinces have submitted their plan, but the number of plans that has been examined are very small.
questions.e: Three agreement decisions: each is singular, that refers to plans, and the number of is singular.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The literacy rate of Sindh is lower than Punjab, and its budget is also more smaller.”?
o: The literacy rate of Sindh is not lower than that of Punjab, and its budget is also smaller.
The literacy rate of Sindh is lower than Punjab, and its budget is also more smaller.
The literacy rate of Sindh is lower than that of Punjab, and its budget is also smaller.
The literacy rate of Sindh are lower than that of Punjab, and its budget is also smaller.
questions.e: Compare rate with rate, and never double the comparative.

questions.s: Timed simulation across the whole syllabus
questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Despite of the objections, the committee suggested to postpone the decision and asked that the file is re-examined.”?
o: Despite the objections, the committee suggested postponing the decision and asked that the file be re-examined.
Despite objections, the committee suggested postponing the decision and asked that the file be re-examined.
Despite the objections, the committee suggested postponing the decision and asked that the file be re-examined not.
Despite of the objections, the committee suggested to postpone the decision and asked that the file is re-examined.
questions.e: Despite takes no of, suggest takes the gerund, and ask that takes the subjunctive.

questions.s: Timed simulation across the whole syllabus
questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “He is working here since 2016 and has completed his training last year, therefore he is eligible for promotion.”?
o: He has been working here since 2016 and completed his training last year; he is therefore eligible for promotion.
He is working here since 2016 and has completed his training last year, therefore he is eligible for promotion.
He has not been working here since 2016 and completed his training last year; he is therefore eligible for promotion.
He have been working here since 2016 and completed his training last year; he is therefore eligible for promotion.
questions.e: Since, a finished time, and a comma splice before therefore.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Karachi is more bigger than any city of Pakistan and it is also the most busiest.”?
o: Karachi is not bigger than any other city in Pakistan, and it is also the busiest.
Karachi is more bigger than any city of Pakistan and it is also the most busiest.
Karachi is bigger than any other city in Pakistan, and it is also the busiest.
Karachi are bigger than any other city in Pakistan, and it is also the busiest.
questions.e: Remove both double markers and exclude Karachi from the group with other.

questions.s: Timed simulation across the whole syllabus
questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The population of Karachi is more bigger than Lahore, and it has less facilities than any city of Pakistan.”?
o: The population of Karachi is bigger than that of Lahore, and the city has fewer facilities than any other city in Pakistan.
The population of Karachi is bigger than that of Lahore, and the city have fewer facilities than any other city in Pakistan.
The population of Karachi is not bigger than that of Lahore, and the city has fewer facilities than any other city in Pakistan.
The population of Karachi is more bigger than Lahore, and it has less facilities than any city of Pakistan.
questions.e: A double comparative, a faulty comparison, less with a countable noun, and a missing other.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “He is the most intelligent of the two brothers and more senior than me by three years.”?
o: He is not the more intelligent of the two brothers and senior to me by three years.
He are the more intelligent of the two brothers and senior to me by three years.
He is the more intelligent of the two brothers and senior to me by three years.
He is the most intelligent of the two brothers and more senior than me by three years.
questions.e: Two items take the comparative, and senior takes to with no more.

questions.s: Timed simulation across the whole syllabus
questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Having reviewed the accounts, three irregularities were found, which was reported to the secretary who ordered an inquiry.”?
o: Having reviewed the accounts, the auditors found three irregularities and reported them to the secretary, who ordered an inquiry.
Having reviewed the accounts, three irregularities were found, which was reported to the secretary who ordered an inquiry.
Having reviewed the accounts, the auditors found three irregularities and reported them to the secretary, who ordered an inquiry not.
Having reviewed the accounts, the auditors found three irregularities and reported them than the secretary, who ordered an inquiry.
questions.e: A dangling participle, a pronoun with no clear antecedent, and an agreement error.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “This scheme is superior than the previous one because it costs lesser and covers more districts.”?
o: This scheme is not superior to the previous one because it costs less and covers more districts.
This scheme is superior than the previous one because it costs lesser and covers more districts.
This scheme is superior to the previous one because it costs less and covers more districts.
This scheme are superior to the previous one because it costs less and covers more districts.
questions.e: Superior takes to, and less is already comparative.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “It may possibly perhaps be argued that there has been continuous interruption in supply every evening.”?
o: It may possibly perhaps be argued that there has been continuous interruption in supply every evening.
It may be argued that supply has been interrupted continually every evening.
It may be argued that supply have been interrupted continually every evening.
It may not be argued that supply has been interrupted continually every evening.
questions.e: One hedge is enough, and repeated interruptions are continual.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The report comprises of four chapters and it implies from the data that enforcement is weak.”?
o: The report comprises of four chapters and it implies from the data that enforcement is weak.
The report comprises four chapters and infers from the data that enforcement is not weak.
The report comprises four chapters and infers from the data that enforcement are weak.
The report comprises four chapters and infers from the data that enforcement is weak.
questions.e: Comprise takes no of; drawing a conclusion from data is inferring.

questions.q: Which Rule is associated with Example Sentence “I visited the Eiffel Tower. He reads the Economist every week. She works in the Parliament House.” in the English reference?
o: Use the with books, journals, and buildings
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 225: Rule “Use the with books, journals, and buildings” corresponds to Example Sentence “I visited the Eiffel Tower. He reads the Economist every week. She works in the Parliament House.”.

questions.s: Modifiers: put the describing words where they belong
questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Having been delayed by three years, the minister finally inaugurated the project.”?
o: Having been delayed by three years, the project was not finally inaugurated by the minister.
Having been delayed by three years, the project were finally inaugurated by the minister.
Having been delayed by three years, the project was finally inaugurated by the minister.
Having been delayed by three years, the minister finally inaugurated the project.
questions.e: The minister was not delayed by three years; the project was.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The govt didn’t do much about the issue & everyone knows it was a total failure.”?
o: The govt didn’t do much about the issue & everyone knows it was a total failure.
The government took little action on the issue, and the initiative is widely regarded as a failure.
The government took little action on the issue, and the initiative are widely regarded as a failure.
The government took little action on the issue, and the initiative is not widely regarded as a failure.
questions.e: Abbreviation, contraction, ampersand and overstatement all removed.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “When the SHO met the complainant, he refused to register the case, and this caused a protest.”?
o: When the SHO met the complainant, the SHO refused to register the case, and this refusal caused a protest not.
When the SHO met the complainant, he refused to register the case, and this caused a protest.
When the SHO met the complainant, the SHO refused to register the case, and this refusal caused a protest.
When the SHO met the complainant, the SHO refused than register the case, and this refusal caused a protest.
questions.e: He was ambiguous and this was empty; naming both removes the guesswork.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Everyone should bring their own copy of the rules, and he must sign the register.”?
o: Everyone should not bring their own copy of the rules and sign the register.
Everyone should bring their own copy of rules and sign the register.
Everyone should bring their own copy of the rules and sign the register.
Everyone should bring their own copy of the rules, and he must sign the register.
questions.e: Mixing they and he for the same antecedent is inconsistent.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Although the policy looks attractive on paper, but its implementation has failed.”?
o: Although the policy looks attractive on paper, its implementation have failed.
Although the policy looks attractive on paper, its implementation has not failed.
Although the policy looks attractive on paper, but its implementation has failed.

وہ لفظ جو کسی شخص، جگہ، چیز یا صفت کا نام ہو

o: الزم — وہ مسدر جس کا فعل فاعل اور مفعول دونوں کو چاہیے، یعنی اس کا اثر دوسرے پر بھی پڑتا ہے۔
جمع — وہ اسم جو کسی چیز کی کثرت یا مقدار ظاہر کرے۔
ذاتی / تفصیلی — وہ مسدر جس کا فعل صرف فاعل کو چاہیے، یعنی اس کا اثر صرف کرنے والے پر ہوتا ہے۔
متعدی — وہ صفت جو کسی چیز کی ذاتی خوبی یا خامی ظاہر کرے۔
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 209: جمع — وہ اسم جو کسی چیز کی کثرت یا مقدار ظاہر کرے۔

o: ایک لفظ دوسرے کا مادہ ہو (جس سے وہ بنا ہو)

o: تصغیر — وہ اسم جو کسی چیز کو بڑا یا اہم ظاہر کرے۔
مکبر — وہ اسم جو کسی شخص کا فرضی یا قلمی نام ہوتا ہے، جو شاعری یا ادبی کاموں میں استعمال ہوتا ہے۔

questions.q: “روزمرہ” کی درست تعریف منتخب کریں۔
o: وہ جملے یا الفاظ جو روزانہ کی بات چیت میں معمولی طور پر استعمال ہوتے ہیں، جن کا مطلب صاف اور واضح ہوتا ہے۔
تشبیہ سے مبالغہ کرتے ہوئے مشبہ کا ذکر چھوڑ دینا اور صرف مشبہ بہ کو بطور حقیقت بیان کرنا۔
کسی چیز کو کسی دوسری چیز کے مشابہ قرار دینا جس میں دونوں کے درمیان کوئی مشترک خوبی ہو۔
ایک جملہ یا قول جو زندگی کے تجربات یا سچائیوں کو سادہ اور اثر دار انداز میں بیان کرتا ہے۔
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 215: روزمرہ — وہ جملے یا الفاظ جو روزانہ کی بات چیت میں معمولی طور پر استعمال ہوتے ہیں، جن کا مطلب صاف اور واضح ہوتا ہے۔

o: وہ اسم جو کسی چیز یا فعل کے لیے آلہ یا اوزار کو ظاہر کرے۔
وہ اسم جو کسی چیز کو بڑا یا اہم ظاہر کرے۔
وہ اسم جو کسی چیز کی چھوٹی صورت یا حقارت ظاہر کرے۔
وہ اسم جو وقت کو ظاہر کرے۔
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 209: تصغیر — وہ اسم جو کسی چیز کی چھوٹی صورت یا حقارت ظاہر کرے۔

questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 214: تملیکی — ملکیت ظاہر کرے (کسی چیز کا مالک کون ہے)

questions.q: ان اصطلاحات—تنوین، تشدید، موقوف و ساکن، اشباع—میں درست اصطلاح اور تعریف کا جوڑا منتخب کریں۔
o: تشدید — وقف کی صورت میں لفظ کا آخری حرف ساکن ہو جاتا ہے۔
تنوین — دو زبر، دو زیر یا دو پیش - آواز میں نون کی جھلک دیتی ہے۔
اشباع — حرف کو دہُرا اور زور سے ادا کرنے کی عالمت۔
موقوف و ساکن — حرکت کو لمبا کر کے پڑھنا

questions.q:
Read the passage: “A municipality assessed a pilot based on the number of complaints received. Complaints increased after a new reporting line became easier to use. Officials decided to measure both the number reported and the number resolved.”

Which measure adds information about the response?
o: The length of the reporting line
questions.e: Resolution indicates how the municipality handled reported cases.

questions.q:
Read the passage: “A municipality assessed a pilot based on the number of complaints received. Complaints increased after a new reporting line became easier to use. Officials decided to measure both the number reported and the number resolved.”

Why could more complaints be misleading?
o: All complaints had been resolved before reporting
A complaint always proves a new problem
Reporting became easier, so more problems may now be visible
questions.e: The reporting channel can affect the observed count.

questions.q: For Prepositions, which Rule–Preposition association is accurate?
o: Used when some work is finished, or for disconnection/cutting — Off
Used for position on a surface — At
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 231: Rule “Used when some work is finished, or for disconnection/cutting” corresponds to Preposition “Off”.

questions.q: In Prepositions, which Preposition corresponds to Rule “Used for benefit or harm”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 232: Rule “Used for benefit or harm” corresponds to Preposition “To”.

questions.q: For Prepositions, which Rule–Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) association is accurate?
o: Sitting beside something — The book is lying on the table.
Used for working position — He sat by the door, waiting for her.
Used for position on a surface — She is sitting at the desk, writing a letter.
Used when some work is finished, or for disconnection/cutting — The power was cut off during the storm. He jumped off the wall.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 231: Rule “Used when some work is finished, or for disconnection/cutting” corresponds to Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) “The power was cut off during the storm. He jumped off the wall.”.

questions.q: In Prepositions, which Rule corresponds to Preposition “For”?
o: Applied for a thing or purpose
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 232: Preposition “For” corresponds to Rule “Applied for a thing or purpose”.

questions.q: In Parts of Speech, which Sentence Example corresponds to Type “Uncountable Noun”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 230: Type “Uncountable Noun” corresponds to Sentence Example “I need some water.”.

questions.q: In Direct and Indirect Speech, which Indirect Speech corresponds to Direct Speech “Present Continuous”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 226: Direct Speech “Present Continuous” corresponds to Indirect Speech “Past Continuous”.

questions.q: In Prepositions, which Definition corresponds to Type “Subordinating Conjunction”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 231: Type “Subordinating Conjunction” corresponds to Definition “Joins dependent clause”.

questions.q: In Parts of Speech, which Definition corresponds to Part of Speech “Adverb”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 229: Part of Speech “Adverb” corresponds to Definition “Modifies verb, adjective, or sentence”.

questions.q: In Direct and Indirect Speech, which Example corresponds to Direct Speech “Next week”?
o: He said, "These flowers are beautiful." → He said that those flowers were beautiful.
He said, "I like this book." → He said that he liked that book.
He said, "I am here." → He said that he was there.
He said, "I will visit next week." → He said that he would visit the following week.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 227: Direct Speech “Next week” corresponds to Example “He said, "I will visit next week." → He said that he would visit the following week.”.

questions.q: In Direct and Indirect Speech, which Indirect Speech corresponds to Direct Speech “He said, "Where are you going?"”?
o: He asked where I was going.
She asked what my name was.
She requested not to disturb her.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 227: Direct Speech “He said, "Where are you going?"” corresponds to Indirect Speech “He asked where I was going.”.

questions.q: In Parts of Speech, which Definition corresponds to Type “Superlative Adjective”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 230: Type “Superlative Adjective” corresponds to Definition “Describes highest degree”.

questions.q: In Parts of Speech, which Example Word corresponds to Type “Concrete Noun”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 229: Type “Concrete Noun” corresponds to Example Word “chair”.

questions.q: In Direct and Indirect Speech, which Direct Speech corresponds to Indirect Speech “Then”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 227: Indirect Speech “Then” corresponds to Direct Speech “Now”.

questions.q: In Parts of Speech, which Example Word corresponds to Type “Superlative Adjective”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 230: Type “Superlative Adjective” corresponds to Example Word “laziest”.

questions.q: In Active and Passive Voice, which Active Formula corresponds to Tense “Present Perfect Continuous ❌”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 224: Tense “Present Perfect Continuous ❌” corresponds to Active Formula “Not Possible”.

questions.q: In Direct and Indirect Speech, which Example corresponds to Direct Speech “These”?
o: He said, "I met him two days ago." → He said that he had met him two days before.
He said, "I have just finished." → He said that he had only finished.
He said, "Come here." → He told me to go there.
He said, "These flowers are beautiful." → He said that those flowers were beautiful.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 227: Direct Speech “These” corresponds to Example “He said, "These flowers are beautiful." → He said that those flowers were beautiful.”.

questions.q: In Sentences, Clauses and Phrases, which Definition / Explanation corresponds to Sentence Type “Compound- Complex Sentence”?
o: A sentence with one independent clause and one or more dependent clauses.
A sentence that has two or I more independent clauses and at least one dependent clause.
A sentence with only one independent clause. It expresses a complete thought.
A sentence with two or more independent clauses, joined by a coordinating conjunction, conjunctive adverb, or semicolon.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 234: Sentence Type “Compound- Complex Sentence” corresponds to Definition / Explanation “A sentence that has two or I more independent clauses and at least one dependent clause.”.

questions.q: In Sentences, Clauses and Phrases, which Rule corresponds to Preposition “From”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 233: Preposition “From” corresponds to Rule “Retreat or reversal movement”.

questions.q: In Sentences, Clauses and Phrases, which Example corresponds to Connector Type “Subordinating Conjunctions (Adverb Clause)”?
o: My friend, who is a doctor, is coming. People who work hard succeed.
Because he was ill, he stayed home. He stayed home because he was ill.
He plays cricket, and she plays football.
What he said shocked everyone. I believe that honesty matters.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 234: Connector Type “Subordinating Conjunctions (Adverb Clause)” corresponds to Example “Because he was ill, he stayed home. He stayed home because he was ill.”.

questions.q: For Sentences, Clauses and Phrases, which Connector Type–Explanation / Usage association is accurate?
o: Coordinating Conjunctions (FANBOYS) — Join two independent clauses in compound sentences
Conjunctive Adverbs — Introduce a dependent clause in complex sentences
Subordinating Conjunctions (Adverb Clause) — Introduce a dependent clause describing a noun
Relative Pronouns (Adjective Clause) — Join two independent clauses, showing relationship (cause, contrast, result, etc.)
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 234: Connector Type “Coordinating Conjunctions (FANBOYS)” corresponds to Explanation / Usage “Join two independent clauses in compound sentences”.

questions.q: For Sentences, Clauses and Phrases, which Rule–Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) association is accurate?
o: Desire/longing related to personality — The army retrogressed from the battlefield. They had to retreat from enemy lines.
Retreat or reversal movement — He sat in the tree, hidden by leaves. He sat on the branch and started whistling.
Confusion over "sat in/on" tree — He is ambitious of fame. She has ambition for power. He aspires to greatness.
Comparison between similar things — He compared one type of mango with another.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 233: Rule “Comparison between similar things” corresponds to Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) “He compared one type of mango with another.”.

questions.s: Concision: saying it in fewer words
questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “In my personal opinion, I believe that each and every candidate should be informed.”?
o: I believe every candidate should be informed.
I believe that every candidate should be informed.
In my personal opinion, I believe that each and every candidate should be informed.
I believe that every candidate should not be informed.
questions.e: Opinion is already personal, and each and every says one thing twice.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Had the warnings been heeded, the disaster could have been avoided. (Confirm whether correct.)”?
o: Had the warnings been heeded, the disaster could have been avoided. (Confirm whether correct.)
questions.e: Correct inverted third conditional (Had … been heeded = If … had been heeded).

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “If institutions are strong, corruption spreads less. (Identify the type and confirm.)”?
o: Correct zero conditional expressing a general truth not.
Correct zero conditional expressing an general truth.
Correct zero conditional expressing a general truth.
If institutions are strong, corruption spreads less. (Identify the type and confirm.)
questions.e: Correct zero conditional expressing a general truth.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “He is living in Islamabad for the last ten years and has bought a house there last year.”?
o: He is living in Islamabad for the last ten years and has bought a house there last year.
He has been living in Islamabad for the last ten years and bought a house there last year.
He have been living in Islamabad for the last ten years and bought a house there last year.
He has not been living in Islamabad for the last ten years and bought a house there last year.
questions.e: For + duration to now takes the present perfect continuous; last year is finished and takes the past simple.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “By the time the notification issued, most candidates already had submitted their applications.”?
o: By the time the notification were issued, most candidates had already submitted their applications.
By the time the notification was issued, most candidates had already submitted their applications.
By the time the notification issued, most candidates already had submitted their applications.
By the time the notification was not issued, most candidates had already submitted their applications.
questions.e: The notification needs a passive verb, and already sits between had and the participle.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The cost of living has raised sharply, and many families has reduced their spending.”?
o: The cost of living have risen sharply, and many families have reduced their spending.
The cost of living has risen sharply, and many families have reduced their spending.
The cost of living has raised sharply, and many families has reduced their spending.
The cost of living has not risen sharply, and many families have reduced their spending.
questions.e: Rise is intransitive; families is plural and takes have.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The government promised to lower taxes, create jobs, and that it would build schools.”?
o: ...promised to lower taxes, create jobs, and build schools not.
The government promised to lower taxes, create jobs, and that it would build schools.
...promised to lower taxes, create jobs, and build schools.
...promised than lower taxes, create jobs, and build schools.
questions.e: ...promised to lower taxes, create jobs, and build schools. (Three bare infinitives after to.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Reading widely and making notes regularly improves a candidate’s recall, and are essential habits.”?
o: Reading widely and making notes regularly improves a candidate’s recall, and are essential habits.
Reading widely and making notes regularly improve a candidate’s recall; they are essential habits.
Reading widely and making notes regularly improve a candidate’s recall; they is essential habits.
Reading widely and making notes regularly improve a candidate’s recall; they are not essential habits.
questions.e: Two separate -ing activities are joined by and, so the subject is plural. The second half needs its own subject.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Good governance means listening to people, to act on evidence, and being accountable.”?
o: Good governance means listening to people, to act on evidence, and being accountable.
...means listening to people, acting on evidence, and being accountable.
...means listening than people, acting on evidence, and being accountable.
...means listening to people, acting on evidence, and being accountable not.
questions.e: ...means listening to people, acting on evidence, and being accountable. (Three gerunds.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Written by a committee of five, the policy contain contradictions on every page.”?
o: Written by an committee of five, the policy contains contradictions on every page.
Written by a committee of five, the policy contains contradictions on every page.
Written by a committee of five, the policy contain contradictions on every page.
Written by a committee of five, the policy contains contradictions on every page not.
questions.e: The opening phrase correctly describes policy; the only fault is agreement — singular policy takes contains.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “When one prepares a topic thoroughly, you remember it longer and we can write faster in the examination.”?
o: When candidates prepare an topic thoroughly, they remember it longer and write faster in the examination.
When candidates prepare a topic thoroughly, they remember it longer and write faster in the examination not.
When one prepares a topic thoroughly, you remember it longer and we can write faster in the examination.
When candidates prepare a topic thoroughly, they remember it longer and write faster in the examination.
questions.e: One person, held steady throughout.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Firstly, the data are incomplete. Secondly, the method was untested. Thirdly, therefore the conclusion is overstated. Fourthly, moreover the annexures are missing.”?
o: Firstly, the data are incomplete. Secondly, the method was untested. Thirdly, therefore the conclusion is overstated. Fourthly, moreover the annexures are missing.
The data are not incomplete and the method untested; the conclusion is therefore overstated. The annexures, moreover, are missing altogether.
The data are incomplete and the method untested; the conclusion are therefore overstated. The annexures, moreover, are missing altogether.

audit exposed fraud. This revelation weakened public trust. Restoring that trust required reform, yet the announced measures remained unfunded.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “He must to inform the office in advance, otherwise he will can lose his allowance.”?

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “If the government would have invested in primary education, literacy rates would be higher today.”?

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Compress without loss: “The government, which had been under considerable pressure from several quarters, finally decided to reverse the decision that it had taken earlier.””?
o: Compress without loss: “The government, which had been under considerable pressure from several quarters, finally decided to reverse the decision that it had taken earlier.”
Under pressure from several quarters, the government finally reversed its earlier decision not.
Under pressure from several quarters, government finally reversed its earlier decision.
Under pressure from several quarters, the government finally reversed its earlier decision.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Repair this compressed sentence: “Announced in 2019 and never funded, failing within two years.””?
o: Announced in 2019 and never funded, scheme failed within two years.
Announced in 2019 and never funded, the scheme failed within two years not.

Announced in 2019 and never funded, the scheme failed within two years.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Repair the frame: “The writer argued that enforcement is weak, and I agree that we must do something about it.””?
o: Repair the frame: “The writer argued that enforcement is weak, and I agree that we must do something about it.”
The writer argues that enforcement is not weak and that it must be strengthened.
The writer argues that enforcement are weak and that it must be strengthened.
The writer argues that enforcement is weak and that it must be strengthened.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Repair the boundary: “The scheme lapsed, funding had stopped in 2019, most districts were affected.””?

The scheme lapsed in most districts after funding stopped in 2019 not.
Repair the boundary: “The scheme lapsed, funding had stopped in 2019, most districts were affected.”
The scheme lapsed in most districts after funding stopped in 2019.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The earthquake was occurred at three in the morning and many houses were collapsed.”?
o: earthquake occurred at three in the morning and many houses collapsed.
The earthquake occurred at three in the morning and many houses collapsed.
The earthquake was occurred at three in the morning and many houses were collapsed.
The earthquake occurred at three in the morning and many houses collapsed not.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Each of the officers have been informed about their transfer, which were notified last week.”?
o: Each of the officers has not been informed of his transfer, which was notified last week.
Each of the officers have been informed of his transfer, which was notified last week.
Each of the officers has been informed of his transfer, which was notified last week.
Each of the officers have been informed about their transfer, which were notified last week.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Although the scheme was well designed, but it failed, because the funds which had been promised was never released.”?
o: Although the scheme was well designed, it failed because the funds that had been promised were never released.
Although the scheme were well designed, it failed because the funds that had been promised were never released.
Although the scheme was not well designed, it failed because the funds that had been promised were never released.
Although the scheme was well designed, but it failed, because the funds which had been promised was never released.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “He said that he is not aware of the irregularities and will cooperate with the inquiry fully.”?
o: He said that he is not aware of the irregularities and will cooperate with the inquiry fully.
He said that he was not not aware of the irregularities and would cooperate fully with the inquiry.
He said that he were not aware of the irregularities and would cooperate fully with the inquiry.
He said that he was not aware of the irregularities and would cooperate fully with the inquiry.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Due to the fact that there was less officers available, the department made a decision to postpone each and every hearing.”?

Because fewer officers was available, the department decided to postpone every hearing.
Because fewer officers were not available, the department decided to postpone every hearing.
Due to the fact that there was less officers available, the department made a decision to postpone each and every hearing.

Having examined the file, a decision was taken by the committee that the case is closed and no further action is required.

questions.q: District-office worksheet — A two-digit number has digit sum 10; reversing its digits increases it by 36. What is the original number?

questions.q: Transport-depot calculation — A train 500 m long clears a 100 m platform in 15 seconds. What is its speed in km/h?

questions.q: Transport-depot calculation — For two years at 15% per annum, by how much does compound interest exceed simple interest on Rs 560000?

questions.q: Survey-unit review — A invests Rs 40000 for 7 months and B invests Rs 6000 for 5 months. If their profit is Rs 3100, what is A's share?
questions.e: Profit follows capital-months. The weights are 280000:30000; A therefore receives Rs 2800.

questions.q: Transport-depot calculation — The mean of 17 observations in a report is 44. One entry, 34, is corrected to 68. What is the corrected mean?
questions.e: The total rises by 34; divided across 17 observations, the mean rises by 2 to 46.

questions.q: Survey-unit review — The mean of 13 observations in a report is 58. One entry, 48, is corrected to 74. What is the corrected mean?
questions.e: The total rises by 26; divided across 13 observations, the mean rises by 2 to 60.

questions.q: Survey-unit review — Worker B takes 59 days for a task. Worker A is 20% more efficient than B. How many days would A need for the same task?
questions.e: Time varies inversely with efficiency, so A's time is 59 × 100/120 = 49.17 days.

questions.q: Training-centre exercise — Worker B takes 60 days for a task. Worker A is 25% more efficient than B. How many days would A need for the same task?
questions.e: Time varies inversely with efficiency, so A's time is 60 × 100/125 = 48 days.

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — A geometric sequence has first term 26 and common ratio 2. What is its 5th term?
District-office worksheet — A geometric sequence has first term 27 and common ratio 3. What is its 6th term?

questions.e: Path area = outer area − inner area = 924 − 58×6 = 576 m².

questions.q: Survey-unit review — A tank contains 590 litres of a 25% solution. 118 litres of the mixture are removed and replaced by water. What is the new concentration?
questions.e: Removing one-fifth of a uniform mixture removes one-fifth of its solute. The remaining concentration is 25% × 4/5 = 20%.

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — A boat's still-water speed is 34 km/h and the stream flows at 6 km/h. How long does a 1120 km upstream and 1120 km downstream round trip take?

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — What is the least number greater than 2550 that leaves remainder 49 when divided by both 50 and 51, given that 50 and 51 are coprime?
questions.e: A common remainder means N − 49 is a multiple of lcm(50, 51) = 2550. The least eligible N is 2550 + 49 = 2599.

questions.q: District-office worksheet — What is the least number greater than 2652 that leaves remainder 50 when divided by both 51 and 52, given that 51 and 52 are coprime?
questions.e: A common remainder means N − 50 is a multiple of lcm(51, 52) = 2652. The least eligible N is 2652 + 50 = 2702.

questions.q: District-office worksheet — A boat's still-water speed is 27 km/h and the stream flows at 4 km/h. How long does a 2139 km upstream and 2139 km downstream round trip take?

questions.e: The bus has a 54 km lead. Relative speed is 10 km/h, so catch-up time is 5.4 hours.

questions.q: District-office worksheet — A bus leaves a district office at 55 km/h. 2 hours later, a car follows on the same route at 66 km/h. How long after the car starts will it catch the bus?
questions.e: The bus has a 110 km lead. Relative speed is 11 km/h, so catch-up time is 10 hours.

questions.q: Transport-depot calculation — Two batches assessed by a transport depot contain 42 and 14 candidates with mean scores 50 and 79. What is the combined mean?
questions.e: Use the weighted mean: (42 × 50 + 14 × 79) ÷ 56 = 57.25.

questions.q: Health-programme report — Two batches assessed by a health programme contain 43 and 15 candidates with mean scores 51 and 80. What is the combined mean?
questions.e: Use the weighted mean: (43 × 51 + 15 × 80) ÷ 58 = 58.5.

questions.q: Scholarship-fund audit — A can complete a project in 420 days and B in 630 days. They work together for 210 days; B then leaves. How many days from the start will A take to finish the project?
questions.e: Together they complete 210 × (1/420 + 1/630) = 5/6. A needs another 70 days for the remaining 1/6, totalling 280.

questions.q: Survey-unit review — A can complete a project in 444 days and B in 666 days. They work together for 222 days; B then leaves. How many days from the start will A take to finish the project?
questions.e: Together they complete 222 × (1/444 + 1/666) = 5/6. A needs another 74 days for the remaining 1/6, totalling 296.

questions.q: Warehouse planning case — a warehouse divides 658 files between teams A and B in the ratio 6:8. How many additional files must A receive for the new ratio A:B to become 12:8?
questions.e: The original shares are 282 and 376. To make A's share 564, it needs 564 − 282 = 282 more files.

questions.q: District-office worksheet — a district office divides 690 files between teams A and B in the ratio 4:6. How many additional files must A receive for the new ratio A:B to become 8:6?
questions.e: The original shares are 276 and 414. To make A's share 552, it needs 552 − 276 = 276 more files.

questions.q: Health-programme report — A supplier wants a 40% profit on an item costing Rs 20000, even after allowing a 30% discount on its marked price. What marked price is required?

questions.q: Scholarship-fund audit — A supplier wants a 30% profit on an item costing Rs 28800, even after allowing a 20% discount on its marked price. What marked price is required?
questions.e: Required selling price is 28800 × 130/100. Since that is 80% of the marked price, divide it by 0.8.

questions.q: Health-programme report — In a survey, 43 chose only A, 25 only B, 15 only C, 7 chose A and B only, 6 A and C only, 4 B and C only, and 2 chose all three. How many chose at least one?

questions.q: Transport-depot calculation — In a survey, 42 chose only A, 24 only B, 14 only C, 6 chose A and B only, 5 A and C only, 3 B and C only, and 1 chose all three. How many chose at least one?
questions.e: The seven disjoint regions are added once: 42+24+14+6+5+3+1 = 95.

questions.q: Transport-depot calculation — Two triangles are similar. A side of 9 cm in the smaller corresponds to 36 cm in the larger. If another smaller side is 8 cm, what is its corresponding larger side?

questions.q: Health-programme report — Two triangles are similar. A side of 10 cm in the smaller corresponds to 50 cm in the larger. If another smaller side is 9 cm, what is its corresponding larger side?
questions.e: The scale factor is 50/10 = 5; therefore 9 × 5 = 45 cm.

questions.q: Scholarship-fund audit — After a 25% discount and then 12.5% sales tax, an equipment bill for a scholarship fund is Rs 23625. What was the listed price?
questions.e: If L is the list price, L × 75/100 × 112.5/100 = 23625, giving L = 28000.

questions.q: District-office worksheet — After a 20% discount and then 10% sales tax, an equipment bill for a district office is Rs 23760. What was the listed price?
questions.e: If L is the list price, L × 80/100 × 110/100 = 23760, giving L = 27000.

questions.q: Transport-depot calculation — a transport depot must select 3 representatives from 8 eligible people. If order does not matter, how many different committees are possible?

questions.q: Transport-depot calculation — Two runners start together in opposite directions on a 740 m circular track at 123.33 m/s and 92.5 m/s. After how many seconds do they first meet?
questions.e: In opposite directions their relative speed is 215.83 m/s, so time is 740 ÷ 215.83 = 3.43 seconds.

questions.q: Health-programme report — Two runners start together in opposite directions on a 760 m circular track at 108.57 m/s and 84.44 m/s. After how many seconds do they first meet?
questions.e: In opposite directions their relative speed is 193.02 m/s, so time is 760 ÷ 193.02 = 3.94 seconds.

questions.q: Scholarship-fund audit — A quarterly table for a scholarship fund records 700, 370, and 120 completed cases in three months. What percentage of the three-month total was completed in the first month?
questions.e: The total is 1190; the first-month share is 700/1190 × 100 = 58.82%.

questions.e: Repository English reference, page 230: Type “Interrogative Pronoun” corresponds to Example Word “who, what”.

She requested not to disturb her.

questions.e: Repository English reference, page 230: Type “Demonstrative Adjective” corresponds to Sentence Example “That house is mine.”.

questions.e: Repository English reference, page 226: Direct Speech “He said, "The sun rises in the east."” corresponds to Indirect Speech “He said that the sun rises in the east.”.

questions.e: Repository English reference, page 233: Preposition “With” corresponds to Rule “Comparison between similar things”.

The policy was not implemented in January.
The policy were implemented in January.
The policy was implemented in January.
questions.e: The policy was implemented in January. (De-inflated.)

o: Before a certain or specific unidentified thing
No article before names of people
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 225: Rule “Before consonant sounds (not just consonants)” corresponds to Example Sentence “He is a teacher. She bought a university bag. (Note: "University" starts with a consonant sound /juː/)”.

o: Use the when speaking of a known person or thing
Use the with names of famous books
Use the with a class of animals, birds, or objects
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 225: Rule “Use the with international organizations” corresponds to Example Sentence “The United Nations passed a new resolution. The World Bank approved the loan.”.

questions.q: Which Rule is associated with Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) “He sat in the tree, hidden by leaves. He sat on the branch and started whistling.” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 233: Rule “Confusion over "sat in/on" tree” corresponds to Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) “He sat in the tree, hidden by leaves. He sat on the branch and started whistling.”.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “She is used to work under pressure and she insists for a written order every time.”?
o: She are used to working under pressure, and she insists on a written order every time.
She is used to working under pressure, and she insists on a written order every time.
She is used to work under pressure and she insists for a written order every time.
She is not used to working under pressure, and she insists on a written order every time.
questions.e: Be used to + -ing; insist on.

questions.q: Which Sentence Type is associated with Definition / Explanation “A sentence with two or more independent clauses, joined by a coordinating conjunction, conjunctive adverb, or semicolon.” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 233: Sentence Type “Compound Sentence” corresponds to Definition / Explanation “A sentence with two or more independent clauses, joined by a coordinating conjunction, conjunctive adverb, or semicolon.”.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The report comprises of four chapters, each of which deals about a different sector.”?
o: The report comprises of four chapters, each of which deals about a different sector.
The report comprises four chapters, each of which deals with a different sector.
The report comprises four chapters, each of which deals with an different sector.
The report comprises four chapters, each of which deals with a different sector not.
questions.e: Comprise takes no of; deal takes with.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The minister resigned after a scandal engulfed his department. (Open with a participle or adverbial.)”?
o: After an scandal engulfed his department, the minister resigned.
After a scandal engulfed his department, the minister resigned not.
The minister resigned after a scandal engulfed his department. (Open with a participle or adverbial.)
After a scandal engulfed his department, the minister resigned.
questions.e: After a scandal engulfed his department, the minister resigned. (Subordinate-clause opener.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The crisis deepened, the currency fell, the markets panicked, the government dithered. (End with a short emphatic sentence.)”?
o: The crisis deepened, the currency fell, the markets panicked, the government dithered. (End with a short emphatic sentence.)
The crisis deepened, the currency fell, and the markets panicked. The government dithered not.
crisis deepened, the currency fell, and the markets panicked. The government dithered.
The crisis deepened, the currency fell, and the markets panicked. The government dithered.
questions.e: The crisis deepened, the currency fell, and the markets panicked. The government dithered. (Short emphatic close.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The reform failed. It was underfunded. It lacked support. It collapsed. (Combine into two varied sentences.)”?
o: The reform failed. It was underfunded. It lacked support. It collapsed. (Combine into two varied sentences.)
Underfunded and unsupported, the reform was not doomed from the start. It collapsed within months.
Underfunded and unsupported, the reform were doomed from the start. It collapsed within months.
Underfunded and unsupported, the reform was doomed from the start. It collapsed within months.
questions.e: Underfunded and unsupported, the reform was doomed from the start. It collapsed within months. (Participial opener + short close.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Although the warnings were clear and the data was available and the experts agreed, nothing was done. (Improve the rhythm.)”?
o: The warnings were clear, the data available, the experts agreed. Still, nothing were done.
The warnings were not clear, the data available, the experts agreed. Still, nothing was done.
Although the warnings were clear and the data was available and the experts agreed, nothing was done. (Improve the rhythm.)
The warnings were clear, the data available, the experts agreed. Still, nothing was done.
questions.e: The warnings were clear, the data available, the experts agreed. Still, nothing was done. (Parallel build + short emphatic turn.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Add a short emphatic sentence after: “For years the state ignored the rising debt, postponing every hard decision and trusting that growth would somehow close the gap.””?
o: Add a short emphatic sentence after: “For years the state ignored the rising debt, postponing every hard decision and trusting that growth would somehow close the gap.”
...trusting that growth would not somehow close the gap. It never did.
...trusting growth would somehow close the gap. It never did.
...trusting that growth would somehow close the gap. It never did.
questions.e: ...trusting that growth would somehow close the gap. It never did. (Short emphatic sentence added.)

questions.q: Which Sentence Type is associated with Definition / Explanation “A sentence with one independent clause and one or more dependent clauses.” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 234: Sentence Type “Complex Sentence” corresponds to Definition / Explanation “A sentence with one independent clause and one or more dependent clauses.”.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “He is looking forward to join the academy and hopes improving his written English there.”?
o: He is looking forward to join the academy and hopes improving his written English there.
He is not looking forward to joining the academy and hopes to improve his written English there.
He are looking forward to joining the academy and hopes to improve his written English there.
He is looking forward to joining the academy and hopes to improve his written English there.
questions.e: To in look forward to is a preposition; hope takes a to-infinitive.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The principal suggested to hold the examination in the afternoon and agreed extending the time limit.”?
o: The principal suggested to hold the examination in the afternoon and agreed extending the time limit.
The principal suggested holding the examination in the afternoon and agreed to extend the time limit.
The principal suggested holding the examination in the afternoon and agreed than extend the time limit.
The principal suggested holding the examination in the afternoon and agreed to extend the time limit not.
questions.e: Suggest takes -ing; agree takes to.

questions.s: Present and past: the four forms of each
questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Nowadays the youth is spending too much time on social media and are neglecting their studies.”?
o: Nowadays young people spend too much time on social media and neglect their studies not.
Nowadays young people spend too much time on social media and neglect their studies without.
Nowadays young people spend too much time on social media and neglect their studies.
Nowadays the youth is spending too much time on social media and are neglecting their studies.
questions.e: A general habit takes the present simple, and the plural subject young people keeps the agreement consistent.

questions.s: Present and past: the four forms of each
questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “In his essay, Orwell was arguing that political language is designed to conceal.”?
o: In his essay, Orwell argues that political language is designed to conceal.
In his essay, Orwell argues that political language are designed to conceal.
In his essay, Orwell argues that political language is not designed to conceal.
In his essay, Orwell was arguing that political language is designed to conceal.
questions.e: Use the literary present when discussing what a writer says in a text.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Turnout was low. Many citizens had lost faith in the process. (Connect, cause before effect.)”?
o: Turnout was low. Many citizens had lost faith in the process. (Connect, cause before effect.)
Many citizens had lost faith in the process. Consequently, turnout was low.
Many citizens had lost faith in the process. Consequently, turnout were low.
Many citizens had not lost faith in the process. Consequently, turnout was low.
questions.e: Many citizens had lost faith in the process. Consequently, turnout was low. (Cause first, effect last.)

questions.s: Future forms and the sequence of tenses
questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “He told the committee that he is not aware of the irregularities and will cooperate fully.”?
o: He told the committee that he was not not aware of the irregularities and would cooperate fully.
He told the committee that he were not aware of the irregularities and would cooperate fully.
He told the committee that he was not aware of the irregularities and would cooperate fully.
He told the committee that he is not aware of the irregularities and will cooperate fully.
questions.e: Both reported verbs backshift after told.

questions.s: Future forms and the sequence of tenses
questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “When the commission will announce the result, thousands of candidates will check the list.”?
o: When the commission announces the result, thousands of candidates will not check the list.
When commission announces the result, thousands of candidates will check the list.
When the commission announces the result, thousands of candidates will check the list.
When the commission will announce the result, thousands of candidates will check the list.
questions.e: A when-clause about the future uses the present simple.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Public trust collapsed. The audit revealed massive fraud. (Reorder for given-new.)”?
o: audit revealed massive fraud. This revelation collapsed public trust.
The audit revealed massive fraud. This revelation collapsed public trust.
Public trust collapsed. The audit revealed massive fraud. (Reorder for given-new.)
The audit revealed massive fraud. This revelation collapsed public trust not.
questions.e: The audit revealed massive fraud. This revelation collapsed public trust. (Cause/given first, new effect last.)

questions.s: Future forms and the sequence of tenses
questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The professor said that the Indus river flowed through four provinces, and that the seminar will start at nine.”?
o: The professor said that the Indus flows through four provinces and that the seminar would not start at nine.
professor said that the Indus flows through four provinces and that the seminar would start at nine.
The professor said that the Indus flows through four provinces and that the seminar would start at nine.
The professor said that the Indus river flowed through four provinces, and that the seminar will start at nine.
questions.e: A permanent geographical fact stays present; the arrangement backshifts to would.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “New schools were built. Literacy then rose. Funding came from a World Bank loan. (Make it flow linearly.)”?
o: New schools were built. Literacy then rose. Funding came from a World Bank loan. (Make it flow linearly.)
A World Bank loan funded new schools. Those schools raised literacy.
an World Bank loan funded new schools. Those schools raised literacy.
A World Bank loan funded new schools. Those schools raised literacy not.
questions.e: A World Bank loan funded new schools. Those schools raised literacy. (Linear: loan > schools > literacy.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The committee included delegates from Lahore, Karachi, and Quetta and three observers.”?

...from Lahore, Karachi, and Quetta; and three observers not.

questions.e: ...from Lahore, Karachi, and Quetta; and three observers. (Semicolon clarifies the higher-level grouping.)

o: an scandal engulfed his ministry. As a result, the minister resigned.
A scandal engulfed his ministry. As a result, the minister resigned.
The minister resigned. A scandal had engulfed his ministry. (Reorder so the cause precedes the effect.)
A scandal engulfed his ministry. As a result, the minister resigned not.
questions.e: A scandal engulfed his ministry. As a result, the minister resigned. (Cause before effect.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The camps lacked water. Millions were displaced by the flood. They gathered in camps. (Order linearly.)”?
o: flood displaced millions. The displaced gathered in camps. Those camps lacked water.
The flood displaced millions. The displaced gathered in camps. Those camps lacked water.
The camps lacked water. Millions were displaced by the flood. They gathered in camps. (Order linearly.)
The flood displaced millions. The displaced gathered in camps. Those camps lacked water not.
questions.e: The flood displaced millions. The displaced gathered in camps. Those camps lacked water. (Linear chain.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The candidate only failed the interview, not the written exam. (Confirm placement.)”?
o: candidate failed only the interview, not the written exam.
The candidate failed only the interview, not the written exam not.
The candidate only failed the interview, not the written exam. (Confirm placement.)
The candidate failed only the interview, not the written exam.
questions.e: The candidate failed only the interview, not the written exam. (Only limits the interview.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The verdict was announced. (Decide whether the agentless passive is acceptable.)”?
o: The verdict was announced. (Decide whether the agentless passive is acceptable.)
questions.e: Acceptable the doer (court/jury) is obvious, so the agentless passive works.

questions.s: Active Voice, Passive Voice, and Causatives
questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The minister got the file to be reviewed by his secretary. (Correct the causative.)”?
o: The minister had his secretary review the file. / had the file reviewed.
