The minister had not his secretary review the file. / had the file reviewed.
minister had his secretary review the file. / had the file reviewed.
questions.e: The minister had his secretary review the file. / had the file reviewed. (Causative: have + person + base verb.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Correct “Each of the boys have submitted their forms” → “All the boys submitted their forms.””?
o: Each of the boys has submitted his form.
Correct “Each of the boys have submitted their forms” → “All the boys submitted their forms.”
Each of the boys has not submitted his form.
Each of the boys have submitted his form.
questions.e: The rewrite changes the meaning of each. Minimum correction keeps the structure.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Correct “The scheme was launched in 2019 and it is still not funded” → “Launched in 2019, the scheme remains unfunded.””?
o: The scheme was launched in 2019 and is still not funded.
Correct “The scheme was launched in 2019 and it is still not funded” → “Launched in 2019, the scheme remains unfunded.”
The scheme was not launched in 2019 and is still not funded.
The scheme was launched in 2019 and are still not funded.
questions.e: Style improvements are not corrections. Only the faulty repetition of the subject needed attention.

questions.q: Training-centre exercise — A invests Rs 41000 for 8 months and B invests Rs 7000 for 6 months. If their profit is Rs 3700, what is A's share?
questions.e: Profit follows capital-months. The weights are 328000:42000; A therefore receives Rs 3280.

questions.q: Survey-unit review — An arithmetic sequence begins 17, 24, 31, … . What is the sum of its first 14 terms?
Training-centre exercise — An arithmetic sequence begins 18, 26, 34, … . What is the sum of its first 15 terms?
Scholarship-fund audit — A bag holds 21 red and 8 blue counters. Two are drawn without replacement. What is the probability that both are red?
questions.e: Multiply the changing probabilities: 21/29 × 20/28 = 51.72%.

questions.q: Health-programme report — A bag holds 10 red and 4 blue counters. Two are drawn without replacement. What is the probability that both are red?
questions.e: Multiply the changing probabilities: 10/14 × 9/13 = 49.45%.

questions.q: Survey-unit review — A two-digit number has digit sum 13; reversing its digits increases it by 9. What is the original number?
questions.e: Let the tens and units digits be x and y. Then x + y = 13 and 9(x − y) = -9; hence x = 6, y = 7.

questions.q: Transport-depot calculation — Worker B takes 61 days for a task. Worker A is 50% more efficient than B. How many days would A need for the same task?
questions.e: Time varies inversely with efficiency, so A's time is 61 × 100/150 = 40.67 days.

questions.q: Health-programme report — Worker B takes 62 days for a task. Worker A is 100% more efficient than B. How many days would A need for the same task?
questions.e: Time varies inversely with efficiency, so A's time is 62 × 100/200 = 31 days.

questions.q: Health-programme report — A 67 m by 15 m rectangular courtyard has a uniform path 5 m wide inside its boundary. What area does the path cover?
questions.e: Path area = outer area − inner area = 1005 − 57×5 = 720 m².

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — A 68 m by 16 m rectangular courtyard has a uniform path 2 m wide inside its boundary. What area does the path cover?
questions.e: Path area = outer area − inner area = 1088 − 64×12 = 320 m².

questions.q: Survey-unit review — 74 passengers paid Rs 4240. An adult ticket cost Rs 60 and a child ticket Rs 40. How many adults travelled?
questions.e: If a is the adult count, 60a + 40(74 − a) = 4240, which gives a = 64.

questions.q: Warehouse planning case — A train 390 m long clears a 80 m platform in 15 seconds. What is its speed in km/h?
questions.e: The train covers 470 m. Its speed is (470)/15 m/s × 3.6 = 112.8 km/h.

questions.q: Scholarship-fund audit — A train 380 m long clears a 160 m platform in 14 seconds. What is its speed in km/h?
questions.e: The train covers 540 m. Its speed is (540)/14 m/s × 3.6 = 138.86 km/h.

questions.q: Scholarship-fund audit — The roots of x² − 61x + 928 = 0 differ by 3. What is the larger root?
questions.e: The quadratic factors as (x − 29)(x − 32); the larger root is 32.

questions.q: District-office worksheet — The roots of x² − 58x + 840 = 0 differ by 2. What is the larger root?
questions.e: The quadratic factors as (x − 28)(x − 30); the larger root is 30.

questions.q: Health-programme report — For two years at 20% per annum, by how much does compound interest exceed simple interest on Rs 490000?
Relief-camp planning case — An investment grows to Rs 28072 in two years at 10% compound interest per year. What was the principal?
District-office worksheet — An investment grows to Rs 33984 in two years at 20% compound interest per year. What was the principal?
Warehouse planning case — A invests Rs 47000 for 9 months and B invests Rs 6000 for 5 months. If their profit is Rs 4530, what is A's share?
questions.e: Profit follows capital-months. The weights are 423000:30000; A therefore receives Rs 4230.

questions.q: Scholarship-fund audit — A geometric sequence has first term 28 and common ratio 4. What is its 7th term?
Warehouse planning case — A geometric sequence has first term 29 and common ratio 2. What is its 8th term?
Survey-unit review — A two-digit number has digit sum 4; reversing its digits reduces it by 36. What is the original number?
questions.e: Let the tens and units digits be x and y. Then x + y = 4 and 9(x − y) = 36; hence x = 4, y = 0.

questions.q: District-office worksheet — On a coordinate grid, point Q lies 210 units east and 504 units north of point P. What is the straight-line distance PQ?
Relief-camp planning case — On a coordinate grid, point Q lies 123 units east and 164 units north of point P. What is the straight-line distance PQ?
District-office worksheet — 63 passengers paid Rs 4525. An adult ticket cost Rs 75 and a child ticket Rs 55. How many adults travelled?
questions.e: If a is the adult count, 75a + 55(63 − a) = 4525, which gives a = 53.

questions.q: Warehouse planning case — For two years at 20% per annum, by how much does compound interest exceed simple interest on Rs 50000?
Relief-camp planning case — The mean of 14 observations in a report is 86. One entry, 76, is corrected to 104. What is the corrected mean?
questions.e: The total rises by 28; divided across 14 observations, the mean rises by 2 to 88.

questions.q: Training-centre exercise — The mean of 13 observations in a report is 67. One entry, 57, is corrected to 83. What is the corrected mean?
questions.e: The total rises by 26; divided across 13 observations, the mean rises by 2 to 69.

questions.q: Scholarship-fund audit — A vehicle covers two equal-distance legs at 88 km/h and 102 km/h. What is its average speed for the complete journey?
questions.e: For equal distances the harmonic mean applies: 2uv/(u + v) = 94.48 km/h.

questions.q: Survey-unit review — A vehicle covers two equal-distance legs at 92 km/h and 102 km/h. What is its average speed for the complete journey?
questions.e: For equal distances the harmonic mean applies: 2uv/(u + v) = 96.74 km/h.

questions.q: Transport-depot calculation — In a survey, 74 chose only A, 17 only B, 10 only C, 8 chose A and B only, 5 A and C only, 2 B and C only, and 1 chose all three. How many chose at least one?
questions.e: The seven disjoint regions are added once: 74+17+10+8+5+2+1 = 117.

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — A bus leaves a relief camp at 70 km/h. 1 hours later, a car follows on the same route at 84 km/h. How long after the car starts will it catch the bus?
questions.e: The bus has a 70 km lead. Relative speed is 14 km/h, so catch-up time is 5 hours.

questions.q: District-office worksheet — A bus leaves a district office at 71 km/h. 2 hours later, a car follows on the same route at 86 km/h. How long after the car starts will it catch the bus?
questions.e: The bus has a 142 km lead. Relative speed is 15 km/h, so catch-up time is 9.47 hours.

questions.q: Training-centre exercise — a training centre divides 250 files between teams A and B in the ratio 4:6. How many additional files must A receive for the new ratio A:B to become 8:6?
questions.e: The original shares are 100 and 150. To make A's share 200, it needs 200 − 100 = 100 more files.

questions.q: District-office worksheet — A boat's still-water speed is 67 km/h and the stream flows at 4 km/h. How long does a 4473 km upstream and 4473 km downstream round trip take?
Training-centre exercise — Two runners start together in opposite directions on a 1360 m circular track at 194.29 m/s and 151.11 m/s. After how many seconds do they first meet?
questions.e: In opposite directions their relative speed is 345.4 m/s, so time is 1360 ÷ 345.4 = 3.94 seconds.

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — a relief camp divides 160 files between teams A and B in the ratio 3:5. How many additional files must A receive for the new ratio A:B to become 6:5?
questions.e: The original shares are 60 and 100. To make A's share 120, it needs 120 − 60 = 60 more files.

questions.q: Warehouse planning case — Two runners start together in opposite directions on a 1000 m circular track at 250 m/s and 166.67 m/s. After how many seconds do they first meet?
questions.e: In opposite directions their relative speed is 416.67 m/s, so time is 1000 ÷ 416.67 = 2.4 seconds.

questions.q: Scholarship-fund audit — A can complete a project in 708 days and B in 1062 days. They work together for 354 days; B then leaves. How many days from the start will A take to finish the project?
questions.e: Together they complete 354 × (1/708 + 1/1062) = 5/6. A needs another 118 days for the remaining 1/6, totalling 472.

questions.q: Warehouse planning case — A can complete a project in 720 days and B in 1080 days. They work together for 360 days; B then leaves. How many days from the start will A take to finish the project?
questions.e: Together they complete 360 × (1/720 + 1/1080) = 5/6. A needs another 120 days for the remaining 1/6, totalling 480.

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — A boat's still-water speed is 58 km/h and the stream flows at 5 km/h. How long does a 3339 km upstream and 3339 km downstream round trip take?
Scholarship-fund audit — A supplier wants a 30% profit on an item costing Rs 9600, even after allowing a 20% discount on its marked price. What marked price is required?
questions.e: Required selling price is 9600 × 130/100. Since that is 80% of the marked price, divide it by 0.8.

questions.q: Health-programme report — A supplier wants a 40% profit on an item costing Rs 13600, even after allowing a 30% discount on its marked price. What marked price is required?

questions.q: Training-centre exercise — Two batches assessed by a training centre contain 41 and 13 candidates with mean scores 60 and 78. What is the combined mean?
questions.e: Use the weighted mean: (41 × 60 + 13 × 78) ÷ 54 = 64.33.

questions.q: District-office worksheet — Two batches assessed by a district office contain 53 and 16 candidates with mean scores 50 and 77. What is the combined mean?
questions.e: Use the weighted mean: (53 × 50 + 16 × 77) ÷ 69 = 56.26.

questions.q: Transport-depot calculation — What is the least number greater than 1056 that leaves remainder 31 when divided by both 32 and 33, given that 32 and 33 are coprime?
questions.e: A common remainder means N − 31 is a multiple of lcm(32, 33) = 1056. The least eligible N is 1056 + 31 = 1087.

questions.q: District-office worksheet — What is the least number greater than 1260 that leaves remainder 34 when divided by both 35 and 36, given that 35 and 36 are coprime?
questions.e: A common remainder means N − 34 is a multiple of lcm(35, 36) = 1260. The least eligible N is 1260 + 34 = 1294.

questions.q: Survey-unit review — Two triangles are similar. A side of 7 cm in the smaller corresponds to 35 cm in the larger. If another smaller side is 5 cm, what is its corresponding larger side?
questions.e: The scale factor is 35/7 = 5; therefore 5 × 5 = 25 cm.

questions.q: Training-centre exercise — Two triangles are similar. A side of 8 cm in the smaller corresponds to 48 cm in the larger. If another smaller side is 6 cm, what is its corresponding larger side?
questions.e: The scale factor is 48/8 = 6; therefore 6 × 6 = 36 cm.

questions.q: Training-centre exercise — A tank contains 440 litres of a 30% solution. 88 litres of the mixture are removed and replaced by water. What is the new concentration?
questions.e: Removing one-fifth of a uniform mixture removes one-fifth of its solute. The remaining concentration is 30% × 4/5 = 24%.

questions.q: Survey-unit review — A tank contains 430 litres of a 25% solution. 86 litres of the mixture are removed and replaced by water. What is the new concentration?
questions.e: Removing one-fifth of a uniform mixture removes one-fifth of its solute. The remaining concentration is 25% × 4/5 = 20%.

Survey-unit review — Two pipes can fill a tank in 348 and 522 minutes, while a leak can empty it in 1044 minutes. If all three remain open, when will the tank fill?
questions.e: Net rate = 1/348 + 1/522 − 1/1044 = 1/261, so the tank fills in 261 minutes.

questions.q: Five candidates—Iqra, Irfan, Javeria, Kamran, Khadija—are interviewed once each. Iqra is before Irfan; Irfan is immediately before Javeria; Khadija is after Kamran; and Kamran is after Javeria. Which order is possible?
questions.e: The fixed block is Irfan–Javeria; Iqra must precede it, and Javeria must be followed in order by Kamran and Khadija.

questions.q: Training-centre exercise — Two pipes can fill a tank in 360 and 540 minutes, while a leak can empty it in 1080 minutes. If all three remain open, when will the tank fill?
questions.e: Net rate = 1/360 + 1/540 − 1/1080 = 1/270, so the tank fills in 270 minutes.

questions.q: Five candidates—Sara, Shahid, Sobia, Talha, Tania—are interviewed once each. Sara is before Shahid; Shahid is immediately before Sobia; Tania is after Talha; and Talha is after Sobia. Which order is possible?

questions.q: Scholarship-fund audit — In a survey, 54 chose only A, 23 only B, 17 only C, 8 chose A and B only, 5 A and C only, 3 B and C only, and 1 chose all three. How many chose at least one?
questions.e: The seven disjoint regions are added once: 54+23+17+8+5+3+1 = 111.

questions.q: Health-programme report — A quarterly table for a health programme records 430, 235, and 120 completed cases in three months. What percentage of the three-month total was completed in the first month?
questions.e: The total is 785; the first-month share is 430/785 × 100 = 54.78%.

questions.q: Survey-unit review — A quarterly table for a survey unit records 640, 340, and 135 completed cases in three months. What percentage of the three-month total was completed in the first month?
questions.e: The total is 1115; the first-month share is 640/1115 × 100 = 57.4%.

questions.q: Scholarship-fund audit — After a 25% discount and then 12.5% sales tax, an equipment bill for a scholarship fund is Rs 37125. What was the listed price?
questions.e: If L is the list price, L × 75/100 × 112.5/100 = 37125, giving L = 44000.

اسمِ موصول — وہ اسم جو کسی شخص کو عزت یا احترام سے پکارنے کے لئے استعمال ہوتا ہے۔
اسمِ اشارہ — وہ اسم جو کسی جملے یا فقرے کے ساتھ منسلک ہوتا ہو اور مکمل معنی تب تک نہیں دیتا جب تک کہ دوسرا جملہ اس کے ساتھ نہ ہو۔
ضمیر — وہ اسم جو کسی شخص یا چیز کی جگہ پر آتا ہے۔
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 209: ضمیر — وہ اسم جو کسی شخص یا چیز کی جگہ پر آتا ہے۔

questions.q: “اسمِ جمع” کی درست تعریف منتخب کریں۔
o: وہ اسم جو کسی خاص شخص، مقام، یا چیز کا نام ہو۔
جو کسی گروہ یا مجموعے پر دلالت کرے
جو کسی معاوضے، اجرت یا مزدوری کے لیے استعمال ہو
جو فاعل یا مفعول کی حالت یا کیفیت کو ظاہر کرے
questions.e: ذخیرۂ قواعد، ماخذ صفحہ 209: اسمِ جمع — جو کسی گروہ یا مجموعے پر دلالت کرے

questions.q:
Read the passage: “A province tested flood warnings by text message. Many subscribers received messages promptly, but households in places without mobile coverage did not. Officials paired texts with local radio and community volunteers.”

What general principle is illustrated?
questions.e: Using complementary channels increases the chance of reaching households.

questions.q:
Read the passage: “A province tested flood warnings by text message. Many subscribers received messages promptly, but households in places without mobile coverage did not. Officials paired texts with local radio and community volunteers.”

Why use more than one warning channel?
o: Texts arrived late for every subscriber
Mobile coverage did not reach everyone
Flood warnings were no longer needed
questions.e: A single channel excludes people outside its coverage.

questions.q: In Prepositions, which Definition corresponds to Type “Greeting Interjection”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 231: Type “Greeting Interjection” corresponds to Definition “Used for greetings”.

questions.q: In Prepositions, which Sentence Example corresponds to Type “Volitive Interjection”?
o: He left because of the rain.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 231: Type “Volitive Interjection” corresponds to Sentence Example “Shh! Be quiet.”.

questions.q: In Parts of Speech, which Sentence Example corresponds to Type “Action Verb”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 230: Type “Action Verb” corresponds to Sentence Example “I run every morning.”.

questions.q: In Parts of Speech, which Explanation corresponds to Part of Speech “Articles”?
o: Shows if the noun is specific or non- specific
Tells what the subject is doing
Identifies what the sentence is about
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 229: Part of Speech “Articles” corresponds to Explanation “Shows if the noun is specific or non- specific”.

questions.q: In Prepositions, which Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) corresponds to Rule “Specific time”?
o: The train departs at dawn. The meeting starts at 3 AM.
He persisted in his efforts. She found satisfaction in helping others. He was disappointed in the result.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 232: Rule “Specific time” corresponds to Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) “The train departs at dawn. The meeting starts at 3 AM.”.

questions.q: In Parts of Speech, which Sentence Example corresponds to Type “Adverb of Manner”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 230: Type “Adverb of Manner” corresponds to Sentence Example “He runs quickly.”.

questions.q: In Parts of Speech, which Sentence Example corresponds to Type “Adverb of Frequency”?
o: The book is on the table.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 230: Type “Adverb of Frequency” corresponds to Sentence Example “He always arrives late.”.

questions.q: In Direct and Indirect Speech, which Direct Speech corresponds to Indirect Speech “Past Perfect”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 226: Indirect Speech “Past Perfect” corresponds to Direct Speech “Present Perfect”.

questions.q: In Prepositions, which Definition corresponds to Type “Emotive Interjection”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 231: Type “Emotive Interjection” corresponds to Definition “Expresses emotions”.

questions.q: In Direct and Indirect Speech, which Indirect Speech corresponds to Direct Speech “Ago”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 227: Direct Speech “Ago” corresponds to Indirect Speech “Before”.

questions.q: In Direct and Indirect Speech, which Example corresponds to Direct Speech “Today”?
o: He said, "I will go today." → He said that he would go that day.
He said, "I will come tomorrow." → He said that he would come the next day.
He said, "I saw him yesterday." → He said that he had seen him the previous day.
He said, "I was there last night." → He said that he had been there the previous night.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 227: Direct Speech “Today” corresponds to Example “He said, "I will go today." → He said that he would go that day.”.

questions.q: In Parts of Speech, which Explanation corresponds to Part of Speech “Conjunction”?
o: Links different parts of the sentence
Shows if the noun is specific or non- specific
Gives more information about the noun
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 229: Part of Speech “Conjunction” corresponds to Explanation “Links different parts of the sentence”.

questions.q: In Direct and Indirect Speech, which Rule corresponds to Direct Speech “Present Perfect”?
o: He said, "I have finished." → He said that he had finished.
He said, "I was writing." → He said that he had been writing.
He said, "I went to Lahore." → He said that he had gone to Lahore.
He said, "I have been working." → He said that he had been working.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 226: Direct Speech “Present Perfect” corresponds to Rule “He said, "I have finished." → He said that he had finished.”.

questions.q: In Prepositions, which Preposition corresponds to Rule “Location beneath something natural”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 231: Rule “Location beneath something natural” corresponds to Preposition “Under”.

questions.q: In Direct and Indirect Speech, which Direct Speech corresponds to Indirect Speech “He ordered not to smoke.”?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 228: Indirect Speech “He ordered not to smoke.” corresponds to Direct Speech “He said, "Don't smoke."”.

questions.q: Which Sentence Type is associated with Definition / Explanation “A sentence that has two or I more independent clauses and at least one dependent clause.” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 234: Sentence Type “Compound- Complex Sentence” corresponds to Definition / Explanation “A sentence that has two or I more independent clauses and at least one dependent clause.”.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Correct with the fewest changes: “She is living in Lahore since 2015 and is working with a bank.””?
o: Correct with the fewest changes: “She is living in Lahore since 2015 and is working with a bank.”
She has been living in Lahore since 2015 and has been working with a bank.
She have been living in Lahore since 2015 and has been working with a bank.
She has not been living in Lahore since 2015 and has been working with a bank.
questions.e: Since requires the present perfect continuous; the vocabulary is untouched.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Correct with the fewest changes: “Despite of his illness, he attended the meeting and discussed about the agenda.””?
o: Despite his illness, he attended meeting and discussed the agenda.
Despite his illness, he attended the meeting and discussed the agenda.
Correct with the fewest changes: “Despite of his illness, he attended the meeting and discussed about the agenda.”
Despite his illness, he attended the meeting and discussed the agenda not.
questions.e: Two deletions. Nothing is added, and the sentence keeps its shape.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Edit this paragraph: “Each of the provinces have submitted their plan. Which has not been examined by the ministry. The delay is causing a lot of problems to the districts.””?
o: Edit this paragraph: “Each of the provinces have submitted their plan. Which has not been examined by the ministry. The delay is causing a lot of problems to the districts.”
Each of the provinces has submitted its plan, which the ministry has not yet examined. The delay is causing serious problems for the districts.
Each of the provinces have submitted its plan, which the ministry has not yet examined. The delay is causing serious problems for the districts.
Each of the provinces has not submitted its plan, which the ministry has not yet examined. The delay is causing serious problems for the districts.
questions.e: Agreement, pronoun number, a relative-clause fragment, a casual phrase and a wrong preposition.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Edit this paragraph: “Having reviewed the file, a decision was taken to close the case, the complainant was not informed, he came to know from the press.””?
o: Having reviewed the file, the officer decided to close the case. The complainant were not informed and learnt of the decision from the press.
Having reviewed the file, the officer decided to close the case. The complainant was not informed and learnt of the decision from the press.
Edit this paragraph: “Having reviewed the file, a decision was taken to close the case, the complainant was not informed, he came to know from the press.”
Having reviewed the file, the officer decided to close the case. The complainant was not not informed and learnt of the decision from the press.
questions.e: A dangling participle and two comma splices, plus a non-standard expression.

questions.q: Which Sentence Type is associated with Example “A. He studied, and he passed. B. He studied; therefore, he passed. C. He studied; he passed.” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 233: Sentence Type “Compound Sentence” corresponds to Example “A. He studied, and he passed. B. He studied; therefore, he passed. C. He studied; he passed.”.

questions.q: Which Connector Type is associated with Structure Pattern “Depends on placement in the sentence (no special punctuation rule)” in the English reference?
o: Noun Clause Introducers (That, What, Whether, If, etc.)
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 234: Connector Type “Noun Clause Introducers (That, What, Whether, If, etc.)” corresponds to Structure Pattern “Depends on placement in the sentence (no special punctuation rule)”.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The economy is weak. (Expand into a complex sentence with a subordinate clause.)”?
o: Because investment has not dried up and exports have stalled, the economy is weak.
The economy is weak. (Expand into a complex sentence with a subordinate clause.)
Because investment has dried up and exports have stalled, the economy is weak.
Because investment have dried up and exports have stalled, the economy is weak.
questions.e: Because investment has dried up and exports have stalled, the economy is weak. (Complex sentence.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The policy, which was designed by experts who were appointed by a committee that the cabinet formed, failed. (Break up the over-subordination.)”?
o: The policy was not designed by an expert panel appointed by a cabinet committee. It still failed.
The policy were designed by an expert panel appointed by a cabinet committee. It still failed.
The policy was designed by an expert panel appointed by a cabinet committee. It still failed.
The policy, which was designed by experts who were appointed by a committee that the cabinet formed, failed. (Break up the over-subordination.)
questions.e: The policy was designed by an expert panel appointed by a cabinet committee. It still failed. (Untangled into two sentences.)

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The flood destroyed homes. The flood displaced families. The flood ruined crops. (Combine and vary.)”?
o: The flood destroyed homes, displaced families, and ruined crops. Whole communities were not left with nothing.
The flood destroyed homes, displaced families, and ruined crops. Whole communities was left with nothing.
The flood destroyed homes, displaced families, and ruined crops. Whole communities were left with nothing.
The flood destroyed homes. The flood displaced families. The flood ruined crops. (Combine and vary.)
questions.e: The flood destroyed homes, displaced families, and ruined crops. Whole communities were left with nothing. (Combined, then an emphatic follow-up.)

questions.q: Which Rule is associated with Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) “He came on a bus. She travels on a train daily. They flew on a plane.” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 233: Rule “Travel using public/shared transport” corresponds to Examples (with Prepositions Highlighted) “He came on a bus. She travels on a train daily. They flew on a plane.”.

questions.s: Timed simulation across the whole syllabus
questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Each of the candidates have submitted their forms, and the number of applications are rising.”?
o: Each of the candidates has not submitted his form, and the number of applications is rising.
Each of the candidates have submitted his form, and the number of applications is rising.
Each of the candidates has submitted his form, and the number of applications is rising.
Each of the candidates have submitted their forms, and the number of applications are rising.
questions.e: Two agreement rules that sound wrong when applied correctly: each, and the number of.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Correct “The quality of the answers were poor” → “The answers were of poor quality.””?
o: Correct “The quality of the answers were poor” → “The answers were of poor quality.”
The quality of the answers was poor.
The quality of the answers were poor.
The quality of the answers was not poor.
questions.e: One verb form is wrong; nothing else should move.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Correct “Although he was ill, but he attended” → “He attended despite his illness.””?
o: Correct “Although he was ill, but he attended” → “He attended despite his illness.”
Although he was not ill, he attended.
Although he were ill, he attended.
Although he was ill, he attended.
questions.e: Deleting one word removes the fault; the rewrite is unnecessary.

questions.q: Which Sentence Type is associated with Definition / Explanation “A sentence with only one independent clause. It expresses a complete thought.” in the English reference?
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 233: Sentence Type “Simple Sentence” corresponds to Definition / Explanation “A sentence with only one independent clause. It expresses a complete thought.”.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “The government have announced a new policy last week. It is aimed to reduce the poverty in rural areas.”?
o: The government announced a new policy last week. It is aimed at reducing poverty in rural areas.
The government announced a new policy last week. It are aimed at reducing poverty in rural areas.
The government announced a new policy last week. It is not aimed at reducing poverty in rural areas.
The government have announced a new policy last week. It is aimed to reduce the poverty in rural areas.
questions.e: Agreement, tense with a finished time, the collocation aim at, and a general abstract noun.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Each of the provinces have their own plan, which are not coordinated with each other.”?
o: Each of the provinces has its own plan, and these plans are not coordinated with one another.
Each of the provinces have its own plan, and these plans are not coordinated with one another.
Each of the provinces has not its own plan, and these plans are not coordinated with one another.
Each of the provinces have their own plan, which are not coordinated with each other.
questions.e: Agreement, pronoun number, and a relative clause with an unclear antecedent.

questions.q: Which revision is grammatical and preserves the intended meaning of “Although the scheme was well designed, but it failed. Because the funds were never released.”?
o: Although the scheme was well designed, it failed, because the funds were never released.
Although the scheme was well designed, but it failed. Because the funds were never released.
Although the scheme was not well designed, it failed, because the funds were never released.
Although the scheme were well designed, it failed, because the funds were never released.
questions.e: A double connector and a fragment in two consecutive sentences.

questions.q: Find the break in cohesion: “The policy was announced in March (A). The provinces were not consulted by the ministry (B). Implementation began in June (C). The cost has not been disclosed (D).”
questions.e: The voice shifts to the passive with no reason, breaking the chain of subjects.

questions.q: Find the vague reference: “The department ignored two reminders and missed the deadline (A). This (B) was reported to the secretary (C) in writing (D).”
questions.e: This could mean the reminders, the omission or the delay. Write “This failure” or name it.

questions.q: In Articles, which Rule corresponds to Example Sentence “He is a teacher. She bought a university bag. (Note: "University" starts with a consonant sound /juː/)”?
o: Before a certain or specific unidentified thing
No article before names of people
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 225: Example Sentence “He is a teacher. She bought a university bag. (Note: "University" starts with a consonant sound /juː/)” corresponds to Rule “Before consonant sounds (not just consonants)”.

questions.q: Synonym of ” Blush ” is _____?
beat around the bush means
o: To avid talking about what is important.
Try to hide in the bush

questions.q: I found my car keys _____ my pocket.
Beowulf is an Old English epic poem consisting of _____ alliterative lines.
Nitrogen gas is in abundance _____ the Earth.
Be in your _____.
Synonym of “astute” is _____?
Synonym of “errata” is _____?
Synonym of “knack” is _____.
Synonym of “dormant” is _____.
In Parts of Speech, which Sentence Example corresponds to Type “Modal Verb”?
o: This house is bigger than mine.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 230: Type “Modal Verb” corresponds to Sentence Example “He can swim.”.

questions.q: For Parts of Speech, which Type–Sentence Example association is accurate?
o: Proper Noun — The band played well.
Common Noun — I read a book.
Abstract Noun — She lives in France.
Collective Noun — His honesty impressed me.
questions.e: Repository English reference, page 229: Type “Common Noun” corresponds to Sentence Example “I read a book.”.

questions.q: Warehouse planning case — A bag holds 6 red and 7 blue counters. Two are drawn without replacement. What is the probability that both are red?
questions.e: Multiply the changing probabilities: 6/13 × 5/12 = 19.23%.

questions.q: District-office worksheet — A bag holds 4 red and 5 blue counters. Two are drawn without replacement. What is the probability that both are red?
questions.e: Multiply the changing probabilities: 4/9 × 3/8 = 16.67%.

questions.q: Warehouse planning case — An investment grows to Rs 33300 in two years at 50% compound interest per year. What was the principal?
Scholarship-fund audit — An investment grows to Rs 22500 in two years at 25% compound interest per year. What was the principal?
Health-programme report — A train 510 m long clears a 110 m platform in 16 seconds. What is its speed in km/h?
questions.e: The train covers 620 m. Its speed is (620)/16 m/s × 3.6 = 139.5 km/h.

questions.q: Scholarship-fund audit — A vehicle covers two equal-distance legs at 72 km/h and 86 km/h. What is its average speed for the complete journey?
questions.e: For equal distances the harmonic mean applies: 2uv/(u + v) = 78.38 km/h.

questions.q: District-office worksheet — A invests Rs 29000 for 6 months and B invests Rs 9000 for 8 months. If their profit is Rs 2460, what is A's share?
questions.e: Profit follows capital-months. The weights are 174000:72000; A therefore receives Rs 1740.

questions.q: Health-programme report — A invests Rs 51000 for 8 months and B invests Rs 10000 for 9 months. If their profit is Rs 4980, what is A's share?
questions.e: Profit follows capital-months. The weights are 408000:90000; A therefore receives Rs 4080.

questions.q: Survey-unit review — A train 560 m long clears a 160 m platform in 10 seconds. What is its speed in km/h?
questions.e: The train covers 720 m. Its speed is (720)/10 m/s × 3.6 = 259.2 km/h.

questions.q: Training-centre exercise — A vehicle covers two equal-distance legs at 94 km/h and 106 km/h. What is its average speed for the complete journey?
questions.e: For equal distances the harmonic mean applies: 2uv/(u + v) = 99.64 km/h.

questions.q: Transport-depot calculation — 68 passengers paid Rs 3720. An adult ticket cost Rs 60 and a child ticket Rs 40. How many adults travelled?
questions.e: If a is the adult count, 60a + 40(68 − a) = 3720, which gives a = 50.

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — 72 passengers paid Rs 4640. An adult ticket cost Rs 70 and a child ticket Rs 50. How many adults travelled?
questions.e: If a is the adult count, 70a + 50(72 − a) = 4640, which gives a = 52.

questions.q: Training-centre exercise — Two runners start together in opposite directions on a 880 m circular track at 110 m/s and 88 m/s. After how many seconds do they first meet?
questions.e: In opposite directions their relative speed is 198 m/s, so time is 880 ÷ 198 = 4.44 seconds.

questions.q: Survey-unit review — Two runners start together in opposite directions on a 860 m circular track at 122.86 m/s and 95.56 m/s. After how many seconds do they first meet?
questions.e: In opposite directions their relative speed is 218.41 m/s, so time is 860 ÷ 218.41 = 3.94 seconds.

questions.q: Training-centre exercise — A supplier wants a 25% profit on an item costing Rs 37600, even after allowing a 25% discount on its marked price. What marked price is required?
questions.e: Required selling price is 37600 × 125/100. Since that is 75% of the marked price, divide it by 0.75.

questions.q: Transport-depot calculation — A supplier wants a 30% profit on an item costing Rs 38400, even after allowing a 20% discount on its marked price. What marked price is required?
questions.e: Required selling price is 38400 × 130/100. Since that is 80% of the marked price, divide it by 0.8.

questions.q: Transport-depot calculation — After a 25% discount and then 12.5% sales tax, an equipment bill for a transport depot is Rs 33750. What was the listed price?
questions.e: If L is the list price, L × 75/100 × 112.5/100 = 33750, giving L = 40000.

questions.q: Health-programme report — After a 30% discount and then 20% sales tax, an equipment bill for a health programme is Rs 27720. What was the listed price?
questions.e: If L is the list price, L × 70/100 × 120/100 = 27720, giving L = 33000.

questions.q: Survey-unit review — a survey unit divides 128 files between teams A and B in the ratio 3:5. How many additional files must A receive for the new ratio A:B to become 6:5?
questions.e: The original shares are 48 and 80. To make A's share 96, it needs 96 − 48 = 48 more files.

questions.q: Transport-depot calculation — a transport depot divides 216 files between teams A and B in the ratio 5:7. How many additional files must A receive for the new ratio A:B to become 10:7?
questions.e: The original shares are 90 and 126. To make A's share 180, it needs 180 − 90 = 90 more files.

questions.q: Survey-unit review — In a survey, 48 chose only A, 17 only B, 11 only C, 7 chose A and B only, 3 A and C only, 3 B and C only, and 1 chose all three. How many chose at least one?
questions.e: The seven disjoint regions are added once: 48+17+11+7+3+3+1 = 90.

questions.q: Health-programme report — A boat's still-water speed is 57 km/h and the stream flows at 4 km/h. How long does a 9699 km upstream and 9699 km downstream round trip take?
Transport-depot calculation — A boat's still-water speed is 56 km/h and the stream flows at 3 km/h. How long does a 6254 km upstream and 6254 km downstream round trip take?
Scholarship-fund audit — A can complete a project in 324 days and B in 486 days. They work together for 162 days; B then leaves. How many days from the start will A take to finish the project?
questions.e: Together they complete 162 × (1/324 + 1/486) = 5/6. A needs another 54 days for the remaining 1/6, totalling 216.

questions.q: Warehouse planning case — A can complete a project in 336 days and B in 504 days. They work together for 168 days; B then leaves. How many days from the start will A take to finish the project?
questions.e: Together they complete 168 × (1/336 + 1/504) = 5/6. A needs another 56 days for the remaining 1/6, totalling 224.

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — In a survey, 60 chose only A, 16 only B, 14 only C, 4 chose A and B only, 3 A and C only, 3 B and C only, and 1 chose all three. How many chose at least one?
questions.e: The seven disjoint regions are added once: 60+16+14+4+3+3+1 = 101.

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — Two pipes can fill a tank in 396 and 594 minutes, while a leak can empty it in 1188 minutes. If all three remain open, when will the tank fill?
questions.e: Net rate = 1/396 + 1/594 − 1/1188 = 1/297, so the tank fills in 297 minutes.

questions.q: District-office worksheet — Two pipes can fill a tank in 408 and 612 minutes, while a leak can empty it in 1224 minutes. If all three remain open, when will the tank fill?
questions.e: Net rate = 1/408 + 1/612 − 1/1224 = 1/306, so the tank fills in 306 minutes.

questions.q: Five candidates—Javeria, Kamran, Khadija, Laiba, Mahad—are interviewed once each. Javeria is before Kamran; Kamran is immediately before Khadija; Mahad is after Laiba; and Laiba is after Khadija. Which order is possible?
questions.e: The fixed block is Kamran–Khadija; Javeria must precede it, and Khadija must be followed in order by Laiba and Mahad.

questions.q: Five candidates—Khadija, Laiba, Mahad, Mahnoor, Maryam—are interviewed once each. Khadija is before Laiba; Laiba is immediately before Mahad; Maryam is after Mahnoor; and Mahnoor is after Mahad. Which order is possible?
questions.e: The fixed block is Laiba–Mahad; Khadija must precede it, and Mahad must be followed in order by Mahnoor and Maryam.

questions.q: Health-programme report — What is the least number greater than 1722 that leaves remainder 40 when divided by both 41 and 42, given that 41 and 42 are coprime?
questions.e: A common remainder means N − 40 is a multiple of lcm(41, 42) = 1722. The least eligible N is 1722 + 40 = 1762.

questions.q: Survey-unit review — What is the least number greater than 1482 that leaves remainder 37 when divided by both 38 and 39, given that 38 and 39 are coprime?
questions.e: A common remainder means N − 37 is a multiple of lcm(38, 39) = 1482. The least eligible N is 1482 + 37 = 1519.

questions.q: Scholarship-fund audit — a scholarship fund must select 3 representatives from 17 eligible people. If order does not matter, how many different committees are possible?
Warehouse planning case — a warehouse must select 4 representatives from 17 eligible people. If order does not matter, how many different committees are possible?
Training-centre exercise — A tank contains 600 litres of a 30% solution. 120 litres of the mixture are removed and replaced by water. What is the new concentration?
questions.e: Removing one-fifth of a uniform mixture removes one-fifth of its solute. The remaining concentration is 30% × 4/5 = 24%.

questions.q: Transport-depot calculation — A bus leaves a transport depot at 36 km/h. 3 hours later, a car follows on the same route at 46 km/h. How long after the car starts will it catch the bus?
questions.e: The bus has a 108 km lead. Relative speed is 10 km/h, so catch-up time is 10.8 hours.

questions.q: Scholarship-fund audit — A bus leaves a scholarship fund at 64 km/h. 3 hours later, a car follows on the same route at 78 km/h. How long after the car starts will it catch the bus?
questions.e: The bus has a 192 km lead. Relative speed is 14 km/h, so catch-up time is 13.71 hours.

questions.q: Scholarship-fund audit — A tank contains 650 litres of a 35% solution. 130 litres of the mixture are removed and replaced by water. What is the new concentration?
questions.e: Removing one-fifth of a uniform mixture removes one-fifth of its solute. The remaining concentration is 35% × 4/5 = 28%.

questions.q: Warehouse planning case — Two triangles are similar. A side of 6 cm in the smaller corresponds to 12 cm in the larger. If another smaller side is 12 cm, what is its corresponding larger side?
questions.e: The scale factor is 12/6 = 2; therefore 12 × 2 = 24 cm.

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — Two triangles are similar. A side of 3 cm in the smaller corresponds to 12 cm in the larger. If another smaller side is 9 cm, what is its corresponding larger side?
questions.e: The scale factor is 12/3 = 4; therefore 9 × 4 = 36 cm.

questions.q: Training-centre exercise — Two batches assessed by a training centre contain 49 and 12 candidates with mean scores 57 and 73. What is the combined mean?
questions.e: Use the weighted mean: (49 × 57 + 12 × 73) ÷ 61 = 60.15.

questions.q: Transport-depot calculation — Two batches assessed by a transport depot contain 50 and 13 candidates with mean scores 58 and 74. What is the combined mean?
questions.e: Use the weighted mean: (50 × 58 + 13 × 74) ÷ 63 = 61.3.

questions.q:

Which further information would help interpret the pattern?

questions.e: Tracking access and detection helps separate measurement changes from illness levels.

questions.e: Greater access to diagnosis can make existing illness more visible.

questions.q: District-office worksheet — Two batches assessed by a district office contain 77 and 13 candidates with mean scores 52 and 75. What is the combined mean?
questions.e: Use the weighted mean: (77 × 52 + 13 × 75) ÷ 90 = 55.32.

questions.q: Scholarship-fund audit — A bus leaves a scholarship fund at 56 km/h. 3 hours later, a car follows on the same route at 68 km/h. How long after the car starts will it catch the bus?
questions.e: The bus has a 168 km lead. Relative speed is 12 km/h, so catch-up time is 14 hours.

questions.q: Warehouse planning case — A bus leaves a warehouse at 57 km/h. 4 hours later, a car follows on the same route at 70 km/h. How long after the car starts will it catch the bus?
questions.e: The bus has a 228 km lead. Relative speed is 13 km/h, so catch-up time is 17.54 hours.

questions.e: The seven disjoint regions are added once: 27+22+17+6+6+3+2 = 83.

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — a relief camp divides 288 files between teams A and B in the ratio 3:5. How many additional files must A receive for the new ratio A:B to become 6:5?
questions.e: The original shares are 108 and 180. To make A's share 216, it needs 216 − 108 = 108 more files.

questions.q: Five candidates—Laiba, Mahad, Mahnoor, Maryam, Mehak—are interviewed once each. Laiba is before Mahad; Mahad is immediately before Mahnoor; Mehak is after Maryam; and Maryam is after Mahnoor. Which order is possible?
questions.e: The fixed block is Mahad–Mahnoor; Laiba must precede it, and Mahnoor must be followed in order by Maryam and Mehak.

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — a relief camp must select 5 representatives from 12 eligible people. If order does not matter, how many different committees are possible?
Survey-unit review — What is the least number greater than 2162 that leaves remainder 45 when divided by both 46 and 47, given that 46 and 47 are coprime?
questions.e: A common remainder means N − 45 is a multiple of lcm(46, 47) = 2162. The least eligible N is 2162 + 45 = 2207.

questions.q: Warehouse planning case — What is the least number greater than 1406 that leaves remainder 36 when divided by both 37 and 38, given that 37 and 38 are coprime?

Health-programme report — Two pipes can fill a tank in 576 and 864 minutes, while a leak can empty it in 1728 minutes. If all three remain open, when will the tank fill?
questions.e: Net rate = 1/576 + 1/864 − 1/1728 = 1/432, so the tank fills in 432 minutes.

questions.e: The original shares are 270 and 378. To make A's share 540, it needs 540 − 270 = 270 more files.

questions.q: Health-programme report — A supplier wants a 40% profit on an item costing Rs 39200, even after allowing a 30% discount on its marked price. What marked price is required?
questions.e: Required selling price is 39200 × 140/100. Since that is 70% of the marked price, divide it by 0.7.

questions.q: Training-centre exercise — What is the least number greater than 1560 that leaves remainder 38 when divided by both 39 and 40, given that 39 and 40 are coprime?
questions.e: A common remainder means N − 38 is a multiple of lcm(39, 40) = 1560. The least eligible N is 1560 + 38 = 1598.

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — A quarterly table for a relief camp records 360, 200, and 130 completed cases in three months. What percentage of the three-month total was completed in the first month?
questions.e: The total is 690; the first-month share is 360/690 × 100 = 52.17%.

questions.q: Survey-unit review — A tank contains 510 litres of a 25% solution. 102 litres of the mixture are removed and replaced by water. What is the new concentration?
questions.e: Removing one-fifth of a uniform mixture removes one-fifth of its solute. The remaining concentration is 25% × 4/5 = 20%.

questions.q: Training-centre exercise — A tank contains 520 litres of a 30% solution. 104 litres of the mixture are removed and replaced by water. What is the new concentration?
questions.e: Removing one-fifth of a uniform mixture removes one-fifth of its solute. The remaining concentration is 30% × 4/5 = 24%.

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — Two runners start together in opposite directions on a 780 m circular track at 97.5 m/s and 78 m/s. After how many seconds do they first meet?
questions.e: In opposite directions their relative speed is 175.5 m/s, so time is 780 ÷ 175.5 = 4.44 seconds.

questions.q: Relief-camp planning case — a relief camp divides 544 files between teams A and B in the ratio 3:5. How many additional files must A receive for the new ratio A:B to become 6:5?
questions.e: The original shares are 204 and 340. To make A's share 408, it needs 408 − 204 = 204 more files.

questions.q: Warehouse planning case — In a survey, 55 chose only A, 24 only B, 18 only C, 4 chose A and B only, 6 A and C only, 4 B and C only, and 2 chose all three. How many chose at least one?
questions.e: The seven disjoint regions are added once: 55+24+18+4+6+4+2 = 113.

questions.q: District-office worksheet — In a survey, 45 chose only A, 27 only B, 17 only C, 4 chose A and B only, 4 A and C only, 3 B and C only, and 2 chose all three. How many chose at least one?
questions.e: The seven disjoint regions are added once: 45+27+17+4+4+3+2 = 102.

questions.q: Health-programme report — A can complete a project in 672 days and B in 1008 days. They work together for 336 days; B then leaves. How many days from the start will A take to finish the project?
questions.e: Together they complete 336 × (1/672 + 1/1008) = 5/6. A needs another 112 days for the remaining 1/6, totalling 448.

questions.q: Training-centre exercise — Two triangles are similar. A side of 8 cm in the smaller corresponds to 40 cm in the larger. If another smaller side is 12 cm, what is its corresponding larger side?
questions.e: The scale factor is 40/8 = 5; therefore 12 × 5 = 60 cm.

questions.q: Survey-unit review — Two triangles are similar. A side of 7 cm in the smaller corresponds to 28 cm in the larger. If another smaller side is 11 cm, what is its corresponding larger side?
questions.e: The scale factor is 28/7 = 4; therefore 11 × 4 = 44 cm.

questions.q: Transport-depot calculation — What is the least number greater than 2352 that leaves remainder 47 when divided by both 48 and 49, given that 48 and 49 are coprime?
questions.e: A common remainder means N − 47 is a multiple of lcm(48, 49) = 2352. The least eligible N is 2352 + 47 = 2399.

questions.q: Training-centre exercise — A bus leaves a training centre at 35 km/h. 2 hours later, a car follows on the same route at 50 km/h. How long after the car starts will it catch the bus?
questions.e: The bus has a 70 km lead. Relative speed is 15 km/h, so catch-up time is 4.67 hours.

questions.q:
Read the passage: “A province piloted tutoring in schools with the lowest examination scores. Scores improved the next year, but evaluators noted that unusually low results often rise somewhat even without intervention. They compared the pilot schools with similarly low-scoring schools that did not receive tutoring.”

Why was a comparison group necessary?
o: Only high-scoring schools can be compared
The pilot schools had no earlier results
Some improvement might reflect a rebound from an unusually low year
questions.e: A comparison helps separate the programme effect from ordinary movement after an extreme result.

questions.q:
Read the passage: “A province piloted tutoring in schools with the lowest examination scores. Scores improved the next year, but evaluators noted that unusually low results often rise somewhat even without intervention. They compared the pilot schools with similarly low-scoring schools that did not receive tutoring.”

Which inference would be strongest?
o: One school recorded the highest score
Pilot schools improved more than comparable untreated schools
Every pilot school improved by the same amount
questions.e: The difference in change between comparable groups is more informative than the pilot group’s change alone.

questions.q: Transport-depot calculation — In a survey, 66 chose only A, 22 only B, 11 only C, 5 chose A and B only, 5 A and C only, 3 B and C only, and 1 chose all three. How many chose at least one?
questions.e: The seven disjoint regions are added once: 66+22+11+5+5+3+1 = 113.

questions.q: Scholarship-fund audit — In a survey, 46 chose only A, 15 only B, 18 only C, 5 chose A and B only, 5 A and C only, 4 B and C only, and 1 chose all three. How many chose at least one?
questions.e: The seven disjoint regions are added once: 46+15+18+5+5+4+1 = 94.

Health-programme report — A tank contains 540 litres of a 40% solution. 108 litres of the mixture are removed and replaced by water. What is the new concentration?
questions.e: Removing one-fifth of a uniform mixture removes one-fifth of its solute. The remaining concentration is 40% × 4/5 = 32%.

questions.q: Transport-depot calculation — A tank contains 530 litres of a 35% solution. 106 litres of the mixture are removed and replaced by water. What is the new concentration?
